review: Anubis 2 DoubleMax: Slot OverviewSlot makers, for whatever reason, have a strong affinity with Anubis, the jackal-headed god of ancient Egypt, the deity in charge of things like mummification, the afterlife, and guide to the underworld. He has appeared in numerous casino games and headlined Reflex Gaming's DoubleMax slot Secret of Anubis (2023). That game must have struck a chord somewhere because the studio has returned to the topic and produced Anubis 2 DoubleMax, a slot which not only alters the title but alters just about everything else, from features to principle stats.Anubis 2 has a classic Reflex Gaming look to it, kind of high resolution in parts, kind of dated in others. Hieroglyphed columns stand to either side of the reels on a blazing red-lit day in ancient Egypt. The artwork is neither outstanding nor hiddy and is joined by an exotically flavoured, swaying soundtrack that fits the mood. The change in title, as displayed above the grid, is unusual and foreshadows a lot of changes to come.Anubis 2 DoubleMax slot - base gameGaming is conducted on a 5x3 matrix, creating winning components left to right from the leftmost side and right to left from the rightmost side. It has 20 paylines with which to do so. The maximum RTP has dropped to 94%, as has winning potential, while the volatility has remained high. As well as stakes of 20 c to $/€100, players may choose to use the Golden Bet, which increases the stake by 25%, causing the Anubis feature to trigger more often.On Anubis 2's list of symbols, we find J-A, scarabs, pharaoh masks, Cleopatra-types, and Anubis, awarding 0.5-1 times the bet for a line of 5 identical royals, or 1.5 to 10 times the bet for 5 identical premium symbols. 5-of-a-kind wins pay both ways. Wilds may land on all reels, but only during the Anubis feature. They replace any pay symbol and have the same value as the Anubis symbol.Anubis 2 DoubleMax: Slot FeaturesAnubis 2 DoubleMax slot - splash screenAnubis 2's main extra is the Anubis feature. The Anubis feature may trigger on any losing spin. It shuffles the reels to produce a winning combination, and after the win is awarded, the reels shuffle again. If a win appears after a shuffle, the feature continues, but if no win occurs after a shuffle, the feature ends. A win multiplier applies to each win awarded in the feature. The multiplier trail starts at x1 and doubles with each step, up to x2,048. Each winning shuffle progresses the multiplier trail by +1 step, and each win is multiplied by the current win multiplier. When the feature ends, the multiplier resets to x1.At the start of the Anubis feature, up to 6 wild or super wild positions are added to random spots on the multiplier trail. If the trail reaches a position continuing one of these wilds/super wilds, they are added to a random reel before the next shuffle. Super wilds only appear during the Anubis feature. They are 3 position high wild symbols.Bonus BuyWith a price tag of 50 times their bet, players can buy the Anubis feature.Anubis 2 DoubleMax slot - free spinsAnubis 2 DoubleMax: Slot VerdictUnexpectedly, Anubis 2 is a very different game from Secret of Anubis. Is it an improvement? That's hard to justify, but it certainly is different. Reflex Gaming has completely revamped the features, removing the Sand Storm feature and axing the Pop and Drop Cascades; even the free spins round is gone. In their place is the Anubis feature, and how you feel about it will likely be the thing which makes or breaks the entire game. On the plus side, the Anubis feature can potentially lead to runs of repeat wins, each win doubling the multiplier the way DoubleMax slots are built to do. On top of this, it is possible to trigger added wilds and even added super wilds. These are indispensable, really, because the shuffle feature literally shuffles the reels as they are, new symbols do not spin in, and there is no cascading remove and replace. So, if the symbols you have on the screen stink, there is a chance the overall result will stink, as well.An unusual system, then, but it is at least worth a look for connoisseurs of DoubleMax slots. Is it better than the way these games usually function? Hate to be that one guy, but not really. The issues are those mentioned above and the way the Anubis feature is completely random. As in, winning combinations do not automatically activate the DoubleMax multiplier, so you kind of want to lose in the base game since only non-winning spins are able to trigger the feature. Exacerbating the oddness is that in a peculiar turn of events, Reflex Gaming has dramatically decreased the max win from 20,000x+ in Secret of Anubis to a small, by comparison, 5,000x.Reflex Gaming, you know, it's a studio which marches to the beat of its own drum, shrugging off fads and fashion to make games that are distinctively theirs, for better or for worse. As a sequel, Anubis 2 reflects the developer's individuality, going against the grain in so many ways, from a changed title, completely revamped features, and seriously reduced winning potential. Usually, you can say that players who like the original will like the sequel as well, but in the case of Anubis 2, this is not so clear-cut since the two slots are so unalike.

title: Mega Mine
structured_summary: Mega Mine is a mining-themed slot set in an idyllic mountain environment, featuring a Western soundtrack. Its standout feature is the Nudging Mystery Stacks, increasing ways to win up to 32,768, especially active in free spins. The reviewer found it slow to excite but acknowledges its huge win potential, up to 50,000x stake. Visually, it combines large gem symbols with a peaceful backdrop, while the audio adds energetic Western vibes.
review: Mega Mine Nudging Ways: Slot OverviewAs the name suggests, developer Relax Gaming is taking players below ground in a mining themed slot called Mega Mine Nudging Ways. It's the first use of their trademarked Nudging Ways feature which appears in the base game and bonus round, squeezing more symbols onto the reels, thereby creating more ways to win. Features that nudge are running red hot at the moment, so if you're up for some pick axing, prospecting, and whatever else it is that goes on beneath the earth's surface, let's tunnel in.Mega Mine Nudging Ways stirred up memories of a couple of games when it first appeared on the screen. One was Yggdrasil's Temple Stackz because of all the big blocky gem symbols on the 5-reel grid. The other was Relax Gaming's previous mining themed slot TNT Tumble, though the two games function in totally different ways. Mega Mine is a less complex mining game and one where most of the time is spend above ground in an idyllic mountain setting surrounded by pines, rocks, and fast-moving clouds. Relax's sound team has paired the visuals with an excellent, full-blown Western track which gets hectic when the momentum's building, in a good way. The music would be perfect in a gunslinger game, and at times it outshines the peaceful mountaintop environment as well as the activity occurring on the reels.Mega Mine packs huge winning potential and quite a volatile math model to match. The game has two RTP forms, depending on how you approach it. In the naturally triggered free spins way, the standard RTP comes in at 96.12%, rising a few levels to 97% when buying free spins. You get the impression the game might have been custom designed with bonus buys in mind since free spins are reasonably priced and where Mega Mine really steps it up a notch. Either way, the game may be played on any device, where bets of 10 p/c to $/€20 may be selected.Matching symbols landing in any row across three or more adjacent reels, starting on the left, forms a pay win. In the regular 5x4 set-up, this means 1,024 ways to win, though due to the Nudging Mystery Stacks, there can be anywhere from 32 to 32,768 ways in play. Landing a five symbol ways win made up of high pays returns a payout of 1 to 5 times the stake. There is also a golden detonator wild symbol, not so prevalent in the base game as it lands in the same way as regular symbols, but more useful in free spins, as you'll see. At all times, wilds substitute for any pay symbol type when evaluating wins.Mega Mine Nudging Ways: Slot FeaturesThe features in Mega Mine are dominated by Relax' new Nudging Ways feature, which pops up in the base game and in free spins. The official name in the paytable is Nudging Mystery Stacks. Nudging Mystery Stacks always nudge to cover the whole reel and reveal the same symbol type. Whenever these symbols appear, they display a value between 2 and 5, which increases by +1 for each row it nudges until it is fully in view. The maximum value they can reveal is 8. The number displayed when the nudging is done results in the number of symbols that each stack reveals. Mystery Stacks can land on all reels, creating up to 32,768 ways to win.As well as regular pays, Mystery Stacks can also reveal scatter symbols. Revealing 2 or more scatters symbols awards 6 free spins, plus an extra free spin for each additional scatter triggering the Mega Free Spins feature. In Mega Free Spins, Nudging Mystery Stacks land more frequently than in the base game and may also reveal stacks of wild symbols.The third extra players may come across in Mega Mine is the feature buy option. It costs 70 times the stake to activate and guarantees at least one Nudging Mystery Stack will land to reveal scatter symbols to trigger the Mega Free Spins game.Mega Mine Nudging Ways: Slot VerdictIt took a little while before Mega Mine began to dazzle, despite being covered in all sorts of precious stones, large and small. One reason was the main Nudging Ways feature has been put to such good use by the likes of Nolimit City, it deadened some of the new feature sheen. What did keep spirits up was the dramatic Western soundtrack that keeps your foot tapping and your hopes alive. As to what was happening on the reels, it took time for Nudging Ways to finally open up and demonstrate their potential.Like actual mining, you ain't gonna find the rich stuff hanging about above ground. You've got to dig deep and uncover the riches that lie beneath the surface. So it is with Mega Mine, where the above-ground base game roars along at a fair pace, but scanty Mystery Stacks and no other features means it is difficult to strike pay dirt up there. Once the game moves on down the mine shaft for free spins, whether bought or not, is where Mystery Stacks get a chance to put together some decent wins, especially so when one or more stacks of wilds hit. Or not, as the returns from bonus games varied wildly from pitifully disappointing to pretty good. Mega Mine failed to deliver truly great results in test runs, yet it can technically reach massive proportions to the tune of up to 50,000 times the stake, making it another Relax Gaming potentially big win slot.To sum up, Mega Mine has decent stats, huge winning possibilities, and a semi new-ish feature to test drive. It wasn't kind to us during our sessions, but if you do catch it when the mine's being fruitful, it's unlikely you'll be regretting your slot choice.

Just don't expect them to be served up in a way not seen before.Of course, not every release has to weave a spellbinding cocktail of dangerously daring theme execution and white-hot innovation. Some, like Tales of Silver Megaways, are happy, competently making use of looks and gaming that have been used on numerous occasions in the past. Hey, some players go for familiarity and more power to them. For those keen on tooling around on familiar waters rather than heading for the deep blue open, Tales of Silver Megaways could be just what the captain ordered.

The other helpful aspect of expanded reels is that they pay anywhere on a payline. In other words, they do not need to be adjacent to each other, similar to the Book of Ra special symbols dynamic.The second feature is a round of Free Spins which is triggered when 3 scatter symbols land in view. However, the gameplay felt stretched thin at times, and the slot looks dated already, bringing the old Merkur game Dragon's Treasure to mind.Players who get a kick out of collecting symbols and filling meters might find a level of satisfaction from the three possibilities. It didn't take huge amounts of time to fill the collection meters either. The best results came from the Jackpot Collection round, even though the biggest jackpot we could extract was the Mini. Combining features did add a measure of extra heat, so mixing and matching them from the bonus buy is a nice touch. Another positive point is the 10k max win, though, outside the Grand Jackpot, there is a steep drop off. The archaic look and feel of Kings of Crystals might well be the deal-breaker. Some might like the old-fashioned appearance. It didn't do a whole lot for us.Strangely, King of Crystals came across underpowered despite all the features and the decent top prize. It was unwilling or unable to really cut loose, at least from what we saw. Imagine an indecisive king, who is hesitant to send his sizeable army to the threats on his borders while everyone is screaming at him to attack, yet he's constantly dithering over maps, his heart not yearning for a scrap. Kings of Crystals felt something like that. It might be okay for a bit of fantasy escapism with a jackpot chase on top if someone is into this thing. Otherwise, it's not the sort of game we'd be scrambling to go to war for.

title: Arthur’s Fortune
structured_summary: Arthur’s Fortune is a medieval-themed slot inspired by Arthurian Legends, set in a romanticized British Isles. It features straightforward gameplay with 5 reels, 20 paylines, and notable Wild Transformation and free spins bonus rounds that enhance winning potential. The reviewer praises its solid, elegant design and exciting bonus features, offering a rewarding experience without overcomplication. Visually, it boasts high-quality graphics and a theatrical soundtrack that vividly bring the Middle Ages to life.
review: Arthur’s Fortune Slot: OverviewSwedish developers Yggdrasil Gaming have decided to go all mythical in their latest slot Arthur’s Fortune. Instead of conjuring up Thor and the lads, they have shifted their focus to the British isles and the Arthurian Legends. Originally dubbed Camelot Gold, the slot received a last-minute name change, and that choice is just one of many inspired decisions that went into making the game. The rest revolve around excellent features, whose simplistic nature in theory bely how effective they are in practice. The graphics and sound have been done in typical Yggdrasil style to a high standard, and bring the Middle Ages to life on the reels in all its romanticised glory.If you play Arthur’s Fortune on a mobile phone the screen is taken up almost completely by the reels. On a desktop or larger device, players are treated to view of a green landscape, with mythical Camelot sitting triumphantly on a hill overlooking the scene. The soundtrack is suitably theatrical; in fact, if you ever used to play the first Battlefield 1942 game, it sounds a lot like the load screen music. The background might be pretty complex, but the game area is not. Made up of 5 reels, 3 rows, and 20 paylines, the setup is straight forward gaming. Perfect for low rollers, bets can be set as low as 4 p/c per spin or changed to a maximum value of $/€100. Pick a bet, spin manually or on auto and that’s all there is to it.Simplicity goes for the rules, which require combinations of three or more matching symbols on a payline for a reward. Yggdrasil has done a nice job with the symbols too, which come in two types – low and high pays. A ‘Ye Olde England’ font has been used to draw the 10-A royals to start the table off. These are followed by high pay character symbols. There is a turquoise knight, a blue knight with an epic mustache, a green night who might be Lancelot, Guinevere, and last but not least King Arthur. Five of the Arthur's worth 25 times the stake, with the rest of the crew not bad either. There is a wild which substitutes for the pay symbols and is worth 27.5 times the stake for 5 of a kind. It also doubles as the scatter which we will look at below.First though, a few facts and figures, starting with the all-important RTP which comes in at a solid 96.2%. Volatility, meanwhile, is quite high but not brutal with a hit rate of 22.17% and the free spins frequency clocks in at once per 130 spins on average. Not bad numbers at all.Arthur’s Fortune Slot: FeaturesFree spins feature in action with wild transformation symbols.So far so, straight forward, but Arthur’s Fortune can pull out some real surprises via its features. First, a Wild Transformation feature can come into play at any moment during the base game and turn up to 10 symbols wild for that spin. When that happens, a wheel spins above the reels, and whatever symbols it lands on are converted into wilds.Wild transformation come to a head during Free Spins which are triggered by the wild/scatter symbol (or via the Orb symbol as explained further below) - 3, 4, or 5 scatters anywhere in view will award free spins and starting wild conversions accordingly:3 scatters - 7 free spins and 1 symbol to wild conversion.4 scatters - 10 free spins and 2 symbol to wild conversions.5 scatters - 14 free spins and 3 symbol to wild conversions.All symbol to wild conversions last for the full duration of the bonus feature. Scatters are also part of the bonus game and landing 2 or more adds more free spins and converts more symbols like so:2 scatters: +1 free spin and 1 additional symbol to wild conversion.3 scatters: +2 free spin and 2 additional symbol to wild conversions.4 scatters: +3 free spin and 3 additional symbol to wild conversions.5 scatters: +4 free spin and 4 additional symbol to wild conversions.Sounds basic on paper maybe, but it’s worth checking out because it can go off the chart when a bunch off wilds are in action. On a further note, the game also contains an Merlin's Orb Bonus symbol. This symbol appears at random during the base game or free spins, and one in view is enough for a reward. In the base game, the orb can contain an instant prize of up to 25 times the stake or 7-14 free spins, with 1-3 symbols wild. If it appears during free spins, it can contain a cash prize of 50x, or 1-14 additional free spins.Arthur’s Fortune Slot: VerdictArthur’s Fortune is one of those solidly built games, simple, but one in which every aspect has been expertly put together. This being Yggdrasil, the game is pleasant to the senses, but its elegance goes deeper than that. Each aspect complements the other and works together to climax in an epic bonus game when firing on all cylinders.It doesn't always work your way, of course. Arthur's Fortune dishes up a fair number of dead spins when he’s not in the mood and bonus games are not guaranteed to be wild fests. But, when he is feeling benevolent, the game literally goes medieval, in a Marsellus Wallace meaning of the word. Sitting back and enjoying the last few spins of the bonus round with a bunch of wild transformations in play (as seen in the video) is quite the experience.Another good thing is that Arthur’s Fortune isn’t one of those slots that hypes up a feature like a wild conversion and then plonks one or two symbols on the fifth reel. Instead, the reels can end up showered in wilds, and when a load of symbols have been converted, wins rack up on practically each free spin. Arthur’s Fortune might not possess the highest potential around, but maxing out at 7,510 times the stake means not too many squires will be complaining.All of these details add up to an excellently constructed slot that covers the basics well while holding back something special for the features. It does it all in an unpretentious way that players looking for a straight forward slot with plenty of sting in its tail will appreciate. If you need a break from cascading features or endless reel options and want a rock-solid slot with an epic bonus game, Arthur’s Fortune is a fine choice.

title: Joker Drop PopWins
structured_summary: Joker Drop PopWins features a classic fruit and joker theme with an expandable PopWins grid for a traditional yet dynamic slot experience. Key features include the licensed PopWins mechanic, two collection meters, a pachinko-style free spins gamble, and a Super Stake option influencing volatility and bonus triggers. The reviewer finds it a solid, familiar take on PopWins, praising its gameplay and max win potential but noting limited innovation. The aesthetics are old-school fruit slot style with straightforward symbols and an engaging, retro audio-visual atmosphere.
review: Joker Drop PopWins: Slot OverviewIn a surprise move, Avatar UX's signature mechanic PopWins has been licensed by a competitor studio, in this case, Stakelogic. Up until now, PopWins has been synonymous with Avatar UX, so there was a measure of intrigue over what a bunch of new thinkers would bring to the table. Then again, cast your minds back to Mystery Drop, the PopWins copycat from Stakelogic we reviewed a few months prior, and the studio had already dropped a few hints – more on this later. For now, what's come out the other side is a game wrapped in a common theme but packing a few interesting features to go with the popping action. The real test comes from seeing a game in action, so let's find out what a third party can do with Avatar UX's contribution to the evolution of slots, officially this time.As mentioned, Joker Drop PopWins' theme isn't the most exciting, based as it is around fruit and jokers in typical Stakelogic fashion. You don't need us to tell you this type of online slot is ever-popular, so it might be of interest to players looking for a traditional looking PopWins game. The setup isn't all that traditional, though, as Joker Drop PopWins is played on an expandable game grid which starts every spin in the base game in a 5x4 layout. However, the symbols, atmosphere, and presentation are full-on old school fruit - a genre Stakelogic is partial to.Playable, popable, or whatever, on any device, players may select stakes from 20 p/c to $/€10 per spin or pay double the amount to activate the Super Stake feature. Doing so pulls scatter symbols into the bonus game, making it retriggerable. The Super Stake also affects the game's volatility, rated 5 out of 5 when switched on or 4 out of 5 when it's off. The RTP comes in a variety of forms as well, from as low as 88% up to 95.8% at best.Joker Drop PopWins is a game that pays both ways, so wins can start from the left side of the game grid or the right. In the starting position, this means players get 1,024 ways to win (not including the pay both way element), rising to 16,807 when the grid is stretched to a maximum of 7-rows high. How it works is whenever a winning combination hits, the symbols involved pop and are replaced with 2 new symbols, growing reels and ways to their maximum size.The symbols used throughout the game are utterly common-looking icons such as 10-A royals, cherries, limes, pears, plums, oranges, grapes, watermelons, and 7s. Any non-royal winning combination made up of 5 symbols is worth a payout of 0.75 to 5 times the base bet. There are wild symbols, but they only appear courtesy of the features; let's check them.Joker Drop PopWins: Slot FeaturesJoker Drop PopWins - free spins gambleAs well as the PopWins mechanic, now licensed, Joker Drop has free spins with a gamble drop feature, two collection meters, and a bonus buy.Collection MetersMiniature coins or diamond icons may randomly appear over regular symbols and are collected when they do land in their respective coin or diamond meter. Filling the diamond meter adds 5 wild symbols to reels 2, 3, or 4. Filling the coin meter adds mini reels to 5 random positions, which each award a cash prize.Free SpinsIn the base game, when all reels reach 7 symbols high, players are awarded 5 free spins. The star meter on the left side records how many reels have reached this height during a spin. Before free spins start, players can gamble for more spins via the gamble drop feature. This is a pachinko style game which drops a ball from the top of the screen into several buckets at the bottom. Land in a red 'x' means you lose and go back to the base game, or you can win extra free spins, up to 15 at the most.Free spins are played on a 5x7 sized grid, using a win multiplier starting at x3. Following each win, the multiplier increases by +1. If you entered the bonus round with the Super Stake feature activated, then diamond scatter symbols may appear - 3 of them in view awards extra free spins. Joker symbols are also used in the free spins round as the wild, replacing any of the pay symbols.Buy BonusIf buying Joker Drop's free spins feature is an option for you, then the cost for doing so is 120x the bet. Once bought, players have the choice of collecting 5 free spins or gambling them on the pachinko board.Joker Drop PopWins: Slot VerdictReviewing Joker Drop was like opening a Russian doll of surprises. The main shock was seeing Stakelogic had licensed PopWins from Avatar UX instead of just brashly using the device and palming it off as their own like they did in Mystery Drop. Apparently, Avatar UX wasn't having other studios benefit from their creative ideas and stepped in. The following discussions resulted in a deal between the two studios whereby Stakelogic would have six months of exclusive rights to the PopWins mechanic. So, all's well that ends well, money talks, and players partial to PopWins get another studio's take on it.So on to Joker Drop. You might have thought after all the legal wrangling and back-room hoopla, Stakelogic might have wanted to make something mind-altering to blow everyone away instead of just doing something fruit related. Furthermore, Stakelogic has pumped out a bunch of fruit-based Megaways games in the past, so our expectations might have been set unrealistically high. Or maybe it was a case of fruit overload. Who knows, anyway, the first look at Joker Drop was nothing special. It doesn't help that Avatar UX itself has already gone down the fruity PopWins avenue in games like CherryPop, and to a swankier extent, PapayaPop – both of which have a more unique look than Joker Drop. There is always the case sticking to something familiar was Stakelogic's goal from the start to reel in players warm to the classical look.Anyway, enough about fruit, let's move to the gameplay. Despite having the license and presumably the blessings of Avatar UX to go hog wild, Stakelogic hasn't been hugely inventive with the PopWins system. The side bits, such as the two collection meters, add a hint of originality, plus there's the pachinko thing, but there isn't much here that hasn't been seen before under Avatar UX's watch. One area the game does compare favourably is in max winnings, which are capped at 20,472x the base bet.In summation, players looking for a Vegasy PopWins experience will find it in Joker Drop, and to Stakelogic's credit, they've done it quite well. The wins pop in a satisfactory manner, the game plays well overall, and the pachinko styled free spins gamble is a fun addition. If you're are after the most traditional looking PopWins slot out there, steeped in fruit and various other classic slot icons, then Joker Drop is probably the one to go for.

title: Piggy Bank Bills
structured_summary: Piggy Bank Bills is a piggy bank-themed slot featuring stacks of banknotes with a unique win mechanic based on matching halves of banknotes. The reviewer finds it an entertaining and novel twist on slot gameplay, offering potential wins up to 5,000x the stake despite its high volatility. The game boasts bright visuals with glowing cash piles and a lively, Caribbean-inspired mariachi soundtrack that enhances the upbeat atmosphere.
review: Piggy Bank Bills: Slot OverviewYeah, yeah, yeah, it's another piggy bank game full of hogs and stacks of banknotes. Bear with us, though, because Piggy Bank Bills from Pragmatic Play plays out in a way you probably aren't used to. Mechanically speaking, it's different, but don't worry, there are plenty of pigs and cash if that's what you want to see in these sorts of games. The way you win is done in a unique way which involves matching the two halves of the same banknote to score coins. The main feature is a round of free spins where random multipliers overlay symbols to potentially aid your chances of raiding the bank.One of the first things that stands out about Piggy Bank Bills is music which sounds like it's escaped from a Mariachi party or a BBQ on a Caribbean beach. Wherever it came from, the lively soundtrack lightens the atmosphere and gets you in the mood to match banknotes. Visually, the game is bright as well, most of the screen space occupied by the 6-reel, 9-payline game grid bearing all manner of banknotes, some whole, most in halves. Around the reels lie piles of cash, glowing with a strange green and gold light. Is this an attempt to give the dough a mystical connotation, perhaps? That or it's radioactive - players' choice. Piggy Bank Bill's doesn't make it easy, though, and its high volatility (rated 5 out of 5) might be a little out of odds with the party vibe it gives off. How players win in Piggy Bank Bills is unusual, as it does not involve forming combinations of left to right matching symbols. Instead, the game grid is divided into 6 reels and 3 rows, where each cell displays half of a banknote. If the banknotes opposite each other on reels 1 and 2, or 3 and 4, or 5 and 6 match, the prize value they display is awarded. Simple as that.There are 10 values you can win - 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, or 1,000 times the bet. Wild halves can land in any position as well, substituting for all symbols except the scatter. When a wild lands opposite any paying banknote, it completes it for a payout of the value. If two wild halves land opposite each other, they join into one bill that takes a random value.Piggy Bank Bills: Slot FeaturesPiggy Bank Bills' features are pretty straightforward where you'll come across 3 minor piggy based features and free spins. The 3 Piggy features are:Piggy Bonus – as the reels spin, a piggy appears to give players a chance to win the free spins bonus.Piggy Win – after the reels stop, there is a chance the piggy randomly picks two or more losing symbols then transforms them into winning combinations.Piggy Wilds – as the reels spin, piggy may place 2, 3 or 4 wilds in random positions on the screen.Free spins are triggered when 2 free spin symbol halves land facing each other, then join into a whole scatter bill to award 8 free spins. If 2 or 3 scatter bills hit, then you get 8 free spins, plus the lowest 1 or 2 paying bills are removed from the reels, respectively.During free spins, random 2x or 3x multipliers may appear over the symbols. If a winning bill is formed, any multiplier on top of it applies to the prize value. If there are 2 multipliers on the same winning bill, they multiply each other. Also, during the bonus round, at random on any spin, the lowest paying symbol remaining on the reels may be removed.Piggy Bank Bills: Slot VerdictSome say banknotes are on the way out as we shift over to a cashless society of debit cards, credit cards, e-wallets, crypto, smartphone payments, etc. It's unlikely Piggy Bank Bills will reverse this alleged trend in any noticeable way, but it is an enjoyable return to the dollar, pound, or Euro bill. And for many, there is something immensely more satisfying about having a wallet full of notes as opposed to just carrying a card around in your pocket.Get lucky, and Piggy Bank Bills might well add to the wad of notes in your pocket. Get those 1,000x halves lining up, maybe throw in a multiplier or two, and it is possible to win up to 5,000 times your stake from the game. Attempting to do so is fairly entertaining too, and there's a novelty factor to the way wins are formed, making a quirky diversion from the standard way of playing slots.One positive thing about the way wins are formed is even if you get nothing on the first two reels, something can still hit on reels 3-4 or reels 5-6, squeezing the maximum amount of tension out of every spin. There's almost a scratch card quality about this system, as you can remain hopeful until the very last symbol has been revealed. In addition, the way the game is presented helps boost optimism as well due to the mountain of banknotes, the happy, smiling cashed-up pigs, but especially the upbeat music, which makes the experience a real capitalistic free for all.As always, when a studio tries something new, it won't suit everyone's tastes. However, the matching symbols system is an interesting concept, making Piggy Bank Bills worth checking out if you are either into the evolution of online slots or entertained by the piggy/money motif in general. In both cases, Piggy Bank Bills offers something new you don't really see in this genre or any other.

title: Wild Wild Bass 2

review: Wild Wild Bass 2: Slot OverviewFolks, folks, ever sat down to enthusiastically feast on a seafood meze that, after countless dishes, has you hating the sight of fish by the end of it? Here's yet another one, this time from developer Stakelogic, going by the name of Wild Wild Bass 2. What makes Wild Wild Bass 2 harder to stomach is that it is almost exactly the same as Wild Wild Bass mechanically, except with a bonus buy tagged on the side.It's hard not to think that Wild Wild Bass and its follow-up release only exist because their maker was desperately trying to latch onto the Big Bass Bonanza bandwagon. The original Wild Wild Bass slot must have successfully found an audience, though, because here we are reviewing a sequel. Like before, a transparent 6-reel gaming grid floats about beneath the surface of the water while fish dart about in the background and bubbles bubble away. It's a fishing slot; what else is there to say? Not the most original-looking example of one, but not bad either. Let's slither along.Wild Wild Bass 2 slot - base gameBaiting up in this fish game means picking a stake of 10 p/c to $/€200 per spin and deciding whether or not to activate the Super Stake feature. Bass symbols land bearing a random money value that is a multiplier of the bet. Bass symbol values are only awarded during the Big Catch or Insane Catch feature.Wild Wild Bass 2: Slot FeaturesWild Wild Bass 2 slot - free spinsWild symbols are central to Wild Wild Bass 2's features. They appear on the first two reels, and landing 2 of them triggers the Big Catch feature or they activate the Insane Catch when the Insane Catch symbol lands, as well.Big CatchWhen 2 wild symbols have triggered the Big Catch, reels 3, 4, 5, and 6 extend by one extra position. As well as creating more ways to win, all money values on Bass symbols are awarded in addition to normal wins. Reels return to their normal height on the next spin.Insane CatchThe Insane Catch symbol appears on reel 6. Landing 2 wild symbols and an Insane Catch symbol triggers the Insane Catch feature where 2, 3, or 4 Insane Spins are awarded. For the Insane Catch feature, reels 1 and 2 merge into one multiplier reel. On each Insane Spin, a multiplier value of x1 to x5 is awarded. Reels 3, 4, 5, and 6 change into 20 independent reels. Only Bass symbols, Insane Catch symbols, or blanks can land. Bass money symbols are awarded with the multiplier applied. At the start of each Insane Spin, the grid is cleared. Landing an Insane Catch symbol awards extra Insane Catch spins.Wild Wild Bass 2 slot - free spinsWild Wild Bass 2: Slot VerdictIt's times like this that it's hard not to question Stakelogic's motto – 'Think Bigger'. How the fudge is taking a slot, keeping most of it the same, but banging on a bonus buy thinking bigger? So, not the most original move, but you would assume Wild Wild Bass 2 arose out of the desire to include a bonus buy option to provide quicker access to the Insane Spins feature. A sound business decision, perhaps, but still, if it all seems a bit much, perhaps it's best just to accept the situation and not think too deeply about it for fear of losing your mind down a deep rabbit hole of catatonic despair.In that spirit, let's approach Wild Wild Bass 2 as if it's just been freshly served. In this scenario, okay, well, it's still a fishing-themed version of Wild Wild Riches with a few extra bits on the side. Again. At least Wild Wild Bass 2 is no worse than its predecessor, and the Insane Catch phase is quite neat. Not exactly hugely effective, though, even with an x5 locked in place as winning potential in Wild Wild Bass 2 maxes out at 10,000x the bet. This figure applies to the base game as well as free spins and compares favourably against much of the piscine competition out there.One thing to assume is that Stakelogic might have been responding to players requesting a bonus buy be added to Wild Wild Bass. Fair enough if that was the case, and anyone who wanted this very thing should be happy with the way Wild Wild Bass 2 has turned out. However, it's hard to shake the feeling Wild Wild Bass 2 is redundant if the bonus buy doesn't appeal and goes straight on the towering mound of fish slots already cluttering up the market.

Legion Gold and the Sphinx of Dead fares about as well as the slot it is copied from, but that's not saying a lot.

title: Unusual Catch
structured_summary: Unusual Catch is a fishing-themed reskin of Northern Lights Gaming's detective slot, shifting the setting from crime-solving to a watery locale. review: Unusual Catch: Slot OverviewWhat do detectives do during their time off when they're not cracking cases to help put baddies behind bars? They probably do a whole range of activities, but some of them, somewhere, surely, go fishing. The lawman who led Northern Lights Gaming's slots Unusual Suspects and More Unusual Suspects is one who likes to take to the water to bait up. He's popped up again to front Unusual Catch, and this game shares more than just a titular link and leading man with the two 'Unusual' slots that preceded it.Indeed, Unusual Catch is a reskin of Unusual Suspects, so just about everything is the same as before from a technical perspective. Naturally, the skin has been altered, so players now spend their time in a watery location rather than a downtown busting crime one. A 5-reel, 4-row matrix is Unusual Catch's gaming area, which has 25 paylines crossing it for evaluating regular wins.Scaly 10, J, Q, K, and A card ranks are Unusual Catch's low pays, awarding 1 times the bet for a line of 5 matching symbols. Hit 5 matching high-pay bottles, hooks, hats/glasses, or dinghies to collect 2 to 10 times your bet.Unusual Catch: Slot FeaturesUnusual Catch slot - free spins gambleAs before, wilds are linked to a lot of the action in Unusual Catch, and they may land on all reels. Landing a line of 5 wilds pays 10x the stake, and wilds can be used to substitute any other pay symbol. If a Purple Wild lands, it spawns more wilds or another Purple Wild symbol. When wilds appear in a position that is already framed, they increase the multiplier by +1 up to a maximum of x5.Angler Wild BonusWhen the Angler symbol lands, it populates all sticky framed positions with wilds. Multipliers on a payline are applied to any win they are part of. In the base game, after the Angler Wild bonus ends, all sticky frames are removed. During free spins, sticky frames remain in place until the round ends.Free Spins BoosterScatters can appear anywhere on the grid. When exactly 2 scatters are in view, they add 1 token to the Booster Meter, which requires 50 tokens to be filled. If the 2 scatters land on the top 3 rows, Nudging Respins are triggered. Any reel with a scatter is held and nudged down one row while the other reels get respun. Nudging Respins continue until a scatter reaches the bottom row or until 5 scatters land.Bad Bass Free SpinsLanding 3, 4, or 5 scatters triggers 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. During the round, when Angler symbols hit, they are collected on the Bonus Trail:Collecting 3 Anglers unlocks Bad Bass 1, awarding +5 free spins with an x2 multiplier.Collecting 6 Anglers unlocks Bad Bass 2, awarding +5 free spins with an x3 multiplier.Collecting 9 Anglers unlocks Bad Bass 3, awarding +5 free spins with an x5 multiplier.Collecting 12 Anglers unlocks Bad Bass 4, awarding +5 free spins with an x10 multiplier.If free spins were triggered and the Booster Meter was full, Big Boss 1 is unlocked. The meter resets after the free spins bonus.Bonus BuyPlayers may trigger the free spins bonus for the precise cost of 38.6x the bet. Sticky frames and free spins Boost Meter progress are not used when buying free spins.GambleAnother way of possibly entering free spins is by using the gamble feature. Players pick their bet, which increases or decreases the green segment on a wheel. If the needle lands on green, free spins are won; if it is on red, they are not. Sticky frames and free spins Boost Meter progress are not used when gambling for free spins.Unusual Catch slot - free spinsUnusual Catch: Slot VerdictUnusual Suspects was a slot that was able to deliver entertaining moments, what with all the wilds jumping about the place and the increasing sticky frame multipliers. So is Unusual Catch, but it wasn't as satisfying as the first time around. Which is kind of funny since it's in possession of the exact same features, and its Angler symbol collection dynamic, reminiscent of Big Bass Bonanza's free spins collection feature, feels ideally geared for a fishing game. Why is that? Perhaps part of the reason is simple second-time round fatigue, a common condition evoked by playing cloned slots. Perhaps it's because fish slots are so utterly common compared to crime games, compared to a lot, if not most, game types, really. Unusual Catch's low-key energy levels and vibe didn't help much, either. No doubt it's a combination of all of these factors.But you know, fish slots are popular, after all, so perhaps Northern Lights Gaming will achieve better success with Unusual Catch than it did from Unusual Suspects. You never know, but the original was more interesting to review on account of not being a fish slot for a change. The moustachioed detective, cracking crimes, taking on the big bosses of the underworld, it was like a little bit of crime solver cosplay. Unusual Catch, eh, it's fish. There's no collecting of fish money symbols for a change, fair dues. title: Lucky Clucks
structured_summary: Lucky Clucks is a farm-themed slot by Crazy Tooth Studio featuring quirky chicken and livestock motifs. Its main features include the BIG BuildUp mechanic with multipliers and wilds, plus Raise the Roof free spins with expanding wilds. The reviewer finds it an acquired taste with modest win potential, appealing mostly to players who enjoy oddball, low-budget titles. Visually, the game has low-quality but endearing graphics and snappy animations, complemented by humorous, irreverent audio.
review: Lucky Clucks: Slot OverviewIf you've ever felt the urge to get amongst a 'frenzy of feathers', then those blue-sky thinkers at Crazy Tooth Studio have released Lucky Clucks, a farm-themed slot to help scratch the itch. As well as loads of livestock, Lucky Clucks features several quirky features built around a concept Crazy Tooth has dubbed the Big BuildUp that involves chickens laying eggs which hatch into multipliers or wilds to potentially power wins. Toss in handfuls of corn to feed a Mother Hen Prize, or land hay bales to trigger Raise the Roof Free Spins; this is classic Crazy Tooth, let's mosey on in.It's impossible to know what will happen when a Crazy Tooth game hits the screens, so here's a heads up. Visually, Lucky Clucks isn't awe-inspiring, though its unusual quality may well appeal to players who enjoy going where CT leads. The graphics are either low quality, poorly designed, or endearing, depending on your personal opinion of these guys' work. Is Lucky Clucks a game that's clinging to the past or just low budget? Since there is no mention of it being retro or old school in the official blurb from the maker, it seems we might have to go with the latter assessment. But hey, beauty is in the eye of the beholder and all that.Lucky Clucks is played on an expandable game grid with 5 reels set up in a default 3-4-4-4-3 configuration. It features an Any Adjacent Pays system, so as long as three or more matching symbols land in any adjacent reels, players score a win – pays do not need to start from the leftmost reel. RTP comes in several forms, 96.19% being the largest possible value, while volatility is high in all versions. The corn-fed action is available on any device, taking bets ranging from between 15 p/c to $/€15 per spin.The farming theme is bolstered by a paytable possessing eleven regular pays, corn symbols, a wild, a scatter, and a bunch of chickens. Regular pay symbols are made up of J-A card ranks, 3 horseshoe tiles, piggies, goats, sheep, and cows. There is little variation in symbol value, which is relatively low, as animal premiums are all worth 0.73x the bet for a five of a kind winning combination. Wild stars substitute for all paying symbols and can land in any reel. Wilds create their own combinations though it's not made clear what the values are.Lucky Clucks: Slot FeaturesCrazy Tooth has brought back their BIG BuildUp feature that we saw before in Banana Drop, while the other extra is Raise The Roof Bonus free spins.BIG BuildUpDuring the base game, chicken symbols may land on the reels. When they hit, they increase the modifier value displayed above them at the top of the four outer reels – this could be a win multiplier or a number of added wilds. Moreover, corn symbols may land on the middle reel; these ones increase the Mother Hen Prize pot displayed above them.The BIG BuildUp feature may trigger randomly on any main game spin to award one or more of the stored Mother Hen Prize, Wild Symbols, or multipliers. Each awarded wild symbol adds an extra position to the reel. If the multipliers are awarded at the same time as the Mother Hen Prize, they multiply this prize only. If multipliers are awarded by themselves, they are applied to any appliable way wins.Raise the Roof BonusLanding 3, 4, or 5 bonus symbols triggers the Raise the Roof Bonus and 5, 7, or 9 free spins, respectively. On every free spin, one or more chickens may land to award wild symbols. Each awarded wild symbol adds an additional position to its reel for the duration of the bonus. Wild symbols persist on the board, moving one position down the reel on each following spin till they fall off. Raise the Roof cannot be retriggered.Lucky Clucks: Slot VerdictAt first, Lucky Clucks was a case of oh here we go again, another wacky release from Crazy Tooth. To be sure, the game is indeed wacky, and like just about everything Crazy Tooth does, Lucky Clucks will be an acquired taste. There are few studios out there that compare to these guys, with the exception of, say, Russian crew Igrosoft, who also stick out like a sore thumb in an entertainment industry tripping over itself to be bigger, brighter, and more innovative. Some may admire the way Crazy Tooth does its thing, following no fad or trend, seemingly oblivious to everything else going on in the iGaming sphere.Anyway, Lucky Clucks did grow on us, slightly, after playing it for a while. It's hardly what you'd call a great game, but players who like a bit of anachronistic quirk might be intrigued. The features aren't bad; the base game occasionally awards something from the BIG BuildUp to keep things bobbing along. Raise the Roof free spins triggered less frequently in a sort of barnyard Hotline 2 type way. The main issues are likely to be the fact Lucky Clucks looks budget, though the animations are snappy, and the low symbol values lead to low overall potential of 2,289x the bet. Despite the highly volatile label, it feels like Lucky Clucks might suit players who like regular features firing off modest payouts.Perhaps there's a narrow niche out there that would be ideal for Lucky Clucks to nest in. If old school looks, humorous critters, or irreverent humour count for more than big wins, Lucky Clucks might be the go. There's an okay game lurking here for the right person, but as is often the case, Crazy Tooth makes you work hard to find it.

title: Divine Lotus
structured_summary: Divine Lotus is an Asian-themed slot inspired by Thunderkick's Pink Elephants, set in a serene sky with lotus flowers and dragons. It features a Mystery Lotus symbol that transforms into high-paying symbols and an innovative free spins round with a lotus meter for extra spins and symbol removal. review: Divine Lotus (Thunderkick): OverviewA Thunderkick slot with 6 reels and 4096 ways to win, seems familiar? There aren't too many of them out there after all, and veteran players won't have any problems identifying Divine Lotus as an Asian-themed version of one of Thunderkick's most successful slots to date, Pink Elephants. So, is it merely a re-skin, or does it bring anything new to the table? And is the generic title a tell-tale of equally generic gameplay? We're about to find out.Just as we predicted, Thunderkick's last slot, Riders of the Storm, went on to become a big hit with players in the community. But things move quickly in this industry, and there's little time to sit back and eat cake while resting on one's laurels, for players are impatiently waiting like hungry hatchlings to be fed new slots. With a zen-like feel, Divine Lotus takes us to a mesmerizing place floating in the sky, a place where mysterious lotus flowers transform into matching symbols and where the free spins round can bring even more lotuses into play, potentially leading to nearly a full screen of matching premium symbols. With a theoretical return to player set to 96.14%, you can play it from 0.10 to €/$100 per spin across all devices.Generally speaking, Asian-themed slots have a tendency to be as generic as Chinese tablet firmware. Thankfully we're spared most of the clichés here. Set amongst the clouds and with floating lush island and majestic waterfalls in the background that drop to the nothingness below, Divine Lotus does indeed live up to its name. On the reels, you'll see dragon scale 9 to A royals as well as a diversity of dragon whelps that are blue, green, yellow, and red in colour. Of these, the red dragon is the most rewarding, giving you 5 times your stake for a 6 of a kind combination. The top symbol, however, is the fiery mama dragon - 6 of her will give you 10 times your stake.As always, Thunderkick displays the value of the symbols relative to the current bet size, which is exactly how it should be. A wild symbol in the form of a "W" is also present. It replaces all symbols but the scatter and lotus.Divine Lotus (Thunderkick): FeaturesFree spins in actionThe first thing that you'll notice to stand out from Pink Elephants is the addition of the Mystery Lotus feature. Currently trending as one of the most popular features on the market, when these mystery symbols land on the reels in the base game, all instances of them will transform into a randomly chosen high-paying symbol.The Mystery Lotus comes to even better use in the Free Spins round which is triggered in a rather unconventional way. To gain access, you need to land lotus scatter symbols on 3 or more reels which will give you 2 free spins. But don't despair - each scatter symbol also awards 1 extra free spin. Thus, 5 scatters spread across 3 reels will give you a starting setup of 7 free spins.Once inside, the backdrop changes from sunrise to sunset, and you'll also notice a lotus meter on the left side of the reels. It keeps track of every lotus flower collected and when enough lotuses have been added to fill the meter, the indicated symbol is removed from the reels and replaced by a Mystery Lotus symbol for the rest of the round as well as rewarding an extra free spin. Moreover, as a result of the transformation, the Mystery Lotus symbol then cannot transform into that particular symbol. Highly volatile, the Divine Lotus free spins feature can lead to payouts of up to 8,709 times your total stake.Divine Lotus (Thunderkick): VerdictAs you can tell, Divine Lotus is obviously built on the Pink Elephant template, and both games are indeed quite similar. When it comes to technicalities such as RTP, volatility, and maximum payout, there's little to set them apart. Therefore, choosing which one to play will mainly come down to personal preference. For those that have moved on from Pink Elephant, or possibly forgotten about it altogether, Divine Lotus offers an opportunity to re-discover it in a totally new setting. Also, with the mystery symbol feature being in high demand these days, it adds a modern touch to the gameplay as well.Divine Lotus may lack the originality to make it as hyped and successful as Riders of the Storm, but being a refined version of Pink Elephants, you really can't go wrong with it either. Obviously, we were hoping for something slightly more unique but regardless, Divine Lotus still manages to muster up enough appeal to draw us in.

title: 3 Secret Cities
structured_summary:

review: 3 Secret Cities: Slot OverviewDeveloper 4ThePLayer continues its trend of using numbers in their game titles (to propel them to the top of lists presumably) while producing slots that deviate from the norm. While not a freaky, out there innovator, 3 Secret Cities nevertheless does things its own way, despite using one of the more common themes to set the stage for the action. The key to them all is the free spins scatter symbol, appearing on reels 1, 3, or 5. If 2 scatters hit on reels 1 and 3, players click one of them to reveal a cash prize worth up to 50x their bet or progression across the locations – Jungle City, Lake City, and Gold City. It’s all been cleverly designed to keep you engaged as you travel deeper into the jungle. Another is the jungle sounds which are low-key most of the time, though they enhance the atmosphere.The action can be laid back a lot of the time too, and it was tough to coax much more than small change wins out of 3 Secret Cities. Fortunately, thanks to the aforementioned benefits, it’s not hard to stay motivated and soldier on. Imagine losing your compass and blindly hacking through the jungle, not knowing where you are going, yet knowing there is treasure out there somewhere. You just have to grit your teeth and get on with the job at hand. When you finally make it to the bonus, clicking through the Temple Pick feature is fun before launching the bonus game you’ve worked so hard to build. It can certainly pay off, and all bonus games have respectable max payout amounts, topping out at the 50,000x win cap.For a different take on Aztec gaming, it’s worth checking out what 3 Secret Cities has to offer. It requires an amount of grit and determination, but what good adventure doesn’t?

This is the pistol, followed by a hat, hip flask, and stirrup as the high pays, then A down to 9 as the low pays. A winning combo of six symbols pays 0.5-1.5x the bet for the royals or 2 to 25 times the stake for the higher value tiles. Appearing on reels 2 to 5 is the wild symbol, able to replace any pay symbols to complete ways wins.Sheriff's Gold Megaways: Slot FeaturesSheriff's Gold Megaways slot - respinsSame looks, same stats, and well, same features as well, really. For this part of the review, we're going to mosey on through a couple of base game modifiers, and Sheriff's Gold Cash Respins.Base Game ModifiersOn any paid spin, modifiers can randomly trigger. One is Max Megaways, which causes the reels to fill with symbols making the maximum 117,649 ways to win appear. Another helpful modifier is the Bonus Add, which creates the chance of triggering Sheriff's Gold Cash Respins, though there is no guarantee the bonus will be awarded.Sheriff's Gold Cash RespinsLanding 5 or more scatters in the base game triggers the Sheriff's Gold Cash Respins feature. The triggering symbols remain locked in place while all other symbols fade away, and 3 repsins are awarded. Only scatters or blanks can land during the feature. New landed scatters lock in place and reset the respin count back to 3. Scatters either display a bet multiplier or Mini, Major, or Mega jackpot symbols; the latter three being worth 10x, 25x, or 50x the bet, respectively. Moreover, if a reel gets filled with locked symbols, a multiplier is generated, which is applied to all prize values on the respective reel. At the end of the round, all scatter values in view are tallied up and awarded.Sheriff's Gold Megaways slot - splash screenSheriff's Gold Megaways: Slot VerdictThere's taking shortcuts to get to the finish line early, then there's doing what iSoftBet has done and changing one word in a game title, then palming it off as something new-ish. Sheriff's Gold Megaways is so peculiar there must be some legal, technical, or jurisdictional reason why it has been made. Even so, was it really worth it? Even more importantly, is it going to spark a slew of 'new' releases where the only 'new' bit is a word or two in the title? Probably not, hopefully not. Full disclosure, as well as the 'Western' to 'Sheriff's' switcharoo, Sheriff's Gold Megaways, didn't ship with a bonus buy. Perhaps that was what prompted the re-release? Who knows, it's a Western mystery up there with what happened to Etta Place, the lesser-known companion of Butch Cassidy and the Sundance kid. Even Etta's real name is a matter of speculation.Putting aside the questions for a moment, let's deal with what we do know. One thing is that Sheriff's Gold Megaways was every bit as good as the previous game, though since it's identical in virtually all ways, it would be strange if it wasn't. The dense Western atmosphere is enjoyable, it isn't as grim as something like Dead or Alive 2 or Tombstone RIP, but it does a good job of drawing players into a bleak world where anything goes. As before, the three Mini, Major, or Mega values are pretty feeble and pale in comparison to what was available in the progenitor slot Aztec Gold Megaways. This doesn't stop Sheriff's Gold Megaways from boasting an impressive max win, though, as Western Gold Megaways came with a tag of 12,000x the bet.As the sun draws down over the dusty plain and wolves begin to howl, our time with Sheriff's Gold Megaways also comes to an end. In an industry rife with clones and copies, reskins and remakes, Sheriff's Gold Megaways still managed to surprise with how little differed between it and its sibling.

title: Ted Megaways
structured_summary: Ted Megaways is a branded slot featuring the foul-mouthed teddy bear from the popular movie, set in a green-hued living room with a lounge jazz soundtrack. The game offers Megaways reels with cascades, Mystery Ted symbols, a Thunder Wheel for free spins, and a feature buy option, though fewer features than the original slot. The reviewer finds it a solid, entertaining game with great build quality but notes it’s leaner and less animated than its predecessor, which may disappoint some fans. Visually and audibly, the game has a simpler design with Ted delivering occasional one-liners over a smooth jazz background.
review: Ted Megaways: OverviewThose masters of the branded slot, Blueprint Gaming, bring back everyone’s favourite irreverent stuffed toy. Based on a friendly, if foul-mouthed bear, the movie tells the tail of John Bennett, a Boston native whose childhood dream brings his teddy bear friend Ted to life. Blueprint originally released a Ted slot version in 2017 which was a real feature overflow, offering six modifiers plus five bonus games to accompany the wisecracks. In the Megaways version,  features have been decreased while other game areas have been boasted. The original turned out to be a hit for the studio, how will the Megaways version fair?Accompanied by a loungey jazz soundtrack that sounds like the theme to Always Sunny in Philadelphia, the game is set in a green-hued living room, while Ted sits to the left, drinking beer and popping one-liners. If anything, it’s a little plainer than the first one, though the reels have been expanded. Thanks to the Megaways engine, players now get 6 main reels with 2-7 symbols on each, as well as a 4 position horizontal reel running along the top. The number of win ways on each spin varies from 324 to 117,649 depending on how stacked the reels are.Not a whole lot is off-limits when it comes to Ted. The marijuana references might have been toned down, but Ted still needs to have endless talks ’with his weed guy.’ Yeah, it’s that sort of game. If it sounds a little too low brow, best to stop reading now. However, if you’re cool with farts and burps et al., then Ted’s humour is like a breath of fresh air in an industry often a little too serious than it possibly needs to be.Players join in the antics by setting bets from 10 p/c to €10 per spin on whatever device they prefer. For veteran players, the math model will come across as rather familiar and has likely been recycled from other Blueprint slots. This means rather high volatility coupled with a fairly high hit rate but low bonus frequency. RTP is borderline ok, balancing on the edge of average at 96.03%.When it comes to the symbols, these remain practically the same as those in the original. From low to high, there are 9-A royals, beer bottles, ducks, and Tami-Lynn. The most valuable symbol is the Ted logo, which pays on two of a kind, up to 50 times the stake for 6 of a kind. Ted himself is the wild, appearing only on the horizontal bonus reel to substitute for anything but scatters or Mystery Symbols.Ted Megaways: Features﻿Ted Megaways doesn’t get as offensive as Ted the movie, but it’s still full of quips from the furry wee guy. He also likes to get in on the action from time to time, but don’t expect as many features this time around. As well as Cascades, players get Mystery Ted, the Thunder Wheel which awards free spins, and a feature buy.First up is the standard Cascade feature which is activated after every win. This system clears winning symbols from the grid, letting fresh ones fall into the empty spaces. Consecutive payouts become possible on one spin since Cascades continue to run as long as new winners continue to appear.The Mystery Ted feature may activate at random on any spin. When it does, Ted’s blasts the reels with his zap gun, adding up to 100 Mystery Symbols to the next spin. Each Mystery Symbol transforms into the same matching symbol to reveal a winning combinations. This could be anything except the scatter.At least 4 scatters in view triggers the Thunder Buddies Bonus. Players can either collect 12 free spins to start the feature, or take a punt on the Thunder Wheel to win more free spins and a higher minimum number of Megaways. Keep in mind, spinning the wheel can just as easily end up winning less than 12 spins too.In both cases, free spins use a progressive win multiplier that starts at x1, increasing by +1 on every cascade. Also, a new Ted symbol enters the game. Every 3 collected Ted symbols adds 2 free spins whilst increasing the minimum number of Megaways, up to 117,649. The feature is similar to Blueprint’s Return of Kong Megaways or iSoftBet’s Morgana Megaways, but with a less elaborate collection mechanic.Non-UK players may also have the option of buying the feature via the Mystery Bonus Buy. For the entry fee of 150 times the stake, players get a spin on the Thunder Wheel to win spins and a starting minimum number of Megaways as noted above.Ted Megaways: VerdictSome players may feel disappointment when they realise how much has been removed from the first slot to make the Megaways version. Visually/thematically, things have remained more or less the same; it’s just the culling of features might be a let-down for some fans. However, the excellent build quality combined with the solid gameplay more than make up for the shortcomings. Few do Megaways or branded slots quite like Blueprint, so the amalgamation of the two elements makes for one entertaining slot.As well as less features, there is less input from Ted. His repertoire of jibes is limited, and they do get a bit repetitive after a while. Without all the bells and whistles the first had, the base game can be a bit of a grind too, though cascades help.When Ted Megaways gets going during free spins, however, the game launches it up several gears. Increasing minimum Megaways works superbly alongside cascades and the unlimited win multiplier to produce some epic results. Even the tokenistic Mystery Symbols play their part to great effect at times.In many ways the two slots are similar, in others, they are very different. The original offers more extras and is a bit more ‘Ted’ than this one. The bear had more of an input, more mouthing off, more animations. This Megaways version is leaner, more streamlined, with massive potential to boot. At the end of the day, both are ‘fur-kin sweet’ options built to satisfy different gaming moods.

title: Reel Desire
structured_summary:
Reel Desire is a disco-themed slot set in a neon-lit nightclub, evoking 70s/80s vibes with music and retro symbols.  
It features high volatility, 1,024 ways to win, Double Wilds with multipliers, full-reel wilds, and dual-mode free spins.  
The reviewer finds it a well-executed homage with massive win potential, though somewhat derivative of similar slots.  
The game offers decent visuals and a foot-tapping soundtrack, capturing disco’s energetic atmosphere without being visually outstanding.
review: Reel Desire: Slot OverviewDisco is one of those eras that seems to have died pretty quickly at the time, yet somehow it has clung on in one form or another ever since. It rears up regularly in pop culture, including slots, to varying degrees of success. One which did hit it big through a combination of red hot features and reckless attitude was Big Time Gaming's hit Danger! High Voltage. Not that it's an overly original idea, but just like most industries, where you find success you find imitators. Flaunting the line is Yggdrasil Gaming's disco-themed slot Reel Desire.In another plot twist, Reel Desire bears some strong resemblance to All41 Studios' release Electric Avenue which in turn happens to be a clone of, well, Danger! High Voltage. Both have gone for the neon 80s thing, though Yggdrasil has set theirs inside the Reel Desire night club. A 5-reel, 1,024 win way action area props up a towering DJ booth, while hearts, kisses, and love signs adorn the background in glowing neon light. Disco was all about the music, not to mention platform shoes, medallions, open chested shirts and outrageous moves. To this end, Reel Desire's soundtrack has a decent foot-tapping quality to it. Yggdrasil paint some of the prettiest slots you'll see, so while Reel Desire doesn't attain that level, it's definitely not a bad looker.﻿Beneath the looks, Reel Desire possesses some desirable stats, possibly better suited for harder-edged gamblers or those chasing down massive wins. For one, volatility is high, paired with a hit rate of 25.7%, and massive potential. Both phases of the game were tempered by features that seemed strategically placed to minimise returns much of the time, yet single spin wins can be insane as can be seen in our video. The RTP mirrors the unofficial slot average of 96% which should suit most players, as will stake selections, ranging from 25 p/c to $/€75 per spin. This being the democratic pastime of disco, where we're all supposedly equal on the dance floor, any device can be used to relive the glory days.Symbols are led by a bunch of neon-lit card suits, diamonds, clubs, spades, and hearts, textured like an LP record, followed by shades, earrings, hi-top shoes, and a Casio wristwatch which have made a comeback of late. The two high pay symbols are a young Don Johnson wannabe and a fly girl type, worth 16-20 times the stake for five of a kind. Wilds help in this endeavour, but they are linked to a couple of features so let's look at them next.Reel Desire: Slot FeaturesWhile the theme brings back memories of Electric Avenue, the features take it back even further to the slot All41 based theirs on. Here we find Double Wilds, Reel Desire, and two Free Spins games.The cassette tape symbol is the wild, appearing on all reels to replace any pay symbol to make a winning combination. At any moment in the base game, a Double Wild may appear on reels 2, 3, or 4. This is a wild possessing an x2 multiplier. These symbols are sticky and trigger a respin when they land.Also occurring only in the base game is the Reel Desire feature. A homage to the Wild Desire feature found in Microgaming's legendary Immortal Romance slot, it turns 1 to 5 reels completely wild when randomly triggered.The final symbol on the paytable is the ghetto blaster scatter symbol. When 3 or more are in view, 10 free spins are awarded. If four or five land, an extra prize of 50x or 500x the bet is added on top. Players then choose one of 2 free spins modes. One is Sticky Wilds where all wild symbols stay sticky for the duration of the free spins session. Or, Multipliers, where each winning spin increases a win multiplier by +1. Free spins can be retriggered in the bonus game, in the same way as they are in the base.Reel Desire: Slot VerdictLet's just say it, if Danger! High Voltage and Electric Avenue hooked up; their illegitimate love child would strongly resemble Reel Desire. All three share a similar vibe, aiming for that 70s/80s disco thing. Then there are features, which again are suspiciously similar - full reel wilds, dual option free spins with either sticky wilds or multipliers. The three games might not be exactly the same, and Reel Desire isn't as blatant a copy as Electric Avenue was. For instance, you get a progressive win multiplier in place of High Voltage Wilds, yet in essence, they are pretty darn close.Yggdrasil's game doesn't have the outrageous attitude of Danger! High Voltage, but if it's absolute biggest wins you're after then you'd have to call it for Reel Desire. Scoring a full-screen of wilds/premiums in Reel Desire means wins of up to 20,480x the bet are possible. Keeping in mind this is off a single spin, and knowing it could happen at any time in the base game adds a level of tension. Even when not filling all five reels, the Reel Desire feature can stoke decent wins, as can Double Wilds on occasion.Unfortunately, the hit frequency for free spins was not available, which could be interesting because they did take their sweet time to trigger. Once in, the bonus games weren’t quite as intense as Danger! High Voltage’s can be. The progressive multiplier performs as well as you'd expect this type of feature to, though it doesn't match the adrenaline found in High Voltage free spins.So, yeah, Reel Desire comes off as an imitation of previous games, yet at the end of the day, it works out pretty well for players. Disco slot options have deepened, and Reel Desire does have a lot of good things to commend it. Stats are positive, the potential is massive, plus the gameplay gets some enjoyable grooves on. Like disco, or trends in general, where one leads others inevitably follow.
