review: Mad Cabs: Slot OverviewDo you long for the good old days playing Crazy Taxi on your Playstation 2? If you answered yes, then Mad Cabs from software developer Iron Dog Studio might be the slot for you. Mad Cabs celebrates paid transportation in a variety of forms while dishing out gaming devices such as Call a Noober, which expands pay symbols, free spins, and a bonus buy feature.According to the Internet, the word 'cab' is the shortened form of 'cabriolet', which was a single horse-drawn two-wheeled vehicle that was popular for hire in Paris and London back in the day. The word has stuck and now refers to a taxi when talking about vehicles for hire. Mad Cabs has taxis, but it also has tuk-tuks and limos sprinkled across its gaming grid. The setting for Mad Cabs is downtown on a street with no people and no cars, so not the best time to be tooling around for a cab, in other words. Upping the 'mad' stakes or attempting to at least is an energetic rock soundtrack, leaning towards pop punk in free spins, and while the total effect might not be as 'mad' as the game's makers were shooting for, it's pretty unique all the same, which is something.Mad Cabs slot - base gameFor more info on the gaming grid, it is made up of 5 reels, holding 4 symbols each, and covered in 20 paylines. To the lower right of the screen is a coins icon where players may select a stake from 20 p/c to $/€50 per spin, and there are three buy features available as well. Running on a medium-high volatile math model, Mad Cabs produces a default RTP of 95.06%, which changes when buying free spins.Mad Cabs has nine regular pay symbols, creating a regular line win when matching symbols land from the left side of the screen over consecutive reels. The lower value 5 are racing-styled 10 to A card ranks awarding 1 to 2 times the bet for a 5 symbol win, while the high pays are a Tuk-Tuk, a Black Cab, a Yellow Taxi, and a Limo. Hitting a 5 OAK premium combination awards 10 to 125 times the stake. Flaming wilds also land on all reels, substituting for all non-special symbols. When making wins of themselves, wilds have the same value as the highest-paying Limo symbol.Mad Cabs: Slot FeaturesMad Cabs slot - free spinsTo potentially up the winning possibilities or pretend to catch a ride, then Mad Cabs' features are the Call a Noober extra, free spins, and bonus buys.Call a NooberIn the base game, landing at least 2 different sets of Mad Cab symbols (premium car symbols) that could form a win triggers Call a Noober. A set consists of 3 or more Tuk-Tuks, Black Cabs, Yellow Cabs, or 2+ Limos. Once activated, one of the Mad Cab symbols on the reels is picked at random and expands to cover the reels they are on. Expanded symbols pay all lines and do not have to be adjacent to award a win. Regular wins are not paid on spins when there is a Call a Noober payout.Free SpinsLanding 3, 4, or 5 Noober scatters in the base game awards 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. Scatters appear on all reels, once per reel, and only appear in the base game. During free spins, the Call a Noober triggers when there are Mad Cab symbols on 3 or more reels. The Mad Cab symbol selected transforms other Mad Cab symbols on the reels to match before expanding occurs.Buy FeatureFrom the feature buy menu, players can buy 5 free spins for 40x the bet, 10 free spins without Tuk-Tuks for 80x the bet, or 10 free spins with only Black Cabs and Yellow Taxis for 80x the bet.Mad Cabs slot - free spinsMad Cabs: Slot VerdictPeople have been paying other people to take them places for hundreds of years, maybe more, and while taxis abound on our streets, they aren't something you see much in gambling. So, it has fallen to Iron Dog Studio to give them some time in the spotlight, and you know, Mad Cabs has its moments, but all in all, it wasn't a game that we'd visualise hailing overly often.One of the concerns revolves around the speed of the game, which is odd given it's about road travel. For instance, the cleverly named Call a Noober sequence is pretty nifty the first few times it occurs but turns into a bit of a time sucker after a while. A switch to turn the animation on or off might have been handy, though it's not so long. What the feature can do, stack the reels with identical symbols is a benefit, however, and one can dream about doing so with the Limo symbol spread across all five reels. In this scenario, the reward would be 2,500x the bet. 'Just' repeat the full-screen Limo 2 further times, and you've hit Mad Cabs' max win of 7,500x the stake. Also, maybe consider not getting the third bonus buy if you're shooting for maximum full-screen glory since it removes Tuk-Tuks as well as Limos from the reels - Black Cab and Yellow Cab full-screen wins are worth 300x and 400x, respectively.The lingering feeling, once we'd reached our destination, was that Mad Cabs was to Iron Dog Studio what Road Rage was to Nolimit City. A deviation from the norm, boasting a few interestingly unusual features, but one which felt a little oddly unfulfilling overall.

title: Money Stacks Megaways
structured_summary: Money Stacks Megaways is a futuristic-themed slot centered around cash stacks and wealth, inspired by Elon Musk's net worth. It features a 6+4 reel Megaways grid with up to 117,649 ways to win, including Cash Collect, free spins with random wild multipliers, Money Spins, and boost pick mechanics. The reviewer finds it an improved, fuller experience over its predecessor but somewhat standard in core gameplay, with a max win of 10,000x. The game offers a high-energy audiovisual experience with flashing lights and dynamic tunes in a Tron-like setting.
review:
Money Stacks Megaways: Slot OverviewAt the time of writing, Elon Musk sat at the top of the world's richest person list with a net worth of more than $300 billion. According to ehd.org, if you piled 100 billion $1 bills on top of each other, the stack would be 10,921.97 km high, or around 28 times higher than the International Space Station. Times that by 3 and a bit, and you've got Elon's net worth in a pile. Quite a stack, quite a mind blowing stack actually, which leads us into today's slot. Designed by Pragmatic Play, Money Stacks Megaways follows on from Money Stacks, delivering a Cash Collect feature, free spins with random wild multipliers, and Money Spins, but this time hosted on a Megaways game grid.That Megaways game grid is made up of 6 main vertical reels, and an up top 4 position reel, producing up to 117,649 ways to win. It sits in a quasi-futuristic room, kinda Tron-ish, kind of dance party-ish, very much like the one used in Money Stacks. As before, three prize values sit by the reels, though their values have been reduced, which is odd; however, the overall potential is double what it was previously.Money Stacks Megaways slot - base gameMoney Stacks Megaways takes bets of 20 c to $/€240 per spin at a base level and has an optional ante bet. Switching the ante bet on doubles the bet, tripling the chance of winning free spins naturally. This is a highly volatile slot, where the largest theoretical RTP value is 96.5%.On its symbol hierarchy, Money Stacks Megaways has 9-10 card ranks, lemons, cherries, grapes, watermelons, and 7s. Winning combinations of 6 matching symbols in length pay 0.4x to 0.8x for the royals or 1x to 10x for the premiums. Wild symbols hit on reels 2, 3, 4, and 5 to substitute any regular paying symbol. When winning ways are formed, the tumble feature removes the winning symbols from the reels and replaces them with a symbol drop, repeating like this till no new win hits.Money Stacks Megaways: Slot FeaturesMoney Stacks Megaways slot - free spinsMoney Collect action is something to keep an eye out for in the base game, while two bonus rounds may be triggered - free spins with random wild multipliers and Money Spins.Money CollectWhen Money symbols hit, they do so with a value of 0.5x to 20x the bet, or the 25x Minor, the 100x Major, or the 1,000x Grand prize. Collect, and Super Collect symbols may land on the leftmost and rightmost reels. When at least one Collect or Super Collect symbol is in view at the same time as Money symbols, the values of all Money symbols are awarded.When landed, the Super Collect symbol first adds a random amount of Money symbols to positions on reels that already have at least one Money symbol on them. Then, the values of all Money symbols on the screen are paid. If 2 Collect or Super Collect symbols hit along with Money symbols, a random multiplier of x2 to x10 is applied to the total value of Money symbols on the screen.Bonus TriggerHitting 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatters pays 2x, 5x, 10x, or 20x, respectively, while also triggering free spins. In the base game, all Money symbols that hit on a spin without Collect symbols or enough scatters to trigger free spins send a ray to a diamond on the screen. At random, when this happens, a number of free spins from the available limit may trigger. Once the bonus triggers, players choose the free spins mode.
Free Spins with Random Wild MultipliersIf the round was triggered by 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatters, then 7, 10, 12, or 15 free spins are granted. Before free spins start, players pick a fuse to reveal a boost for the round. The boost could be +1, +2, or +3 free spins, +1x, +2x, or +3x added to the general multiplier, or more of the highest value pay symbols added to the reels for the whole round.Free spins start with an x1 multiplier (it can be increased be boosts before the round). Every tumble increases the multiplier by +1 till the end of the round. All wins are multiplied by this multiplier. During the feature, wild symbols have a multiplier of x2, x3, or x5. This multiplier applies to all winning combinations the wild is part of. If more wilds are part of the same win, their multipliers multiply each other. Hitting 2-6 scatters lengthens the feature by awarding 2-6 extra free spins.Money SpinsIf this round was triggered by 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatters, then 2, 3, 5, or 7 Money Spins are awarded, respectively. Before the feature starts, players pick fuses which reveal boosts until 'That's the end' is revealed. Possible boosts are +1 free spin, +1x added to the general multiplier that applies to all collections in the round, 2 guaranteed Collect symbols on each free spin, 2 guaranteed Super Collect symbols on each free spin, or More Megaways, increasing the number of symbols which can land on each reel. During the feature, only Money, Collect, Super Collect, and blank symbols may land. At least one Collect or Super Collect is guaranteed to hit on every spin. If the round has a general multiplier triggered through a boost from the fuse pick, the multiplier applies to all money awards. This feature cannot be retrigged.Feature BuyThe free spins round can be bought from the base game for 120x to trigger it with at least 3 scatters, 180x with at least 4 scatters, 240x with at least 5 scatters, or 300x with 6 scatters.Money Stacks Megaways slot - money spinsMoney Stacks Megaways: Slot VerdictWell, that was okay. Megaways does what it's meant to do in a makeover by expanding Money Stacks Megaways into a bigger game than Money Stacks was. The super-sized gaming area has been joined by a few extra add-ons that weren't available last time, as well. One of these is the boost picks at the start of both features - one pick for wild multiplier free spins, possibly more picks with Money Spins. Boosts are always good when you can get them, as are general multipliers, which were also unavailable in Money Stacks. The new mechanical setup and the new features make Money Stacks Megaways a bigger, fuller, rounder experience than Money Stacks while also wedging a bit of extra space between itself and slots like Mask of Amun, Blazing Bison Gold Blitz, and Gold Blitz.Still, Money Stacks Megaways' core elements are a tad bland. One of the bonus rounds is a fairly standard Megaways rising win multiplier feature; the other is a fairly standard Money symbol collection game. There are loads of those on the market already. Admittedly, a highlight was winning Money Spins with two guaranteed Super Collect symbols on each spin. Get those two, and not only are they able to add cash to the reels, but you also benefit from a multiplier for the collect on each spin as well. That wasn't too bad. Neither is Money Stacks Megaways's max win, which at 10,000x is double its predecessor. The game does try quite hard to overload the senses with high-energy tunes and a flashing light show, as well as expanding the gameplay using things like the pick-me boosts, so while at heart, Money Stacks Megaways is a bit of a copycat, it is an improvement over the previous game.

title: War Of Gods
structured_summary: War of Gods pits Greek gods Zeus and Hades against each other in a mythological battle theme. The game features three bonus modes with symbol upgrades, reel expansions, and sticky high-paying symbols but no wilds or free spins. The reviewer praises its epic presentation and complex features but criticizes the low RTP (95.66%) and modest max win of 2,518x bet. Visually, the slot impresses with fiery underworld scenes, classical imagery, and a dramatic symphonic soundtrack.
review: War of Gods: Slot OverviewSome studios pack the power of Zeus into their games while others seek to harness the clout of Hades. Few are as audacious as to bring both deities together in one game to let them duke it out as Red Tiger has in War of Gods. Well, apart from games like 2 Gods Zeus vs Thor or Artemis vs Medusa which attempted to do that exact thing. Bolstering the fantastic classic imagery, players get three bonus games, where symbols may be upgraded, and reels or rows expanded.Let’s start with a little story from the world of Ancient Greece. According to legend, after overthrowing the titans, Hades, Zeus and Poseidon (who were brothers) each drew lots to decide which part of the world they would rule. Poseidon got the sea, Zeus the heavens, and unfortunately for Hades, he got the short straw, meaning the underworld. Perhaps this was what put him in a warring mood? We can only speculate motives since they are not explicit in Red Tiger’s game. Maybe it’s just a brother thing. Then again, Hades did abduct Zeus’ daughter Persephone to be his consort, so maybe it’s that? Whatever the case, Zeus battling Hades is a mighty theme, providing a bunch of great concepts to make use of.To Red Tiger’s credit, they’ve done a remarkable job of bringing the sibling rivalry to the small screen. War of Gods is played out on a 5-reel grid (expandable during certain features), deep in the bowels of the fiery underworld amidst fallen columns, Sisyphus with a boulder on his back, and plenty of lighting raining down from the heavens, heralding Zeus’ approach. The soundtrack is suitably epic; the result making an excellent first impression.It’s a shame the rest of the game doesn’t hit the same heights. A tingle of disappointment occurs when perusing the help file in which we find a somewhat lower than average default RTP of 95.66%. No less disappointing is the calculated max potential, though we’ll leave the reveal for the verdict. Offering bets from 10 p/c to $/€20 per spin, expect volatility to be high along  with a hit frequency hovering somewhere around the 20-30% mark.At the default grid size of 5x4, players get 30 paylines to land winning combinations of three or more of a kind on. There is a stack of symbols at hand too; around half are special symbols used during features, the rest are eight regular pays. In this latter category we find clubs, diamonds, hearts, and spades as the lows, followed by parchment, horn cups, shields, and helms as the highs. On the default size, five of a kind wins are as good as it gets, producing high pay wins worth 4 to 10 times the stake. With so many symbols on the paytable, it might be a bit of a surprise to learn there is no wild in War of Gods.War of Gods: Slot Features﻿As well as being a wild-free zone, there are no free spins, but three bonus games to play for. With names like Wrath of Zeus, Hades Hellfire, and Warring Gods, don’t expect a whole lot of light-hearted laughs to go with the higher winning opportunities they offer.Hitting two 1x2 sized Zeus symbols on the first and last reels triggers the Wrath of Zeus feature. In this game, only high-paying Zeus symbols appear. Whenever these 1x1 symbols land, they turn sticky for the duration, possibly transforming into 1x4 Super Symbols. In this feature, a special upgrade symbol may also land increasing the value of Zeus symbols up to three times - landing a line of five of the highest paying Zeus symbols is worth 20x the bet. Wrath of Zeus continues as long as new symbols keep appearing on the reels.When two Hades symbols land, they trigger the Hades Hellfire feature where only high paying Hades symbols appear. As before, Hades symbols are held in place when they hit and may transform into 1x4 sized paying tiles. In this one, a special expand symbol may land to expand the grid up to 7x6 in size, thus increasing the total number of paylines to 60. Each new row expands Hades Super symbols up to 1x6 in size worth 50x the bet for seven of a kind. Hades Hellfire also ends when no new symbols land on the reels.The third bonus game is Warring Gods, triggered when Zeus and Hades land in the base game. This feature uses Zeus/Hades special symbols which, again, lock and possibly expand when they land. The rules are basically the same as before, though one difference is upgrade and expand symbols are both available. A full line of seven Hades/Zeus symbols is worth 100x the bet.War of Gods: Slot VerdictWar of Gods is a game that gets off to a great start but doesn’t capitalise on the impact. Red Tiger regularly designs great looking games, and Wrath of Gods is another strong example. It’s a game that comes across as all business, making full use of the theme to create a deep atmosphere worthy of the two titans it portrays. There’s an almost biblical quality to the visuals, while the symphonic soundtrack adds extra drama.The gameplay is pretty good too, though like many Red Tiger slots, triggering the good parts can take time. Hold and win features are common, yet rarely do you get three of them in one game, nor so many variations within them. In some ways, it brings to mind Red Tiger’s Clash of the Beasts the way you can have one or the other god, or both at the same time. Like Clash of the Beasts, when the siblings fight it out is where hitting the game’s max potential has its best chance of occurring. By best we are talking about a figure of 2,518 times the bet which is seriously underwhelming on a game like this. Perhaps the prize money was converted from drachmas or something?To sum up, War of Gods is brilliantly presented, and the features are great, offering a lot more complexity than your usual hold and win feature. It’s a real shame War of Gods is ultimately let down by underperforming stats, and mediocre potential returns.

title: WitchyPoppins
structured_summary: WitchyPoppins is a Halloween-themed fantasy slot featuring witches in a dim forest setting. It includes PopWins, nudges, free spins with increasing multipliers, pay anywhere symbols, and multiple bonus buy options. The reviewer finds it a solid, entertaining reskin of PixiePop, offering engaging free spins and up to 20,000x wins despite a less thrilling base game. Visually, it’s pleasantly styled with neat animations and fitting, charming music, creating a cozy Halloween vibe.
review: WitchyPoppins: Slot OverviewPop addicts AvatarUX are letting players celebrate the Halloween season, should they so choose, with WitchyPoppins, essentially a reskin of the not-long-cold slot PixiePop. Indeed, PixiePop only came out a few or so months before WitchyPoppins, so someone at the studio must have liked the setup. This setup includes pops 'n nudges in the base game, while free spins are where WitchyPoppins dumps in a win multiplier that gets boosted by multiplicative or additive symbols and a pay anywhere symbol, as well as bags of bonus buy options.Another thing WitchyPoppins shares with its predecessor is the fact they are both fantasy-leaning slots. Where PixiePop had fairies, WitchyPoppins has, you guessed it, witches. The witches of the tale inhabit a dimly lit part of the forest in the base game (brightly illuminated in free spins), where the main background items are trees. WitchyPoppins certainly isn't as visually hectic as DonKey & the GOATS, the last AvatarUX review was. But, it is pleasant looking in a vaguely Fantasma Games kind of way, plus the little symbol animations and whatnot are neatly done, as is the music.WitchyPoppins slot - base gameTime for some numbers, starting with bet selection, which goes from 20 c to $/€100 per spin. The RTP is the same as the mould slot, at 96.04%, which appears to apply no matter how someone chooses to play the game. One way of doing so is activating the ante bet. This increases the regular stake by 25%, causing scatter symbols to hit at a higher frequency. With its highly volatile math model, WitchyPoppins is played on a stretchable game grid of 5 reels and 3 rows at the start of each base game spin.WitchyPoppins pays left to right from the first reel and right to left from the right reel, though 5 OAK wins pay only from one side. This means ways to win from 486 to 65,536 (including both ways). Arcane 10 to A card royals are the low pays, worth 1 to 1.5 times the bet for a 5 symbol win; then there are 5 witchy character high pay symbols, worth 2 to 6 times the bet for a 5 OAK hit. Appearing on reels 2, 3, and 4 is WitchyPoppins' wild symbol, able to substitute for any regular pay symbol.WitchyPoppins: Slot FeaturesWitchyPoppins slot - free spinsIf you've tried PixiePop, you'll know the score here since both games share features. These are PopWins, nudges, free spins, multiplicative multipliers, additive multipliers, a pay anywhere symbol, and a bunch of feature buys.PopWinsThe PopWins mechanic removes winning symbols from the reels and replaces them with two new ones, increasing the reel height and ways to win. In the base game, the reels can grow to 6 positions high. From then on, winning symbols are replaced by just one new symbol.NudgeThe nudge mechanic randomly bump reels up or down, thereby improving your win. They do this by nudging a scatter symbol to trigger free spins in the base game or extra free spins in the bonus round, nudging a symbol to trigger a higher reel height, nudging a pay anywhere symbol, or nudging a wild symbol.Free SpinsCollecting at least 3 scatter symbols grants access to free spins. When scatters land during the round, they award an extra 1, 2, or 3 extra free spins. Landing 3, 4, or 5 scatters in the base game awards 5-7, 6-8, or 7-9 free spins, and the game grid expands to 4, 5, or 6 reels high, respectively. When PopWins occur now, the reels top out at 8 positions high and reset to the lowest common reel height. If all reels reach 8 rows, then +2 free spins are awarded.Free spins have a win multiplier that increases by +1 following each pop. Landing a multiplicative multiplier symbol as well as a win multiplies the win multiplier by 2-11, while an additive multiplier symbol (when a win occurs) adds 5-50 to the multiplier. Potential multiplier values vary between natural triggers or bought bonus rounds.There's more, too. Before free spins start, a random high pay symbol is chosen to be the pay anywhere symbol. This symbol does not need to be adjacent to payout, but it still needs 3+ symbols on separate reels to count towards a win. Values for 5-6, 7-8, 9-10, 11-15, 16-20, 21-25, 26-30, or 31-35 pay anywhere symbols are 12.5x, 25x, 50x, 100x, 125x, 200x, 400x, or 500x the bet, respectively.Xpress Buy BonusFrom the Xpress feature buy menu, players have access to these:Buy Bonus – 5 to 7 free spins with 1,024 ways for 125x the bet.Buy Bonus Plus – 6 to 8 free spins with 3,125 ways for 250x the bet.Buy Bonus Premium – 7 to 9 free spins with 7,776 ways for 500x the bet.Buy Bonus Max – 8 to 10 free spins with 7,776 ways + higher multiplicative and additive multipliers for 1,000x the bet.WitchyPoppins slot - feature buy menuWitchyPoppins: Slot VerdictCircling back to DonKey & the GOATS for a moment, the last AvatarUX review shocked, like questioning if this was real life, by not being a PopWins slot. As anyone who's been following AvatarUX will know, PopWins is the studio's bread and butter, having released a monumental number of these slots by now. If you missed the poppin' action last time, then be chilled to know WitchyPoppins keeps the mechanic alive. It keeps a bunch of other stuff alive as well since it's basically a redo of PixiePop and all (a few non-theme details have changed). That might not be the most exciting news for PopWins fans waiting for a brand new iteration of their favourite mechanic to hear. However, WitchyPoppins is a seasonal slot, and since so many other casino game makers are in the habit of dropping reskins/clones in this scenario, it should be no major jump scare to find out AvatarUX has done the same here.It does mean if PixiePop got your pulse racing, then WitchyPoppins probably will do as well (and vice versa). Certainly, it's not lacking anything the older game had which has not been passed down. The base game isn't the most exciting at times since it's all just PopWins and nudges when you're lucky, but WitchyPoppins does have quite a lot going on in the free spins bonus round. Not to mention several ways of buying your way to them for players that way inclined. The dream result is the same as before, at 20,000 times the bet, and the slick collection of free spins features means solid hits are as entertaining here as practically any PopWins game.Like a lot of Halloween slots, WitchyPoppins is more charming than actually scary. AvatarUX has ensured the game should be fine for punters to play on their own on a dark and stormy All Hallows' Eve night. For an edgier alternative, you might want to try Print Studios' horror fest Darkness. That's a slot jumpy players would do well to keep the lights on for. All told, WitchyPoppins might lose cool points amongst some gamblers for basically being a reskin, but it's not a bad option for players looking for some light-hearted Halloween action with a bit of popping happening on the side.

title: Cash Pump
structured_summary: Cash Pump is a high-octane, gas pump-themed slot with a retro 1950s vibe inspired by classic fruit symbols and Route 66 imagery. It features four separate 3x3 grids, stacked wilds that clone across grids with multipliers, and an unlimited retriggerable free spins round boosting win potential. The reviewer praises its uniqueness, high volatility, generous RTP, and thrilling multiplier mechanics despite a familiar layout. Visually nostalgic with a vintage feel, the game’s aesthetics and audio complement its bold, fast-paced theme.
review: Cash Pump (Play'n GO): OverviewYou have to hand it to them. In spite of the unceasingly intense production rate with up to four scheduled releases per month, Play'n GO still manages to maintain a surprisingly high level of quality. What's even more impressive maybe, is their ability to add just enough twist to the flavour, be it through the audiovisual presentation or the mechanics, to stay relevant and on top of the game. Sure, they have stirred up a lot of controversy within the industry by shamelessly cloning the works of other providers, but strangely enough, it only seems to have worked to their advantage - at least when looking at it from the outside.If you've never seen a video slot in the shape of a gas pump, well, here's one for you then. Before you say it's a ridiculous idea, just try to imagine all the great promotional slogans casinos and the generic affiliate sites out there will be able to fire off! - "It's time to put the pedal to the metal" or "Buckle up and get ready to ride", the options are endless. Whatever the case, one thing is for sure - Cash Pump is a high-octane slot that's not only extremely volatile (see, we can do it too), it also comes with a win potential that is double that of what you typically see in Play'n GO slots.The first thing you're likely to notice, however, may not be the unusual gas pump design, but the layout of the reels. Made up of four 3x3 separate grid slots, you can match 3 symbols across any of the 20 paylines (5 paylines on each) on all four grids to land a win. During your session, stacked wilds may duplicate themselves and spread across all four grids while also activating a random multiplier of up to 4x. The game also benefits from a free spins round with unlimited retriggers and win multipliers. You can play it from 0.20 to €/$100 per spin across all devices.On the visual side of things, there's a 50s kind of retro vibe going, possibly inspired in part by Evel Knievel. Set against a backdrop of what could very well be the legendary Route 66, the lower-paying symbols spinning on the reels are comprised of a collection of classic fruit slot symbols, namely cherries, oranges, plums and watermelons. Of significantly higher value are the game's two only premium symbols which are presented by triple lucky 7s and bar symbols. These will give you 2.5 or 5 times your stake respectively for a 3 of a kind combination.Cash Pump (Play'n GO): FeaturesFree spins feature in actionCentral to the gameplay in Cash Pump is the daredevil wild with the image of a grinning stunt performer. Appearing only on the centre reel of each set, it not only carries out the usual duties of the wild, but it also has extraordinary abilities. Dubbed the Stacked Wilds feature, whenever a full stack of wilds lands on the middle position of any of the four sets, it clones itself across all grids to help you land winning combinations. Moreover, a random multiplier of between 1x - 4x is applied as well.To unlock Cash Pump's true potential, you will have to see one scatter symbol appearing on the centre reel of each grid set. Starting with 7 Free Spins, collecting another 4 scatters during the feature awards an additional 5 free spins. Better yet, each retrigger also doubles the value of the four active random multipliers seen in the multiplier gauge (which are positioned directly above grid number 2). The first retrigger will thus increase the multipliers accordingly: 1x becomes 2x, 2x becomes 4x, 3x becomes 6x, and 4x becomes 8x. Landing yet another retrigger will repeat this pattern, with no limit to how high the multipliers can reach. The maximum win potential, on the other hand, is limited to 10,000 times your stake, which is far higher than usual when it comes to Play'n GO.Cash Pump (Play'n GO): VerdictCash Pump is undoubtedly unique coming from Play'n GO, but most veteran gamblers will have seen similar layouts before as it has been widely used by WMS in the past. If you want a more recent example, something along the lines can also be found in Luck O' The Irish from Blueprint Gaming. If you're unfamiliar with those slots, don't waste your time researching them. The fact is that Cash Pump is much better in almost every way. The unlimited win multiplier, for example, is a timely addition that has become extremely popular - faster than you know it, the multiplier can skyrocket to extreme levels, drastically intensifying the action.Generally speaking, we're not big fans of the split grid approach and usually tend to avoid those games. Nevertheless, Cash Pump is original enough to make us want to explore all 16 corners of it and the high potential and volatility is, of course, hard to resist for any hardcore gambler. Furthermore, the 96.86% RTP is unusually generous (unless you're playing at a casino that has it set to the lower 94.75% RTP option) and can help make it bearable in spite of the high volatility. To speak in automobile terminology -  Cash Pump is not a slot intended for road trips along senic coastal roads, but rather one you take to the racing circuit to push it to the limits.

title: Diamond Vortex
structured_summary: Diamond Vortex is a hexagonal grid slot set in deep space with a cosmic, interstellar theme. It features cluster wins, rotating rings with Spots and Zones, two types of wilds, a win multiplier mechanic, symbol transformations, and free spins with retriggers. The reviewer praises its sophisticated design and enjoyable gameplay, highlighting its potential for extended win sequences and a max win of 5,000x stake. Visually, it combines minimalist, galactic aesthetics reminiscent of Honey Rush and Starburst, complemented by a fitting space-themed audio atmosphere.
review: Diamond Vortex: OverviewSwedish developer Play’n GO certainly goes for grid slots, and on the whole, they have been hugely successful. One of the benefits of using this format is the flexibility it affords. From the volcanic shaped shenanigans of Gold Volcano to the 5x5 madness of Moon Princess, you can choose pretty much any form you like. This time, Play’n GO dust off their draft rulers to create the hexagonally shaped Diamond Vortex.Diamond Vortex isn’t the first time the studio has used a hexagon. It also turned up in bee infested slot Honey Rush, both games arranging the grid in a 4-5-6-7-6-5-4 row formation. Now, instead of being set in the deep woods, Diamond Vortex is located off-world in deep space before a swirling nebula. In some ways, Diamond Vortex lacks the warmth of Honey Rush, but does have a charm of its own, nonetheless.Playable from 20 p/c up to $/€100 per spin, across a range of devices, Diamond Vortex benefits from a default RTP of 96.20%, though operators can alter this so you may come across lower settings. Not that we need to tell you, but it always pays to check to make sure you’re getting the best version. The other piece of the math model puzzle is volatility, rated 7 out of 10 by the developer, or medium/high.The aim of the game is to form clusters of identical symbols for a winner. At least 6 or more connected matching symbols constitute a cluster, which is then removed from the board to let new symbols cascade into the gaps. This creates more chances to win and continues to do so as long as winners continue to land. Multiple clusters of the same symbol type which are not connecting are paid as separate cluster wins.The symbols involved are an odd lot, possessing a faint fruit look despite being chunks of interstellar rock. Low pays are 4 single pieces painted in various colours, while the high pays are made up of 4 larger quartz-like chunks. Values range from 10x for a group of 35+ low pays, up to 100x for 35 or more of the pinky premium.Diamond Vortex: FeaturesDiamond Vortex - free spinsOkay players, prepare for a bit of a feature overload. As is usually the case, these things are a lot easy to grasp in action than the written word, but let’s give it a crack regardless.First, the game board is made up of three concentric rings, each one containing a Spot and a Zone. Zones are fixed in place at the top of each ring, while Spots begin at the bottom and rotate as win sequences occur until they reach a Zone.On every win, the Rotate feature is triggered. This mechanic moves the innermost ring clockwise, the centre ring anti-clockwise, and the outer ring also clockwise. Non-winning symbols move with the rings before new symbols are dropped into the gaps. Kind in mind Spots move, but Zones never do.Diamond Vortex includes two different wilds – a standard Core Wild and a Sticky Wild. There is just one Core Wild which sits in the middle of the grid, while Sticky Wilds may be added during cascades. When a Sticky Wild is used in a win, it remains on the grid, but hops to a new ring, closer to the Core Wild.Whenever a Sticky Wild hops onto the Core Wild, the Consume feature is activated. review: Night Trax: Slot OverviewKnown for their love of the inert monatomic gas, Swedish developer ELK Studios turns up the neon for their hot 80s styled game, Night Trax. Respins continue until no new symbols are added to paylines or no new paylines are created. The diagonal arrows function a little bit differently to the horizontal ones. Diagonal arrows connect through their endpoints in multiple directions. When diagonal arrows create a split in two different directions, a multiplier of x2-x32 is added for those paylines.Night Trax is a game with a solid max win, and getting near it is possible in the bonus game, triggered when 3 bonus symbols land in the base game. These 3 bonus symbols are converted to random multiplier values when the feature starts.The bonus game starts with 3 free spins, and the reels contain only sticky multipliers, arrows, or blank spaces. Landing a multiplier resets the free spins counter back to 3. Arrows connect multipliers, so let's say there is an x10 multiplier on reel one and an x1 on reel three (in the same row). If an arrow lands between them, it transforms into an x10 symbol and adds 10 to the value on reel three.If the grid fills with symbols, then the values are summarised, and the counter resets. Then, on each countdown, it adds the summed multipliers for an overall total to be awarded.Lastly, the X-iter offers players the chance to switch the game into 5 different modes, these are:5x the bet guarantees a winning spin.25x the bet guarantees three spins with at least one wild symbol.100x the bet guarantees a game round with entry to the bonus game.250x the bet guarantees three spins with only diagonal arrow symbols.500x the bet guarantees a game round with entry to the bonus game with boosted multipliers.Night Trax: Slot VerdictFrom the massive ways of Nitropolis or its follow-up, the reel dynamics of the Gold series, or oddballs like Dream Diver, ELK has proven to be a studio unafraid to push boundaries, try new themes, or experiment with traditional slot configurations. Others might find it all a bit fiddly.Moving on to the bonus round, which is a simple hold & win game at heart. However, the upgrading arrow element is a new twist. The multipliers can add up, however, and buying the Super Bonus during testing tended to work out fairly well. Some burned, some rewarded, and it is possible to win as much as 10,000x the bet from Night Trax, so there's plenty to play for.As mentioned, the only way to know if you'll like Night Trax is by trying it out. It's fantastic ELK keeps its foot on the creative gas, but there is a question mark over how Night Trax will be received. It is very niche; in fact, it's almost a niche within a niche, maybe even three levels, so it's hard to see Night Trax becoming a hit. Then again, some may love it. title: Keep 'Em Cool
structured_summary:
Keep 'Em Cool is a seaside-themed cluster slot by Hacksaw Gaming featuring a sunny beach setting with a quirky pig character.  
Key features include frozen symbols with three states, Cocktail Glass re-freezes, Blender symbol absorptions, a Sunset Picnic bonus game, and two bonus buy options.  
The reviewer found the game visually pleasant but somewhat plain and lacking the usual excitement and multipliers typical of Hacksaw titles.  
Aesthetics are bright and simple with light blue waters and golden sands, accompanied by a relaxing audio backdrop, though overall immersion felt limited.
review: Keep 'Em Cool: Slot OverviewGrab ya bucket and spade players; software designer Hacksaw Gaming is taking us to the seaside in an online slot titled Keep 'Em Cool, which is a sunny cluster paying grid slot with a chilly twist on the regular cascading wins dynamic. Frozen symbols are what shake things up, and they are joined by Cocktail Glass re-freezes, Blender symbol absorptions, a Sunset Picnic Bonus Game, and two buy bonus choices.If you really wanted to be cool, would you make a move to a sunny tropical beach location? Anyway, a beach is where we're at, and quite a nice one at that. A little plain, though perhaps simplifying life is the goal when heading to this spot for some R&R. Everything necessary for laxing out is here – light blue water, golden sands, an inviting sky, palms, and, err, a pig. Yep, a pig in a scuba mask and floatation device, no less. Not sure at all why, yet it adds a touch, a minor touch, of personality in what would have been a pretty but pretty empty view. Initially, Keep 'Em Cool seemed like a mix between Slotmill's Super Fruit Smash and ELK Studios' Tropicool slots, though the gameplay is very different.Keep 'Em Cool slot - base gameA visit to Keep 'Em Cool's paytable is where users are able to verify which RTP model they have before them. There are four possible values depending on the market, the maximum figure being 96.19%. In all of them, Keep 'Em Cool's volatility has been rated medium (3 out of 5), and the hit frequency remains the same at 31.12%. As a cluster paying slot, wins are created when at least 5 matching symbols are sitting adjacent to each other in vertical or horizontal directions.The gaming is held on a 5x5 sized board, where stakes of 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin can be wagered. All of the pay symbols are fruits of various descriptions, such as apples, bananas, oranges, cherries, plums, dragon fruit, and strawberries. Five-of-a-kind wins might not be anything special, awarding 0.1 to 1 times the bet, but at the upper levels, a 21+ sized cluster is worth 400 to 5,000 times the bet. Wild symbols are not used in Keep 'Em Cool.Keep 'Em Cool: Slot FeaturesKeep 'Em Cool slot - free spinsWhat Keep 'Em Cool does have are Frozen symbols. This means each pay symbol is always in one of three states – unfrozen, half-frozen, or fully frozen. When a winning combination hits, the unfrozen symbols in a win are removed from the board. In addition, after wins have been awarded, all unfrozen symbols in view are removed, whether they were part of a win or not. Fully frozen or half-frozen symbols remain on the grid even if they were not in a win and drop to the bottom of the grid. These symbols change states, so frozen become half-frozen, and half-frozen becomes unfrozen. New symbols then drop down from above to fill in any gaps. This system repeats until no more winning combinations are on the grid.Cocktail Glass SymbolWhen a winning combination occurs with a Cocktail Glass scatter in view, all symbols of the winning type are converted into a fully frozen state. It is possible this happens to more than one symbol type at the same time. A number displayed on the Cocktail Glass represents the number of re-freezes it has left, with a starting maximum of 5. The Cocktail Glass is removed on the next symbol removed after the final re-freeze.Blender SymbolWhen the Blender scatter symbol hits, it is activated and picks one type of symbol to absorb. All instances of the chosen symbol are absorbed, and new symbols drop down from above, continuing until there are no more symbols of the chosen type. At the end of the spin, the Blender awards a payout equal to the number of absorbed symbols as per the paytable values. The Blender starts with a count of 2 and adds 1 for each absorbed symbol.Sunset Picnic Bonus GameWhen Picnic Basket scatters land in the base game, they are collected in a meter by the grid. If 3 Picnic Baskets are collected on the same base game spin, the Sunset Picnic bonus is triggered. Each Picnic Basket reveals a number of 3-5, and the total is how many free spins are awarded. During the Sunset Picnic bonus, Cocktail Glasses and Blenders have a higher chance of landing. Landing Picnic Basket symbols in the feature awards an extra 2 to 5 free spins per basket.Buy BonusKeep 'Em Cool's bonus buy menu offers two ways of playing the game. For 3x the bet, players can activate Bonushunt FeatureSpins, which are highly volatile and where each spin is 5 times more likely to trigger a bonus game. The maximum RTP for it is 96.25%. The second is buying the Sunset Picnic bonus for 100x the bet. This is also highly volatile, with a maximum RTP of 96.22%.Keep 'Em Cool slot - feature buy optionsKeep 'Em Cool: Slot VerdictDo you ever feel like summer's too hot, winter's too cold, autumn's too windy, and spring has just a little too much chill in the air to be completely satisfying? Perhaps part of the human condition is often not being completely happy with where we are, always wanting to be somewhere else, experiencing something else. Maybe that's one reason why our ancestors upped and marched out of Africa 100,000+ years ago, or so they say, eventually wandering across almost the entire globe, even ending up in remote islands that took unbelievable amounts of courage to reach.Such were the thoughts provoked by Keep 'Em Cool, and a wandering mind isn't always a great sign when reviewing an online slot. Keep 'Em Cool; not sure. It didn't have the same level of immersion Hacksaw Gaming slots usually do. It looks nice, if a little plain. The piggy character is a friendly addition, but it kind of felt like a panicked afterthought to give the game personality rather than playing a critical or logical role in the game. Frozen symbols are an interesting idea, and it wouldn't be terrible if they returned again. Keep 'Em Cool seemed like it might be a test case for them, where if they work out here, maybe Hacksaw Gaming would put them to use in a future project, one with a bit more oomph. The Blender concept is an intriguing one as well, though good luck chasing them down as they were elusive as fudge while reviewing Keep 'Em Cool.A conspicuous absence of any multiplying feature, which is often a focal point in a Hacksaw Gaming production probably added to Keep 'Em Cool hollowness. The lack of any 'x-ing' meant Keep 'Em Cool had less of the usual suspense that Hacksaw Gaming slots load on, where the action can go from 0 to 100 miles per hour in a moment. What Keep 'Em Cool does is pretty neat; nothing wrong with it, but more thrilling times have been found among its competitors.

title: Temple Stacks
structured_summary: Temple Stacks is an Aztec/Mayan-themed slot featuring an exotic jungle atmosphere. It introduces Yggdrasil’s new Splitz mechanic with expanding reels and up to 248,832 win ways. review: Temple Stacks (Yggdrasil Gaming): OverviewYggdrasil prove once again that they are a company that isn't afraid of trying new things. Their latest slot Temple Stacks manages a couple of firsts for the company as well as slightly pushing the slots envelope. For one, it is the first time we get to see their new Splitz game mechanic in action. The second major tweak is the game's potential which appears to be Yggdrasil's biggest to date. On all fronts, the numbers associated with Temple Stacks are big. Of course, big numbers on their own don't guarantee a good game so let's fire the beast up and see what it can do.If you know the numbers before trying the game, then the first impressions don’t exactly tally with what loads up. Graphically, Yggdrasil has reined in their creative team and produced something a little lower key than usual - though it's not a bad looker by any means. If you are playing on mobile, be sure to tilt your device to have it on landscape mode. That way, the game grid is framed by some exotic jungle imagery that you don't get on portrait mood. A little thing, but it adds to the atmosphere. Pick a bet between 10 p/c and $/€100, and away we go – either manually or by setting up to an infinite number of auto spins.As mentioned before, Yggdrasil run the game using their brand new Splitz engine. This Megaways-esque system provides 5 reels, 3 rows and 243 win ways – to start with. Winning combinations are formed when three or more of the same symbols land on adjacent reels from left to right. As you would expect, these numbers increase as the grid expands. At full power, up to 12 symbols can appear on each reel which creates a whopping 248,832 win ways. Interestingly, Yggdrasil has forgone any sort of cascade wins system, which makes a change for this style of game. RTP is nice and average at 96.1%, and volatility sits in a satisfying medium to high range.The symbols themselves are simply crafted. There are 5 low pay symbols with Aztec/Mayan designs on them, along with 5 high pay symbols of different coloured square gems – orange, purple, green, blue and red. When it comes to value, low pay symbols return up to 0.5x, the high pay up to 1x the stake. The one exception is the red square which is worth 2.5 times the stake. Sounds pitiful on paper, but don't write it off just yet. Due to the number of win ways and features, Temple Stacks is capable of producing substantial payouts.Temple Stacks (Yggdrasil Gaming): FeaturesFree spins round in actionThe most frequent feature is the Splitz Mystery Stacks with appears often. These Stacks can appear on any reel during the base game as well as free spins and either cover 1-2 symbols or a full reel. During the base game, Mystery Stacks split into 3-9 symbols, and 3-12 during free spins and is the key for maxing out win ways. All Mystery Stacks reveal the same symbol which can be anything except hybrid or scatter symbols.Sometimes, multiple Mystery Stacks appear on the reels, and a winning combination is guaranteed to land. Then, 3 different symbol types and their associated prizes appear above the reels. This effect produces some intense moments before the Stacks finally stop spinning and reveal which symbol is the winner.The game contains a scatter symbol in the form of a spiky shield - 3 or more are needed to trigger Free Spins, and if 2 land, then they become Scatter Wild Hybrid symbols. The 2 scatters are then held in place while the other reels Respin in hopes of landing more scatters, or at least utilising their wild capabilities to create winners. Get lucky, and land 3, 4, or 5 scatters and you receive 1x, 10x, or 100x the stake as well as trigger free spins.There are 4 free spin levels, each with different game rules and volatility. They are unlocked one by one at first, but after that, players are free to choose whichever one they like. The 4 levels are steel, bronze, silver, and gold, which come with 3-9, 4-10, 5-11, or 6-12 Mystery Stack Splitz respectively. However, the higher the Splitz, the less free spins there will initially be:3 scatters – 15 steel, 9 bronze, 6 silver, and 3 gold free spins.4 scatters – 20 steel, 12 bronze, 8 silver, and 4 gold free spins.5 scatters – 35 steel, 21 bronze, 14 silver, and 7 gold free spins.Scatters/hybrids continue to appear during the bonus rounds, and three or more will add extra free spins according to the list above.Temple Stacks (Yggdrasil Gaming): VerdictWith the Megaways engine being in such high demand, it was just a matter of time before we would start to see different variations on the market. What pretty much started with Perfect Gems by Play'n GO has now spawned countless other copycats. Temple Stacks does have shades of Megaways to it yes, but on the whole, there's sufficient distance from Big Time Gaming's invention.Overall, it's a solid game although we do find the visual appearance to be slightly more generic than we're used to coming from Yggdrasil. You should also prepare for some mediocre sessions. The above average volatility can result in runs of dead spins, and low symbol values aren't worth much without features or multiple lines in play. The mathematical model is simply not as sophisticated or refined as what you usually tend to get with the Megaways engine.When it does go off, the good times can be outstanding. We brought up the fact that Temple Stack carries some of Yggdrasil's biggest stats, and the juiciest is the potential which can reach up to 25,000 times the stake. Now, exceptional Yggdrasil wins are relatively scarce when you browse the various casino communities out there, and if this one too fails to produce some extraordinary hits, then may it's time for Yggdrasil to consider recruiting some new mathemagicians. Only time will tell.The sum things up - if we had to offer some constructive criticism it would be that Temple Stacks can feel a little impersonal at times. The high pay symbols are a little dull and a bit more character might have been a nice. As it is, however, Temple Stacks is a solid game with massive potential and an intriguing new game mechanic that is well worth checking out.

title: Dropz

review: Dropz: Slot OverviewYou might need a new toothbrush after playing this one, folks. Dropz is a game from developer ELK Studios that dresses up its action in one of the more sugary slot themes out there, the candy, sweet stuff, lollies one, or whatever you happen to call it. To provide some balance, ELK has stuffed a few fruity items in there, as well as a stack of features from Avalanches; symbol unlocks, level upgrades, a progressive win multiplier, and free spins.Pick the candy theme, and you kind of have to design a game that looks like Dropz. Some of them appear to have been given eyes, which instead of being totally cute, are actually a teensy bit creepy, bringing on one or two memories of Chucky or Mr Hopp. The jazzy 70s symphonically swingy soundtrack brings the happy vibe back, though, and Dropz provides a fairly tasty snack for both eyes and ears.Dropz slot - base gamePicking a bet is step one, where options range from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin, playable on both desktop computers and handheld devices. In its default base game state, Dropz is played on a 6x6 sized grid, but only three symbols on each reel are active – the rest are covered in value-less chocolate blocker tiles, which can be removed as part of the Avalanche function. Behind the scenes, Dropz runs on a medium/highly volatile math model, producing a maximum return to player value of 94%.When symbols drop into the grid, they form regular ways wins when three or more identical symbols land on consecutive reels starting from the left. The four low pay symbols on the pay table are hard candies of various shapes and colours, then come lemons, grapes, apples, strawberries, and liquorice '7s'. Let's do so, and the first feature to cover is Avalanches, which triggers when a win lands. The winning symbols are removed from the grid, as are any chocolate blocker symbols next to an exploding winning symbol. Empty spaces are filled by symbols falling from above, and the Avalanche feature ends when no new win hits. If removed chocolate blocks hold any special symbol or features, they are activated.Special SymbolsOne special symbol to unlock is the wild, which substitutes for any normal al pay symbol – regular wilds are removed by the Avalanche mechanic when used in a win. Another is the Locked Wild, displaying the number 3, signifying the fact it stays on the board for three wins. Dropz symbols award 1-2 extra drops in both the base and bonus game. Lastly, the Level Up symbol activates the next level:Level 1 (starting level) – six rows with 3 active rows and 3 rows of chocolate blockers.Level 2 – seven rows with 3 active rows and 4 rows of chocolate blockers.Level 3 – eight rows with 3 active rows and 5 rows of chocolate blockers.Levels unlock when no more wins happen, and any multipliers, Pair Matching meter progress, or collected bonus symbols carry over to the new level.Symbol Pairs & MultipliersOn the top left is the Pair Matching meter, indicating specific symbol pairs. Any pairs present on the game grid contribute to the meter, which, when full, adds a value to the win multiplier. Pairs removed from the board also remove symbols and chocolates above or below them, making room for symbols to Avalanche in. Multipliers reset between paid spins.ReDropzCollecting 3 bonus symbols through an Avalanche sequence awards 5 free ReDropz on an 8-row high game grid with 3 active rows and 5 chocolate rows. No extra chocolate blockers are added during the feature on future spins, but new features can appear in the chocolate which is there. Wilds remain between spins, and there is no level progression used in Free Dropz.X-IterWhere available, the X-iter menu provides five ways of playing Dropz. All have an RTP of 94%.Bonus Hunt – 2x the bet to buy a game round with more bonus symbols, doubling the chance of triggering the bonus game.Feature Crescendo – 5x the bet to buy a game round with more features or '7' symbols on the grid.Feature Wilds – 25x the bet to buy a game round with 3 locked wilds on the grid.Buy Bonus – 100x the bet to buy the bonus game.Super Bonus – 500x the bet to buy the bonus game with a starting win multiplier of x10.Dropz slot - free spinsDropz: Slot VerdictOkay, it's actually pretty clear what the goal of Dropz is after perusing the rules, but it is one of the more complex sweet-themed slots we've crossed paths with. It's a snowballing machine of a game, where winning ways lead to Avalanches, which lead to chocolate block removals, symbol unlocks, Multiplier Pairs boosting the win multiplier, level ups, with ReDropz tied on top like a bow. Pretty straightforward, in theory, but not always so straightforward in practice. A lot of things have to come together to overcome any inertia and coax Dropz into doing something cool.It's certainly got the ability to do so, yet numerically speaking, Dropz is a game of two halves. A Jekyll and Hyde, if you will. On the positive side is the massive 25,000x the bet max win; on the Hyde side is the 94% RTP which some may find a little hard to stomach. It doesn't prevent Dropz from being an entertaining slot, with more integrants to keep tabs on, more features that can meld, mould and drip off each other, plus bigger potential than most competitors in this category possess. All in all, Dropz ended up being quite a unique game, similar in some ways to earlier slots ELK has done, like Tropicool, Tropicool 2, or Illogicool at a stretch, but delivers its own sticky, sugary morass of gameplay and features regardless.Dropz isn't all sugar, spice, and all things nice, though. For example, if shopping around for the most generous return values out there is a must, then Dropz might struggle to pass muster. Its 94% top value is another example of ELK's downward trajectory and may be as palatable as a bad batch of Salmiakki. If that's not a concern, then there is a load of glazed goodness here to digest.

The name 'Wild Outlaws' could be seen as a bit of a boast when you think about it, conjuring up images of badasses riding roughshod over the frontier, sticking up stage coaches, shooting up the saloon, and generally getting into all sorts of crazy shenanigans. With that in mind, let's mosey on into Wild Outlaws and see what sort of Western escapade the Light & Wonder team has cooked up.Have to say, the first impressions weren't amazing. Wild West slots are preposterously numerous; barely a month seems to go by without a bunch of them being heaped on the pile. Light & Wonder themselves are no frontier first-timers, but you might think the opposite after a cursory glance at Wild Outlaws. It just looks kinda old, its classic one-horse town lacks personality or visual appeal, and the game struggles to kindle much of the genre's romance. The music's pretty neat, though.Wild Outlaws slot - base gameLeaving the audio-visuals behind for now, Wild Outlaws is played on a 6-reel game panel; each reel holds 4 symbols, arming players with 4,096 ways to win. A maximum of 30 free spins can be won, and wins cannot be higher than 10,000x the bet.Wild Outlaws slot - gamble feature in actionWild Outlaws: Slot VerdictPresumably, it's possible to be wild and not be an outlaw, so is it just as possible to be an outlaw and not be wild? Probably, dunno, whatever; maybe Wittgenstein's language games were on our mind, but that's just one of the questions which arose while reviewing Wild Outlaws. Other ponderings arose, too, like, was this game made recently? Again, presumably yes, but darn if it doesn't look dated, and as can often be the case, it's hard to work out if the studio went for a retro look on purpose or not. Wild Outlaws looks like it could have come out years before the last Light & Wonder Western slot we reviewed, Wild Showdown, so who knows?It's a shame because there are some interesting ideas going on here. Things like the Premium Play mode are intriguing, and it doesn't require huge wins to trigger, either. Get a win of more than 1.6x, and you're in with a chance to boost it from a multiplier or even trigger free spins, which did actually occur in the review, so it is a definite possibility. Even the Gamble feature is a temptation since it pops up on 5x the bet wins or higher – both of these add-ons have relatively low requirements for entry. As a comparison, Big Time Gaming's Win Exchange typically kicks in at the 25-100x range to gamble or the 100x swap for free spins. They have different gamblers in their scopes, no doubt, but both studios' methods have their merits, and Wild Outlaws' way of doing things feels like it would appeal to certain gamblers.The rest of the features aren't bad either, so the deal breaker here would seem to be Wild Outlaws' outer wrapper and lack of strong personality, though beauty is in the eye of the beholder and all that. If the game had more charisma, a bit more energy, or didn't look so dated, the good things Wild Outlaws does have might have shined brighter.

title: Sky Bounty
structured_summary:

review: Sky Bounty: Slot OverviewKrakens are no strangers to the world of online slots, and few developers have sighted these mythical creatures more than Pragmatic Play. The studio has built a mini-series around them, containing Release the Kraken and Release the Kraken 2. While today's game Sky Bounty doesn't seem to be directly linked, it contains strands which tenuously echo those two prior slots. One is the appearance of tentacled creatures; another is the word 'Kraken's' next to Sky Bounty's title. As well as that, all three games have some sort of wild-related feature, and the one used here is a pretty good one. So, if you're ready to get all Krakened, let's take to the skies.Take to the skies with octopi-related characters... aren't they creatures of the sea, you might be asking? Normally yes, but apparently the Kraken of this tale has learnt how to survive out of the water, obtain a flying ship, and pilot it through the clouds looking for loot. Clearly, a certain suspension of disbelief will have to take place when entering Sky Bounty's world. Though soaring through the skies on an aerial pirate ship with tentacles makes a nice change from being cast to the bottom of the sea. It's too bad Pragmatic Play didn't push the theme even further; see where it took players. But as is often the case from this studio, it's come up with an interesting idea, made it look nice, yet for some reason stopped short of really running with it.Sky Bounty slot - base gameLike the theme use, Sky Bounty's grid set-up is slightly odd, too, made up of 6 reels and 6 rows of symbols. Instead of being a cluster pays or a pay anywhere slot, as first suspected, it's got 50 paylines for evaluating wins. Digging deeper like a burrowing crustacean, we find Sky Bounty's math model, which is highly volatile and comes in different RTP ranges. The default value is 96.05% when betting regularly, 96.06% with the Ante Bet switched on, or 96.07% when buying free spins. For all three methods, a base bet will have to be selected, and the options are 25 p/c to $/€250.Next on the list are 7 variously coloured and shaped gemstones as Sky Bounty's lower paying symbols, followed by a bottle of rum, a wheel, a cannon, and a pair of crossed swords as the higher value picture symbols. Hitting a 6 OAK low pay win awards 2 to 3 times the bet, rising like a floating pirate ship to 6-20 times the bet for the remaining symbols. Wilds are a pretty big deal in Sky Bounty, more so in the bonus game. In both phases of play, wilds can land on any reel, substituting for any pay symbol. If wilds manage to make wins of themselves, they award up to 20 times the stake for a 6-wild win.Sky Bounty: Slot FeaturesSky Bounty slot - free spinsSky Bounty jazzes up its base game by dropping in a Random Expanding Wild feature from time to time. This feature is used in free spins, too, but there, it has more of a persistent nature. Here's how it works.Random Expanding Wild FeatureThis feature can trigger randomly in the base game. When it does, a frame of 2x2, 3x3, 4x4, 5x5, or 6x6 appears over random symbols. If, on that spin, a wild symbol lands within the frame, the wild expands to become the frame's size. If more than one wild lands within a frame, the expanded wild gets a multiplier equal to the number of wilds the frame contains. The multiplier applies to all wins passing through the expanded wild.Free SpinsSky Bounty's free spins round is triggered when at least 3 scatter symbols land in view. As well as receiving 6 free spins. In free spins, a frame remains on the grid for its full duration, moving positions between each spin. It starts at 2x2 in size, and wilds that land within it expand to fill it, as in the base game. When scatter symbols hit, they are collected. Every 3 scatter symbols collected increases the frame size to 3x3, 4x4, 5x5, then 6x6, awarding +2 free spins each time. After the fourth time, scatter symbols do not land on the reels. If the feature was triggered with 4, 5, or 6 scatter symbols, the round starts with 1, 2, or 3 scatter symbols already collected.Ante Bet & Buy Free SpinsActivating Sky Bounty's Ante Bet places more scatter symbols on the reels for an increase to the stake of 20%, while free spins can be bought for 100x the bet. Bought free spins land 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatter symbols to trigger the feature.Sky Bounty slot - free spinsSky Bounty: Slot VerdictOn the whole, Sky Bounty provided a satisfactory gaming experience, containing many of the pros and cons that often accompany a Pragmatic Play release. Whilst mostly positive, one suspects that with a bit of a prod, extra time spent on development, or more love poured into the creative process, Sky Bounty might have elevated itself from average/above average to something even greater. But whatever the reason, the studio is happy pushing games out at an astonishing speed, though with few slots really blossoming into classics despite the large number of them.However, even if Pragmatic Play does favour quantity, the quality is often quite high. Or, high enough. Sky Bounty is another example, containing interesting ideas such as skyfaring Krakens and swabs of the stratosphere, as well as intriguing gaming devices. The expanding wild feature definitely has merits. There's a mildly Fat Rabbit feel to it, but this is no straightforward expanding wild. It has one or two extra parts that have to synchronise before the feature really goes off. An interesting symbiotic effect is created between the bonus symbol collection and the growing frame since the larger the frame gets, the greater the likelihood of landing a wild within it, potentially leading to a sizable wild symbol - full screen in the best-case scenario. If you're lucky, a multiplier might compound the thrills. The growing frame feature helps balance the reels and ways set-up, which felt a little off in the beginning. It's also good for producing wins of up to 5,000x the bet at the most too, which is Sky Bounty's win cap.So there are positive things to say about Sky Bounty, but again, it's a Pragmatic Play slot that takes you up to a compelling point, then kind of leaves you there wanting more. This is an excellent trait in a storyteller, perhaps, but it can be frustrating when reviewing slots, imagining how a stronger push could have made a game that little bit extra special. Add up everything Sky Bounty has to offer, and you've got a good Kraken game on your hands. Good, but one suspects with a bit of additional time, resources, or love, Sky Bounty could have been more uniquely memorable.

title: Wolf Hunters

review: Wolf Hunters IntroductionWolf Hunters is a Video Slot produced by Yggdrasil Gaming with 5 reels, 3 rows, and 20 fixed paylines. It's playable on all devices between €0.20 and €100 and is somewhere in the medium to high variance range. Visually, the game has a dark Immortal Romance kind of feel to it with a backdrop set against a dark Transylvanian type castle. The story revolves around two unnamed characters, the Hhunter, and Huntress, sent out to fight werewolves.The game has 7 regular symbols that win if 3 or more are lined up in sequence on a payline. The Werewolf, which is the most valuable symbols, is worth 25x for 5 across a single payline. There is 1 Werewolf symbol that functions as a high pay symbol unless it is defeated at which point it transforms into a sticky wild. There is also a sticky wild symbol that always awards respins and 2 different Free Spin symbols that activate Free Spins.Wolf Hunters FeaturesHunter vs Werewolf battleThe Werewolf - The Werewolf is the highest paying symbol and can land on any reel. When it lands, a random hunter tries to hit it, if they succeed, the Werewolf symbol turns into a sticky wild and awards 1 respin. If the Hunter is unsuccessful then the Werewolf symbol acts as a regular high pay symbol. Each hit on the Werewolf decreases its life total by 1. When the Werewolf life total is reduced to 0/600, Slayer Free Spins are activated.The Hunter and Huntress - When the Werewolf appears on the reels in the base game 1 random hunter tries to attack it. When a Werewolf symbol appears, one hunter strikes, if unsuccessful, the second hunter steps in for a second chance. Landing 2 Free Spin Symbols in Free Spin mode awards 2 additional Free Spins.Hunter and Huntress Free Spin upgrades - Free Spin symbols can be collected during all Free Spin modes. Once upgraded, when the Hunter gets a hit on the Werewolf, the Werewolf turns into a wild which expands up and down by 1 reel position. Collecting 3 Huntress Free Spin symbols upgrades the Huntress and awards 2 Free Spins. Once upgraded, when the Huntress gets a hit on the Werewolf, the Werewolf turns into a wild which expands left by 1 reel position. The upgraded hunter always attacks the Werewolf first.Scatter Free Spins - Triggered by landing 2 Free Spin symbols in one spin in the base game. Players are awarded 10 Free Spins with the possibility of triggering more Free Spins.Rage Free Spins - 7 Rage Free Spins are awarded when any hunter collects 100 Rage points. In Rage Free Spins the enraged Hunter is upgraded for the entire Free Spin session and does not collect any more Free Spin symbols or rage points. After Rage Free Spins are complete the enraged Hunter’s Rage collection is reset to 0.Slayer Free Spins - 10 Slayer Free Spins are awarded when the Werewolf's health bar is reduced to 0. Slayer Free Spins feature no Free Spin symbols and all Werewolf symbols are replaced with wild symbols on the reels. After Slayer Free Spins are complete, the Werewolf’s health bar is restored to 600.Wolf Hunters ConclusionWolf Hunters appears to share many similarities with Vikings Go To Hell and could possibly be a clone or built on the same mathematical model. The volatility and max win potential are likely within the same range too which is around 3000x.We're not big fans of Yggdrasil slots utilising progress meters to trigger free spins, and there have been some discussions before in terms of the legitimacy of these meters, with some suspecting the RTP to take a dive as the numbers creep closer to triggering a feature. title: Mystery Spin Deluxe Megaways
structured_summary: Mystery Spin Deluxe Megaways is a retro-themed fruit machine slot inspired by NetEnt’s Twin Spin, featuring a classic disco vibe. It offers up to 117,649 Megaways with linked reels, Mystery Symbols that transform for bigger wins, and a Mystery Spin feature for added excitement. The reviewer finds it a solid, entertaining adaptation but criticizes its lack of originality and lower-than-expected payouts. Visually vibrant with a nostalgic feel, the game includes disco-style music reminiscent of the original Twin Spin soundtrack.
review: Mystery Spin Deluxe Megaways (Blueprint Gaming): ReviewThe idea of combining Megaways with linked reels is not a unique concept and is something we've seen already in Big Time Gaming's mega potential monster Queen of Riches. NetEnt's original version meanwhile, which used to be one of its most talked about games back in the days, has died a slow death as players began giving up on it with claims that it had started to behave differently and that it had been modified following the conversion to the html5 format. In fact, lengthy discussions have ensued on forums around the web, debating whether it has been nerfed or not.Some five years after the release of Twin Spin, NetEnt had the chance to make things right and to further build on the success of the brand, but failed utterly. Twin Spin Deluxe, released in 2018, turned out to be a dreadful medium variance 6-reel creation with cluster pays, and a max win of 1000 times your stake. If you're waiting for a caped hero to bring Twin Spin into the modern era, your call has been answered, for Blueprint Gaming has seized the opportunity to fill the void that NetEnt left in the wake of its blunder. Knowing how protective NetEnt is of its intellectual property, however, don't be too surprised if this one gets pulled from the market.Mystery Spin Deluxe Megaways is a 6-reel slot that offers up to 117,649 ways to win. Making use of Big Time Gaming's trendy mechanic in combination with synced reels, it comes with Mystery Symbol feature that randomly transforms all instances of it into one of the regular symbols. There's also a Mystery Spin feature where only Mystery Symbols will appear on the linked reels. You can play Mystery Spin Deluxe Megaways across all devices from 10 cents to 10€ per spin.Those familiar with the original will find similar elements in Blueprint's version. While it's undoubtedly a fresh vision and a fabulous adaptation, you can't disregard the fact that it's so similar in look and feel that it cannot be regarded as anything else other than an attempt to capitalise on Twin Spin's fame. Just like the original, Mystery Spin Deluxe Megaways is a vibrant slot with a retro/classic fruit machine feel, and even the disco background music is basically a cover of Twin Spin's soundtrack.Symbols on the reels include A, K, Q, J and 10 royal values as well as more lucrative cherries, lemons, grapes, oranges, and watermelons. The most rewarding is the lucky seven which yields 10 times your stake for a combination of 6. There's a wild included as well which you don't get to see too often.Mystery Spin Deluxe Megaways (Blueprint Gaming): FeaturesMystery symbols in viewBeing a Megaways slot, the rows vary on each spin and can randomly appear between 2 to 7 symbols high. Unlike other Megaways offerings, however, it comes with a set of fixed win ways (since the reels are linked) that can give you 729, 4096, 15625, 46656 or 117649 ways to win.Blueprint Gaming can't get enough of its Mystery Symbols feature and you can expect more of it in this game as well. When the Mystery Symbols hit, all instances of them will transform into a randomly chosen regular symbol for increased winning potential. The main attraction, of course, is the linked reels feature, or the In Sync feature as Blueprint calls it. When randomly activated, up to 6 reels can spin in synchronisation, showing matching symbols on all linked reels. Moreover, the symbols can also appear super stacked on the reels. In combination with the randomly triggered Mystery Spin feature, where only Mystery Symbols will appear on the linked reels, the outcome can result in a max payout of 10,000 times your total stake.Mystery Spin Deluxe Megaways (Blueprint Gaming): VerdictUsing NetEnt's Twin Spin as a basis, Blueprint doesn't push the limits of the fundamental idea too far and they certainly haven't wasted the gripping premise of the game by over-complicating things. If we were to design a Megaways version of the original ourselves, this is pretty much how it would come out. The only gripe we have with it is, well, that it's essentially a copy of the original, not only in terms of gameplay, but visually as well, something that could very well end up causing some friction between NetEnt and Blueprint.Though an overall entertaining and solid game, it doesn't come without some minor annoying moments. For example, seeing how frequently the game expands to its full 117k win ways setting (more often than what you usually see in Megaways slots), you would expect it to reward bigger wins. You'll soon find yourself rolling your eyes as nothing ever seems to come out of it, or even worse, when symbols fail to connect in spite of the massive number of paylines.When comparing Queen of Riches, Twin Spin and Mystery Spin Deluxe Megaways, three of the most prominent synched reel slots on the market, Queen of Riches comes out as the champion every day of the week as we find it to be much more explosive, volatile, and original. With that said, they're both fantastic games and if you're looking to kill some time playing online slots, you can't go wrong with either. Nevertheless, we'll have to wait and see if slips through NetEnt's team of lawyers.

title: Roar of the Bear Megaways

When the bonus spins are finished, the number of free spins in view is added up and awarded, while the Golden Claws indicate the initial size of the roaming wild.In free spins, the main reels 2 to 5 are fixed, so they always land 5 symbols in the marked section. Within this section, a roaming wild appears in random positions while the reels are spinning. When Golden Claw symbols hit, they are collected. For each 3 Golden Claw symbols collected, the roaming wild grows in size, and +2 free spins are added. The roaming wilds sizes are 1x2 – 2x2 – 2x3 – 3x3.Bonus Buy & Wild BetThe bonus buy is where players can pay 100x the bet to trigger the bonus round, while the Wild Bet, when switched on, increases the stake by 50%, upping the chance of triggering modifiers and the bonus feature.Roar of the Bear Megaways slot - free spinsRoar of the Bear Megaways: Slot VerdictTyrant King sparked the Apex Predator series off with a loud roar, Ocean Hunter reined everything back to a damp whimper, and as stated above, Roar of the Bear Megaways sits somewhere between the two. Possibly leaning closer to the shark game than the dinosaur one. The bear in the forest theme has been adequately pulled off, nothing special about it. A regular troop of animals appear on the reels, the background is nicely if generically drawn, making Roar of the Bear Megaways easy on the eyes if a tad unexciting due to the profusion of nature slots looking like this.On a mechanical side, the larger-than-normal Megaways game board isn't just for show, which adds a certain level of allure. You get a bunch of additional ways, plus the Eagle Wild and Salmon Wild features make use of the extra real estate – when they trigger, which probably isn't going to be a lot of the time. But they're complimentary features rather than the main event. The key feature in Roar of the Bear Megaways is its growing, roaming free spins wild symbol. Funny thing, too, as if it's got a mind of its own and prefers to hang out as far to the right of the game board as it possibly can a lot of the time. Occasionally, it'll venture towards the left side of the screen and could be useful for knocking together a decent win.In other words, positive and negative outcomes are both possible, yet overall, Roar of the Bear Megaways didn't latch on like others of its kind, such as Push Gaming's 'Fat' slots. Roar of the Bear Megaways was okay by the end, but it felt like iSoftBet's enthusiasm in the Apex Predator idea had waned.

title: Worms of Valor
