review: Worms of Valor: Slot OverviewMasters of pop, AvatarUX, return, and for this outing, they've burrowed into the dirt to unearth the online slot Worms of Valor. There might be a fighting focus, but the chipper backing tune gives the game a wacky slapstick feel. Worms of Valor, on the whole, has gone hard on the slapstick angle. Like, say, Kitty POPpins or, at a stretch, Critter Pop, Worms of Valor is all about levelling up the adorability meter while gambling.Worms of Valor slot - base gameThe worms might be here to entertain with their adorable ways, but beneath the surface, Worms of Valor is serious business powered by a highly volatile math model, pushing out an RTP of 96%. Maybe the design team is sick of the word PopWins, and any excuse, even the most minor one, to use a different label is welcome. Players don't seem to be sick of these types of games, though, judging by the consistent frequency AvatarUX churns them out.Worms of Valor is a good example, too. Double Lux enabled bonus buys will retrigger again (once) if the total win is 20x the bet or less. The RTP for this is 96.18%.Living With Stan slot - free spinsLiving With Stan: Slot VerdictWhatever your thoughts on Lucksome's slot might be, smash or pass, you can't accuse the studio of clinging to a single type with a kung-fu grip. Rather, it crafts an amiable backstory through a pregame story sequence before moving into a charming prehistoric game world with a 10,000x max win (up to $250,000), where intertwined features are linked to the family's struggle to get their gear back. title: Medallion Megaways
structured_summary: Medallion Megaways is a luxury Saharan desert-themed slot featuring gemstones and mystical symbols. review: Medallion Megaways (Fantasma Games): OverviewHaving read our reviews, developers sometimes reach out to us for different reasons. Usually, it's just a matter of factual errors that need to be corrected, but on rare occasions, they want to comment on a negative review. On one such occasion, one particular developer wished to explain why they had chosen to "play it safe", as we so elegantly had put it, by letting us know that, as a small studio they really couldn't afford to take any chances. Fair enough, we thought, albeit a bit ironic given the fact that the industry is all about chance and risk.Small-scaled studio Fantasma Games' first Megaways slot, however, was anything but safe. In fact, Flower Fortune Megaways was so unique we actually questioned whether they had ever played, or even seen, a Megaways game before creating one of their own. A mix of Nintendo-like visuals, soothing music and Candy Crush elements, Fantasma's debut Megaways offering went on to become a hit and was well-received by both recreational players and the casino community alike. In short, Fantasma's gamble had paid off. Unfortunately, the same cannot be said for those mentioned in our first example who's game we can hardly even remember the title of, that's how generic it is.Now, if you've played Flower Fortune, your first impression of Fantasma's second Megaways release Medallion Megaways might very well be the same as ours - disappointing. Has the studio we previously praised for being bold and creative suddenly become all comfortable? Is that a pair of dad jeans they're wearing now? Set to find out, we fired up Medallion Megaways and started spinning frantically. First, let's look at the technical details. Medallion Megaways is a 6x6 grid video slot with cascading reels that can produce a random number of win ways from between 64 to 46,656. Medium variance and playable from 0.10 to €/$80 per spin, it incorporates expanding wilds, respins and a free spins game with an increasing multiplier.One aspect where Medallion Megaways unarguably does stand out is the visuals department. Set in a luxury tent in the Saharan desert, Fantasma has managed to forge quite an atmospheric setting with plenty of cosiness and warmth. And if you're impressed by the airy ambience here, just wait until you trigger the bonus. That's where the magic happens, after all. One complaint we had with Flower Fortune was the design of the symbols which we felt looked dull and generic. In Medallion Megaways, they're made up of essentially the same assortment of gemstones, but the high-value ones are now marked with triangles, crescent moons, and stars that, quite frankly, look like communist symbols. The most rewarding symbol, however, is the one carrying the golden snake - it'll give you 30 times your stake for six on a payline. The crystal is the wild and appears on reels 2-5. Aside from substituting for all regular symbols, it has other properties as well, which we will cover below.Medallion Megaways (Fantasma Games): FeaturesFree spins in actionLike the majority of Megaways slots, Medallion Megaways is played using Cascading Reels which means that winning symbols are removed and replaced with new ones, allowing you to win repeatedly from a single spin. There's also a Win Multiplier in the base game that increases by 1x with each successive cascade and resets back to zero on a non-winning spin.There are also a couple of mysterious medallions to keep an eye out for here. These can appear following any base game spin to activate (golden medallion) or deactivate (silver medallion) the feature amulets, which are positioned below the reel set, and their corresponding features. These features are:Expanding Wilds - when the wild amulet is activated, all crystal wilds landing on reels 2-5 expand to fully cover the reels. Moreover, each expanding wild also carries a multiplier of 2x, 3x, 4x, 5x, or 6x.Void Respin - when the respin amulet is in play, the void respin symbol may appear in view. Each of these landing on the reels will remove 2-10 symbols that are not part of any winning combination.The Free Spins feature is activated in the same manner - the golden medallion appears and activates the free spins amulet. With 10 free spins awarded (which cannot be retriggered), the win multiplier does not reset during the round and both the expanding wild and void respin features are active throughout as well.Medallion Megaways (Fantasma Games): VerdictSo at this point you might be asking, is Medallion Megaways a clone of Flower Fortunes or does it hold its own? Well, it's not a clone, and although several parts have been recycled, the mathematical design, as well as the features, are entirely unique to this game. The truth is that Medallion Megaways is a significantly tamer slot, or so it seems to us at least. By the end of our 3-hour test run, the balance almost appeared to have remained static, which means it can serve as an excellent alternative for those looking for some value in the form of playtime. 15-30x base game hits are delivered quite consistently, and you rarely have to wait too long for a bonus to drop. The good news is that, in spite of the low volatility, there's still plenty of potential with a max win of around 12,000 times your stake.The visual design is superb, as are the sound effects. It's a bit strange, however, to see the Megaways counter display 6-digit numbers when, mathematically, the game can "only" generate 46,656 win ways. Unless we're complete idiots, that's only 5 digits. All in all, Medallion Megaways is a decent slot, but it's hard to get excited about it when the novelty of the concept has worn off, making it feel like a yesterdays slot.

review: The Wild Class: Slot OverviewCast your mind or imagination back to 1983, the year when The Red Hot Chilli Peppers formed, the North American video game industry almost crashed, Twisted Sister released You Can't Stop Rock' n' Roll, Michael Jackson popularised the moonwalk, and Return of the Jedi ignited cinemas. The good news for many is that The Wild Class has more in common with the original movie starring Michael J. Fox, or even the Jason Bateman ones, than the series that came along in 2011. The game is not set at a high school as you might expect (though probably a good idea since this is online gambling) but at an amusement park instead. The park is also haunted, for good measure, though ghosts and goblins make way for the lupine terrors. When a full stack of the same symbol covers the full reel it lands on, the win multiplier increases by 1. The current multiplier value is displayed on a full moon located at the upper right side of the screen. Any winning combinations in view are modified by the current win multiplier. The win multiplier resets between each paid spin in the base game.Appearing on all reels is the scatter symbol - 3 or more in view triggers Blood Moon Spins. No matter how many scatters trigger the feature, it always starts with 7 free spins. However, the number of scatters determines how many human symbols transform into wild werewolf symbols:3 scatters trigger Fury, where 1 human symbol becomes a wild werewolf version.4 scatters trigger Carnage, where 2 human symbols become wild werewolf versions.5 scatters trigger Rampage, where all 3 human symbols become wild werewolf versions.The selection of which human transforms into a werewolf is made at random. Also, any win multiplier carries over from the base game and does not reset between free spins. Should scatter symbols land during the bonus game, then +1 extra spin is awarded per scatter, up to a maximum of 30 spins.The Wild Class: Slot VerdictWe've said it before, but it seems Play'n GO's demanding schedule forces the team to constantly be on the lookout for new ways to entertain. In this case, it's The Wild Class' theme that provides the initial spark of interest. Its features aren't particularly new, yet the stacked symbols, full reel wilds, and the game's overall look gives it a vintage slot feel. This is kind of appropriate, since The Wild Class is set back in the heady days of 1983 before irony permeated pop culture, where 'jocks' were kings of the school, and 'nerds' were there to be tormented in front of the cheerleader squad. In a satisfying turn of events, we know the 'nerds' got their own back during the tech revolution, though the jocks are still probably doing alright via pro sports and all that.So onto The Wild Class, which is a professionally designed slot that isn't anywhere near as revolutionary, yet still has enough atmosphere and features to be entertaining. Suspend disbelief for a while, and the theme comes across in a fun, preppy, all-American high school way. This is a formula which has proved popular in loads of shows or movies, and Play'n GO has translated it to an online slot quite well too. The features are all dependable performers, where full reel wilds are capable of working hand in hand with the win multiplier to produce exciting results. More so in free spins, of course, since the multiplier isn't reset there until the bonus round ends. Get a real full moon run on, and wins of up to 6,666 times the stake are possible.So, after day has broken, and the werewolves have transformed back into their human form, what's left is a game possessing enough elements to provide an entertaining session, with a quirky theme on top. The Wild Class is a tad forgettable and unlikely to make a big splash, but enjoyable enough at the time when you're collecting multipliers while keeping an eye out for werewolves lurking in dark corners.

title: Coba Reborn
structured_summary: Coba Reborn is a jungle-themed slot featuring snakes and exotic flora, continuing the serpent motif from its predecessor. It offers cluster pays, an Avalanche feature, snake progress mechanics, and unique orchid-powered snake abilities, with high volatility and an RTP of 94%. The reviewer found it a thoughtful reboot balancing new features with reduced payouts, resulting in a familiar yet nuanced gameplay experience. Visually, the game is darker and moodier than the original, with rich jungle and ancient ruin aesthetics complemented by atmospheric audio.
review: ﻿Coba Reborn: Slot OverviewLike a snake charmer playing their flute to raise a serpent from a basket, ELK Studios has played a tune of its own with similar results. What this means is the slithering snake in a jungle action found in Coba has returned in the form of Coba Reborn. The original wowed with its unusual serpent symbol eating mechanic and overall dazzling design. For the Reborn version, ELK Studios returns most of what made the first game tick while adding in a few flowery extras (literally) and tweaking some of the dials here and there to make a game that is familiar yet new-ish at the same time.Whilst the music has stayed more or less the same, it's like ELK Studios swapped out the gold filter for a blue/grey one when making Coba Reborn. This game is darker, moodier looking than the original, though hardly less eye-catching. An exotic culture remains the dominant visual influence, though Coba Reborn is located in a danker part of the world than before. A game grid covered in snake heads, on the sides as well as the top, lies buried in deep bush, surrounded by thick fauna and what looks like ancient ruins in the background. Standard stuff in some ways, yet the ELK Studios team has made it look good, drawing on the experience gleaned not just from Coba, but games like Pacific Gold and Voodoo Gold.As well as some front-end adjustments, changes have been made on the back end too. One notable difference is that the volatility for Coba Reborn has been dialled up to high, compared to medium in the previous game. Another is that the RTP has dipped to 94%. This return value applies whether you're betting 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin in the regular manner or have activated the bonus mode and are buying features from the X-iter menu. Played on a 7x7-sized gaming panel, Coba Reborn's cluster pays win system means rewards are given when at least 5 matching symbols are connected to each other anywhere on the board.Symbol values, too, have been pruned back, quite significantly in certain areas. Coba Reborn's low pays are a green turtle, blue lizard, and bronze monkey symbol, while the high pays are a green gem, blues gem, red gem, and a gold mask symbol. Landing a 5 OAK winning cluster awards 0.05 to 1 times the bet, and at the upper end, a 15+ sized cluster win awards 1.5 to 50 times the bet. When wild symbols appear, they may be used to substitute any regular paying symbol.Coba Reborn: Slot FeaturesCoba Reborn slot - base gameIt's time for snakes and flowers as we go over Coba Reborn's features. Let's start with winning symbols, which are removed from the board when they form and are replaced by symbols dropping from above. Winning symbols are collected by the snake progress meter, and the Avalanche feature continues functioning like this until no new win appears.Snake Progress MeterWhen the snake progress meter is half-filled, wild symbols are randomly placed on the grid after the symbol refill. If the meter is completely filled, snakes are released depending on the level reached. Reach levels 1, 2, or 3 and 3 snakes are released from random entry points on the sides of the grid. Reach level 4, and 6 snakes are released from random entry points.SnakesA snake is a linear cluster of symbols that grows as the snake moves across the grid. Snakes are at least 5 symbols long and always form part of a winning cluster or part of a larger cluster. A yellow body snake means it will survive till the next avalanche; a blue body means it may die. Snakes always start in a yellow survival state, surviving the first avalanche drop. The first symbol a snake moves over becomes the snake's symbol, indicated on its head. Snakes become wild if the first symbol is an orchid. Symbols a snake moves over are transformed into its symbol, except for orchids or wilds.If a snake moves over the same symbol type as itself, it grows in length, and its body becomes yellow – the same applies when snakes eat wild symbols. If a snake does not move over (eat) its symbol type, wild or orchid, during its whole movement, it dies and is removed from the grid before any win evaluations. Snakes with a wild as their symbol turn crossed symbols into wild symbols. These snakes must eat wilds, multiplier wilds, or orchids to grow and survive. Wild wins pay as the highest value symbol.Where snakes cross paths, a multiplier wild symbol is created. They start at x2 and are doubled on each cross at the same position. When more than one multiplier is used in a win, the values are multiplied together first. A snake eating a wild multiplier grows and turns yellow. Lastly, a snake that crosses itself or bites its tail without the ouroboros feature active dies and is removed from the reels.Coba Reborn slot - bonus roundOrchidsCoba Reborn has 4 different orchid symbols, each one possessing its own feature:Blood Orchid – when 2 of these symbols are in view, a snake spawns from each. Or, a blood orchid can drain another type of orchid in view and spawn a snake from its position. A former blood orchid position turns wild once the snake has moved. When a snake eats a blood orchid, a random number of snakes appear from random entry points on the sides of the grid.Hydra Orchid – when a snake eats a hydra orchid, it spawns another snake behind its head with the same symbol type. If the eating snake has the rebirth or ouroboros feature, these are passed on to the new snake.Rebirth Orchid – when a snake eats a rebirth orchid, it can be resurrected from the dead to the same length and keep the ouroboros feature if it had it. The rebirth feature persists across multiple avalanche drops.Ouroboros Orchid – when a snake eats an ouroboros orchid, it can cross itself without dying. The crossing grows the snake which enters the survival state (yellow-bodied). The crossing position becomes a multiplier wild.Snakes may have both rebirth and ouroboros features but cannot eat another rebirth or ouroboros orchid if it already carries them.X-iterA staple ELK Studios addition, the X-iter allows players to take on Coba Reborn in different game modes.Boosted Chance – one drop for 2x the bet with more than double the chance of reaching the first level on the snake meter.Flower Power – 10x the bet for one drop with at least 3 random orchids.All Ouroboros – 25x the bet for a game round with double blood orchids. All snakes can cross themselves.Bali Boost – 100x the bet for a game round guaranteed to reach level 1.Coba – 500x the bet for a game round that starts on level 4 with 6 snakes awarded.Coba Reborn slot - feature buy menuCoba Reborn: Slot VerdictIt took time to form a definitive opinion about Coba Reborn. One reason why it didn't wow right away is because, in some ways, it is close to the original, and sequels often struggle to stand out of the shadow of what preceded them, whether in slots, books, movies, or any creative endeavour. It just didn't have the same shock of being new about it. Following on from the initial reaction was a feeling that with Coba Reborn, ELK Studios giveth on the one hand and taketh on the other. Additions are obvious things like the flower features and higher volatility, which some players may favour (others may not), so in this regard, the gameplay has received a reboot, or rebirth, as the case may be.On the other hand, ELK has sliced the RTP back, which never feels great, while taking an axe to the pay symbols and decimating the larger cluster values. So while the extra features are doing their best to augment the Coba Reborn experience, reductions are there, holding them back from getting too wild and crazy. On an eyeball level, this balancing act seemed to mean lengthy chain of events can occur in Coba Reborn with, at times, surprisingly limited results. Of course, Coba Reborn has the guns to produce big results, satisfyingly so, too, when the snakes are slithering around doing their thing aided by orchids, which are stunning flowers, BTW. The game has the same impressive 25,000x the bet max win as before, which would be insane to see hit using this particular system.Still, it was hard to call Coba Reborn a major improvement over the original. At best, it felt about the same as Coba, maybe slightly more elaborate, though when factoring in things like the RTP drop, some might see it as inferior. However, interest in the new orchids and their abilities did grow as the review progressed, as they provided a new slant on how the action in Coba Reborn unfolds. By the end, the reaction was positive enough to recommend Coba Reborn to those who enjoyed the slithering goodness possible in the original Coba slot, with one or two reservations.

title: Reactoonz 2
structured_summary: Reactoonz 2 is a quirky, sci-fi themed grid slot featuring charming alien critters. It offers cascade cluster wins, multiple wild types, and a multi-level Quantumeter that triggers powerful wilds and multipliers. The reviewer finds it a fun, energetic sequel with familiar yet enhanced gameplay and a slightly higher max win. The game's visuals are colorful and lively, complemented by a zippy soundtrack that matches its frenetic pace.
review: Reactoonz 2: OverviewEveryone’s favourite googly-eyed goons are back in Reactoonz 2, the sequel to one of Play’n GO’s finest ever grid slots. The original was a sensation, so there was plenty of anticipation over the follow-up. The changes might not seem huge initially, but are more than enough to single the two games out. An extra collection meter has been added for one, modifiers rearranged, and wilds have a few nifty tricks they can pull. Underlying it all is the frenetic activity and amiable characters that made the first one great. Is it better, is it worse? Let’s take a look.Reactoonz 2 - Gargantoon featureThe opening look is reassuringly familiar. Reactoonz 2 retains the 7x7 format, with a rather plain blue background and a zippy soundtrack. The right-hand side of the screen has been changed though. There are now two intriguing meter/charge areas that fire into life when cluster wins stack up. Play’n GO has gone for a ‘give em the same, but a bit more’ approach to the design.Reactoonz 2 may be played on any device from mobile to desktop by setting bets from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin. The stats are fairly similar to Reactoonz, though RTP has dipped slightly to 96.2% on the default setting. Volatility remains high (8/10), so players can enjoy a similarly tuned math model as the original, which is definitely one of the highlights.Making a return performance is the same 8 chaps making up the paytable’s regular symbols. They are split into two groups - the one eyes and the two-eyed symbols. Players get a win when clusters of five or more matching symbols touch horizontally or vertically – triggering the cascade feature. Clusters of 15+ are the most valuable combinations possible, ranging from 3x to 500x the stake. The highest paying premium has also taken a hit in value.The remaining four symbols are wilds of varying abilities. The least desirable in is the uncharged wild. These wilds appear on cascades, but do not form wins on their own. They can, however, change to electric wilds when they are next to a win, or when the Wild Pair Explosion triggers. All other wilds substitute for any pay symbol, covered in the next section.Reactoonz 2: FeaturesThis bit might not make much sense after one read through, though the gist is straightforward – winning clusters fill charge meters to trigger bigger and better features. Let’s look at the details.The key to it all is the cascade feature. Winning clusters are removed to let new symbols fall into the gaps, resulting in potential more wins. Cascades continue to pop and fill meters until no new winners appear.On each spin, one of the one-eyed symbols is randomly chosen to fluctuate. If fluctuating symbols win, then an electric wild appears in one of the newly vacated spaces while also filling the Fluctometer. When this meter is totally full, 1-3 electric wilds are added to the grid. The Fluctometer can be recharged more than once, but is disabled if the Gargantoon is released.Electric wilds substitute for any pay symbol and zap Reactoonz as well. Any non-wild symbols removed by the electric wild charge the Quantumeter. Each symbol is worth one charge. The Quantumeter continues to charge after releasing an Energoon, but is disabled if a Gargantoon is unleashed. Collect 55, 85, 110, or 135 charges to reach level 1, 2, 3, or 4 respectively. Each level releases a different wild:Level 1 unleashes four 1x1 Energoon wilds.Level 2 unleashes a single 2x2 Energoon wild.Level 3 unleashes a single 3x3 Gargantoon wild.Level 4 adds an x2 multiplier for all wins including the Gargantoon wilds.After a 3x3 Gargantoon triggers a cascade, it breaks into two 2x2 Gargantoon wilds. After they trigger a cascade, they are replaced by nine 1x1 Gargantoon wilds.Wait, we’re not finished yet. When all features are done, and there are 2 or more Electric wilds remaining in view, the Wild Pair Explosion feature is triggered. If there are 2 electric wilds adjacent to each other, all symbols, except wilds, are removed from the grid. If the wilds are not adjacent, the symbols between two of them as well as the surrounding symbols are destroyed (not including wilds). Any symbols removed do not payout, but they do charge the Quantumeter.Reactoonz 2: VerdictIt’s a pretty safe bet that fans of the original Reactoonz slot, or grid slots enthusiasts in general, will be pretty excited about what Play’n GO has designed for the follow-up. Reading the rules will quite possibly confuse you more than just winding Reactoonz 2 up and having a bash. As before, consecutive cluster wins build up ever more impressive features as they tick along. This time around its electric wilds you want to charge the four-level Quantumeter. The more levels, the more beneficial things will be. Have a crack in demo, and all should become clear enough.It’s not a paradigm shift, but enough has been changed to give Reactoonz 2 a different feel. The potential has been given a slight increase as well, now maxing out at 5,083 times the stake. Not a massive upgrade compared to the first one, but hey, an epic win should you get the critters performing to that level. The game is still all about its critters too, which remain super personable. The way they shimmy and shake when hit by lightning is amusing, ensuring the sequel is as charming as ever. More importantly, Reactoonz 2 has the same highly compelling gameplay - once you’ve figured out what the heck is going on.All up, Reactoonz 2 is just as mental, if not more so, than the original. When features are firing it’s like you’ve lit all your fireworks at once. Reactoonz 2 is a worthy follow up to one of Play’n GO’s most popular slots but unlikely to have quite the same impact. It’s a bit too similar to the first to make the same tidal wave impression perhaps but is still immense fun to play regardless.Don't MissDid you know Play'n GO have created a backstory to the Reactoonz universe? Titled Dr Toonz, the game centers around Dr. Toonz, the scientist who created the Reactoonz creatures.

title: Brazil Bomba
structured_summary: Brazil Bomba is a Rio Carnival-themed slot capturing a laid-back, festive atmosphere with feathered dancers and beach vibes. It features cluster pays with 8 reels, a Bomb symbol that clears symbols, multipliers that build with consecutive wins, and free spins that retain multipliers. review: Brazil Bomba (Yggdrasil Gaming): OverviewThe internet has a bunch of definitions and translations for the word bomba. Many are a little inappropriate for a wholesome game review so won’t be repeated here. In our case, it stands for a bomb, and this energetic new slot from Yggdrasil Gaming is full of them. Interestingly, there is a bit of debate online about the correct translation of the word. Portuguese being the national language, the two words that pop up are bomba and bombear. Yes, this might be a little pedantic, but it’s our job to dissect games and present the findings. Not to worry, bomba is widely accepted so let’s go with that and let a few off on Yggdrasil’s new slot.Brazil Bomba is based around the carnival in Rio de Janeiro. This multi-day festival is called the biggest show on earth, and 2 million+ people throng the streets. Brazil Bomba taps into the spirit but is more laid back feel than extravagant. Still, we get one of those feathered dancers on the side of the screen celebrating wins and nuking symbols from time to time. If you can’t see her, you are probably in portrait mode on a mobile. Turn it to landscape and there we go. She stands beside the game area which is made up of 8 reels and 6 rows. We also get plenty of fireworks and beach action so the atmosphere is nicely warm and exotic.Being Yggdrasil's first ever cluster pays slot, winning clusters are formed by 6 or more matching icons. Winning symbols can touch horizontally, vertically, and even diagonally, which is a little unorthodox. It is also possible for any pay symbol to completely stack the reels. Fill the screen with 48 red samba drum symbol, and you will earn a tidy 1,000 times the stake making it the highest paying symbol. The rest, in descending order, are what appears to be yellow, pink, purple, green, and blue drums or fire crackers boxes. The low pays are red, yellow, pink and purple diamond shapes. The paytable is worth a look. It lists every single symbol combination from 6 – 48 and how much they pay according to your current bet size. There are reams of figures and scrolling through them is like how Neo sees the Matrix.Speaking of figures, those that power Brazil Bomba are respectable. First up is an RTP of 96.3%, along with an encouraging hit rate of 22.81%. Volatility is not as high as some recently released slots with similar reel setups but is still capable of intense gaming with a 8.5/10 medium-high setting. A good range of betting options is on hand. Though the highest of rollers might feel left out by stakes that start at 10 p/c and go as high as $/€50. One thing that does not appear is wild symbols. It is a little surprising with how heavily they feature in other similar styled games - grid slots for instance. That might be a little disappointing at first, but Brazil Bomba’s features manage to make do just fine without one.Brazil Bomba (Yggdrasil Gaming): FeaturesFree spins feature in play with Bomb feature activatedBrazil Bomba doesn’t exactly overflow with features the way the Rio Carnival does. But what it does have works well. The first to be aware of is Dropdown Wins - when a winning cluster is formed, it is removed from the reels to let a fresh batch of symbols fall into place which can lead to more winners. The Dropdown Win feature repeats until no more clusters appear.Well, it wouldn’t be a bomba without a bomb showing up somewhere. The Bomb Symbol can land anywhere during the base and bonus games. When it activates, it explodes in a star formation removing up to 16 symbols to let new ones fall into place. It does not remove free spin symbols or other bomb symbols, though only one bomb symbol can explode per Dropdown.Working hand in hand with Dropdowns is the Multiplier. Every Dropdown win or Bomb feature activates the multiplier for the following Dropdown and adds +1 each time. It keeps increasing while Bombs or Dropdown wins occur. During the base game, it resets back to normal at the start of each new spin.The final symbol in the game is the scatter. When 3, 4, 5, or 6 of these are in view, they award 5, 10, 15, or 20 Free Spins respectively. The major bonus during free spins is that the multiplier does not reset but continues to climb ever higher as more wins occur.Brazil Bomba (Yggdrasil Gaming): VerdictFor a slot based on the Rio Carnival, Yggdrasil could have gone completely wild, but the end result more moderate. This goes for graphics, effects, and also for features and mechanics. It’s not as volatile as many recent grid slots which rely on two or more features coming together for big hits. Brazil Bomba is simpler and not so all or nothing as a game like Dragonfall for example. It's also not as sophisticated or refined as those grid slots coming from Play'n GO.With Brazil Bomba, you just need to be concerned about one thing – landing free spins and letting the multiplier do the rest. Not saying that is easy, it’s just less reliant on several moving parts. It is good to know that when free spins happen, the game’s potential can be worth the wait. On max bet, the default maximum win is 8,975.6 times the stake. Not the most rewarding slot perhaps, but certainly rewarding all the same.To sum up, Brazil Bomba is not the carnivalistic mega volatile extravaganza or feature-rich game it could have been. But that’s not necessarily a bad thing. It offers a more straight forward slot experience with pleasing effects and features, and a solid potential backing it all up. The base game can dish up high-value clusters which are made even more desirable by the Multiplier. Or, score a good roll during free spins and you’ll feel like dancing samba at the Copacabana Palace. Overall, it's not a bad first cluster pays slot yet it could have been better given the competition that is out there.

review: Break Da Bank Again 4Tune Reels: Slot OverviewNot being bank robbers, we'll have to presume that there's a compulsion, once someone's knocked over one bank, to repeat the action all over again? At least, this appears to be the thinking behind the classic Break Da Bank slot series from casino games maker Games Global (formerly known as Microgaming), which has gone through numerous iterations since it was released. These days Games Global doesn't awaken from its slumber to release a slot very often, and when it does, it's not unusual for them to revisit past glories. So it is with Break Da Bank Again 4Tune Reels, a reworking of the classic slot Break Da Bank Again, this time with 4 reel sets working in unison at the same time.Released all the way back in 2008, the original Break Da Bank Again is getting on in years now and was one of those old-school slots where its gaming grid took up the bulk of the view. Strange then to see 4 grids all at once, taking up less of the screen than before. If you like richly detailed visuals in a modern slot to help set a thematic mood, then Break Da Bank Again 4Tune Reels might disappoint because its plain purple background and minimal (non-symbol) banking references don't conjure up much of an atmosphere. Nit-picking, of course, since Break Da Bank Again 4Tune Reels is part of a long, ongoing range of slots that's as much about keeping the past alive as anything else. In that regard, it's probably a success because Break Da Bank Again 4Tune Reels provides a steady retro-infused stream of events.Break Da Bank Again 4Tune Reels slot - base gameThe effect of the 4Tune mechanic has had an effect on the bet levels, which vary from 36 p/c to $/€90, as each of the 5x3 grid matrices has 9 fixed paylines for landing winning combinations on. The game is medium volatile and can be found with RTP values of 95.43%, 94.03%, or the lowest is 92.05%. There aren't a lot of stand-out statistics, but what may catch your eye is a hit rate, according to the game info of 63.26%, which is extraordinary if correct. Doesn't mean players are going to clean the game out, but is worth a mention.Winning combinations are 3 to 5 OAK in length, and there are ten regular pay symbols landing across the board. These are 10 through A card ranks as the lower value symbols and a stack of coins, a cheque, a bundle of banknotes, gold bars, and a chunky gemstone as the highs. The reward for hitting a 5 low pay symbol win is approximately 1.39x to 2.5x, or for a 5 premium symbol win, 5.56x to 41.67x the bet. Wilds are worth even more, maxing out at 208.33x the bet for a 5 wild winning line, or they can be used to substitute any pay symbol. In addition, wild wins are multiplied by x5 in the base game, increasing to x25 in free spins.Break Da Bank Again 4Tune Reels: Slot FeaturesBreak Da Bank Again 4Tune Reels slot - paytable based on a €1.08 betAside from the extra number of game grids, there's nothing else really new to discover in Break Da Bank Again 4Tune Reels. Its features remain the multiplying wild bit which was already mentioned, and free spins.Free SpinsBank vault doors are the game's free spins scatter symbol. Landing 3, 4, or 5 of them awards 15, 20, or 25 free spins, respectively. Technically, it is possible to trigger free spins simultaneously across all four slots. During free spins, all wins are multiplied by x5, and landing a scatter symbol awards an additional free spin.Break Da Bank Again 4Tune Reels slot - free spinsBreak Da Bank Again 4Tune Reels: Slot VerdictThese quad reel set slots are really hit or miss. They haven't massively caught on, though studios do come back to the idea every so often to make use of what they have to offer. Their success seems to depend on how much they feel like a cheap trick used to squeeze extra mileage out of a game or whether all those extra screens have been judiciously blended with the features. For instance, take The Dog House Multihold, a game where Pragmatic Play very cleverly incorporated a cloning sticky wild feature which worked perfectly with its four sets of reels during the bonus round. Break Da Bank Again 4Tune Reels, by contrast, just feels like four Break Da Bank Again slots playing at the same time. And strangely, this does not necessarily translate into 4 times the fun.One reason why is that landing at least three scatters and triggering free spins on one grid from the base game only means just one grid is active in the bonus round. Triggering free spins on more than one set of reels at the same time may not be an easy task, but it might be more fun when it does happen. The selling point here appears to be that having 4 grids translates to '4x the chance to trigger free spins and win big.' Although, the wins aren't super big. Whilst it might be possible to win up to 4,300 times the bet, the exposure limit means when players bet at the highest stake level this figure is reduced to 1,098.22xAll in all, Break Da Bank Again 4Tune Reels performed pretty much as expected, with no major 'what the' moments. If the thought of four Break Da Bank Agains functioning at the same time sounds neat, then great; otherwise, this'll probably fail to impress much.

title: Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold
structured_summary: Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold combines Irish leprechaun charm with a fishing theme for a unique slot experience. The reviewer praises it as a bigger, more detailed upgrade that appeals strongly to fans of both Irish and fishing slots. Visually richer than its predecessors, it offers a lively underwater setting paired with an energetic Celtic rock soundtrack.
review: Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold: Slot OverviewWhen making the previous game, Fishin' Pots of Gold, it was as if one side of Gameburger Studios wanted a fishing slot, and the other side wanted leprechauns, so they compromised by mashing both tropes together. Now we've got Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold, a slot that takes much of what was on offer in games like 9 Pots of Gold and Fishin' Pots of Gold, then bigs them up. The result is a slot which offers Cash Symbol collects, jackpots, free spins with an expanded grid, an Accumulation Trail with Cash Multipliers, Upsizer, and a feature buy.Not only is Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold bigger, it arguably looks better than the two previous games, with more details to absorb. Especially more so than 9 Pots of Gold, which was essentially 9 Masks of Fire with a Celtic cover. There's also plenty of Lucky Lad Flynn, so fans of the happy-go-lucky leprechaun get to celebrate his return. The base game starts out beneath the surface of the sea, where a 5x3 grid hovers between a flotilla of boats, fish, weeds, and the sea bed. Jigging its way over the top is a boisterous rock track made in the style of Dropkick Murphys with distorted guitar and Celtic touches, energising the proceedings.Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold slot - base gameFishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold is available in a variety of RTP configurations topping out at 96.05% and bottoming out at 86.73%, depending on the market. Volatility has been marked as 'Very High', while the hit rate is 19.48% on the highest RTP model. Players can bait up and cast off on any device, where stakes of 20 p/c to $/€25 may be locked in.Initially, the grid has 10 paylines to land winning combinations of three to five of a kind across. The pay symbols split the two themes between them as well. The low pays have Celtic-ish patterns adorning the 10-A card royals, whereas the high pays are all fishing-related items, such as floats, hooks, anchors, and boats. Winning lines pay 10x the bet for landing five royals or 50-200x the bet for five of the premium symbols. The fish Cash Symbols also payout up to 20x the bet for five of a kind landing across a payline.Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold: Slot FeaturesFishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold slot - free spinsA couple of features keep the base game moving along, such as the Collect feature and the Fish Flurry. Free spins have the potential to take players closer to the end of the rainbow and can be augmented by the Upsizer feature if they are triggered naturally.Collect FeatureLucky Lad Flynn dressed in fishing garb is the Collect Symbol which lands on the last reel in the base game or all reels during free spins. Not only is the Collect Symbol wild, but it also collects Cash Symbols or Jackpot Symbols if any are in view when it lands. Cash symbols are worth up to 1,000x, while the jackpots pay 15x, 50x, 750x, or 7,500x the bet when the Mini, Minor, Major, or Mega symbols are hauled in, respectively.Fish FlurryThe Fish Flurry can activate on non-winning spins when a Collect Symbol lands. When it does, 1 to 5 Cash Symbols are added to the reels to be collected.Free SpinsWhen 3, 4, or 5 scatters symbols are in view, players win 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. If triggered naturally, players may have the chance of paying extra via the Upsizer feature to activate a starting cash multiplier of x2, x3, x5, or x10.When free spins are active, the reels expand to 5 rows high, and 10 paylines are added. An Accumulation Trail is also added. The Accumulation Trail collects each Collect Symbol that lands on a free spin. When 3, 6, 9, or 12 are collected, the Cash Symbol multiplier becomes x2, x3, x5, and x10. This multiplier is applied to wins from Cash Symbol collects only. In addition, every 3 Collect Symbols collected (up to 12) awards an extra +5 free spins.Feature BuyIf on the lower right side of the screen the Feature Buy is displayed, clicking it gives players three free spins buy options. These are 10, 15, or 20 free spins for 75x, 120x, or 150x the bet, respectively. Keep in mind that when buying free spins, the Upsizer menu will not be there.Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold slot - bonus buy optionsFishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold: Slot VerdictWhile reviewing Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold, we got to wondering; so far, Gameburger Studios has slung out 9 Pots of Gold, Fishin' Pots of Gold, and now Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold. Where could they go next? At a guess… Maybe hammer in some Ra-style expanding fish symbols to make Book of Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold? After that, how about Book of Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold Megaways? The mind reels at the possibilities.Reeling in the knee-slappers for a bit, if you've played an Irish-themed game and a fishin' slot, then the amalgamation of the two runs pretty much how you'd expect it. The jolly Irishness is accentuated by the sunny day on the water effect to create an experience that is surely about as positive as it gets for players drawn to this sort of thing. The Mega jackpot is quite high for this kind of game, and the 1,000x fish symbol landed teasingly often during the review. Never at the same time as the Money Collect symbol, but it's there for lucky anglers to potentially reel in. Should the x10 multiplier be active when pulling in the top fish, it would be worth a cool 10,000x on its own, while max exposure equates to 22,826x the bet. By all accounts, this is definitely a BIGGER game than that which preceded it.To sum up, if you like slots featuring fishing and leprechauns, the merging of the two things in Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold is pretty much the acme of gaming. It is rather targeted, as Irish and Fishing slots do have an intrinsic polarising effect - either you like them, or you don't. If you do, the Irish/fishing mashup in Fishin' BIGGER Pots Of Gold presents an unmissable fusion.

title: Mad Blast
structured_summary: Mad Blast features a sci-fi, mechanical workshop theme centered around the Mad Tinkerer and robotic elements. The game offers cascading wins, a Total Multiplier that can reach x2,048, Multiplier Boost and Extra Life symbols, free spins with multiplier resets, and a unique Multiplier Strike Out feature. The reviewer finds Mad Blast a solid, well-crafted scatter-paying slot that innovates subtly but largely follows existing trends. Its aesthetics combine a tame workshop setting with engaging sci-fi visuals and fitting mechanical audio cues enhancing the experience.
review: Mad Blast: Slot OverviewThanks in large part to games like Sweet Bonanza and Gates of Olympus, scatter-paying slots have exploded in popularity, with every other studio seeming to get in on the action. Push Gaming is a developer that has dropped some doozies when it comes to cluster paying slots, Fire Hopper and Jammin' Jars, for instance, but it hasn't dominated to the same extent with scatter pays. Rat King was good, Jaguar Drop less so. Push Gaming is back at it in Mad Blast, this time combining scatter-paying combinations with a doubling-up win multiplier that, yes, is a lot like the one used in Yggdrasil Gaming and partners' DoubleMax slots.Mad Blast takes place in the workshop of an entity known as the Mad Tinkerer, though their working area seems pretty tame. There's a hammer on the wall and pliers, but it seems a drab place to conduct experiments. Perhaps the Mad Tinkerer channels all the creative juices into their creations and leaves the workshop spare to cut down on distractions. When free spins trigger, a robot trundles into the background, so in general, the sci-fi, mechanical theme carries the game quite well.Mad Blast slot - base gamePlayed on a 5x6 gaming area, wins in Mad Blast are created when at least 8 matching pay symbols land anywhere on the grid. Winning combinations trigger a cascade mechanism and a multiplier feature. Push Gaming has set the game's volatility to a high setting, and the most preferable RTP value is the 96.34% version. Base stakes range from 10 c to $/€100, though the Push Bet doubles the base bet when actuated, increasing the chance of winning free spins.Five boxes, coloured blue, purple, green, pink, and yellow, are Mad Blast's low pays, while its highs are 4 robotic symbols. Winning combinations of 8-9 in size pay 0.3 to 10 times the stake, and the largest 12+ scatter wins award 2 to 50 times the bet. Wild symbols are not part of Mad Blast in any phase.Mad Blast: Slot FeaturesMad Blast slot - free spinsMad Blast operates a cascading wins system, which removes winning symbols, causing a symbol drop to fill the vacated spaces. As well as this is a Total Multiplier, Multiplier Boost symbols, Extra Life symbols, free spins, Multiplier Strike Out and bonus buys.Total Multiplier & Multiplier Boost SymbolThe total multiplier is always present, and it applies to each winning combination. For each winning cascade, the Total Multiplier doubles in value, but it resets after a non-winning cascade. In the base game, the Total Multiplier starts at x1 and can go as high as x2,048. The Multiplier Boost symbol is available in the base game and in free spins. It activates with any winning combination, increasing the Total Multiplier by the number of steps displayed on the symbol. The Multiplier Boost symbol can have step values of 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5.Extra Life SymbolThe Extra Life symbol is also available in the base game and in free spins. It activates on a non-winning cascade, removing all paying symbols from the reels, except scatters, Multiplier Boosts, and all instances of the most common paying symbol. It will leave the highest-paying symbol if more than one symbol type is equally common.Free SpinsHitting 3 scatters in the base game awards 8 free spins with a starting Total Multiplier of x2, Landing 4 scatters in the base game awards 10 free spins with a starting Total Multiplier of x4, while 5 triggering scatters in the base game awards 12 free spins with a starting Total Multiplier of x8. The Total Multiplier resets to the lowest possible value for the start of a new free spin, and each scatter landing in the feature awards +1 free spin.Multiplier Strike OutThis feature is only available during free spins. After 3 consecutive winning cascades, the Multiplier Strike Out feature triggers, and the last active Total Multiplier step is deleted from the Total Multiplier list. It cannot delete the 2,048x.Bonus BuyPlayers are able to buy free spins with an x2 initial multiplier for 150x the bet or free spins with an x8 initial multiplier for 750x the bet.Mad Blast slot - free spinsMad Blast: Slot VerdictPush Gaming is a name synonymous with wild innovation; however, of late, the studio seems to have cooled in this regard. Mad Blast has been billed as a 'one-of-a-kind experience', yet developer Bang Bang Games might beg to differ since it's the maker behind The Runemakers DoubleMax, a scatter pays meets DoubleMax slot. Push Gaming might counter that argument by citing features such as the Multiplier Strike Out, and fair enough. But on the whole, Mad Blast feels like further evidence of Push Gaming's transition from bold trendsetter to follower of fashion.For all that, Mad Blast is a good scatter-paying slot. It has been made to a high standard, and the innovations or changes, shall we say, while perhaps subtle on paper, are able to fizz and pop in practice. It might cause consternation amongst DoubleMax fans to know the Total Multiplier in the bonus round does not persist between free spins but returns to its lowest possible value - depending on how many scatters triggered the feature. However, doing things this way meant the number of winning combinations seemed to be fairly plentiful, given that they have more room to manoeuvre instead of getting stuck at a higher multiplier level and being hit with dead free spins, so to speak. The Multiplier Strike Out is a clever idea, as well, and being able to skip one or more Total Multiplier levels is useful. As is the Multiplier Boost symbol.An attractive 10,000x win cap rounds the game off, and while it seems unlikely Mad Blast will revolutionize the scatter-pays or double win multiplier space the way other certain Push Gaming slots have done for their genres, this is undoubtedly a well-built release even if it 'borrows' one or two ideas from elsewhere.

title: Toro 7s
structured_summary: Toro 7s is a retro-style slot themed around a North American road trip to Las Vegas, concluding ELK Studios' Wild Toro World Tour. The game features Nudging Wilds, free spins, a Lucky Sevens bonus, and five X-iter modes for varied gameplay and added excitement. The reviewer finds it a solid classic series entry with enjoyable bonus modes but notes the low hit rate and extra cost for top features may deter some players. Aesthetically, it offers a glitzy yet slightly disjointed Vegas vibe with a powerful rock stadium soundtrack enhancing the experience.
review: Toro 7s: Slot OverviewToro 7s from ELK Studios is the third and final stop on their Wild Toro World Tour, bringing to a close the studio's three-slot release celebrating 5 years of Wild Toro. Stop number one was sunny Spain for Wild Toro 2, before heading to Egypt for some Toro inspired 'book' action in Book of Toro, before landing in one of the world's major gambling hubs, Las Vegas for Toro 7s. Not only is Toro 7s part of the Wild Toro World Tour, but it also fits into the ELK Classic Series of slots, offering compact, retro-style gaming, packing plenty of modern surprises – with a Toro twist.It's been some time since we've seen a new Classic Series slot from ELK, the last one being Knockout Diamonds, dropping about a year ago. Toro 7s brought back memories of a few of them, like Win Win and Ivanhoe, while its closest relation, at least aesthetically, has to be Route 777. Like that one, Toro 7s is a North American highway odyssey, on a road trip to Las Vegas, Nevada by convertible or motorbike. The game has plenty of open-top spirit, but it's arguably not as freewheeling as Route 777 was, not as strong on the desert atmosphere. The soundtrack, excellent as ever from ELK, has a big rock stadium feel, compared to the one in Route 777, which felt like a bar fight was about to break out at any moment.The classic gaming is available to play on any device from 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin. Stats are classic ELK too, meaning a highly volatile math model churning out an RTP figure of 95%. As well as regular mode gambling, there is the X-iter menu offering 5 different ways of playing Toro 7s, each more potent and expensive the higher you move up the list.While the features are extensive, at its core Toro 7s is indeed classic gaming occurring on a 3-reel, 3-row reelset with 17 connecting paylines. Symbols are old school, too, where the lower values include cherries, oranges, plums, and Bars worth 0.5 to 2.5x the bet, while high pays are green, blue, and red 7s worth 3.5 to 10x your stake. Two wilds appear in the game, a Matador on reel 2 and Toro on reel 3. Both replace any paying symbol to complete wins and trigger certain extra effects.Toro 7s: Slot FeaturesELK has wedged a surprising number of features into Toro 7s for a game that looks simple at first glance. As well as Nudging Wilds are free spins, a Lucky Sevens bonus game, and five X-iter game modes.Nudging WildsWhen the Matador wild symbol lands, it triggers the Nudging Respins feature. The Matador awards respins in which he moves down a position on each respin until he falls out of view. Toro wilds come with x5 multipliers and also trigger respins when they land until they fall off the grid. If Toro and the Matador land at the same time, Toro locks in position until the Matador is nudged out of view, then he begins his nudging respins.Free SpinsLanding 3 scatter symbols anywhere in view awards 10 free spins. During these regular free spins, the key change is all wins are multiplied by x5.Lucky SevensIf 3 scatter symbols land during free spins, they trigger the Lucky Sevens bonus game. Here you want to collect green 7s on reel 1, blue 7s on reel 2, and red 7s on reel 3. Doing so advances you through the Lucky Sevens paytable. Here, 3 spins are awarded, and any line win or landing the right seven symbol on its designated reel reset spins back to 3. Collecting 5 of each coloured 7 symbol awards the game's 10,000x maximum payout.X-iterClicking the X-iter button, which is essentially a range of feature buy options, on the left side of the reels activates bonus mode, displaying five options along the bottom of the screen and their associated cost. Worth noting is that all X-iter game modes have the same return figure as the regular mode's value of 95%:Chili Spin – 5x the bet for 1 high volatility spin where the only pay symbols are cherries or sevens.Nudging Respins – 10x the bet for 1 spin with a guaranteed Matador or Toro.Nudging Chili Respins – 25x the bet for 1 Chili Spin plus a guaranteed Matador or Toro.Bonus – 100x the bet to guarantee access to free spins.Super Chili Bonus – 500x the bet to access a high volatility round of Chili free spins where the multiplier increases by one on every spin, respin nudge, or Lucky Sevens feature spin.Toro 7s: Slot VerdictPlayers might be in one of gambling's heartlands, but they're a long way from Toro and the Matador's home turf, which was a bit unsettling. There's less of a Spanish flavour making Toro 7s feel a bit unfamiliar at first. It doesn't help that the background imagery looks like a derelict patch of ground on the outskirts of a city, while the jumbotron above the game grid blasts a palm-lined ride into Las Vegas. It sort of comes together, sort of doesn't. Let's just say the slight confusion adds to the Toro mystique and just go with it.Gaming wise, Toro 7s is solidly back on ELK Classic Series ground which in itself might be enough to separate the keen from the disinterested. As far as these sorts of games go, Toro 7s is a good one though being so close to Route 777 dilutes the effect. If Route 777 was like free riding through the desert on a beat-up old chopper staying at dive motels, rewriting the rules, Toro 7s is like Vegas after the conglomerates moved in. Glitzier, more comfortable, though lacking the untamed allure of the good old days.Actually playing Toro 7s was a lot more exciting when the Bonus modes were activated. The low hit rate and comparatively lengthy wait between features made regular mode harder work by comparison. It's a shame Toro doesn't chase the Matador across the grid at any stage because the amusing interplay is gone. Also, the most fun came from Chili spins where only cherries or 7s are used. Since this is only possible from the X-iter menu, having to pay extra may rub some players up the wrong way. The RTP remains the same in all cases, but as always, the 500x Super Bonus costs a hefty chunk of change to trigger though it was by far the most thrilling way of tackling Toro 7s. However you manage it, the most you can win amounts to 10,000 times your stake.And so concludes The Wild Toro World Tour, which proved to be hugely entertaining on the whole. ELK has managed to marry strong aspects of classical gaming throughout the trilogy with white-hot modern features. There's loads of good stuff for players to discover on the World Tour, though, in Toro 7s, it'll help if you're partial to old school gambling and don't mind upping the ante to access the best it has to offer.

title: Immortal Romance Vein of Gold
structured_summary: Immortal Romance Vein of Gold is a vampire-themed slot continuing the undead romance saga with a fiery red and gold color scheme. It features a 6x4 grid, Collect symbols, respins, multiple jackpots, bonus multipliers, free spins, and a Vein of Gold bonus round with bonus buy options. The reviewer finds it a fairly standard cash collect game that fails to innovate, feeling like a missed opportunity to fully leverage the Immortal Romance brand. Visually, the game uses bold red, yellow, and purple tones with decent but unremarkable presentation and audio.
review: Immortal Romance Vein of Gold: Slot OverviewBack when they were known as Microgaming, and some might say still relevant, software provider Games Global released what would become one of the gold-standard vampire slots on the market in the form of Immortal Romance. What could have ended up a cheesy Twilight on the reels event turned out to be a gripping tale of vampiric romance. Many moons later, partner Stormcraft Studios crafted Immortal Romance 2, which, while decent enough, failed to fully recapture the magic that made the original so special. If, at first, you don't succeed, then try, try again, and Stormcraft Studios has returned to the loved-up undead to design Immortal Romance Vein of Gold.The four characters from IR2 make a return appearance for Immortal Romance Vein of Gold, though much actual romance is a little lacking. That could be a good or bad thing. A blazing red background has been placed to spruce up the base game, switching to yellow tones for the Vein of Gold bonus and purple colourations during free spins. The presentation is okay, but nothing special, a foreshadowing of the game to come.Immortal Romance Vein of Gold slot - base gameA golden-framed 6x4 grid is Immortal Romance Vein of Gold's active gaming area. It uses a ways system to create winning combinations, and there are 4,096 of them. The game is highly volatile, and it comes with three RTP configurations, the highest of which is 96%. Players may wager 20 c to $/€50 per spin and buy bonus round entrance if they'd like.Blood red J-A card ranks are followed by a fountain, a gate, a book, and 4 character symbols as Immortal Romance Vein of Gold's pay symbols. The Jack to gate symbols are worth 1 to 1.4 times the bet for 6-of-a-kind, while the rest pay 2 to 5 times the bet when landing 6 OAK. Wilds appear on all reels except the leftmost in the base game and all reels 2, 3, and 4 in free spins. Wilds substitute all symbols except scatters, Cash, or Collect.Immortal Romance Vein of Gold: Slot FeaturesImmortal Romance Vein of Gold slot - Vein of Gold featureThere is a lot of text in this section, and the features boil down to a Collect feature, respins, Jackpot prizes, a Bonus Multiplier, a couple of bonus rounds, and bonus buys.Collect Feature & RespinsImmortal Romance Vein of Gold has Collect symbols and Cash symbols. Collect symbols land on the leftmost and rightmost reel, and when they hit alongside Cash symbols, the values from all Cash symbols are awarded. Landing a Collect symbol but no Cash symbols or a bonus trigger awards 1 respin. The leftmost and rightmost reels lock while reels 2-4 respin to land Cash symbols or blank positions. At least one Cash symbol is guaranteed to land.Rising Rewards JackpotLanding a Cash symbol without Collect symbols accumulates tokens in the base game. When tokens are accumulated, they increase at least one Jackpot value. Collecting tokens also grants a chance of triggering the Jackpot feature in the base game, where it is possible to win Cash prizes and Jackpots - at least one Jackpot is awarded. The Jackpot values are 5x-25x for the Mini, 10x-50x for the Minor, 100x-250x for the Major, and 1,000x-2,500x for the Mega.Rising Rewards MultiplierThe Bonus Multiplier is displayed in a meter, and it can be increased in the base game. This multiplier applies to all wins in the free spins and Vein of Gold rounds. Its value increases by 0.5x when 2 scatters land in the base game without triggering the Bonus Choice - up to a maximum of x5. It resets to x1 after free spins or Vein of Gold is complete, but it may randomly increase by 0.5x to 1x when returning to the base game.Bonus FeaturesLanding 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatters awards 8 free spins or 2 Vein of Gold spins, 12 free spins or 3 Vein of Gold spins, 20 free spins or 5 Vein of Gold spins, or 30 free spins or 7 Vein of Gold spins, respectively. Players choose either free spins or Vein of Gold spins when triggered.Free Spins - An x2, x3, or x5 multiplier is randomly awarded for each wild in a winning way. Each wild multiplier multiplies the win on that way, and the Bonus Multiplier multiplies the total win of each spin. Retriggering the feature occurs when 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatter hits to award +5, +8, +12, +20 or +30 free spins, respectively. Oddly, the 4 highest-paying symbols do not appear in free spins.Vein of Gold - During this feature, regular pay symbols do not land, but a Collect symbol is guaranteed to hit on every spin to collect any Cash symbols, and each spin guarantees a win. Collect Retrigger symbols and Retrigger symbols are also present on the reels. The Collect Retrigger awards all Cash symbols and awards +1 spin, while the Retrigger symbol awards +1 free spin only. Cash symbols of up to 100x the bet may land during the feature, and the Bonus Multiplier multipliers the total win of each spin.Feature BuyPlayers are able to buy instant access to the Bonus Choice triggered by 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatters, costing 30x, 50x, 80x, or 120x the bet, respectively.Immortal Romance Vein of Gold slot - free spinsImmortal Romance Vein of Gold: Slot VerdictIt's fairly safe to say that if Immortal Romance 2 didn't get your blood pumping, neither will Immortal Romance Vein of Gold. Games Global and its buddies have been making these sorts of slots for years now, and it shows. Despite possessing impeccable slot pedigree, Immortal Romance Vein of Gold is a run-of-the-mill Cash collect game with Jackpots and a couple of bonus rounds tacked on. It seems to be a common formula. For example, a similarly featured slot from Fortune Factory Studios called Mask of Amun was reviewed mid-ish 2022, and Immortal Romance Vein of Gold hasn't really progressed much, if anything, since then.In other words, collecting Cash symbols and tokens keeps the base game chugging along as users keep their fingers crossed enough scatters land to instigate the Bonus Choice. Tough choice? Maybe. Vein of Gold spins might match players who can't get enough collecting in their lives; free spins drop wild multipliers to boost wins. Both benefit from the Bonus Multiplier, which can be grown in the base game, and Jackpot values are displayed as a motivator throughout. Jackpots must be grown in the main game to reach their full, if limited, potential, which is a requirement that may delight some gamblers as much as it repels others. Grown to full capacity or not, the Mega Jackpot isn't enormous, though Immortal Romance Vein of Gold's full winning potential of 5,500x is preferable to being drained of fluids by a Nosferatu type.Still, it's hard not to feel like Immortal Romance Vein of Gold is a bit of a waste of the Immortal Romance IP, used as it is as a vehicle for a bunch of regular, arguably overdone features. Ah well, the Games Global crew does like these sorts of extras, so here's another one like-minded enthusiasts might want to sink their fangs into.

title: Gems Inferno Megaways
structured_summary: Gems Inferno Megaways is a gem-themed slot by Red Tiger featuring a mystical underground forge setting. The game includes cascading wins, gem sacks, and a hold & respin bonus round with gem multipliers up to 2,000x. The reviewer finds it lightweight and simple, with below-average max win potential of 2,553x, appealing mainly to casual players. Visually, it looks decent but lacks Red Tiger’s usual detailed polish, with standard audio and modest design elements.
review: Gems Inferno Megaways: Slot OverviewGems, gems, gems, stones so shiny they are worth a stack of change. Some of them are, at least, like sizable diamonds, rubies, emeralds and so forth. Kinda weird when you think about it since they're basically just pretty rocks, but what can you do? Due to their alluring appearance and link to monetary value, gems are regular companions when playing online slots, too, and here's another one for mineralogists to savour. Gems Inferno Megaways comes courtesy of software provider Red Tiger and possesses a relatively low tier hold 'n win round as its main feature.Is Gems Inferno Megaways held in the place where gems are made? Let's suspend disbelief for a moment and pretend valuable rocks are crafted here, deep underground, in a forge by fantastical creatures, forever striving to create the ideal combination of atoms. A rock so close to perfection it mesmerises anyone who beholds its glittering splendour. Oh, dear. It's not always a great sign when the mind wanders on such a tangent at the start of an online slot review. Gems Inferno Megaways triggered such a response, probably because a cursory test run of how it functioned failed to sink its hooks in very deeply. It looks okay for the most part, though bits of Gems Inferno Megaways, like its prize value display, came across as a little dinky. As mentioned, Gems Inferno Megaways looks pretty good, but it doesn't have the usual attention to every single little detail thing that Red Tiger slots usually come with. Or do they? Gems Inferno Megaways got us second-guessing now.Gems Inferno Megaways slot - base gameLet's use the cold steel of statistics to anchor ourselves for a bit. Firstly, Gems Inferno Megaways is a medium-high volatile slot, producing two default RTP values, depending on how the game is played. Wager 10 p/c to $/€40 on single spins, and the return value is 95.67%. Alternatively, buy the bonus round for 80 times the bet and the return value shifts to 95.73%. The active gaming area has been constructed using 6 main reels that spin top to bottom, while a 4 symbol bonus reel has been placed up top, spinning in a horizontal manner. The number of symbols landing on the main reels can change, as can ways to win, which maxes out at 117,649 at full capacity.On to the symbol side of Gems Inferno Megaways, where there are quite a few gems dotted amongst them. Not so much the low pay 10 to A card royals, but the high pays include what look like two ring symbols, a necklace, and a crown. Hitting a 6-of-a-kind winning way across the game board pays 0.4 to 0.6 times the bet for the low pays or 0.8 to 1.5 times the bet for the highs. For a game with no multipliers, those are pretty sad values. There is a wild, though, helping complete wins by substituting for any regular pay symbol. Wilds only appear on the top reel. Chain reactions also form after a winning way hits, as well. This pay system removes winning symbols and replaces them with symbols falling down from above.Gems Inferno Megaways: Slot FeaturesGems Inferno Megaways slot - respin featureNow for the full-blown gem symbols, which can land anywhere on the reels. The Magic Gem symbols have values of 1x to 100x; Diamonds are worth 10x the bet, Red Diamonds are worth 50x the bet, Pink Diamonds are 250x the bet, while the Blue Diamond is the biggest at 2,000x the bet. Only one Pink Diamond and only one Blue Diamond can land on a single spin or a single bonus round execution. The prize on Magic Gems is shown as a monetary value, while all others display a multiplier.Gem SackGem sack scatters may land on the top reel. When a gem sack hits, it randomly places up to 3 gem scatters of any kind in random grid positions.Gemmed!Gemmed! is triggered when at least 6 gems of any kind land. It is a hold & respin bonus round, which starts with 3 respins and all triggering gems locked in place. During the feature, any new gems that land are also locked in place on the reels while resetting the spin counter to 3. Gem sacks may land during the round, but they do not lock in place like gem symbols. Gemmed! ends when the respins have been used or the whole reel set is filled with gems. Then the value of all prizes in view is awarded.Gems Inferno Megaways slot - respin featureGems Inferno Megaways: Slot VerdictReviewing Gems Inferno Megaways was like the slot equivalent of patronising an expensively pretentious restaurant which serves tiny morsels of neatly arranged food, where after hovering up the dish in 1 or 2 bites, the overriding reaction is, 'Is that it?'
