title: Pray For Three
structured_summary: Pray for Three immerses players in a devilish underworld tale featuring two fallen sisters ruling the damned. The game offers 3,125 ways to win, cascading reels, a Wheel of Sin multiplier feature, and three escalating free spin bonuses. The reviewer finds it a creatively presented, multiplier-driven slot that, while not groundbreaking, is a compelling addition to Hacksaw Gaming's lineup. Its monochrome, early cartoon style visuals paired with a jazzy cabaret soundtrack enhance the naughty yet playful atmosphere.
review: Pray for Three: Slot OverviewThe online gambling landscape is dotted with repeated tales of adventurers scouring Ancient Egypt for the umpteenth time, jokers getting up to mischief, or pirates pirating; then there are stories like the one behind Hacksaw Gaming's slot Pray for Three. This game tells of two fallen sisters, Scary Mary and Morbid Magda, who have been cast down from heaven for their sins, and have embraced the inferno, so instead of praying for salvation to get them out of fiery damnation, these diabolical sisters are making the most of the situation by looking for ways to rule the damned…Pray for Three is a black-and-white return to the underworld of SixSixSix, but instead of Balthazar and Beelzebub joining players on their journey, here they bump into the two aforementioned sisters who somehow manage to look both innocent and sinister at the same time. Like its predecessor, splashes of cyan brighten up the monochrome decor, and the game retains the same early animated cartoon vibe as the previous slot. At the same time, a plinky/jazz cabaret soundtrack makes the ideal fit for furthering the little bit naughty, a little bit nice, but mainly naughty, vibe.Pray For Three slot - base gameFor a change, Hacksaw Gaming has used a ways to win pay system in Pray for Three, meaning that on the 5x5 grid, there are no less than 3,125 ways to win, with all combinations starting from the leftmost reel. Winning symbols are removed, causing new and remaining symbols to cascade downwards to replace them, providing another chance to win, with cascades repeating like this until no new win is created. The game's medium-high volatile math model leads to a maximum RTP of 96.33%, and players are able to wager 10 c to $/€100 per spin.Nails, a candle, a whip, an hourglass, and a tombstone are Pray for Three's lower-paying greyed-out symbols, awarding 0.3x the bet for a five-of-a-kind winning combination. Then there's a cup, a bird, a snake, what might be a lamb, and a bleeding-eyed something as the high pay symbols, awarding up to 0.4x to 4x the bet. Wilds may appear on any reel, substituting all of the regular paying symbols, and are worth 5x the bet when landing a line of five wilds.Pray for Three: Slot FeaturesPray For Three slot - free spinsTo start with, Pray for Three has a Total Win Bar that collects all wins during a spin and displays the total at the top of the grid. It also has a Wheel of Sin, three bonus rounds - Wicked Ways, Living on a Prayer, and Flames of Fortune, as well as feature buys.Wheel of SinThe Wheel of Sin also sits outside the reels, and when activated, up to three sections reveal an Adding or a Multiplying value. The first section can have Adding Multipliers of x2 to x333, the second section Adding Multiplier of x2 to x333 or Multiplying Multipliers of x2 to x33, while the third section has only Multiplying Multipliers of x2 to x33. Landing a Prayer Hand or Divine Prayer Hand on the grid during a win activates the Wheel of Sin. A Prayer Hand reveals a number from 1 to 3, indicating how many sections of the wheel will activate, while the Divine Prayer Hand activates all three sections.Wicked Ways BonusLanding 3 FS scatters in the base game triggers this bonus with 10 free spins. The Wicked Ways bonus has the same mechanics as the base game, with an increased chance of landing both types of Prayer Hand symbols and wilds. In all bonus rounds, FS scatters appear on the leftmost, middle, and rightmost reels, where landing 2 or 3 FS scatters awards a further +2 or +4 free spins, respectively.Living on a Prayer BonusActivating this bonus with 10 free spins occurs by landing 4 FS scatters in the base game. This bonus has the same mechanics as Wicked Ways, with an increased chance of landing Divine Prayer Hands. Regular Prayer Hands do not appear.Flames of Fortune BonusThis bonus and 10 free spins are awarded when 5 FS scatters hit in the base game. In addition to having the same mechanics as Wicked Ways, there is a greater chance of landing wilds, and each spin guarantees that one Divine Prayer Hand will land.Bonus BuysActivating BonusHunt FeatureSpins makes each spin 5 times more likely to trigger a bonus game at a cost of 3x per spin. Hail Mary FeatureSpins cost 50x to guarantee a win and a Prayer Hand or Divine Prayer Hand on each spin. Wicked Ways can be bought for 100x the bet or Living on a Prayer for 225x the bet.Pray For Three slot - free spinsPray for Three: Slot VerdictPray for Three might have returned the spirit and the colour palette of SixSixSix, but it's quite a different game in practice. For one thing, Wicked Wheels have been removed, so there are no blue or red '6' symbols leading to cash prizes or free spins. Now, the aim is to land Prayer Hands or, better yet, Divine Prayer Hands at the same time as winning combinations in order to pep the payout with up to three combinable multiplier values - additive and multiplicative. When peering down from a high level, it's not the most original idea Hacksaw Gaming has ever had. Similar things have occurred before in games like Klowns or partner studio Backseat Gaming's slots Roman Bonanza and Pirate Bonanza 2.But, the delivery system has been redesigned, and when combined with a slightly sinister monochrome underworld populated by Scary Mary and Morbid Magda (and if you can make it to Flames of Fortune, the winged character from SixSixSix), Pray for Three becomes a real treat for followers of Hacksaw Gaming's tinderbox style. Speaking of Flames of Fortune, like Reign of Rome or Le Bandit, the studio has again dangled a 'Hidden Epic Bonus' before gamblers to grind their way towards since it cannot be bought. It's a highly desirable feature since every spin lands the coveted Divine Prayer Hand symbol. Even still, both Prayer Hands hit in the lesser bonus rounds, as well as in the base game, so the suspense of watching the Wheel of Sin spin is present in all phases of play.This also means that the game's 13,333x win cap can be hit in all game modes, too, so even outside of the Hidden Epic Bonus, players are kept on their toes. Such is the explosive nature of Hacksaw Gaming slots that rely on the power of multipliers to pop. Pray for Three is another one, mixing a triple-section multiplier wheel with masses of ways to win, which might not be the studio's most cutting-edge piece of work but is nevertheless a neatly constructed, creatively presented slot.

title: Shadow Strike
structured_summary: Shadow Strike is a martial arts-themed slot set in an exotic Asian dojo, immersing players in a kung fu showdown. It features three distinct bonus rounds, Ninja Reels with wild multipliers, and a bonus buy option for high volatility gameplay. The reviewer praises its blend of familiar Hacksaw Gaming mechanics with Backseat Gaming's unique touches, noting its potential for big wins but limited retrigger opportunities. The game boasts serene Asian-inspired visuals and gentle background music, creating a peaceful yet engaging atmosphere.
review: Shadow Strike: Slot OverviewHacksaw Gaming partner Backseat Gaming busts out the 'hi-yahs!' for its martial arts-themed online slot Shadow Strike. Hopefully, you've been brushing up on your kung fu for this one, as it warns players, 'prepare to strike, or be stricken!' We're guessing no one wants to be stricken, and there are numerous ways to at least attempt striking, such as in Shadow Strike's three different bonus rounds or via its clutch of feature buys.Win or lose, Shadow Strike has picked a picturesque place for showdowns to occur. It's set in an exotic Asian spot, where gentle music plinks in the background, and a gaming grid sits nestled within a curved roof structure. We're out in the middle of nature for this one; perhaps quiet solitude is conducive to practising katas or something. A myriad of special features and a connection to Hacksaw Gaming, in general, mean Shadow Strike probably won't stay quiet for long, though. The busier the better, really, from a gambler's point of view.Shadow Strike slot - base gamePlayed on a 5-reel gaming grid, you'll notice that for much of the time, the top two rows are locked, while the main 4-row grid is active. The two outer rows are Ninja Reels, and we'll get to them shortly. Before then, know that Shadow Strike has 14 paylines evaluating wins, and it takes wagers of 10 cents to $/€100 per spin, selectable on the recognisably Hacksaw UI. Five ways to play are available at the bonus buy, as well, while the general volatility is in the medium-high range (4.5 out of 5).The 4 low pay symbols depict 4 kinds of weapons, whereas the high pays show 4 different warrior symbols. Hitting a line of 5 lows awards 2 to 5 times the bet, while 5 of the same warrior symbol pays 7.5 to 20 times the bet. When wilds are in view on the grid, they're able to substitute for all of the regular paying symbols. Since wilds can land on all reels, a line of 5 of them is worth 20 times the stake.Shadow Strike: Slot FeaturesShadow Strike slot - The Secret of the Scroll featureFirst on the extensive list of features, we've got Ninja Reels. Above and below the main reels are 2 extra Ninja Reels. When they are unlocked, Ninja Reels are able to introduce wilds, MultiSplit, and +FS symbols. The other symbols on Ninja Reels are non-paying dead symbols. In the base game, both Ninja Reels are locked at the start of each spin and become unlocked if any of the 3 different bonus symbols land on the main grid.Wild SymbolWhen a wild symbol lands on a Ninja Reel, it creates a new wild symbol in a random position on the corresponding main reel. Wild symbols that land or are created on the main grid have a chance of getting a multiplier of x2 to x50. If more than one wild symbol is part of the same winning combination, the multiplier values are added before being applied.MultiSplit SymbolThese symbols land only on a Ninja Reel displaying a multiplier of x2 to x50. When a MultiSplit appears, it multiplies the multiplier value of all wild symbols on its corresponding reel on the main grid. If a MultiSplit passes over a wild that does not have a multiplier value, the MultiSplit's multiplier value is added to the wild.The Mysteries of the Dojo Bonus GamePlayers get 10, 12, or 14 free Mysteries of the Dojo free spins by landing 3, 4, or 5 Dojo Bonus scatters in the base game, respectively. During this bonus, both Ninja Reels are unlocked on every spin. Wild symbols that land or are created on the main grid remain sticky. Landing a +FS symbol on a Ninja Reels grants +1-3 free spins per symbol.The Secrets of the Scroll Bonus GameHitting 3, 4, or 5 Scroll scatters in the base game awards 10, 12, or 14 free spins as part of this feature, respectively. Both Ninja Reels are unlocked for the entirety as well, but here, wilds on the main grid expand to become full reel wilds. landing a +FS symbol on a Ninja Reels grants +1-3 free spins per symbol.The Wisdom of the Koi Bonus GameTriggered by landing 3 Koi scatter symbols in the base game, this bonus is played in 2 phases. First is the Collection Phase, which starts with 3 lives, and only non-winning, wild, multiplier, or MultiSplit symbols appear on the main grid. Lives reset when a new wild, multiplier, or MultiSplit symbol lands. Following 3 non-winning spins, the phase ends. Above each reel is a multiplier starting on x1. By landing multiplier symbols, the reel multipliers above them are increased. Also, below the main grid is a Ninja Reel which is initially locked. Each locked position can be unlocked for the Payout Phase by landing a MultiSplit on the main grid's corresponding reel.Next is the Payout Phase, where 3 final spins are awarded. All collected wilds land randomly on the main grid on each spin. Each wild has a multiplier corresponding to its reel multiplier. Unlocked positions on the bottom Ninja Reel can also reveal MultiSplit symbols to boost the multipliers of wild symbols.Bonus BuySpecial features can be bought from the bonus buy, such as the following, which are all highly volatile:BonusHunt FeatureSpins - 2x the bet, each spin is 3 times more likely to trigger a bonus game. RTP 96.27%.Ninja Power FeatureSpins - 50x the bet, where 2-5 wilds are guaranteed on the top Ninja Reel and at least 1 MultiSplit on the bottom Ninja Reel. RTP 96.31%.The Mysteries of the Dojo Bonus Game - 100x the bet. RTP 96.34%.The Secrets of the Scroll Bonus Game - 150x the bet. RTP 96.32%.The Wisdom of the Koi Bonus Game - 200x the bet. RTP 96.27%.Shadow Strike slot - The Wisdom of the Koi featureShadow Strike: Slot VerdictWhat is up with the Hacksaw Gaming studio family at the moment, huh? Backseat is dropping fighty games like this one, and Blademaster, Bullshark released Wild Dojo Strike not long back, and Hacksaw, cripes, they've been slinging out fight slots such as Fist of Destruction and Gladiator Legends. It feels like the trio of studios are working out anger issues through their creations, or, they just really like punchy, kicky, warrior slots. Fair dues. You can imagine work parties, where the three crews meet up for a cage fight, maybe chop pieces of wood to splinters with their bare hands, possibly pound the speed bag while chugging back pre-workout smoothies.Jokes aside now, the studios seem happy sharing slot ideas around, which is cute. Shadow Strike's third bonus round, The Wisdom of the Koi bonus game, for instance, branches off from something like Alpha Eagle's Eagle Link round, where the feature is split into two parts - the Collection Phase and the Payout Phase. The first is a major influencing factor on the second, and if you can get a stack of wilds and a good number of reel multipliers to dump them on, it might turn out well. Or vice versa. Since there are 3 set in stone, non-retriggerable spins to carve out coins during the Payout Phase, there isn't much room for error. However, if The Wisdom of the Koi bonus game is giving you a bloody nose, possibly be comforted by the fact Shadow Strike's 15,000x the bet max win is achievable in all game modes.Shadow Strike has a tinge of familiarity to its features with a layer of Backseat Gaming flair on top. The familiarity of the features was cool, and they've got the juice to really pop, but at times, Shadow Strike felt as much a Hacksaw Gaming production as a Backseat Gaming one, though this is not exactly a criticism, more of an observation.

title: Clash of the Seraphim
structured_summary: Clash of the Seraphim is a biblical-themed slot portraying an epic battle between angels and demons. It features a 7x7 cluster pay grid with cascading wins, moving Light and Dark drop areas, two selectable free spins modes, and wild multipliers. The reviewer found the gameplay less engaging than the lofty storyline, with moments of thrill mainly during wild-triggered drop area conversions. The game boasts decent artwork with contrasting light and dark visuals, complemented by a dramatic, soaring soundtrack.
review: Clash of the Seraphim: Slot OverviewBlue Guru Games style themselves as storytellers, and for its online slot Clash of the Seraphim, the team has gone pretty epic. Clash of the Seraphim talks about a scenario where 'A biblical battle between the forces of good and evil rages on unseen around us.' There's more; 'Since the War in Heaven the seven Seraphim and their armies have been battling Lucifer's fallen legions for control of creation.' Heavy stuff, but if you're up for some good versus evil, light versus dark on the reels, come have a gander at the online slot Clash of the Seraphim.The clash of goodies and baddies is reinforced from the get-go, where an angelic figure hovers on the right side of the screen, opposite her dark side adversary. The rest of the background follows this pattern with light rays, white clouds, and blue skies squaring off against dark, stormy skies and a general sense of foreboding. In the middle of the standoff floats a transparent 7x7 game grid covered in more good and bad symbols. Capping off the epicness is a dramatic soundtrack, rising and falling as play unfolds.Clash of the Seraphim slot - base gameClash of the Seraphim is a cluster paying slot where wins are formed when five or more matching symbols land adjacent to each other, connecting vertically or horizontally. Winning symbols are removed from the grid, and symbols cascade down into the newly made spaces. If a new cluster is formed after the cascade, the process triggers again. The game is powered by a highly volatile math model, producing a return to player figure of 95.51%. Joining the grapple of light and darkness is made possible on any device, while participants can select a stake of 10 p/c to $/€200 per paid game round.There aren't a whole lot of pay symbols on the grid to go over. They consist of green gems, red gems, green backgrounded spears, red backgrounded spears, an angel, and the baddie character. Entry-level wins range from 0.1x to 0.5x the bet for five of a kind, maxing out at 30x to 1,000x the bet for a 40-49 matching symbol win. Winged shield 'W' symbols are wild, substituting for all symbols except scatters.Clash of the Seraphim: Slot FeaturesClash of the Seraphim slot - free spins optionsThe battle in Clash of the Seraphim is helped along to its crescendo by features such as drop areas and two selectable free spins bonus rounds.Drop AreasThe game board has three drop areas – a Dark area, a Light area, and a Scatter area. After every spin, the Light and Dark areas move position whilst also being able to change size. In the base game, the size varies from 2x2 to 3x7. However, the size restriction does not apply to free spins. The Scatter area is always the bottom position of the middle reel in the base game. The Scatter area is removed for free spins. If a wild symbol lands in a Dark or Light drop area, all symbols in the area are converted into wilds. Landing more than one wild in the same area applies a multiplier that is equal to the number of wild symbols.Dark and Light GamesThe eye of Seraphim scatter symbol appears at random on the middle reel and if it drops to the bottom Scatter area, called the Eternal Gate area, the Free Games feature is activated. Once triggered, players can choose the more volatile 8 Dark Free Games or the lesser volatile 15 Light Free Games. During each Free Game choice, only the corresponding Light or Dark drop area appears on the reels. Also, the drop area size limit is withdrawn. Scatter symbols do not appear in free spins, so the feature cannot be retriggered.On a last note, players may have the option of buying free spins rather than waiting for the scatter to naturally appear in the Scatter area. The cost is 75x the bet and has the same RTP – 95.51%. Once bought, a game round occurs where the scatter is guaranteed to end up in the Scatter area.Clash of the Seraphim slot - free spinsClash of the Seraphim: Slot VerdictAfter tangling with tentacles in Octopus Armada, it was surprising to see Blue Guru get all biblical for Clash of the Seraphim. The story is pretty interesting, recounting a classic good against evil tale, but it's too bad there's no real battling to be had in the actual game. It's just an angel on one side, a baddie on the other, with a grid in the middle where symbols cluster up and drop areas move from spin to spin. The War in Heaven idea did pique interest, yet the follow-through tended to flounder, the gameplay feeling eclipsed by the lofty heights set by the back story.There are moments to be had in Clash of the Seraphim, though. Well, mainly one type of moment, really, when wilds land in a Light or Dark drop area and transform all others within it wild. This could, admittedly, from time to time, create a bit of a thrill. More so during free spins since there the drop areas could get quite large. There was a noticeable difference between the two free spins options, too, and Dark Free Games could be ridiculously punishing. As well as cobbling together sizable clusters within its drop area, Dark Free Games had no qualms producing no wins, except those garnered on the triggering spin. Drop area conversions were critical in creating larger cluster wins, which was good since smaller sized clusters don't have particularly exciting values. Neither does Clash of the Seraphim on the whole either, really, which generated its highest payout of 3,938x the bet during 10 billion simulated spins.Blue Guru Games is certainly magpie minded when it comes to selecting themes for their slots, swinging wildly from one topic to another. Clash of the Seraphim is another one with an intriguing back story, possessing decent artwork and a soaring soundtrack, yet the action struggled to reach the heights of the game's premise.

title: Planet Fortune
structured_summary: Planet Fortune is a retro-futuristic slot with 5 reels, 4 rows, and 40 fixed paylines. It features stacked premium symbols, a random Magnetic Mayhem feature, and walking wilds during free spins. The reviewer finds it straightforward but not innovative, lacking standout features or high win potential. The game sports a classic reel setup with a robot-themed wild and simple visuals, though audio details were not highlighted.
review: Planet Fortune: IntroductionIt just happens to be so, that about a month ago we actually reached out to Play'N Go and demanded a slot with sticky wilds. Being great fans of this type of feature, our argument was that every great slot provider must have at least one slot featuring sticky wilds.We certainly got our hopes up when we read the information sheet which stated; "During free spins, all wild symbols that appear will be "sticky" on the reels." At this point the excitement was real and we couldn't wait for the test run. Then we kept on reading..."When the free spin starts, all wilds will remain on the reels but “walk” horizontally to the reel to the left. If the wild is on reel 1, it will walk off the reel and disappear."Play'n GO, how in the world can that be concidered sticky wilds? Those are "walking wilds". Sticky wilds are supposed to stick, not disappear. Oh well...Planet Fortune is what Play'n GO describes as a "retro-futuristic" game. The slot has 5 reels, 4 rows and 40 fixed paylines. The bet size range from 0.20 to 100 and max win is 2500x. According to information from PnG, Planet Fortune is a high volatile game, but it has to be put into perspective. It is certainly no Dead or Alive in comparison.If playing on a casino using a Malta license for the game, you can expect an RTP of either 96.50% or 94.49%. Any other type of license may offer an RTP much lower than this. If uncertain, check the help file of the game. If RTP is not stated, you're not playing on a Malta license.There are 6 premium symbols which are all placed on stacks of 2, 3 or 4 symbols. The low value symbols are not stacked and are represented by A, K, Q, J and 10. The game also includes a wild symbol, which is represented by a robot, and of course, substitutes for any other symbol.Planet Fortune: Main Game & Free SpinsUnlike many of the other slots released by PnG in recent times, Planet Fortune is straight forward and easy to learn. It has a classic reel setup and no crazy combinations or features that will give you headaches. There are pretty much two objectives in the main game - to land as many stacked reels with premium symbols as possible and to land 3 robot wilds to trigger the free spins.To add more action, there's something called the Magnetic Mayhem. When this random feature is triggered, two or three reels stick together by 2x2 or 3x3 sized symbols. In other words, you will not get fully stacked reels. Unfortunately, wilds can not appear on the attached Mayhem reels.Three or more robots appearing on any reels will award you 10 free spins, or Robot Revolution Free Spins, as PnG likes to call it. Everytime a wild symbol lands during the free spins, it will stay on the screen, but walk move to the left by 1 for every spin. This is a feature better known as "walking wilds". The free spins feature cannot be re-triggered.Planet Fortune: ConclusionPlanet Fortune is not a revolutionary game and it offers nothing new or innovative. It's one of those games that people will try a few times when they see it in the new slots category, but will eventually fall into oblivion. There are so many slots being produced these days that game providers needs something extra to win the player over - be it innovative features or, even better, crazy high potential. To be frank, this game has none of those.

title: Thoro
structured_summary: Thoro is a Norse mythology-themed slot featuring the matador Toro as Thor, battling Loki in the floating realm of Asgard. The game offers unique features like Lightning symbol wins, Loki Respins, Thoro Thunder Strike, Mjolnir boosts, and multiple free spin rounds with an X-iter bonus buy. The reviewer praises its blend of familiar gameplay with fresh mechanics and a max win of 10,000x the bet, making it engaging and rewarding. Visually, Thoro impresses with high-quality graphics and a thunderous heavy metal soundtrack that complements its mythological theme.
review: Thoro: Slot OverviewThe online slot Wild Toro was one of ELK Studios' popular earlier releases, and after lying fallow for 5 years, was brought bucking back to life in 2021 with a 3 slot world tour, which kicked off with the release of Wild Toro 2. Since then, the wild and crazy dude has mixed it up with bison in Buffalo Toro, sampled Japanese culture in Toro Shogun, and clashed in the arena of Gladiatoro. He's like someone who got a sniff of travel and now wants to see the whole world, ticking destinations off a bucket list as long as their arm. This time, Toro is getting all Norse in the online slot Thoro, with the Matador in tow as Loki, and a hearty shovelling of accompanying features.First things first, Thoro, huh? Good name, mixing Toro with the famous god of thunder and lightning, Thor. (Sorry for stating the obvious). In this game, Thoro is all set to inherit the throne of Asgard, but his mischievous brother Loki has other plans… Thoro is played on a 5-reel, 4-row gaming grid, set amidst the floating world of Asgard, up there amongst the clouds and the Bifrost. Obviously, Thoro is a long, long way from the sultry Spanish plaza of Wild Toro, but the humorous showdown between man and beast lives on, as do some of the features.Thoro slot - base gameOne way of winning a spot of dosh in Thoro is by landing matching symbols on adjacent reels from the leftmost side of the matrix. Symbols in adjacent reels must be connected either horizontally or diagonally to form a combination. As well as five X-iter betting modes, gamblers can choose a stake of 20 c to $/€100 per spin in this medium-high volatile slot where the RTP comes in at 94%.Glowing runes carved into stones are Thoro's 4 low pay symbols, whereas a horn, a daggered pig, a cup of bubbly, and a helmet are the high pays. Lines of 5 matching runes are worth 0.4 to 0.8 times the bet; hitting 5 identical highs pays 0.9 to 5 times the bet. Wild symbols help complete winning combinations by substituting any regular paying symbol. An all-wild win has the same value as the highest pay symbol.Thoro: Slot FeaturesThoro slot - free spinsBlasting out of Asgard are Lightning symbol wins, Loki Respins, a Thoro Thunder Strike feature, a Mjolnir feature, free spins, super free spins, and X-iter bonus buys.Lightning SymbolsLightning symbols are needed to win prizes from the Lightning paytable displayed next to the reels. Lighting symbols are present on reels 2, 3, and 4. On its lowest level, 4 to 11 landed Lightning symbols pay 2x to 1,000x the bet. However, the Lightning paytable can be upgraded to higher prize values. Hitting 12 Lightning symbols pays the remaining amount needed to award Thoro's max win. Free spins scatter symbols also count as Lightning symbols.Loki RespinLanding 2 or more Loki symbols awards a Loki Respin. For the respin, Loki symbols are sticky and remain in position. Getting additional Loki symbols on a Loki Respin awards an additional respin.Thoro Thunder StrikeThoro is a walking wild that moves left until spinning out from the leftmost reel, triggering a respin for each step. Only one Thoro can be on the grid at once. Lightning and scatter symbols are sticky during Thoro respins. Any Lightning symbol payout only occurs once Thoro spins out. Hitting a Thoro symbol when there is at least one Loki symbol in view, or hitting a Loki when Thoro is in view, triggers the Thoro Thunderstrike feature. title: Cashed in Stone
structured_summary: Cashed in Stone is a Stone Age-themed slot set in a cartoon prehistoric world featuring cavemen and dinosaur bones. It offers a 6x4 layout with cascading wins, four random reel modifiers, a Big Money Wheel bonus, and a multi-level free spins trail. The reviewer finds it an improvement over Viking Hoard with more frequent features but still slow gameplay and clunky graphics, making it only moderately enjoyable. The game’s visuals are basic and cartoonish with a humorous caveman mascot, while the audio adds lightheartedness to the experience.
review: Cashed in Stone: OverviewSG Digital developer Core Gaming has a thing about the past. This time they have gone all the way back to the dawn of humanity. When it comes to human history, it doesn’t get much older than the Stone Age where Cashed in Stone is set. This is a cartoon world of knuckle draggers with sloping foreheads bashing each other with dinosaur bones. The previous Core Gaming title to come our way was Viking Hoard, which was a real test of patience and fortitude. So it was with some trepidation that we fired up Cashed in Stone.Visually, prehistoric isn’t a bad word to describe the game, particularly the UI. The graphic standard isn’t high, though the rolling hills of the background are pleasant. Cashed in Stone comes with its own mascot. A cute wee caveman, who looks a little like Animal from the Muppets. He adds a much-needed dose of humour to lighten what could have been a starchy slot. The setup uses a 6 reel, 4 row format with 4,096 ways to win. As with Viking Hoard, the symbols fall into place and are part of a cascading win system. Winners are removed to let new symbols tumble to create chains of wins from one spin. Players choose bets from 25 p/c up to $/€100 per spin on virtually any device.Winning combinations are formed by matching 3 or more of a kind. The paytable is made up of 10 – A royals and a bunch of high pays. This includes a bone with meat, a stone axe, a necklace, and a BAR symbol. The most valuable is the Logo which only needs two of a kind and pays 40 times the stake for a six of a kind combo. Due key factors that we will look at, RTP ranges from 96% down to an unusually low 91.95%. Volatility is in the low/medium region but plays and feels quite high at times - although nothing like the dull uneventful slogs that Viking Hoard could produce. Rounding off the paytable is the wild symbol which can substitute for any of the regular pay symbols.Cashed in Stone: FeaturesCashed in Stone comes with a surprising amount of features, some of which require player input. These come in the form of reel modifiers, collectable free spins, and a bonus game for good measure. To the modifiers first and there are four of them which can randomly appear on any base game spin. We have:Stackin’ Wilds: a random number of reels turn completely wild. If used as part of a winning combination, they are removed in a cascade.Multiplyin’ Times: a win multiplier is introduced which increases with winning cascade for one spin.Cashin’ Drop: the game selects one pay symbol and drops it in the game at extra-large 3x3 size.Smashin’ Wilds: the caveman bashes symbols turning them wild.The caveman symbol is the scatter and three in view trigger the Big Money Wheel Bonus game. During this round, a two-tier prize wheel is spun. The first wheel is split into segments containing multipliers of x1 – x5. If the wheel stops on a multiplier segment, it is applied to the total bet and can turn into a red cross. The wheel keeps spinning and adding up wins unless the wheel stops on a red cross then the game is over. There is one other segment though, which is a green arrow. If the wheel stops on this, then it unlocks the second tier wheel which has the same rules but multipliers of x10 – x250.The last feature of note are the Free Spins which are little more complicated than normal. When players land a free spins symbol, it moves the spins trail up one notch. The spins trail has three sections; The lower section has 1-5 free spins with 2 guaranteed wilds each. The middle section is 5-10 free spins with three wilds. The final section is 10 free spins with a 2x2 wild on each spin. Players can choose to activate their accumulated free spins at any time by hitting the green button beneath the trail. The only exception is the final section which triggers automatically when it is reached. One interesting aspect of free spins is that when they are activated, the bet level used is an average of all stakes in the game up until that point. Free spins cannot be retriggered.Cashed in Stone: VerdictAfter a few initial spins, memories of Viking Hoard came flooding in like a Nam flashback. Remembering what it took to land features in that slot a question arose – are we up to this again? Fortunately, features drop more frequently with Cashed in Stone. The math model has had the ‘ruthlessness’ setting turned down which is appreciated. In saying that, patience is still needed. It can take a lot of spins to reach the end of the free spins trail. The free spins option is a little controversial.Triggering lower amounts of free spins drastically reduces the RTP rate. It can go as diabolically low as 91.95%. Then again, if you commit to going all the way, you need to be prepared for the investment in time and coins to get there. So it is worth it? Potentially the game is capped at 250,000 from one spin which is high. Realistically, players are likely looking at max returns of around 5,000 times the stake.Cashed in Stone is not a copy of Viking Hoard, but they have a lot in common. The main problem is that what was annoying about Viking Hoard remains just as annoying this time around. Graphics are clunky, and the base game can be glacial. To its credit, you will probably experience more features with Cashed in Stone than with Viking Hoard. Despite the wee caveman’s best efforts, Cashed in Stone just isn’t all that fun to play. Fans of prehistory might find value, and it is an improvement from Core Gaming. In summation, Cashed in Stone is more enjoyable than Viking Hoard was, but still about as fun as being smacked over the head with a dinosaur bone.

title: Retro Galaxy

review: Retro Galaxy: OverviewGet all nostalgic in Retro Galaxy, a neon-filled slot from Microgaming partner Half Pixel Studios. Half Pixel is one of these smaller outfits with a minimal online footprint - not even a website to delve into. If you have a little Google, it’s not the web designer in Albuquerque or the computer network company in Bratislava of the same name. For now, they remain a mystery, with just their work to judge them by.If Retro Galaxy is anything to go by, Half Pixel is a studio with a passion for the past. Not only does Retro Galaxy combine futuristic elements with an 80s look, which is quite popular at the moment, but the game is full of classic Microgaming features of yesteryear.Visually, the action takes place above a horizontal grid-like surface, stretching to the horizon where a galactic cluster can be viewed. The reels are transparent, so more of the view can be seen, and bordered by a sort of fighter pilot HUD. An 80s inspired Synthwave track accompanies the visuals, providing the final brush-stroke on the retro picture. The overall effect is pleasant, a little underwhelming, but perfectly functional all the same time.Half Pixel has set Retro Galaxy up in a 5x3 pattern, offering 243 ways to win. Three or more matching symbols consecutively from the first reel form a combo, regardless of the row they are on. Whenever a winner lands it triggers a couple of key features – Rolling Reels, and the Multiplier Trail, both of which are covered in the next section.Allowing players to get their nostalgia fix on any device, Retro Galaxy is playable from 20 p/c to $/€20 per spin. Stats are one of the game’s highlights, starting with a nice average figure of 96.05% for the RTP rate. Wins land fairly thickly thanks to a hit rate better than 1 in 3, or, 34.41%, which works well with the features to give the game flow. However, the math model is highly volatile, making it a poor fit for those looking for a casual ride into the past.A bit of free association turns up the words ‘neon’, ‘Miami’, and ‘chrome when it comes to the paytable symbols. Low pays are bold pink 10-A icons, worth 1 – 1.5x for five of a kind. High pays are lightning bolts, stars, BARs, Sevens, and a colourful geometric shape. Land five of the premiums for returns of 5 to 30 times the stake. The jazzy looking wild isn’t worth anything on its own, but it does substitutes for any symbol except the scatter. The wild appears on reels 2, 3, 4, and 5 in the base game or free spins.Retro Galaxy: FeaturesRetro Galaxy - free spinsNostalgia is once again the name of the game when it comes to features, since all are classics such as Rolling Reels, Multiplier Trails, and free spins which have all appeared in classic Microgaming slots such as Immortal Romance and Jungle Jim.Whenever a winning combination lands on the reels, the Rolling Reels feature comes into play to remove winning symbols from the reels, allowing new ones to drop in. These new symbols may lead to more wins, and Rolling Reels continue to roll until no new winners appear.While this is going on, the Multiplier Trail is working its magic. This is a win multiplier, starting at x1 on the initial spin, increasing to x2 on the first roll, x3 on the second roll, and maxing at x5 for any subsequent rolls – during the base game.Landing at least 3 scatter symbols anywhere on the reels triggers the free spins feature - 3, 4, or 5 awards 10, 15, or 20 free spins, plus a prize of 2, 10, or 100 times the bet respectively. During free spins, the Multiplier Trail gets a boost, starting at x2, and rising by +1 with every roll to a maximum of 15x. The Multiplier Trail does reset between free spins as it does in the main game. Should three scatters land on a free spin, five extra spins are added to the remaining total.Retro Galaxy: VerdictRetro Galaxy has its moments, though they have pretty much all been seen before in one form or another. Rolling Reels, Multiplier Trails, plus 243 win ways is a proven formula that has served developer Microgaming well in the past and haven't been used with much imagination here. As such, it comes across as a rather bland and unoriginal creation that piggybacks off of old Microgaming merits.Besides features, Retro Galaxy’s potential is its trump card. At full stretch, the game is capable of hitting wins of up to 7,300 times the stake. Potential like this helps make Retro Galaxy a viable option for those looking for dependable gameplay along with solid payouts.Despite the positive stats and mechanics, Retro Galaxy isn’t exactly an unmissable slot. Perhaps it’s the bandwagon feel of the theme or the rehashing of older features, but the game lacks much wow factor. Retro Galaxy comes across as a slot Microgaming has tested their partner with making before setting them a more ambitious project. This is pure speculation, of course, just an impression Retro Galaxy gives off.If Retro Galaxy was a test, then Half Pixel has probably passed it - just barely. You won’t find much new here, either in terms of gameplay or theme, although that probably won't stop some from thinking it's an okay slot.

title: Christmas Bonanza
structured_summary: Christmas Bonanza blends gold mining with a subtle Christmas theme, featuring snowy visuals and gift box symbols. review: Christmas Bonanza: Slot OverviewGold mining might not be the first thing which comes to mind when thinking about Christmas, but that might well change if developer Big Time Gaming has anything to say about it. If another win is created after the symbols drop/move, it also vanishes from the board, and the process repeats itself as long as new wins continue to land.Free SpinsGold square symbols are the scatters, and spelling G. O. L. D with 4 of them triggers 12 free spins. Should more than 4 scatters land, each additional scatter adds +5 extra free spins to the pot. However, even if you missed Bonanza the first time around, it's nigh on impossible to deny the contribution it has made to the evolution of online slots.As such, there's not much to say about Christmas Bonanza which hasn't been said before about Bonanza on numerous occasions. It brings together the magic of Megaways, reactions, and win multipliers in a way that was practically unmissable at the time and which others have tried to greater or lesser success to cash in on ever since. Even its advertised potential stands up well in an industry that routinely trundles out games with 100,000x+ max wins.  Some on paper, some proven to perform. Christmas Bonanza has the goods to pop off wins worth up to 5,400x the bet in the base game and 26,000x in free spins for those who'd like the cold hard numbers. It has to be said though; if the original Bonanza is anything to go by, you have about a snowball's chance in hell of landing anything over 2,000x in the Christmas version.Perhaps the only slight criticism, if we're digging deep, is that the game isn't hugely Christmassy; whether this was done on purpose or not, who knows? title: Frost Queen Jackpots
structured_summary: Frost Queen Jackpots is a chilly, snow-themed slot inspired by Victorian detective tales with a winter fantasy twist. review: Frost Queen Jackpots: Slot OverviewA few years back, developer Yggdrasil Gaming released a local progressive jackpot slot based around the famous Victorian private dick titled Holmes and the Stolen Stones. The Pick & Click Chest game is triggered when two mirror scatter symbols land. Here, 5 chests appear on screen for the player to pick one, revealing a prize of 1x -4x the bet, 10 free spins, or a random key.Land 3 or more scatter symbols to trigger the Magic Mirror feature plus a win of 50x or 500x the bet if 4 or 5 land. The Magic Mirror feature awards free spins or the Treasure Chest Bonus Game. As well as the two methods mentioned above, if players collect 5 identical keys in the base game, they win 10 free spins plus 1 jackpot gem.During free spins, the value of line wins are multiplied by x3, and the goal is to collect five identically coloured gems. Should this happen, the corresponding jackpot is awarded. Each jackpot pays a minimum prize of:Blue jackpot – seed value of $/€40Green jackpot – seed value of $/€200Purple jackpot – seed value of $/€600Red jackpot – seed value of $/€1,500Orange jackpot – seed value of $/€15,000Alternatively, if the Magic Mirror triggers the Treasure Chest Bonus Game, players choose one of 3 chests on each level. Finding a reward moves players to the next chamber, until they click to reveal an avalanche which ends the feature. Chests can contain bet wins of 5x to 100x, or random keys for the free spins collection.Frost Queen Jackpots: Slot VerdictJust like a Disney movie, Frost Queen Jackpots has been made for general audience consumption. The math model is light, the aesthetics provide a bit of an escape, and there are five progressive jackpots to spin for – what more could the non-discerning player ask for? Anyone who prefers a bit more edge will fail to find much warmth in Frost Queen, and non-jackpot wins aren't exactly massive.So is it an improvement on Holmes and the Stolen Stones, or Jackpot Raiders for that matter which follows a similar structure? In some ways yes, in some ways no. For one, there are slightly more features, plus more ways to trigger the good bits. Frost Queen possesses an easier going nature, dishing up more wins, more frequent keys and in general feels user-friendlier. On the downside, Frost Queen doesn't have quite as good an atmosphere as Holmes did, particularly in the music department.Frost Queen’s gameplay does seem to flow more smoothly than Holmes did too. The Pick & Click feature might not sound like much, but it does negate the monotony by providing a little thrill every now and then. The minuscule bet wins are a little pointless, yet keys help. It's worth repeating this, collecting keys does not award jackpots, which it is easy to assume unless you've read the rules. On the whole, if you play Holmes after this one, you notice the long stretches of not much going on, which the Pick & Click negates to an extent.Yggdrasil has created a rather clever game in Frost Queen. The key collection system gives the slot purpose, extending game time since it encourages hitting the spin button. Pick & Click Chests help here too, breaking up the slog with the odd win or two providing an extra incentive. To sum up, Frost Queen Jackpots might not be a high powered thrill fest, but it is bound to offer an enjoyable jackpot chase for certain players.

Relaxing to be sure, but hardly an adrenaline rush.Thankfully, it's not all laid back basking in the sun. Wilds, respins, and multipliers are on hand to provide thrills, and hopefully, build up some solid wins. Features tended to trigger quite frequently during testing too, rarely leading to big wins, though often enough to interrupt the monotony of staring at a dull blue screen. That included a few free spins rounds as well as Wild Respins.Still, the high potential might provide enough of a motivator for many on its own. Action heats up when multipliers build, plus the way they multiply each other can get exciting. The sheer number of wild multipliers and the way they act offers something a little different overall. If you're after big wins alongside high volatility and don't mind the low sensorial effects, Neptune's Riches Ocean of Wilds could be worth a look.

title: CherryPop
structured_summary: CherryPop is a classic fruit-themed slot featuring AvatarUX's unique PopWins mechanic for expanding reels and winning ways. Key features include cascading wins, expanding reels up to 9 rows, free spins with progressive multipliers, and a bonus buy option. The reviewer finds it a balanced, accessible PopWins entry with high volatility and strong win potential, though the base game can feel repetitive. Visually, it sports a clean, commercial design with a pink frame, colorful blurry backdrop, and subtle 80s electronic soundtrack.
review: CherryPop: OverviewThe fruit-themed slot CherryPop is the third from independent developer AvatarUX to use their expansive PopWins mechanic. The first two in the range, PopRocks and WildPops, had a distinctly Eastern feel to them, from noir to full-on Asian. The third version returns to gambling roots in a classic fruity indulgence. Brace for plenty of old-school symbols, on a grid that can seriously expand, packing in free spins, and like the previous two, massive potential.CherryPop - base gameWhen it comes to looks, CherryPop is the most commercial of the range so far. A burning pink frame surrounds the slot, which is 5 reels wide and 3 rows high in the default mode, but expandable up the ying-yang when features kick in. Behind the grid is a purple, blue, pinky backdrop, designed in the blurry style Avatar UX seems to favour. The word basic springs to mind, though the design is pleasantly clean, regardless. The final touch is the soundtrack. No Zoot Suit Riot, unfortunately, but some low-key 80s electronica contributing to a positive feel.Playable from 20 p/c to $/€40 per spin, the stats produced by the game are certainly a standout, such as RTP which isn't amazing, but above average on 96.2%. The action moves at a fair pace too thanks in part to winners showing up every 1 in 5 spins or so (a hit rate of 22% officially). Yet, don't expect too many big payouts during the base game when they do. PopWins slots are notorious for being highly volatile and CherryPop is certainly that.The primary rule is that three or more adjacent matching symbols from the first or fifth reel trigger a payout. Technically there are 243 ways to win in default mode, but in essence, this is doubled to 486 since the game pays both ways. Some designers might have left a fruit slot at that, but Avatar UX isn't a studio which does things by halves.Before finding out what CherryPop is capable of when its foot is on the gas, let's take a quick look at the paytable. There are a lot of pay symbols, 13 to be precise, which can crowd the slot in smaller configurations. At the bottom end of the paytable are 10-A royals, followed by grapes, melons, oranges, horseshoes, clovers, bells, diamonds, and cherries. Non-royal values are worth up to 15 times the stake for five cherries. Keep in mind cherries only appear from pops or free spins.CherryPop: FeaturesIt might look like quite an average, albeit shiny, classic fruit slot in a screenshot, but the features ensure this is no ordinary fruity game. As you'd expect if you've played the previous two, the PopWins function is the central feature, complemented by free spins, and the bonus buy.Every hit triggers the PopWins feature. When so happens, winning symbols are cleared from the screen, and each empty position is replaced with two new symbols. Since there are more symbols than there was before, reels are expanded to accommodate them – up to 6 rows high in the base game. Consecutive wins are possible using the new symbols, and the process continues until no new winners appear. Then the reels are reset.If all 5 reels expand to 6 rows in height, 5 free spins are triggered. However, before the bonus game starts, players get the chance to gamble their spins on the Gamble Wheel. Successful gambles award up to 16 free spins, or you can lose the lot - then it's back to the main game empty-handed.Free spins up the ante by introducing a progressive win multiplier starting at x2. Each PopWin increases the multiplier by +1, without limit. PopWins also expand the reels like they do in the base game. The difference now is reels can reach 9 rows in height.When all reels are 9 rows high, the win multiplier gets a +3 boost. Also, each subsequent PopWin from then on increases the multiplier by +4 rather than +1. On a full 9 row grid, there are 59,049 ways to win in play – double when you factor in the pay both ways. When a spin without a PopWin occurs, reels return to the height of the shortest reel, rather than reset completely.Finally, there is one new feature – a bonus buy option. For the cost of 75 times the stake, you'll simply get instant access to the bonus.CherryPop: VerdictOf the three PopWins slots released so far, CherryPop sort of sits in the middle of the other two. What do we mean? Well, the first one was very volatile, either going nowhere or blasting into orbit on very lengthy win sequences. It also has the highest potential. The second one, WildPops, is the less brutal, throwing in random wild lifelines to keep the action flowing, yet decreasing the potential.That brings us to CherryPop, which is more forgiving than the first, yet more brutal than the second. You do miss the random wild feature of WildPops, and to be honest, CherryPop's base game does get a bit repetitive if you struggle to hit free spins. The generic theme doesn't help, yet the game has been attractively presented for a fruit slot. What might make CherryPop more appealing than the others is the buy feature, allowing you to avoid the base game battling altogether.Whether you dig CherryPop comes down to your thoughts on the PopWins mechanic really. Hitting a base game lull can be tiring since there are no other modifiers going on. Yet, get it snowballing and buckle in - the potential for long drawn out sequences is impressive. Expanding reels are as fun as ever, and the inclusion of a pay both ways system only adds to the mayhem. Rewards certainly aren't an issue if you do manage to wind CherryPop up, where wins of up to 20,000 times the stake are possible.If anything, AvatarUX shows there are plenty more twists to be made in the classic/fruit slot genre. Players in the mood for this style with an unusual mechanic and solid stats will do well to give CherryPop a spin. Overall there is a compellingly simple nature to CherryPop, making it easy to spin again, or hit the bonus buy button just one more time.PopWins is an intriguing mechanic with possibilities, and CherryPop comes across as the most mainstream, accessible one so far. Still, despite the enjoyable gaming, it doesn't feel like Avatar UX has quite achieved their breakout performance with the mechanic just yet.

title: Jade of the Jungle
structured_summary: Jade of the Jungle is a Central American-themed slot featuring two independently spinning 3x3 grids set against a jungle backdrop with a step pyramid. Key features include a Super Stake option triggering symbol removal spins and a free spins mode that eliminates low-paying symbols for better wins. The review finds the game moderately interesting but ultimately gimmicky, lacking strong interaction between grids or standout innovation. Visually, the game is pleasant but not striking, with relaxing panpipe music that intensifies with rhythmic drums during spins.
review: Jade of the Jungle: Slot OverviewDeveloper Stakelogic and independent associates Jelly are the teams behind the Central American themed slot Jade of the Jungle. This part of the world is a regular haunt of slots designers, so doing something out of the norm is practically a must if a game is to have any chance of finding an audience. In the case of Jade of the Jungle, the makers have squeezed in two independently spinning game grids instead of one. It's a technique that is gaining traction, but it's not an everyday occurrence, so could this method be the thing to make Jade of the Jungle stand out? Only one way to know.Right in the middle of Jade of the Jungle are two 3x3 game panels, separated by a swirling stone statue. They are surrounded by trees, vines, bushes, and a step pyramid in the background, so players will have no problem identifying where in the world they are. Overall, Jade of the Jungle is a nice-looking game, not particularly striking, though pleasant all the same. The soundtrack is relaxing too, all panpipes and whatnot while the action is static, before layering a rhythmical drumbeat over the top when the reels are spinning.Each reel set in Jade of the Jungle has 7 fixed paylines to land winning combinations of matching symbols across. This is a medium-high volatile game, producing a theoretical RTP of 95.30%, which isn't bad in itself, yet when combined with the averageness of everything else, doesn't quite add value. Be aware that RTP comes in a number of lesser configurations, bottoming out at 88.06% in some markets. Regular stakes may be set from 25 p/c to $/€125 per spin or doubled when clicking on the Super Stake bet option. Activating Super Stake unlocks a feature which is not available when playing normally.Now, a run-through of regular symbols, where from low to high we find four Aztec-y icons, a serpent, a bird, two faces, and a sparkly piece of jade - values for the three most valuable symbols are 4 to 10 times the stake. The final symbol for now is the wild which lands anywhere to replace all symbols except the scatter.Jade of the Jungle: Slot FeaturesJade of the Jungle - Nudge feature in playThere are two features to cover here, one being the Super Stake feature players pay extra for, while the other is free spins with a symbol removal system.Super Stake FeatureIf you've switched Super Stake on, there is a chance an extra feature randomly appears. When triggered, a regular paying symbol is chosen. All other symbols except for wilds or the chosen symbol are removed from the reels. Players get 1 spin with additional chosen symbols and wilds added to the reels. Just so you know, the RTP remains the same whether Super Stake is switched on or off.Free SpinsScatters appear on reels 1 or 3 on both reel sets. When landing 3 or 4 scatter symbols across one or both reel sets, players are awarded 8 or 12 free spins, respectively. During free spins, whenever a scatter lands, the lowest paying symbol is removed from the reels for the remainder of the feature, and +1 or +2 additional free spins are awarded. The point here, obviously, is to have as many symbols removed as possible until you are only left with the most valuable ones.Jade of the Jungle: Slot VerdictMost developers in the slots industry continually push for novelty in an effort to entertain players hungry for new ideas. Sometimes a new concept works, and a studio hits it out of the park, creating the next big thing. Other times it lands somewhere in midfield to entertain for a while, or, a new feature utterly misses the mark, passing by on its way to the great slots garbage compactor never to be seen or heard from again. Jade of the Jungle hovers around the middle while teetering dangerously towards the compactor. Its six reels provoked a minor stab of interest, as did the Super Stake feature and symbol removal free spins, causing the game to start on a positive note.Interest wanes once you realise Jade of the Jungle is just two 3x3 slots spinning at once. There is little interaction between the two-game panels as well, which is surprising but not a requirement of using multi-grids to power the action. If you were waiting for synced reels or symbol swaps, there's none of that. Nor do they link up in the bonus game into one large 6-reel grid, which is what we first suspected before checking the rules. No, it's just two-reel sets spinning next to each other. Two for the price of one? Kind of, though not really, since the RTP is a little lower than usual and getting hits on both reel sets at once doesn't always happen. The duel reel method might work for players who prefer a longer spin time though we could be grasping at straws now. One exception was when the Super Stake feature triggered and wins generally hit on both grids, sometimes producing better payouts than what we squeezed out of free spins.It's interesting, Jade of the Jungle's home screen advertised a bonus game that consisted of five win spins a la Pimped with a x5 multiplier on hand boosting payouts. However, Jelly or Stakelogic must have changed their mind during the construction phase and switched to the symbol upgrade system instead. This free spins system works okay when you've knocked out a bunch of the lower-paying symbols - just don't expect Jade of the Jungle to really step up, as the most you can win here is 2,976x your bet.In the end, Jade of the Jungle was okay for a few spins, a quick trip back to Central America and all that. Yet there's nothing which quickened many pulses. Despite supplying two simultaneously spinning grids there's no major advantage over having just one, creating a gimmicky, 'look at me' impression as much as anything else.

title: Asgardian Fire
structured_summary: Asgardian Fire immerses players in a Norse mythology theme set in the realm of Odin with powerful godly imagery. The game features Rolling Reels, Escalating Ways up to 262,144 ways to win, Jumbo Blocks, persistent wilds, free spins with an Elevator mechanic, and a feature buy option. The reviewer praises its impressive graphics and soundtrack, calling it a must-try for Norse slot fans despite familiar mechanics borrowed from other slots. Visually stunning with dynamic animations and a rock-inspired audio backdrop, the game delivers a strong audiovisual experience.
review: Asgardian Fire: Slot OverviewWelcome to Asgard, home of the Norse Gods, ruled by Odin, the All-Father, he who traded an eye to drink at Mímir's well. Yeah, yeah, yeah, another mythology slot set in the home of some gods again, no big deal. Right? Well, it kind of is a big deal if Games Global partner Neon Valley Studios has anything to say about it. For Asgardian Fire, the studio has pulled out its best slide rulers and paint brushes, then set to work making a cracker of a Norse mythology game. Spoiler alert, the team has borrowed one or two ideas from one of its competitors, which will soon become apparent. But if you're willing to overlook that, then there is a fine example of Norse mythology-themed gaming to be sampled in Asgardian Fire.First things first, Asgardian Fire's graphical standard is quite exceptional. Players are drawn into an awe-inspiring world where the base game, with its rocky landscape beneath the aurora borealis, is pretty enough but trigger free spins, and play moves to an even more celestial realm, full of thick golden glowing clouds and what could be Odin's residence behind the active gaming panel, visible when symbols are rolling. This is powerful subject matter, and Neon Valley Studios has brought plenty of power to bear for Asgardian Fire.Asgardian Fire slot - base gameNow's when things get thornier because Asgardian Fire uses a reel setup taken straight from ELK Studios' 'Gold' range of slots. Each base game spin starts with 6 reels and 4 rows of symbols, with 4,096 ways to win. When winning combinations hit, the symbols are removed by the Rolling Reels feature, and replaced by symbols from above, then an extra row is added to the grid. The reels can expand up to 8 rows high at the most, where 262,144 ways to win become active. In the base game, when no more wins appear, the grid resets to its resting 6x4 size. In Asgardian Fire, this expansion system is known as Escalating Ways.Asgardian Fire's math model has garnered a 'very high' rating in terms of volatility and is available in four RTP models, 96% being the highest. It takes bets of 20 p/c to $/€50 and spits out a win, theoretically at a hit rate of 26.29% on the highest RTP model. Should a win be 6 symbols in length, it'll pay 0.4x the bet when made up of J-A card ranks, 1x to 1.2x the bet for the wolf, axes, hammer, or ravens symbols, before rising to 2.2x-5x the bet for the 4 top value character symbols. Also, appearing on reels on all but the leftmost reel is Asgardian Fire's wild symbol, substituting for all symbols except scatters.Asgardian Fire: Slot FeaturesAsgardian Fire slot - free spinsAlong with Rolling Reels and Escalating Ways, Asgardian Fire has Jumbo Blocks, a Wild Fill Feature, Second Chance, free spins with Elevator, persistent wilds, a feature buy, plus the Upsizer.Jumbo BlocksAny symbol except scatters or wilds can land as a Jumbo Block. Jumbo Blocks may appear during Rolling Reels in sizes of 2x2, 3x3, or 4x4. They can appear on reels 2 to 6.Wild Fill FeatureWhen Jumbo Blocks land, if there are empty spaces beneath them, these empty spaces are filled with wild symbols.Scatter and Second ChanceEach scatter that lands activates the Second Chance feature, which triggers after all wins are complete. Up to 12 symbols in a diamond-shaped area around each scatter explode, making way for symbols to cascade in. Wilds, Jumbo Blocks, or other scatters do not explode.Free SpinsLanding 3 scatter symbols awards 6 free spins, plus 3 extra free spins for each additional scatter in view. Free spins can be retriggered, and before they begin, the Upsizer feature displays the cost of buying extra free spins. The options may be 9, 12, 15, or 25. The Upsizer is not available from the feature buy. Now, free spins start with the Elevator set to 4 rows. After each winning spin, the Elevator moves up 1 row to a maximum of 8 rows high. The Elevator locks in the minimum number of rows and ways to win for the remainder of the feature. Also, in free spins, when all wins are complete, any wilds left on the grid drop to the bottom of the reels. Wilds persist until they are part of a win.Feature BuyFrom the bonus buy menu, players may buy 6, 9, 12, 15, or 25 free spins for the cost of 70x, 100x, 125x, 140x, or 300x the bet, respectively.Asgardian Fire slot - feature buy optionsAsgardian Fire: Slot VerdictWith Asgardian Fire, Neon Valley Studios has designed the Norse slot equivalent of a banquet overflowing with roast boars, mead, and walnut bread. The team has lavished Asgardian Fire with eye-popping graphics and head-banging tunes. Screenshots don't really do the game justice because the excellent animations, the dynamic reel, the zooming in and out only get a chance to sparkle when in motion. For fans of Norse-themed slots, this one is a must-try. You'd be forgiven for thinking the studio was based way up in the Arctic regions of Scandinavia (rather than Las Vegas), its workers poring over dusty, ancient books, dissecting Sagas, studying up on local lore in preparation for Asgardian Fire's development. That or they really liked the movie Thor: Ragnarok because Asgardian Fire's punchy visuals coupled with a rock-influenced soundtrack awakened memories of that bit in the film after Odin reminds Thor he's the God of Thunder, not the God of Hammers, then goes on a rampage to the sounds of Led Zeppelin's Immigrant Song.If so, then movies aren't Asgardian Fire's only influence because its core mechanics are very close, if not exactly the same as those found in numerous 'Gold' slots from ELK Studios – and by extension Blueprint Gaming's slot Viking Fury. Visually too, there were echoes of Relax Gaming's slot Volatile Vikings, and for some reason, Rise of the Mountain King came to mind. Maybe it's all the celestial-ness going on. What we're trying to say is Asgardian Fire isn't the most original Norse-themed slot players are likely to bump into.However, if you're willing to ignore the elephant in the room, then there is a cracking game here for Norse mythology fans to experience. On the front end, Neon Valley Studios has made great use of the subject matter, and Asgardian Fire packs a mighty audio-visual wallop. At 5,000x the bet, its max win while decent could've walloped harder, but if that figure and the clear imitation aren't a bother, Asgardian Fire is worth getting the hammer a-swinging for.

title: Hyper Burst
structured_summary: Hyper Burst is a volcano-themed slot by Yggdrasil featuring a dreamy island vibe with a mystical atmosphere. Its main attraction is the Hyper Respins feature, expanding colossal lava reels and increasing multipliers up to 10x during consecutive wins. The reviewer finds the game rewarding when the feature triggers big wins but notes it can be slow and frustrating otherwise. The aesthetics include misty landscapes and intense tribal drumming that build excitement as the respins progress.
review: Hyper Burst: OverviewThe latent power of volcanoes drives the action in Hyper Burst from Yggdrasil Gaming. With streamlined features, Hyper Burst can nevertheless pull in all sorts of modifiers when respins are doing their thing. The result is a game that plays out much like the volcano it portrays. Meaning, Hyper Burst can lie dormant a lot of the time, but every so often blows its stack in an impressive fashion.The first look at Hyper Burst brought the slot Tahiti Gold to mind, yet it's not quite so moody. The volcano in the distance isn't as intimidating as the one found in ELK's version. Hyper Burst is dreamier. You can imagine 'Over the Rainbow' playing on a ukulele as you float over the misty trees and turquoise water into the scene, much like the intro to Coming to America.Hyper Burst - 10x respinWhen Hyper Burst gets going it's a different story. In the beginning, the sounds are menacing enough. When respins build, the drumming and chanting increases, so when big wins occur, it feels like some sort of bizarre island ritual is taking place. It gets pretty intense.Hyper Burst can be played on any device, with bets from 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin available. The activity takes place on a game grid consisting of 6 reels, 4 rows, and 25 paylines, producing an RTP rate of 96.02%. The modest number of paylines isn't super effective in pulling in wins a lot of the time - until colossal symbols are created via the features.Wins are fairly regular in theory, officially better than 1 in 5 spins due to a hit frequency of 22.3%. It might not feel like it a lot of the time though. Rounding off the math model is a medium/high volatility, so don't expect to go all the way with Hyper Respins too often.To land a win, you need three to six matching symbols, left to right on a payline. Symbols reinforce the Gold series vibe, well the premiums at least, which are four masks in blue, green, purple and red colours. Premiums are worth 4 to 8 times the stake for combinations of six of a kind. At the lower end of the paytable is Jack to Ace card royals, worth 1 to 2 times the bet for a line of six.The golden wild appears in any position to substitute for all other symbols. It is also by far the most valuable tile in the game - six of a kind is worth 100x, and the likelihood of landing a line of wilds increases when they appear in colossal sizes. That completes the picture when it comes to symbols in Hyper Burst. There are no scatters, yet there is an extensive respins feature generating the game's best moments.Hyper Burst: FeaturesWhile there might technically be only one overarching feature – Hyper Respins, several extras splinter off them to enhance the experience. Every win triggers Respin Mode which comes with additional bonuses. The first respin joins 2 of the middle four reels together to form a 2x2 colossal lava reel. Each consecutive win in Respin Mode triggers another respin and makes the lava reel grow in size. The next increment expands the colossal lava reel to 3x3, and finally to 4x4 in size which is known as the Giga reel – no relation to Giga Blox.When the 4x4 reel is active the game shifts from Respin Mode to Hyper Mode. Here, wins continue to trigger respins, but a win multiplier also comes into play. The multiplier starts at x2, moving up through x3, x5, topping out at x10 if you keep on winning. There is no limit to how many respins will mount up as long as consecutive winners continue to be hit.Hyper Burst: VerdictIt's almost as if Yggdrasil took a page out of their partner Avatar UX's playbook when designing Hyper Burst. Similar to slots in the PopWins range, the aim of Hyper Burst is to get on a massive roll where features build off of each other, getting bigger and more potent as they move forward. In this regard, it's also similar to Yggdrasil's own Valley of the Gods 2. Like the Egyptian themed sequel, when a bunch of Hyper Respins link up, they can be a real treat. The earth-shaking effects amplify the enjoyment too, a nice touch from the Yggdrasil sound team there.They say it only takes a spark to light a volcano, which might be true, but sparks can also burn out quickly on their own without making much of a fuss. Hyper Burst is a game that has to go all the way, or a significant part of the way, to get much out of it. During testing, part of the way meant wins in the 200x+ region, but getting past that amount was a hyper rare occurrence. Interestingly, after a session of ups and downs, the bankroll ended up pretty much where it started.There are loads of single or double respins which don't go anywhere. Yet despite that, Like Valley of the Gods 2, it's easy to hit the play button one more time. Just one good roll is all it would take to hit Hyper Burst's potential of 12,800 times the stake. Okay, it would have to be a pretty epic chain of respins, but still, knowing it is possible makes it easy to justify repeat playing.It can get frustrating if you're caught in a patch of dead spins, or short runs of respins which are more tease than thrill. Still, Hyper Burst is a good example of a game that does perfectly well without a tradition free spins bonus, so if you're into extended cascade sequences and potent respins, it's most definitely worth a look.

title: Hyper Star
structured_summary: Hyper Star is a Vegas-themed slot featuring a bright, nightclub vibe with classic casino symbols. The game includes Rolling Reels, Multiplier Trails, Free Spins, and three jackpot levels for varied gameplay. The reviewer found the slot visually flashy but ultimately unoriginal and uninspiring in its gameplay. Its aesthetics combine dazzling lights and reflective surfaces with a lounge-style soundtrack, creating a somewhat subdued casino atmosphere.
review: Hyper Star: Slot OverviewMicrogaming associates Gameburger Studios adds to their 'Hyper' range of slots with a brash Vegas wannabe titled Hyper Star. So far, sister slots in the studio's Hyper series have been pretty run of the mill games, often clinging to the coattails of Gameburger's hit 9 Masks of Fire. Hyper Star splits into a different direction, but where it ends up is just as run of the mill really, relying on dazzling visuals to try to jazz up common features such as Rolling Reels, Multiplier Trails, Free Spins, and Jackpots.Hyper Star bills itself as 'an undisclosed fun place of gaming and clubbing at night, hinting Las Vegas.' That's a pretty accurate description as the game certainly is bright, lit by a multitude of lights and reflective surfaces like a rhinestone jacket or the inside of a disco ball. Hyper Star might have worked better if Gameburger had pushed the Vegas concept even further, going completely over the top. There is plenty of sparkle as it is, but when combined with the loungey soundtrack, it kind of felt we were stuck outside the casino queueing up instead of going wild in the middle of a heaving gambling den.Played on a 5x3 sized game area, Hyper Star is available on any device, offering stakes of 20 p/c to $/€40 per spin. With volatility rated as 'Very High', the game is RTP variable, where the most optimal return value is 96.05% - beware, depending on the market, Hyper Star may be set as low as 86.72%. The hit rate, meanwhile, weighs in at 32.88% and occurs when at least three matching symbols land left to right in adjacent reels from the Lefthand side. Keeping track of paylines is irrelevant, meaning players get 243 ways to win.The symbols used throughout Hyper Star further the Las Vegas hinting and consist of clubs, diamonds, hearts, spades, cherries, dice, casino chips, bells, dollar signs, and sevens. From the dice up, rewards for landing a five of a kid win range from 3 to 10 times your stake. Lastly, appearing on reels 2, 3, or 4 are Star wilds, substituting for all symbols, including scatters. Wilds are also needed to trigger the Jackpot Game; let's take a look.Hyper Star: Slot FeaturesHyper Star - jackpot gameWhen playing Hyper Star, the features players can look forward to are made up of Rolling Reels, a Multiplier Trail, Free Spins, and Jackpots.Rolling ReelsRolling Reels are active in both the base game and in free spins. This mechanic removes winning symbols from the reels, making way for new symbols to drop down into the gaps. Rolling Reels can award consecutive wins from a single spin, only ending when no new winning combination is formed from a drop.Multiplier ReelThe Multiplier Reel is tied directly to Rolling Reels, being a win multiplier which increases with each consecutive Roll. During the base game, the trail increases from x1 on the initial land to x2, x3, then x5 on the first, second, and third Roll, respectively. During free spins, the Multiplier Trail increases to x3, x6, x9, then x15.Free SpinsLanding 3 or more scatter symbols in any position awards free spins. Each triggering way awards 8 free spins, up to a possible starting number of 32. Free spins use the higher win multiplier trail going up to x15 as stated above whilst its reels also hold more wild stars. Free spins are retrigged when at least 3 scatter symbols hit.JackpotsJackpots can be won from the base game or free spins. Whenever wild symbols land, they are collected, and when Rolling Reels sequences are complete, there is a chance the Jackpot Bonus triggers. If activated, one of the three jackpots is awarded. Jackpots hold fixed values of 15x, 100x, or 5,000x the bet for the Minor, Major, and Grand prize.Hyper Star: Slot VerdictYeah, nah, don't know, we just weren't feeling this one. Probably because despite all the glitz and glam, Hyper Star's looks and style of gaming has been done so many times before, it felt a bit plasticky. The slot does try hard to overcome the underlying banality with an abundance of flashing lights and faux Las Vegas decor but winds up chilling off the strip like a big-budget travel deal gone awry. No doubt players who like this combination of features will probably be thrilled with a new flashy addition to the fold. Otherwise, Hyper Star delivers quotidian gaming that can be found anywhere and everywhere.There's not much to add about the features since they're the sort of thing players will be well accustomed to. Rolling Reels do play well with the 243 ways to win system, and Multiplier Trails in both phases of play is a bonus too. This sort of setup has been a crowd-pleaser since it was popularized by the likes of Gonzo's Quest back in the day and is still going strong. Players following Gameburger's 'Hyper' range might be happy seeing something that doesn't follow the 9 Masks of Fire script like Hyper Strike or Hyper Joker did. Though at heart, the games all share a similar template of spinning for jackpot prizes. As to top rewards, the Grand jackpot in Hyper Star is more than double what is possible in the two previously mentioned Hyper games, yet the overall potential is about the same, maxing out at 7,250 times the stake.Hyper Star does its thing capably enough, but what it had to offer was just too commonplace to get enthusiastic about. So, after a run-through, there was little to no compunction to cross paths with Hyper Star a second time.

title: Amped
structured_summary: Amped is a neon retro-themed slot centered around music and amplifiers, blending hip, minimalist vibes with EDM elements. It features four distinct free spin modes triggered by colored scatter wilds, plus scatter wild respins in the base game. The reviewer finds it a middle-of-the-road, low-to-medium volatility game that offers steady engagement but lacks excitement or depth. Visually, Amped uses bright, simple symbols with equalizer effects and a laid-back techno soundtrack, creating a chilled, understated club atmosphere.
review: Amped: Slot OverviewDeveloper Relax Gaming engages in a bit of entendre in their musically based slot Amped. Not only does it refer to the amplifier in a stereo system, it also takes advantage of the hip use of the word to ‘get excited’. It’s quite a hip game all round, riding the neon retro fad that’s popular in iGaming. Amped offers several popular features as well, four of them to power four different kinds of free spins rounds. title: Cursed Treasure
structured_summary:
