review: Legend of the Sword: Slot OverviewIf there is a style of gameplay the Microgaming family of designers can't get enough of it is the one sparked by Gameburger Studio's 9 Masks of Fire. The technique of using scatter symbols to trigger prizes of ascending values constantly oozes out of the workshop, appearing again and again under various guises. This time it has been paired with another regular of the slot's scene - King Arthur and his knights of the round table. If you've played 9 Masks or any of its imitators, you'll have a good idea of what to expect from Legend of the Sword. However, developer Snowborn has clipped on a couple of less common elements, so if you're up for pulling swords out of stones, let's see what they are.Displayed on a piece of parchment taking up most of the screen is Legend of the Sword's 5-reel, 3,125 payline game grid. To the left of it, a prize ladder lays out the various rewards players can win in relation to the number of Excalibur Scatters in view or collected during free spins. The values are multiples of the bet, so they automatically update when changing stakes. The rest of the screen is taken up by Arthurian imagery, including Excalibur stuck in a stone, forests, mountains, and mythical Camelot teetering on a rocky outcrop. The mythical feeling is increased by a rich, chorus led soundtrack and some glowing dots on the screen. Are they fireflies or spirits? It's hard to say, but whatever they are, they succeed in adding a dash of mystery.Playable on smartphones, tablets, or desktop devices, Legend of the Sword offers stakes of 20 p/c to $/€24 per spin. The RTP is pretty decent if playing the most generous 96.12% version; otherwise, there's also a 94.08% version, or lower depending on the market. Players into these game types should be aware that Legend of the Sword's math model is highly volatile, though it technically lands a winning combination 36.82% of the time.Wins hit when three or more matching symbols land left to right in any position from the left-hand side. This provides 3,125 ways to win, which is unusual to find in these sorts of games. Sword symbols are what you want to see in great numbers as they are the scatter, while regular paying tiles include four-card suit low pays, then shields, battle helms, cups, and crowns as the four premiums. When landing a five-symbol combination made up of high pays, a payout of 4 to 10 times the stake is coming your way. There's also a wild, substituting for any symbol on the reels except Excalibur Scatters or Camelot Free Spins symbols.Legend of the Sword: Slot FeaturesThe Excalibur Scatters feature might be the main event, but Legend of the Sword also offers a slightly unorthodox round of free spins to go with it. To get your hands on an instant cash prize in the base game, you'll need to land 5 or more Excalibur Scatters. The amount of cash awarded is 2, 5, 10, 100, 1,000, or 10,000 times the bet when 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, or 10 scatters are in view.It is possible to win scatter prizes during the free spins bonus game as well, and players get a helping hand in doing so. Free spins activate when 3 Camelot symbols land in the base game to trigger the Camelot Free Spins feature.The round initially begins with 3 spins. Excalibur Scatters are collected when they land and also reset the spin counter. In addition, each Excalibur Scatter collected increases a win multiplier by +1, which is applied to any regular ways win. After free spins have finished, the total number of collected scatter symbols is tallied up, and any applicable prize is awarded – as described above.Legend of the Sword: Slot VerdictOkay, we get it, the Microgaming team like the 9 Masks of Fire thing. Snowborn certainly does, since Legend of the Sword is their third game so far to use the format, making up nearly half of their portfolio. Legend of the Sword follows on from Egyptian Tombs and Coin Bash, all focusing on the scatter win concept. Each one has offered slightly different side extras, and their themes have had nothing in common. Features wise, Legend of the Slot is quite close to Just For The Win's slot Elven Gold. Both have a touch of fantasy about them, revolve around scatter wins, and have a similar three free spins bonus game.Where Legend of the Sword differs is its win multiplier during free spins and its pay all-ways system. You might think this would lead to better non-scatter wins during free spins, yet it didn't tend to be the case, during testing at least. To be fair, the potential for decent ways wins appears to be there for the lucky. The main event will always be the scatter collection prize of up to 10,000x the bet. Unless you rack up at least 9 scatters, don't expect to collect a whole lot, however.If you're looking to squeeze the biggest payouts possible from this category of games, then Legend of the Sword's max win puts it around the middle of the scale. It's not the highest - that would be Emerald Gold with its 25,000x, though Legend is a lot more impressive than 9 Mask's original 2,000x top prize.Essentially, Legend of the Sword still boils down to landing as many scatters as possible to tap its riches. It is an ok example, and if you add up the individual parts, it does offer a somewhat unique experience – for connoisseurs or enthusiasts at least. Players not as excited by this sort of gaming or who are suffering from 9 Masks fatigue might not pick up on the nuances or be all that convinced by them.

title: Forge of Fortunes

review: Forge of Fortunes: Slot OverviewEver been flicking through the cluster of streaming services such as Netflix, Prime Video, or Disney+, et al. and felt so overwhelmed by the options you felt the urge to flee to the nearest windmill and read a book in peace? Payouts start at 2x the bet then rise through 3x, 5x, 8x, 10x, 15x, 20x, 30x, 50x, 75x, 100x, 200x, 500x, 1,000x, and maxing out at 2,500x the bet for the respective number of consecutive winning respins.There are a couple of things to look out for. Playing Forge of Fortunes brought to mind a relatively recent release titled Viral Spiral, another pared-back slot from Red Tiger, so if you're into the simplicity of it all, that one might be worth checking out as well.There's not a lot to it, yet for the most part, Forge of Fortunes provided a surprisingly entertaining time. Play'n GO has instilled the slot with a solid replayability factor, making it easy to bang away on the spin button. How have they done so? During testing, Forge of Fortunes felt quite well balanced between dead spins and wins. This is important in a slot with such binary outcomes - when you press the play button, you either get 2 or 3 golden nuggets in the required position, and something happens, or nothing does. You could say this in most, if not all slots, yet the outcomes could be starker in a game with so few bells and whistles. It also helps that the developers have squeezed a lot out of the visuals while meshing the theme with the Forging Re-spins feature. A decent number of respin triggers occurred during our sessions to charge off on, though, for us, they didn't run too far, the slag symbol dropping in to slam the brakes on. The 2,500x max win isn't exactly huge either. However, when keeping in mind everything else Forge of Fortunes has going on, it's a relatively lofty target.For a mining-themed game that is as straightforward to play as it is weighty in feel, Forge of Fortunes is a potential option - like a rock in a mine shaft, ready to be pounded around a bit. Whether the results turn out to be metaphorical fool's gold or the real deal depends on how those Forging Re-spins turn out. It's hard to envisage Forge of Fortunes having a massive shelf life, but its one-line antics can be fun while they last.

title: Charlie Chance in the Curse of Cleopatra
structured_summary: Charlie Chance in the Curse of Cleopatra features an adventurous Egyptian tomb-raiding theme with a comedic twist. review: Charlie Chance and the Curse of Cleopatra: Slot OverviewAh, Charlie Chance, we meet again. You have to feel for the guy or even wonder why he keeps on bothering. Then again, if life knocks you down, you've just gotta get up, dust yourself off, and keep on livin' - like our man Charlie. This time he's out of the underworld at least, yet he hasn't completely turned his fortune around. Now, he's traipsed off to Egypt for some tomb raiding in the hopes of stumbling across Pharaohs' riches. This being Charlie, though, he's woken up Cleopatra, who really isn't too happy about the turn of events. Let's not fret over exactly how she reawakened, to instead help Charlie return Cleopatra to her former non-mummified glory and hopefully pick up a few coins along the way.Curse of Cleopatra differs radically from the previous two games in the series in terms of gameplay, yet much of what made Hell To Pay and the XREELZ unique remains. Basically, this means a 1930s animated Betty Boop vibe, which Play'n GO has recaptured for Curse of Cleopatra. In the middle of the tomb lies a 6x6 grid, which pays when clusters of at least 5 matching symbols land adjacent to each other. The rest of the visuals depict riches, chests, mummies, and skeletons, all with a lean toward the comedic rather than the spooky. In fact, the game isn't a million miles away from the Asterix and Cleopatra film, the Belgian animated one that is, released in the 1960s, possessing a similarly fun attitude.Playable on any desktop, tablet, or mobile device, Charlie Chance and the Curse of Cleopatra comes with stake levels of 20 p/c to $/€100 per spin. Be on the lookout for RTP values which vary depending on the market. The one you want is 96.25%, dropping to 94.27% or lower in the less desirable options. If you prefer playing the most volatile grid slots on the market, you better look away now because Curse of Cleopatra's math has a medium setting, rated at 6 out of 10. However, winning potential is quite comparable to the best that Play'n GO has to offer in this slot category.When winning clusters hit, they are removed from the grid by the cascade system, refilling the empty positions with batches of new symbols. This can cause other clusters to form, repeating the cascade process until no new wins hit. Consecutive wins not only pile on coin wins, they lead directly into several of the features. The pay symbols include 8 hieroglyphics of varying descriptions, ranging in value from 20 to 500 times the total stake for clusters of 15+ premium symbols. Charlie actually helps you out here, as he appears on the Charlie Mega Wild to replace any other pay symbols. He only appears via one of the modifiers; let's check it out.Charlie Chance and the Curse of Cleopatra: Slot FeaturesThe end goal of Charlie Chance and the Curse of Cleopatra is triggering its free spins bonus round, which is supplemented by a win multiplier plus three side modifiers. The win multiplier is active in both base and bonus games. It starts on x1, and for every 3 consecutive cascades, it increases by +1. In the base game, the multiplier maxes out at x3, while in free spins, it can go higher.Randomly, on any spin, the Flying Scarab Wilds feature may trigger. When it does, 5-8 flying scarabs float around the screen then land on the grid. These wilds substitute all other symbols except the scatter.On any random non-winning spin, the Serpent's Trail feature may activate. When triggered, a snake appears on the grid and creates a chain of symbols. This chain of symbols is either destroyed from view or transformed into the same matching symbol.The third modifier is Cleo's Columns which also triggers on random spins. When activated, a pair of reels land displaying matching symbols – new symbols that land on these reels via cascades do not synchronise. This is how the Charlie Mega symbol may appear, which locks in position through the cascade sequence, then any low-value symbols connecting are removed, and new symbols fall into the gaps. Charlie Mega symbols then turn wild, and any wins are paid.Landing 3 scatter symbols awards 8 free spins, while any additional scatters in view award an extra +4 free spins each. Any current win multiplier is carried over. In free spins, the win multiplier increases every 3 consecutive cascades like the base game, but now it can go as high as x10 and does not reset between free spins. Cleo's Columns is also active on every free spin, with the chance of activating the Charlie Mega symbol. Lastly, each scatter that lands awards +1 additional free spin, up to a cap of 150.Charlie Chance and the Curse of Cleopatra: Slot VerdictThey might all share a parallel look, yet Play'n GO takes the Charlie Chance series on a satisfying new tangent in Curse of Cleopatra. So far, we've gone from pacey 3-reel gaming to 5-reel multiplier mayhem, and now to a full-blown grid slot replete with cascades alongside all the trimmings typically associated with this style. Through it all, two things have tied the series together – the attractive 1930s visuals and Charlie Chance's vacillating fortunes.From a monetary standpoint, if you could pick one game to maximise Charlie's luck on, it wouldn't be this one. Of the three, Curse of Cleopatra offers the lowest potential in the range so far. It's not exactly a pinchfist, though, offering top rewards of 5,500x the bet, which compares favourably with Play'n GO's big grid slot hits, Reactoonz or the follow-up Reactoonz 2, for example. The gameplay isn't a paradigm shift over what Play'n GO has released before, but there are no issues over what Charlie Chance and the Curse of Cleopatra does either.Unless you're a grid slot bruiser who requires an ultra tightly wound math model capable of producing monumental wins, there's a lot to like about Curse of Cleopatra. Its combination of flowing gameplay, positive off-beat visuals, and intermeshable features make it easy to just go along with Charlie on his search for riches to see where he ends up.

title: Baker's Treat
structured_summary:

review: Baker's Treat: Slot ReviewBaker's Treat is a 5-reel, 3-row video slot with 15 fixed paylines which pays left to right and right to left. Player's can bet from 0.15 to 75 EUR per spin. The game definately has a British touch to it, or as Play'n GO puts it - It is the most quintessentially British thing since someone put milk in tea.As can be seen in the screenshot above, the reel set is made out of an outdoor table with cakes as symbols. A bit unusual, but not something we haven't seen before. The soundtrack is fun and happy, with the sound level increasing as wins are accumulated, much in the same manner as on Reactoonz and many other slots developed by Play'n GO.Baker's Treat comes with 5 low value symbols - the pink, yellow, purple and green Macarons. The 5 premium symbols are represented by various desserts - Strawberry Sponges, Lemon Cheesecakes, Carrot Cakes, Blueberry Pies and Cupcakes. There's of course also a Wild symbol in this game which comes in the form of a Berry Layer cake (don't ask).The Strawberry Sponge and the Wild are the top symbols, both with the same value, giving you 40 times the bet for 5 across a payline.Baker's Treat: FeaturesBaker's Treat comes with a main game feature and a bonus feature called Bake Off. They may seem a bit complicated to understand at first, but we'll do our best to explain.Each reel has it's own cake assigned to it, with the most valuable ones furthest to the right. Displayed above the reels are token collecting meters. If a full stack of premium cakes lands on it's associated reel the player collects one token. When 3 tokens have been collected to fill the meter, the Flour Power Spins is triggered. The Flour Power Spins bet value will be the average total bet from every spin that results in a symbol collection.Each cake (reel set) has it's own unique feaure that will be played when a symbol collection has been completed as described above. They are as followed:Cupcake Power: 3 Free Spins in which two reels are matchingBlueberry Pie Power: 3 Free Spins in which one reel is wild.Carrot Cake Power: 3 Free Spins in which all Carrot Cake symbols are upgraded to Wild.Lemon Cheesecake Power: 3 Free Spins in which all regular Wilds expand to fill the reel.Strawberry Sponge Power: 3 Free Spins in which all Macarons are converted into one type of Macaron.The biggest potential can be found in the Bake Off feature through which it is possible to win up to 5000x. If all 5 cake symbols land on their associated reels, the Bake Off feature is triggered. An extra spin is awarded if a cake is stacked on it's reel as the Bake Off feature is triggered, so in case you would trigger all cakes stacked you would go into the Bake Off feature with 10 free spins. Moreover, if the Bake Off feature is triggered during a Flour Power Spin, an instant prize of 80x will be awarded.Now, the thing with the Bake Off feature is that one Flour Power feature is activated on each spin and remains active throughout Bake Off. Going into this bonus with extra spins means every extra spin will be played with all features activated!Baker's Treat: ConclusionBaker's Treat will definitely not appeal to everyone due to its theme and visuals, but it nevertheless turned out to be quite an enjoyable game, so don't judge the book by its cover. It's kind of relaxing in a weird way and an all around feel-good game. With that said, we can't help to feel like something's missing, and aside from the 5 collect features in the main game, we would like to have seen something with a bit more potential. But as there is none, players will more or less be left chasing the Bake Off feature.Baker's Treat is a high variance game (9 out of 10 on Play'n GO's volatility index) with a default RTP of 96.04%. It offers respectable 5000x potential, so it may be worth giving a few spins even if you're into British tea parties (lol).

title: I Hate Fairytales
structured_summary: I Hate Fairytales offers a rebellious twist on classic fairytales, featuring edgy characters in a graffiti-covered fantasy world. review: I Hate Fairytales: Slot OverviewFairytales have been around for a long time, and the classics remain amongst us to this very day. As for personal fairytales, these change with tides, moods, and current zeitgeists. Where once it might have been the dream of many to marry a prince or princess and live happily ever after, modern fairytales often ditch all that in favour of getting big on social media to accrue truckloads of cash and clout.Software provider Elysium Studios, as of early 2024 acquired by supplier Swintt for an undisclosed sum, has taken it upon themselves to rewrite some of the classic stories. The slot is I Hate Fairytales, which thrusts players into an enchanting world of magic and wonder, but one flipped on its head by a cast of characters fed up with the usual fairytale shtick. In this fantasy land of graffiti-ridden castles, players bump into characters such as Snow Wild, Aria, and Rapunsell, in a world that might have been designed by Walt Disney if he'd gotten fed up with the kiddie stuff, rebelled, switching from sugar, spice and all things nice, to all things… nasty. A little bit nasty.I Hate Fairytales slot - base gameThe gambling action in I Hate Fairytales occurs on a 5x4 reelset where 1,024 ways to win are provided for calculating wins. Pulling levers and whatnot, hidden away out of sight, is a 4 out of 5 medium/high volatile math model, generating a maximum RTP of 94%. The coin+ button opens up the game's stake selection, where options range from 20 c to $/€40.I Hate Fairytales' pay symbols are quite neat, made up of 4 low-pay cupcakes with nibbles taken out of them and four high-pay characters, including a unicorn blowing a rainbow from its rear end. Hitting 5 OAK winning combinations awards 0.3 to 0.6 times the bet for the cupcakes and 0.7 to 1 times the bet for the remaining pay symbols. Wilds assist in the formation of winning combinations by replacing any of the regular pay symbols.I Hate Fairytales: Slot FeaturesI Hate Fairytales slot - Smash bonusI Hate Fairytales randomly drops 3 character-linked features onto its reels in the base game and in the free spins bonus round. The characters are Snow Wild, Aria, and Rapunsell.Snow Wild randomly shows up to place wild symbols on the screen.Aria randomly places wilds that cover whole reels and grant respins. On each free respin, each Mega Wild moves one reel to the left until it drops off the grid. Free respins continue until there are no more Mega Wilds in view.Rapunsell randomly expands the reels upwards, and a win multiplier is assigned to each expanded reel. Free respins are also awarded. On each respin the expanded reels shrink, as do the win multipliers. Free spins continue until all expanded reels return to their original size. All ways wins are multiplied by the sum of the win multipliers of participating reels.Free SpinsGetting 3 free spins scatter symbols on the leftmost, middle, and rightmost reels awards 8 free spins. For the free spins round, all reels expand to become 6 rows high, and the 3 Princess features may randomly activate. In free spins, Rapunsell does not expand reels. Instead, the Rapunsell feature randomly places win multipliers above reels, which do not reset until the round ends. A multiplier placed on an existing multiplier adds to its value.Smash BonusHitting 3 bonus scatter symbols on the leftmost, middle, and rightmost reels triggers the Smash Bonus. In this round, players click the entities on the screen with a hammer to reveal a bet multiplier. When all entities have been beaten out of existence, the total prize amount is paid.Bonus BuyBoth of I Hate Fairytales' bonus rounds can be bought from the bonus buy. Free spins for 150 times the bet and the Smash Bonus for 27 times the bet.I Hate Fairytales slot - free spinsI Hate Fairytales: Slot VerdictNot knocking all those Jack and the Beanstalk games, but it was refreshing to see non-kiddy versions of fairy tales turn up in a slot. Elysium Studios probably had a little chuckle or two to themselves when making I Hate Fairytales, and a unicorn spewing forth a rainbow from its butt cheeks is inspired. All rib-tickling stuff, and it wouldn't be the worst thing if Elysium pushed the humour angle even further in future releases. But, it is a fine line between humour and disgust, and some jokes are only funny for those who are in on the gag.Another stand out was I Hate Fairytales' Smash Bonus. It's not every day you get to bop little beasties for cash prizes. This was not where big cash prizes eventuated, however. The most that was coaxed out of the Smash Bonus was 50x the bet. Whether big rare prizes are a possibility or not is not made clear. Maybe they are, maybe they aren't. The lack of transparency was not encouraging in all honesty. What was encouraging was I Hate Fairytales' impressive (at least on paper) 33,934x winning potential, meaning that either a monster reward lurks in the Smash Bonus or, what seems more likely, the free spins combination of larger reel set, multipliers and wild features contain quite a punch.Someone at Elysium Studios might hate fairytales, but the game they've crafted is hard to dislike. While it may not boast the highest production values in slots, it's clear that a lot of creativity and effort went into its design. Aside from the RTP, which many studios seem to be lowering themselves to these days anyway, I Hate Fairytales serves up a playful fairytale alternative, with a set of features of the odd curiosity type as well as the slap you across the cheek with a leather riding glove type.

review: Wild Expedition: Slot OverviewFollowing in the footsteps of fantasy couple crossovers like Belle and Chewbacca or Daenerys and Kratos, online slot Wild Expedition from Red Tiger mashes two personalities you might not have envisaged hooking up. When a Cara symbol lands next to a Nick symbol, Nick turns into a wild and locks for the next spin. If Red Tiger went to the bother of naming them, they could have fleshed out the story to build a stronger empathetic connection with them. As it is, you basically want 'Nick' to show up in his wild form, helped by 'Cara' who turns him sticky to string together wins. Usually, though, they are replacing regular pay symbols to complete line wins.9 Masks of Fire HyperSpins: Slot Features9 Masks of Fire HyperSpins - free spinsThe motivation for the re-release was to marry 9 Masks of Fire to the HyperSpins mechanic. The rest remains the same, meaning players get free spins with multipliers and mask scatter prizes.The HyperSpins feature is only available in the base game and allows players to spin individual reels as many times as they like. This gives you the opportunity to land needed extra scatter symbols, more mask symbols, or complete line wins. The cost of spinning each reel is dependent on what is already on the reels. Only wins involving the respun reel are paid, and changing the stake will keep the reels as they are but increase the HyperSpins cost.Keep an eye out for Mask symbols, appearing in any position - landing 3 or more of them awards a cash prize. The greater the number of masks in view, the larger the reward, so 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9 masks on the reels equates to a win worth 1x, 5, 15x, 40x, 100x, 500x, or 2,000x the bet respectively.Scatter symbols appear on reels 2, 3, or 4, and 3 of them in view awards a spin of the free spin wheel, plus a payout of 1x the bet. Each wedge of the free spins wheel contains a number of free spins and a multiplier value. It is possible to win 10 to 30 free spins with an x2 or x3 multiplier. The multiplier applies to all wins in free spins except mask scatter prizes. Moreover,  landing 3 scatter symbols retriggers the feature, awarding the same number of free spins that were initially won from the wheel.9 Masks of Fire HyperSpins: Slot VerdictAs you'd probably imagine, since the main gameplay has remained untouched, how you thought about the original slot will dictate your thoughts on this one. HyperSpins is an aftermarket add-on that in no way changes the core experience. For some, this will be music to their ears. The first one seemed to release a flood gate of similarly styled scatter prize-winning slots. Like they say, 'ya cain't beat the original', so a re-release might be just what fans need to reignite the love affair. On the other side of the coin, if you missed the point of the first 9 Masks, this one won't hit any harder either.HyperSpins are an acquired taste as well, but in this game, they make a bit more sense. For instance, let's say you've got a few masks on several of the reels. It can cost significantly less to spin an individual reel in hopes of landing more masks and scoring some prize money than hitting the actual spin button. Sometimes this pays off to a hilarious degree. At others, you can find yourself smashing the HyperSpins button like a woodpecker on crack and getting absolutely nothing for your troubles except a hole where your balance used to be.One suggestion might be to try and not see the HyperSpins feature as a way of gaming the system, even though sometimes it can seem that way. In many ways, HyperSpins makes the ideal partner to 9 Masks of Fire, so the amalgamation makes a lot of sense. It adds a new dynamic to the way you can attack the game, which fans of the first may appreciate.

title: Spin Spin Sugar
structured_summary: Spin Spin Sugar is a candy-themed slot featuring a sweet, sugary world with traditional confectionery visuals. It offers familiar mechanics including a Link&Win bonus ladder, free spins with multipliers, and an optional Upsizer feature for boosting rounds. The reviewer finds it entertaining but not particularly original, offering solid gameplay with a high volatility and decent win potential. The game’s aesthetics are soft pinks and purples with upbeat audio and cheerful candy-themed scenery, providing a classic, indulgent slot experience.
review: Spin Spin Sugar: Slot OverviewIf your teeth haven't already decayed and fallen out from the inundation of sweet-themed slots, and you're in the mood, why not come have a look at another one from Games Global partner Slingshot Studios? The name of the game is Spin Spin Sugar, which brings together a real mix of familiar features and mechanics shared amongst the Games Global family of studios. A Link&Win element is there, somewhat unsurprisingly, as its one of Slingshot Studios' more beloved gadgets of late, alongside a 9 Masks of Fire style bonus symbol prize ladder (including a twist), plus free spins with a line win multiplier, and optional Upsizer feature boosts.Quite a pick 'n mix of gaming devices then, and for the outer layer holding it all together, Slingshot Studios has used a traditional design for its sweet-filled game. This means heavy use of soft pinky, purpley colours, an upbeat soundtrack, rolling hills covered in candy canes, plus a general happy-go-lucky, why not indulge a bit every now and then (sensibly) type vibe. A classic sweet slot, in other words, that should charm the eyes and ears of fans of this style.Spin Spin Sugar slot - base gameJust as Spin Spin Sugar's audio-visuals have been designed in a way that is unlikely to cause much surprise for players used to candy slots, the same assessment applies to the game's numbers. For one, it comes with a maximum RTP value of 96.26%, though three lower settings are available, and runs on a highly volatile math model. Playable on any device, Spin Spin Sugar provides stake levels of 20 p/c to $/€50 per paid spin and shoots off wins at a rate of 38.83% on the top RTP configuration model.The gaming occurs on a 5-reel, 4-row matrix, with 40 paylines supplied for landing normal line wins on. Winning lines are made up of three to five-of-a-kind and must start on the leftmost side of the board. One exception is the high-pay single sevens, double sevens, or triple sevens – these symbols will also pay when any combination of sevens hits. Sitting below them on the hierarchy of payouts are four lower-value candy symbols. Landing a 5 OAK low pay win awards 1 to 1.75 times the bet, while the sevens pay anywhere from 2 to 15 times the bet. Leading the way, values-wise, is the wild symbol, worth 60 times the stake for a line of five, or wilds can be used to substitute for any normal pay symbol.Spin Spin Sugar: Slot FeaturesSpin Spin Sugar slot - Upsizer featureBroken down into its constituent parts, there isn't much new going on in Spin Spin Sugar. But combine everything together, coat it in sugar, and the game starts to display more of an individual personality. Here we find the Link&Win Ladder feature, free spins with a Free Spins Randomizer, and the Upsizer.Link&Win Ladder FeatureThis feature triggers in the base game or during free spins when at least 3 bonus symbols hit on reels 2 to 4. When that happens, the triggering bonus symbols are held, and 3 respins are awarded on the middle three reels. If new bonus symbols hit, they are locked in position and set the respins back to 3. When respins end or the grid is filled an award is made. This equates to 1x, 3x, 5x, 10x, 20x, 50x, 100x, 250x, 1,000x, or 5,000x the bet when 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, or 12 bonus symbols are in view, respectively.Free SpinsTo get into free spins, you'll need 3 scatter symbols to land on reels 2 to 4 (awarding 1x the bet). Then, the Free Spins Randomizer spins to award 8-15 free spins, a multiplier of x2-x5, and a bonus level density of 1-4. Before free spins begin, however, players may be able to boost them via the Upsizer feature. The cost of upgrading each of the three parts of the round – free spins, multiplier, or Bonus level density is clearly displayed on the screen. As mentioned, it is possible to trigger the Link&Win Ladder feature from free spins, and free spins can be retriggered. The only other thing to mention is that the multiplier applies only to line wins.Spin Spin Sugar slot - free spinsSpin Spin Sugar: Slot VerdictSpin Spin Sugar was a game which might have been a clone, but then again, it might have just felt like that because a lot, maybe all, of its gaming features have appeared elsewhere in one form or another. On a feature level, it's very close to a previous Slingshot Studios game called Jade Shuriken, which dropped about half a year or so back before Spin Spin Sugar did. However, a number of changes have been made since then. As well as one or two feature tweaks, Spin Spin Sugar is a lot more volatile than Jade Shuriken was and packs twice the potential, which is kind of interesting considering Jade Shuriken was an action-packed slot about battling warriors.Jade Shuriken was a more strikingly memorable game visually, though, with neat, animated cartoon-style graphics and a greater original overall feel. Spin Spin Sugar, by comparison, is much more; how can we put it? Commonplace? Confectionary slots aren't exactly in short supply, and Spin Spin Sugar doesn't do a heck of a lot to make it really stand out from the pack.It doesn't do anything despicable either, though, and neatly integrates its free spins round with the ever-popular bonus symbol/cash prize ladder mechanic that has been prevalent for a while. Factor in the free spins line multiplier, variable bonus symbol density, not to mention the Link&Win slant to the cash prize ladder feature, and there's likely to be a level of entertainment to be had here for certain sweet-toothed gamblers. Maybe swap expectations of something ground-breaking with a less ambitious serving of proven features in an agreeable confectionery setting, and Spin Spin Sugar might be worth a try.

title: Om Nom
structured_summary: Om Nom is a casual slot themed around junk food with a Candy Crush vibe, offering a cozy and familiar gaming experience. It features a Mystery Symbol multiplier and free spins with added wilds, enhancing winning potential up to 4,800x stake. The reviewer praises its simple yet captivating gameplay, improved payout potential, and charming design. The game sports minimalist graphics with symbols resembling smartphone icons and a jazzy soundtrack that complements the relaxed yet engaging atmosphere.
review: Om Nom (Hacksaw Gaming): OverviewThe oddly named Om Nom is Hacksaw Gaming’s second slot in their Pocketz Series optimized for mobile devices. The last one, Stick 'Em, was released not long ago and went on to become a minor hit in the gaming community. The company famous for producing online scratch cards turned out a fiendishly simple slot that was very hard to put down. Having a surprise hit on their hands might have made other companies feel like they had to try something bold and adventurous, not Hacksaw Gaming. They have stuck to an unpretentious formula that has a basic but pleasant look to it, and gameplay that is every bit as good as the first, perhaps better.The theme might have changed, but the game looks and feels similar. That is not a bad thing at all; it produces a nice comfortably familiar feel - the mark of a good sequel. While Stick 'Em was a bit of a mash-up of different symbols and imagery, Om Nom has a more coherent theme. It is all about junk food now, or comfort food as it is often called, with more than a little touch of Candy Crush to it. The name makes more sense when you see all that spinning food.The design is even more spartan that Stick 'Em was with a plain diamond-patterned two-tone background. Hacksaw stuck with 4 reels and 4 rows, but there have been several tweaks made under the hood. Win ways have been trimmed to 256, while volatility has been turned up to put it in the medium/high category. RTP is also slightly higher at 96.28%, which is always appreciated, but nothing compared to the increase in payout potential which is almost double Stick 'Em. So what we are dealing with is the same outer layer, the charm and playability, but a much gruntier engine humming away behind the scenes.Winning combinations are formed by landing 3 or more of the same symbols on adjacent reels from right to left. Each symbol is fresh from the designer and custom-built for the game, which is makes a refreshing change. There aren’t really high or low pay symbols as such because there isn’t a huge difference in value. The paytable has 8 base game symbols in total, made up of a cupcake, chocolate bar, iced lolly, popcorn, hamburger, fries, pizza slice, and an anthropomorphised doughnut dude. This last one is worth 2 times the stake for 4 of a kind. That doesn’t sound like much, but multiple combinations at once, and extra features can strike out of nowhere to dramatically improve the results.Om Nom (Hacksaw Gaming): FeaturesFree spins round in actionHacksaw has gone with few but effective when it comes to features, and there is a good mix of base and bonus game action. First up is the Multiplier feature which can launch at any time. On each spin, the game randomly selects a symbol which is displayed in the Om Nom logo above the grid. This is the Mystery Symbol, and if it matches winning symbols on the grid for that spin, then a chart next to it called the multiplier spinner comes to life. Each flipped page of the multiplier spinner has a number, and when it comes to a stop, that number is multiplied to the winning total. The multiplier spinner starts at x2 and can go as high as x100.The second feature is the Free Spins bonus which is triggered when 3 free spins symbols land. The mystery symbol/multiplier spinner stays in the game, but wilds are now introduced to the reels, which increases the chances of forming combinations and utilising the multiplier.Om Nom (Hacksaw Gaming): VerdictHacksaw Gaming has hit on just the right formula for crafting a successful follow-up slot. Keep the bits that everyone enjoyed and modify just enough elements to make it feel new. Like its predecessor, Om Nom has a great look to it and plenty of charm. Its symbols resemble modern smartphone icons, and the experience is like a compelling game from the app store. The soundtrack is spot on too with a jazzy infectious groove that helps you settle into the action. The overall effect is a slot that is both relaxing and exciting at the same time.We were curious to see where Hacksaw would go after the success of Stick 'Em. Fans will be glad to see that they have stuck with the minimalist graphics and extras, so they don’t get in the way of the pacey gameplay. Along with those positive aspects is the potential which has almost doubled this time round. Pretty much every other stat in the game might be held low, but potential bucks that trend by offering up to 4,800 times the stake. A figure that looks at odds with its cute innocent nature.Om Nom proves yet again that slots don’t have to overflow with features, graphics, and extras to provide a good time. Simple, straight forward gameplay can be just as captivating. Om Nom is the perfect alternative to all the mega slots floating around. Don’t get us wrong, there's a place and time for those as well and sometimes the mood strikes to go large and heroic. Yet, there are times for switching off and having some light hearted action that doesn’t involve too much brainpower and isn’t a clichéd 3x3 fruit slot.No it’s not an epic gaming experience, but for a slot, you can easily dip in and out of at any time, it is hard to beat. Fans of Stick 'Em, as well as newcomers, will find plenty to like about Om Nom - despite the whacky name. It’s just a shame old Canny the Can is absent this time around.

title: Wheel O'Gold
structured_summary: Wheel O'Gold is a leprechaun-themed slot set in lush meadows with classic symbols like four-leaf clovers and horseshoes. It features a 6x5 grid with scatter pays, tumbling wins, multipliers triggered by consecutive tumbles, free spins, and a bonus buy option. The reviewer finds its multiplier system simpler and distinct from similar games, with solid winning potential up to 10,000x the bet. Visually, it offers a textbook leprechaun vibe with bright greens and rainbows, accompanied by cheerful, fitting audio.
review: Wheel O'Gold: Slot Overview'Sprawling meadows', an 'overarching rainbow', symbols that include four-leaf clovers and horseshoes, it can only be another leprechaun-themed slot bounding over the hills towards us, surely? And so it is in Pragmatic Play's online slot Wheel O'Gold. For this game, Pragmatic Play has used the opportunity to once again give players some scatter-paying action, a mechanic the studio has fallen head over heels for of late, as has much of the online gambling industry. You might be tempted to think Wheel O'Gold is a Gates of Olympus 1000 clone dressed up in a top hat and buckled shoes, but while there are similarities, Wheel O'Gold uses a different method for adding and building those all-important multipliers.An absolutely textbook, classic, pleasantly generic vision of leprechaun gaming greets players once Wheel O'Gold loads. Clovers line the bottom of the screen before transitioning into lush green meadows, mountains, and a rainbow-adorned sky. A leprechaun fellow, all big smile and bushy beard bobs up and down beside the gaming grid, meaning the visual layout follows in Gates' footsteps. Wheel O'Gold is a leprechaun game, alright; not much more to add than that.Wheel O'Gold slot by Pragmatic PlayWheel O'Gold is also a highly volatile slot (carrying a 5 out of 5 rating), available in several RTP settings, with 96.02% being the highest. At least, this is the value created when betting 20 c to $/€240 per spin as normal and when using the ante bet. With the ante bet activated, more scatter symbols are present on the reels, though players pay an extra 25% for the privilege.Set within a golden patterned frame is Wheel O'Gold's 6-reel, 5-row gaming grid, using a scatter-paying mechanism to create wins. How it works is that instead of ways or paylines, when at least 8 identical pay symbols land on the board in any position, they create a winning scatter. After a scatter win has paid out, the winning symbols involved in it explode from the reels, making spaces on the grid. Symbols drop down to plug the spaces and provide a new chance to win. Sequences of tumble wins end when no new scatter win is created after a tumble. As to the pay symbols, they include blue, purple, pink, and red gems as the low pays, then a gold clover, a pipe, a mug of beer, a horseshoe, and a top hat as the high pays. For landing 8-9 matching symbols, the resulting payout is 0.2 to 4 times the bet, while at the upper end, 1 to 25 times the bet is paid for hitting 12+ of a kind. No wilds land in Wheel O'Gold.Wheel O'Gold: Slot FeaturesWheel O'Gold slot - free spinsWhen listed, Wheel O'Gold's features – tumbles, multipliers, free spins, and bonus buys, sounds the same as a good number of Pragmatic Play's scatter paying slots, but the trick here is how the multipliers appear and how they may be increased.Multiplier FeatureIn the base game, when 5 consecutive tumbles happen on the same spin after the fifth spin, a wheel covered in multipliers appears. One multiplier is randomly selected and is used to multiply all subsequent wins from the spin. Possible multiplier values are x2 to x50.Free SpinsHitting 4, 5, or 6 scatter symbols in the base game awards 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. At the start of the free spins phase, the wheel appears to award a random multiplier. This multiplier applies to all wins during the round. Whenever a scatter symbol lands, it is collected by a meter. For every 4 collected scatter symbols, +4 free spins are added to the remaining amount, and the wheel spins again, adding its new multiplier to the existing multiplier until the end of the round.Buy Free SpinsPlayers may buy the free spins round from the base game for 100 times the total bet. When buying free spins like this, 4, 5, or 6 scatter symbols randomly hit to trigger it, and the RTP is 95.94%.Wheel O'Gold slot - bonus buyWheel O'Gold: Slot VerdictEver wonder if there is a set-aside department at Pragmatic Play's HQ that is solely dedicated to crafting new scatter-paying slots? Imagine the team that came up with Gates of Olympus, who did such a good job their employer has tasked them from now till the end of time with squeezing, cajoling, and massaging out new ways of delivering scatter wins with multipliers mixed in. Wheel O'Gold's a bit different, to be sure. Instead of relying on multiplier symbols to drop from the sky onto the board, you need a solid run of consecutive tumble wins or free spin scatter symbols to get the wheel a-spinning. Is it better this way, or is it worse? Neither method is a clear-cut winner over the other. Let's just say they're different, and players get an extra choice if more choices were really needed or not.An interesting quirk about Wheel O'Gold is that the multiplier values on its wheel are a lot less impressive than those found in Gates of Olympus-style slots. Here, the biggest is x50; there, they generally go up to x500. The multiplier can stack in free spins via the scatter symbol collection process, but it doesn't feel as impressive. However, this intuitive impression is crushed by the weight of Wheel O'Gold's winning potential, as its 10,000x the bet win cap is double what's possible in Gates of Olympus. So, if a blast of good luck is flowing through Wheel O'Gold, it's as capable of turning up a sizable pot of gold at the end of a rainbow as just about any other scatter-paying slot Pragmatic Play has made.Another thing about Wheel O'Gold, which might appeal to scatter-paying enthusiasts, is that the multiplier system is simpler. For instance, when you start free spins, you get a multiplier at the beginning, and it applies to every win from there on out. There is no need to land a multiplier symbol at the same time as a win to benefit from the round's total multiplier. From a technical perspective, Wheel O'Gold has something somewhat innovative for scatter-paying cork sniffers to play around with, though the generic theme might dampen the impressions of originality.

title: 60 Second Heist
structured_summary: 60 Second Heist is a high-octane slot themed around a fast-paced, cinematic car heist reminiscent of 'Gone in 60 Seconds.' It features a unique timed free spins bonus round, Turbo Lock Respins, and a progressive multiplier with a max win potential of 60,000x. The reviewer appreciates its originality and transparency, noting some minor technical quirks but overall finds it a thrilling and rewarding experience. The game sports a retro, coastal aesthetic with a vibe similar to classic racing games, though the spinning reel sounds were seen as somewhat distracting.
review: 60 Second Heist: Slot OverviewEven for experienced heisters, 60 seconds to pull off a job does not leave much margin for error. A heist like that's gotta be planned down to the last millisecond and executed flawlessly. Not just any petty thief could pull off such a precise job. It would need someone with the skill set of, say, Memphis Raines, the retired car thief from 'Gone in 60 Seconds' who had to steal 50 cars in one night to save his brother's life. Memphis Raines was played by Nicolas Cage if you missed the film, so you know something big is going down.So it is in 60 Second Heist from developer 4ThePlayer, which is a game very loosely reminiscent of the 2000 movie involving cash, cars, and criminals. It also includes an unusual, though not totally unique time-based bonus round, which has the technical capabilities of going bananas in more ways than one. First, let's lay the scene, where the action takes place on an oceanside street behind a red supercar as it zooms next to a police car. Does that mean the heist went over the allocated 60 seconds if the cops are onto them?There's a sort of South of France, Monaco, or Californian feeling to the setting. 4ThePlayer has left this part open so players can pick the location suiting their imaginations best. 60 Second Heist has a slightly retro feel to it, and the first thing that came to mind was not a slot, but the classic video game series Outrun. On the not so great side, the noise reels made as they spun kind of killed the mood, though perhaps this was an early demo crinkle 4ThePlayer is planning to iron out.A highly volatile slot offering bets from 10 p/c to $/€10, numbers are one of 60 Second Heist's stronger points. The goodwill begins with a theoretical return value of 96.5%, with hits coming at a frequency of 21.34%. To have a shot at its 60,000x max potential, you'll need to push the progressive multiplier in free spins as hard as possible. On the road to doing so, ten regular symbols line 60 Second Heist's 5x4, 1,024 ways game grid. Half of them are 10-A royals worth 1-2x the bet for five of a kind, followed by dollar bills, diamonds, gold, and two-character symbols worth 2 to 4x the stake for five. Wilds appear in two forms depending on whether you are in the base or bonus game. In either state, wilds do the same thing, which is a substitute for all symbols except the scatter.60 Second Heist: Slot FeaturesExtras appear in both phases of play, with the main game benefiting from a Turbo Lock Respins feature. The real fun happens when the bonus round triggers, though, where a timed round of free spins is awarded.Turbo Lock RespinsThis feature may trigger after any winning base game spin. All winning symbols are locked in place while the remaining positions respin. Any new winning symbols lock for another respin. This process continues for five seconds, then the final win is awarded.Win Time Free SpinsScatter symbols appear on reels 1, 3, or 5, and having 3 in view at the same time triggers the free spins feature. Players do not get a set amount of spins here. Instead, a clock starts ticking down from 60 seconds, and the round ends when it reaches zero. If this occurs while the reels are spinning, the current spin and any wins from it are awarded before the feature closes. Also, keep an eye on the border of the reels on which a light progresses. Each time it does a complete lap, the win multiplier increases by +1, which is applied to all following wins.A couple of special symbols may land during free spins, too. One is the Boost Scatter which increases the speed of the reel spin, win count, and the light going around the board for a short period of time. Extra Time Scatters may also land, adding additional seconds to the clock.Bonus BetWhere available, players can adjust a slider on the bonus bet feature. Increasing the stake results in an improved chance of triggering free spins. The costs will be clearly labelled.60 Second Heist: Slot VerdictYou kind of have to admire what 4ThePlayer is up to at the moment. They are totally upfront about things like stats, as they carve out a personal niche using unusual themes and original, or fairly original, gameplay. We say fairly original because while a timed bonus round is unusual, we have seen it before, most recently in Joker Troupe and Land of Zenith by Push Gaming. Like those slots, it won't be everyone's cup of tea, but at the least, it's something different to experiment with.For the most part, Win Time Free Spins were positive. There were a couple of technical irritations, like the painfully slow way the Extra Time symbol floats to the timer. It takes like forever and might have been better if scatters added fewer seconds but did it faster. The way win countups eat into the timer can be annoying, as well. Eh, personal preference, and other players might not be bothered so much by these details. Plus, it makes landing the Boost Scatter Symbol more exciting.It's certainly possible to get your money's worth from free spins as Extra Time Symbols landed in abundance for us during the review. Build a decent multiplier at the same time, and things can get pretty racy. Win Time Free Spins weren't as downright chaotic as Land of Zenith's could be, yet the results can be mind-blowing. It's kind of hard to believe at first, and you'd be forgiven for scoffing at the stated 60,000x max win, yet after seeing 90K Yeti Gigablox go nuclear on film, we've got an open mind as to what 60 Second Heist can do.In many ways, 60 Second Heist is classic 4ThePlayer. Experimental, a bit out there, a bit gimmicky but hard to knock due to the transparency of the studio and their willingness to try new things.

title: Holy Hand Grenade
structured_summary: Holy Hand Grenade is a medieval-themed slot inspired by Monty Python’s surreal humor and set in a quirky, explosive world. The reviewer praises its creative gameplay and entertaining volatility, recommending it for players seeking a challenging and unique slot experience. The game boasts immersive period-themed visuals and an atmospheric soundtrack with goat bleats and medieval tunes enhancing the quirky fantasy setting.
review: Holy Hand Grenade: Slot Overview'And Saint Attila raised the hand grenade up on high, saying, 'O Lord, bless this thy hand grenade, that with it thou mayst blow thine enemies to tiny bits, in thy mercy.' And the Lord did grin. And the people did feast upon the lambs, and sloths, and carp, and anchovies, and orangutans, and breakfast cereals, and fruit bats, and large chulapas.' So was it said of the Holy Hand Grenade of Antioch as described in the Book of Armaments, chapter 2, verses 9-21. If that sounds a little bit bizarre, don't worry; it comes from the fecund minds of the British surrealist comedy group Monty Python and may or may not have served as inspiration for a mediaeval-themed online slot, shot through with humour and explosions from the creative minds at Print Studios.Make sure your tunic and cloak are in place before stepping into the world of Holy Hand Grenade, as Print Studios has rewound the clock to ye olde Medieval times. Outside a sturdy stone structure is where the beginning of this surreal adventure begins, before heading inside for the bonus round where bombs, flames, and goats(?) abound… Till then, take a moment to soak in a taste of the bygone era before roads, suburbs, and malls bulldozed the natural world into submission. An excellent period soundtrack punctuated with goat bleats and 'Hallelujahs' should help with the fantasy.Holy Hand Grenade slot - base gameWith a highly volatile math model calling the shots, so to speak, Holy Hand Grenade produces three return-to-player values depending on how the game is played. In the regular mode, wagering 10 p/c to $/€60 per spin, the value is 96.45%, or with the Scatter Boost on, thereby getting more scatters for an extra 50% cost it is 96.64%, while buying free spins for 95x the bet has a value of 96.82%. All theoretical, of course, and any device may be used for playing Holy Hand Grenade.A 5-reel, 4-row gaming panel is provided in the base game, which is expanded to 6-reels, 5-rows in the free spins bonus round. On the smaller gaming grid, 26 paylines are built in, rising to 52 for free spins. Winning lines of regular symbols pay from left to right on adjacent reels, starting from reel number 1. Landing a 5-of-a-kind winning line pays out from 1 to 20 times the bet for the diamond, spade, heart, club, bag, candles, woman, man, and bishop symbols, while payouts bump up to 2x to 50x the bet for a 6 OAK hit when the sixth reel is added. While there is plenty of humour, action and explosions, Holy Hand Grenade does not have a wild symbol.Holy Hand Grenade: Slot FeaturesHoly Hand Grenade slot - free spinsWhat it does have, though, are Superspinners, a Holy Hand Grenade feature, and free spins.SuperSpinnersSuperSpinners are those little markers you can see in between the reels. Sometimes the SuperSpinners will display a number; other times, they will be blank. If a winning line passes through a SuperSpinner displaying a number, the number multiplies the win. If a win passes through more than one SuperSpinner, then each SuperSpinner applies its value to the win in succession.Holy Hand Grenade FeatureWhen a Holy Hand Grenade hits, it explodes after any win evaluations have taken place and transforms a random number of adjacently linked symbols into the same random symbol. After the symbol transformation has occurred, a new win evaluation may take place.Free SpinsLanding 3, 4, or 5 goat-adorned scatter symbols awards payers 7, 9, or 11 free spins, respectively. As mentioned, for the free spins round, the grid expands to 6x5, and 52 winlines. In free spins, when a Holy Hand Grenade symbol hits, it marks its position with a frame for the full duration of the feature. If a Holy Hand Grenade affects a framed position, an extra Holy Hand Grenade triggers from the corresponding position. If a Holy Hand Grenade lands in a framed position, a bigger explosion results. Each landed Holy Hand Grenade also awards +2 free spins.Holy Hand Grenade slot - free spinsHoly Hand Grenade: Slot VerdictLike a lot of what Print Studios has done to date, Holy Hand Grenade came flying in from left field like a creative breath of fresh air. Wins are awarded after every respin. If a respin occurs and no positions are added to the respins area, the feature concludes.Scatter symbols land on reels 1, 2 or 4 to trigger 777 Mega Deluxe Bonus Spins. The triggering scatters transform into x2 or x5 wild multipliers which remain locked in place for the duration of Bonus Spins. Any new wild multipliers are also locked in position. 4 spins are awarded at the start of the feature, which cannot be retriggered, and any winning spin triggers the Respin Insanity feature.777 Mega Deluxe: Slot VerdictFor a Crazy Tooth slot, 777 Mega Deluxe might not be as wild and crazy as they sometimes are, but it's not your typical fruity filled slot. However, it's also not likely to be hugely attractive for casual players not besotted with this specific genre. For one, it is what it is, but what it is doesn't look great. title: Vault Cracker
structured_summary: Vault Cracker is a lighthearted, cartoon-themed slot centered around a heist with playful characters. The game sports simple, nostalgic graphics reminiscent of older slots, paired with a smooth swing soundtrack and lively animations.
review: Vault Cracker: Slot OverviewProving that fun things can come in small packages is Vault Cracker from developer Red Tiger. If you didn't know, you might not automatically guess who was behind this game as it doesn't feel like one of their typical releases. Vault Cracker sees Red Tiger take an unexpected break from the mythological, Asian-themed, uber-polished slots we've come to expect from them. It isn't a hugely thrilling slot, but Vault Cracker is quite an enjoyable wee game to play despite possessing major statistical drawbacks.In some ways, Vault Cracker harkens back to Red Tiger's earlier releases like say, Piggy Pirates or Reel Heist for example. It shares their humorous, cartoon character-driven approach, yet in an updated form. In fact, the graphical quality (which provides a significant amount of the charm) comes across like an older NetEnt slot before the demand for highly volatile massive potential gaming set in. That last sentence should serve as a clue about what you can expect to find here. However, despite not being a slot you can push gambling limits with, Vault Cracker manages to be quite amusing all the same.Vault Cracker is a basic affair, played using 5 reels along with 10 paylines to land winners on. The grid has been laid out on a desk next to various safe cracking tools of the trade such as listening devices and blueprints. A low key swing track accompanied by entertaining animations rounds off the experience, adding a touch of class to the simple design. Low to medium variance and offering a default RTP of 95.66%, players can get in on the heist by selecting bets from 10 p/c to $/€200 per spin. Wins land pretty frequently, as do features. During testing, Vault Cracker fell into a pattern of draining the balance for a bit, followed by a feature drop to bring things back to baseline. Naturally, everyone's fortune is different, though if lady luck is smiling you're better off taking advantage of another game, because Vault Cracker's potential is rather underwhelming.As for the paytable, 10 to Ace icons make up the low pay side, while toy pistols, piggy banks, necklaces, and cash sacks are used to represent the premiums. Scoring a full line of five high pays is worth a payout of 2.5 to 10 times your stake. There is no wild, but there are a few special symbols supplying the main thrills.Vault Cracker: Slot FeaturesVault Cracker - Heist feature in actionA debonair thief and his less sophisticated sidekick are the pathways to best results when playing Vault Cracker. The chap holding a pistol and swag bag is the hold-up artist symbol, appearing on the last reel only. When he lands at the same time as safe symbols, he cracks them open, awarding whatever prize they're storing inside - gold, bronze, and silver safes reveal cash prizes worth up to 30x, 15x or 5x, respectively.When a non-paying 1x2 sized Heist Master symbol lands on the middle reel, the Heist feature is triggered. This shifts the game to a streak respin bonus round, where only safe symbols may land and one respin is awarded. When new safes land, they award another respin. If no new safe lands, all currently locked safes open to reveal their rewards.The bonus game might not be over though, since players then get a spin of the Second Chance Wheel which is split into a green and a red segment. Landing on green means the Heist feature continues. Each time this occurs, the red segment gets larger the next time the Second Chance Wheel triggers. Triggering the Second Chance Wheel a fourth time instantly ends the Heist feature.If players manage to fill all possible positions with safe symbols during the Heist feature, a locked diamond position is opened. Unlocked diamonds award a multiplier of the total Heist win.Lastly, Vault Cracker may also ship with an additional gamble feature. Here players can improve a payout by landing on the green segment of a Gamble Wheel following a win.Vault Cracker: Slot VerdictSometimes, despite your best efforts, you can't help but enjoy something you technically know you're not supposed to. Like singing Taylor Swift songs into a hairbrush or flipping on The Vampire Diaries when no one's home, there is just something about Vault Cracker which makes it easy to play. There’s an entertaining mix of visual quality, playful theme, and the fact it doesn't take itself seriously going on. Vault Cracker isn't like the games we've seen from Red Tiger recently, so there's a surprise factor as well. Who knows, after the two studios merged, maybe Vault Cracker was a half-finished NetEnt project that Red Tiger completed for them? This is just out loud thinking, of course.Now on to the less exciting news, which is winning potential. It doesn't take long to work out a full grid of the top premium is worth 100x, or that 13 Gold Safes during the Heist feature, at most, add up to just 390 times your stake. Even in a dream scenario of popping a diamond multiplier, the best you can hope for is 1,410x the stake. It is what it is.There's little chance of Vault Cracker starring in big win clips any time soon - the limited potential precludes that from ever happening. Yet, if you're okay with the fact you're not playing a high powered gambling machine, Vault Cracker is a neat diversion for wiling away a few spins on. For casual, Saturday morning cartoon style shenanigans, Vault Cracker might be an okay choice provided you have no desire to go large.

title: Cannonade!
structured_summary: Cannonade! is a maritime-themed slot centered on naval warfare, treasure hunting, and pirate battles aboard a cannon-laden galleon. It features a unique Win Streak mechanic with blocker tiles that unlock more ways to win, free spins with symbol removal, and bonus buy options. The reviewer finds it an intriguing, though not top-tier, Yggdrasil slot that innovates on sticky win respins and offers up to 20,000x potential wins. Visually, the game presents a dramatic seascape with ships under moody skies and a painterly sunrise or sunset, enhancing its swashbuckling atmosphere.
review: ﻿Cannonade!: Slot OverviewCasino game maker Yggdrasil Gaming has proven a dab hand at piraty/high seas slots as seen previously in Pirates Smugglers Paradise and Pirates 2: Mutiny. Now the team is back, bobbing up and down on the water in an online slot they've named Cannonade! If you were wondering, Google's definition of a cannonade is 'a period of continuous heavy gunfire', which brought to mind olden times galleons sailing up to each other before letting rip with every cannon on board. When you think of the noise, all of those cannon balls flying around shredding through sails, and wooden planks, it must have been terrifying. More so since if the galleon sank, what could you do? There were no mobile phones or rescue choppers coming to pick anyone up.Now back to Cannonade!, which presents a romanticised version of naval warfare based around weighing anchor, searching for treasure, and fighting off pirates. The fiery action is presented on a 5-reel, 6-row grid, slapped on a boat bristling with cannons, carvings and sails. At the start of the base game, half of the reel positions (15) are active, while the other half are inactive, covered by blocker tiles. The inactive position can be unlocked when winning ways start landing. The rest of the base game scene depicts ships floating on the water under an ominous dark cloudy sky transitioning to a blazing sunrise or sunset on the horizon like a Turner painting. It's certainly swashbuckling; let's mosey on.Cannonade! slot - base gameAvailable on any device, there are a number of ways of possibly tackling Cannonade!, depending on the market. One is by simply picking a bet of 20 p/c to $/€20 and banging away on the spin button. Another way is by activating the Golden Bet, which increases the stake by 50% to have extra scatter symbols on the reels, boosting the chance of triggering free spins. The third is by buying free spins. In all cases, it appears the maximum return to player value is 96%, though lower models may be available, and volatility has been classified as 'Super High'.In the default fifty-ftifty inactive/active grid state, players get 120 ways to win, rising to 7,776 when all positions have been unlocked. Wins occur when identical symbols land on adjacent reels, starting from the leftmost side of the panel. Ten pay symbols appear on the board. The first six are axes, rifles, cannons, swords, and pistols, paying 0.2 to 0.3x for five of a kind, then four seafaring type characters worth 0.4 to 2 times the stake for five of a kind. Last but not least, there are no wild symbols to be found in Cannonade!Cannonade!: Slot FeaturesCannonade! slot - free spinsWhen winning ways hit, they trigger Cannonade!'s Win Streak feature. The winning symbols are locked in place, and one blocked position from the reels they landed on is removed allowing new symbols to appear there. Then, the unlocked symbols respin. If new winning symbols hit, they are locked in place as well, remove blocked positions from their reels, and another respin occurs. If more than one symbol type creates a win, the lowest-value winning symbol is upgraded to the highest-paying locked symbol. This continues until no new winning symbol hits, then a win evaluation takes place.Free SpinsCollecting 3, 4, or 5 scatter symbols on a single spin awards 6, 9, or 12 free spins, respectively. Before free spins start, players may have the option of gambling them to possibly win more or collect what was awarded and go right into the feature. To gamble, a red and green segmented wheel spins. Landing on green awards +3 free spins, while landing on red loses all free spins. Win Streaks remain active in free spins, and the rules are the same as the base game, with one exception. During the feature, when a scatter symbol lands, it awards +1 free spins, and the lowest paying symbol is removed from the reels.Buy BonusIf available, Cannonade! comes with two bonus buy choices. One costs 100x the bet and gets you 6 free spins, or 500x the bet for 15 free spins.Cannonade! slot - free spinsCannonade!: Slot VerdictThe Streak Wins, sticky win concept, whilst not super common, is one that arises from the depths every now and then. NetEnt popularised them in amclassic slots like Jack Hammer and Long Pao, Quickspin in Blue Fortune, and Thunderkick in Odin's Gamble. If those online slots tickled your fancy, then consider having a crack at Cannonade! too. It does things with the mechanic rarely, if ever seen before, while using the sticking winning symbol/respin process. It does so in a fairly absorbing maritime setting which, while not the most imaginative theme, has been handled pretty well, for the most part, to create a sensation of salty danger; though the quick shifts between game phases were a little abrupt.On to Win Streaks, and what's interesting is that they've been combined with a blocker tile removal element, clearing the way for new symbols to land on the board and boosting ways to win in the process. There are certainly a lot more possible ways to win in Cannonade! then there were in the games mentioned above, and clearing blocker tiles can be satisfying. In addition, there's the chance, though it wasn't easy to do during testing, of removing lower-paying symbols from the reels during free spins - theoretically upping the chances of streaking together better value symbol wins. On the subject of wins, Cannonade! delivers a sizable number, as the load screen touts potential of up to 20,000x the bet.All in all, Cannonade! should be an intriguing option for gamblers into this style of play. It didn't feel quite as sharp as some of Yggdrasil's A* slots, although we might have been affected by the memory of Calavera Crush, which despite being a completely different type of game, was strangely brought to mind. Anyway, Cannonade! has its innovative moments, and as mentioned, if this method of building wins appeals, the game is worth a bash.

title: Reel King Mega
structured_summary: Reel King Mega revisits the classic UK pub slot theme with a nostalgic fruit machine style and a touch of Las Vegas flair. It features Super Symbols, a King's Crown wild transformation, a unique Reel King bonus game, and a Gamble Wheel with 100% RTP. review: Reel King Mega (Red Tiger): ReviewTo most continental gamblers, Reel King is just another Novomatic slot. Mention it to UK players, however, and they might start to reminisce of the good ol' days, or start to sweat profusely while sharing bitter recollections of shameful drunken sessions. Originally released by Barcrest, Reel King is a classic slot machine that became a favourite in pubs all over the UK, and subsequently turned into an online slot by Novomatic after acquiring a license from Barcrest. Passing the torch on to Red Tiger, Reel King becomes Reel King Mega, rolling out on the digital shelves to take on a new generation of players who, before long, will have epic stories of their own to tell.With the classic fruit machine style preserved, and with a touch of Las Vegas, Reel King Mega is a 5-reel, 20-payline slot developed by Novomatic subsidiary Astra Group and powered by Red Tiger. Playable across all devices from as little as 20 cents to 200€ per spin, the game comes with Super Symbols that can appear 2x2 in size, a randomly triggered base game feature that transforms standard symbols into wilds, and a unique bonus game with a mini slot machine featuring its own special reels.The paytable is undoubtedly an odd one, but that's always been the point of Reel King, to stand out as unique and quirky. With the order of the symbols thrown around, on the reels you'll see lower value cherries, plums, 10's and J's alongside more rewarding Q's, K's and bags full of gold coins - the latter being the most rewarding, giving you 25 times your stake for 5 in line. The fool's hat is the wild which substitutes for all symbols. All symbols can appear 2x2 in size, even the wild! These are known as Super Symbols.Reel King Mega (Red Tiger): FeaturesThe Reel King feature in actionReel King Mega comes with a randomly triggered base game feature known as the King's Crown feature. When triggered, which happens quite frequently, the crown sitting on the title logo will start to bounce around on the reels while swapping symbols into wilds, including Super Symbols. Most of the time you'll get one or two wilds, but the feature is capable of giving you more than that.The vast majority of the bigger wins will come from the Reel King feature - this bonus game is not triggered the traditional way of landing 3 scatter symbols. Instead, it comes into play when all 5 reels are highlighted with a yellow background. Once triggered, up to 5 cartoon king's may appear on the reels, each with its own special set of reels. The king will spin his reels, giving you 2, 5, 10, or 25 times your stake for 3 of a kind mixed, blue, yellow or red sevens respectively. The feature continues until a losing spin occurs.There's also a Gamble Wheel feature for those that are feeling extra lucky, and which, according to the paytable, is 100% random with 100% RTP.Reel King Mega (Red Tiger): VerdictCapitalising on the well-known brand that Reel King is, Red Tiger's version is a game that will entertain a small niche of players, but lacks the mass appeal to go viral. For this reason, regular players might find the 500 xbet potential, low volatility and dated design a bit unsexy, while those with a more personal connection to the brand will actively seek it out for a walk down memory lane. The whole point of Reel King Mega was never to compete with the big titles - it's a game for enthusiasts made by even bigger enthusiasts, and that is exactly how it needs to be appreciated.

title: Bull In A China Shop

review: Bull In A China Shop: Slot OverviewYou have to hand it to Play’n GO. With such a high work rate you’d think they’d struggle to keep coming up with new ideas. Yet somehow their creative team consistently conjures up interesting concepts, features, or gameplay. Of course, not all of them are hits, but it is surprising how often they do something clever that is obvious in hindsight.
