Aesthetics include a 19th-century steampunk vibe with brass elements and a stirring soundtrack, though more Jules Verne-themed visuals could enhance the experience.
review: Wins of Nautilus Megaways: Slot OverviewDeep breath players, developer Fantasma Games is taking you on a 20,000-league journey beneath the waves in their online slot Wins of Nautilus Megaways, inspired by the writings of Jules Verne. If you otherwise didn’t know, 20,000 leagues equate to around 80,000 km, or nearly twice the Earth's circumference. The book plots the travels of the Nautilus submarine under its commander Captain Nemo, who is a sort of billionaire seeking to remove himself from and be beyond the reach of any government. As such, Nemo can pretty much do whatever he wants down there. Fortunately, his desires revolve around gaining scientific knowledge rather than being some Dr Evil type, taking his frustrations out on civilisation by trying to destroy it.Anyhoo, that brings us to Wins of Nautilus Megaways, which plants players aboard the Nautilus as it rests beneath the ocean's surface. Full wall portals reveal a murky undersea vista made up of wrecked ships, weeds, and plenty of fish floating around. For the most part, Wins of Nautilus Megaways is pretty rousing, in a 19th century way, with loads of brass about the place and a stirring soundtrack to inflame any adventurous spirits. It wouldn't have hurt to have gone a bit heavier on the Jules Verne, but what Fantasma went with has plenty of pluck.Wins of Nautilus Megaways' setup is fairly standard, played on a game grid made up of a 6-reel main panel, with a 4-position horizontal reel running along the top - a rather typical Megaways set up in other words. The symbols appearing on the main reels change with every spin, producing 324 to 117,649 ways to win each time. There are no qualms over stats, including good potential, and a decent RTP of 96.1%, with 69.59% going to the base game, 26.51% to free spins. The gaming is quite pacey, thanks to a hit frequency of 30.76%, leading into an Avalanche feature, making for a fairly eventful journey beneath the waves.All ten pay symbols require at least three to form a winning combination, starting from the leftmost side of the panel. Low pays are J-A card tiles worth up to 0.75 to 1.25x the bet, mids are anchors, shells, and diving helmets worth 1.5 to 2x, while high pays are three unusual characters that payout 3 to 5 times your stake for six of a kind. Onwards to the features.Wins of Nautilus Megaways: Slot FeaturesWins of Nautilus Megaways - free spinsAvalanches are the most common extra to be found in this deep-sea dive and are accompanied by Countdown Bombs, Full Reel Wilds, Respins, plus Deep Sea Free Spins.AvalanchesEvery winning combination kicks off the Avalanche mechanic, which removes the respective symbols from the reels. The remaining symbols drop down into the empty positions giving players another chance to win. Avalanches keep going until no new winning combination forms.Countdown Bombs & Fully Stacked WildsCountdown Bomb symbols appear on the top reel or on reels 2-5. Each one appears with a number on them from 1 to 4. Whenever an Avalanche is activated, the number on all Countdown Bombs in view decreases by 1. When a counter reaches zero, it explodes and creates a full reel wild symbol with a multiplier equal to 2 times the starting counter value. If this occurs to two Countdown Bombs on the same reel, their initial values are added together before being multiplied by 2 and given to the full reel wild.RespinsRespin symbols appear on reels 2-5 in the form of a grinning shark and activate the Respin feature when in view. Each Respin symbol removes itself plus 2-10 random pay symbols, thereby triggering an Avalanche.Deep Sea Free SpinsScatter symbols appear on any reel in the base game or in free spins. They are collected on the Bonus Meter during an Avalanche sequence, and if at least 3 accumulate, then 12 Deep Sea Free Spins are awarded. Collecting more than 3 adds +5 free spins per additional bonus symbol. Free spins can be retriggered in the same way during the feature. Now, most rules remain the same for free spins, with the added bonus of a win multiplier that starts at x1 and is increased by +1 following each Avalanche.Buy Free SpinsIf possible to buy free spins, the cost is 60x the bet, which starts a game round guaranteed to activate Deep Sea Free Spins. RTP increases to 97% when doing so.Wins of Nautilus Megaways: Slot VerdictAfter Caravan of Riches kind of lost us, we're back on firm ground again in Wins of Nautilus Megaways. Fantasma returns to making a playable Megaways slot with a good number of interesting aspects. Wins of Nautilus might not be one of Fantasma's experiential Megaways games like Flower Fortunes, or Heroes Hunt 2, though it loses nothing for being more conventional. As mentioned, it wouldn't have hurt if the studio got even more Jules Verne-y, maybe dropped in a Kraken, or used more exotic undersea scenery. But there is enough brass gadgetry and electrification buzzing around the screen to scratch some of the Steampunk itch. Plus, there are loads of Kraken games out there anyway.It helps that the features Fantasma has included complement the game nicely. Countdown Bombs provide a measure of tension as they slowly tick down through Avalanches, and the ensuing Full Reel Wild multipliers can be highly useful. Wilds directly led to the best results during the test run, when they were created in free spins alongside the progressive win multiplier. Having more than one at once is an exciting proposal as well, though this never managed to materialise while we were playing. Like Nemo searching for wrecked bullion, double wilds are no doubt out there somewhere and would be a boon to have when chasing down Wins of Nautilus Megaways' max win of 10,000x the bet.So no, Wins of Nautilus Megaways isn't as wildly experimental as they can be from Fantasma, but that's a non-issue. Players get a well-made Megaways game, which performs well while offering an attractive setting for its wholesome mix of features, stats, and potential.

title: Tivoli
structured_summary: Tivoli is a slot themed around the historic Danish amusement park, capturing its fairy-tale charm and nostalgic atmosphere. review: Tivoli: Slot OverviewPlayers enter a world of fairy-tale like mystery when firing up Tivoli, a slot from Blueprint Gaming based on the famous Danish pleasure garden. Established in 1843, Tivoli Gardens is one of the oldest amusement parks in the world, second only to Dyrehavsbakken, located up the road in Klampenborg. Tivoli is the more famous thanks to its central Copenhagen location, and the fact Dyrehavsbakken doesn't roll off English speaking tongues as easily as its slightly younger sibling's does. Tivoli Gardens is full of rides, arcades, gardens, and more. Blueprint Gaming seeks to capture this entertainment in their slot version, which uses gameplay and features copied straight from Reel Time Gaming's cult classic Fishin' Frenzy.It is hard to suppress a gasp of wonderment when Tivoli the slot lights up the screen. Okay, maybe a small gasp, yet Tivoli is quite a charming game indeed. It has a look that hints at Art Deco though something more unique. Like a Belle Epoch era with a clean Danish feel. It really is handsome, and the lively music makes you want to drop the 21st-century cynicism as you stroll through the gate to experience all this magical garden has to offer. Almost like shedding a few decades to relive a carefree youth. You can't escape reality forever of course, and after a few spins, it all comes crashing in. But for a few initial fleeting moments, Tivoli the game transports you back in time when there was still wonder in the world.Players can take in the amusement park on any device, choosing bets from 10 p/c up to a possible $/€500 per spin at the upper end. The Tivoli experience is a medium volatile one, meaning it's usually not an insane ride of a game. It's more like an old wooden roller coaster that isn't so hair raising yet still manages to delight at times. Since Tivoli is essentially a clone of Fishin' Frenzy, the same RTP value of 96.12% applies.Winning means landing three or more identical symbols side by side from the first reel onwards. The one exception is the top premium symbol needs only two to pay out. Blueprint Gaming has done a great job of expressing the theme through the symbols. At first, we get a bunch of pleasingly designed 10-A card icons, followed by ticket symbols, and several park rides. These include the Himmelskibet, Ballongyngen, Rutschebanen, and Radiobilerne. Five of kind wins are generous too, at 50 to 200 times the stake for the theme park ride premiums.Tivoli: Slot FeaturesLanding on any reel is the Tivoli entrance symbol which is the scatter. When 3, 4, or 5 grace the game, players are awarded 10, 15, or 20 free spins respectively. During free spins, the Ticket Collector scatter symbol becomes active. On his own, 2, 3, 4, or 5 Ticket Collectors are worth a payout of 1x, 10x, 50x, or 500x the bet.Whenever the Ticket Collector lands on a spin, he pulls in the value imprinted on all of the ticket symbols in view. Individually, these tickets have prizes of 2x, 5x, 10x, 15x, 20x, 25x, or 50x the bet attached to them. Free spins cannot be retriggered so once they wind down to zero the feature is over.Tivoli: Slot VerdictTivoli is quite an intriguing slot. Blueprint Gaming has captured a strong dose of Tivoli’s magic by using popup book graphics that are genuinely captivating. The soundtrack is just as stirring, and animations such as the firework effects have been put to good use. It all combines to create a carefree look; some might say a little kiddy, with a carnival atmosphere to reproduce a golden age feel the amusement park is famous for. This is a place to forget about the outside world while discovering new wonders to lose yourself in. For a time at least, it's hard not to surrender and be sucked into Tivoli the slot's enchanting world.If you're not a major fan of Fishin' Frenzy, then the enchantment probably won't last all that long. The limited gameplay comes screaming to the forefront, shifting the daydream into a more general glazy eyed lethargy. Sure it's cloned off Fishin' Frenzy which was a hit (mainly in the UK), but the original is getting on in years and is showing its age. Tivoli's fab new graphics elongate the playing time, though once the first impressions wear off, the slow pace plus a narrow range of features become apparent.The extras do make sense though. Like a fisherman hauling in fish, the ticket collector collecting tickets is a logical use of the feature. Also, like the original, it is still a thrill when the collector rakes in a bunch of tickets during free spins. Don't expect vast fortunes while playing Tivoli. However, picking up a few of the 50x tickets can accrue decent payout totals. Exactly what the game is capable of is hard to say. The paytable mentions a max cap of $250,000 or 50,000x (whichever comes first), but don't expect the top payout to be anywhere near 50,000x (nor even half of that).Blueprint Gaming has done a great job of converting Fishin' Frenzy to a new format aimed at Danish players. It's not exactly high adrenaline gaming, but the gameplay works like a charm with the dreamy garden theme to produce a relaxing environment to try your luck in.

title: Bloodaxe
structured_summary: Bloodaxe is a Viking-themed slot featuring a gritty, immersive Norse world with realistic warrior characters. review: Bloodaxe: Slot OverviewThey say you shouldn't judge a book by its cover and all that, but something told us a slot named Bloodaxe wasn't going to be a jolly leprechaun jaunt or a game about candy. A quick glance confirmed this suspicion, and Bloodaxe, from Relax Gaming partners Four Leaf Gaming, is, in fact a slot containing one of the more boisterous peoples of the past, the mighty Vikings. Since Bloodaxe is a Four Leaf Gaming production, it contains a multitude of gambling options and wheels that usually accompany one of its games. As well as the usuals, Bloodaxe has Wild Axes, free spins, and the sticky wilded Bloodaxe Spins.Four Leaf Gaming has gone for a somewhat realistic representation of its Viking characters, and they all look like they mean business. The studio has picked a frigid day to hold the base game, where the grid sits by a grand building while snow drizzles about the place. Probably not the best day to set sail and plunder foreign lands. To put a positive spin on the weather, days like that provide the perfect opportunity to stay indoors, guilt-free, feasting on boar and downing frothy mugs of mead. Or, in this day and age, bad weather might mean firing up the gaming console or lounging on the couch watching Netflix. Are we getting soft?Bloodaxe slot - base gameBah, acting all tough in Bloodaxe means picking a stake of 20 c to $/€40 and pounding the play button. It's played on a 5-reel game board with 4 rows of symbols and 25 ways to win. Winning lines of symbols pay left to right from the first reel onwards and require at least 3 matching symbols to do so. With its highly volatile math model, Bloodaxe theoretically returns 95% to players - the same when buying free spins.Axes do not appear on any of the pay symbols, which instead include 4 coins as the low pays and 4 characters as the high pays. Win lines, including 5 matching low pays award 1.5 to 3 times the bet, while 5 OAK premium wins pay 10 to 20 times the bet. Where an axe finally comes into play is on the wild symbol. Wilds are present on all reels, substituting for any regular pay symbol and awarding 20x the bet for a five-wild winning line.Bloodaxe: Slot FeaturesBloodaxe slot - free spins gambleWild axes are also critical components in the base and bonus game in other ways, too. In the base game, when wilds hit, an axe is tossed at the target above it. Depending on where the axe hits, the reel collector is filled with 1, 2, or 3 points. When a collection meter reaches 4 points on any reel, 4 respins with an expanding wild on the reel are awarded. If any other reel's collection is filled during respins, it also becomes an expanded wild reel, and the respin counter is reset to 4.Free SpinsLanding 3, 4, or 5 scatter symbols in the base game awards 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. When free spins end, 4 Bloodaxe spins are awarded. For the Bloodaxe spins, a number of wilds corresponding to the number on the collectors is added to the respective reels. Free spins can be bought for the cost of 78x the bet.Bonus BoosterBefore free spins begin, players can gamble to win 1, 2, or 3 extra spins. The gamble can be repeated up to a maximum total of 25 spins.Bonus ReplayWhen free spins end under a certain threshold, players can gamble their winnings for the chance to replay them. A losing spin returns you to the base game.Super SpinnerThe Super Spinner may be triggered each time a coin is collected. Coins land randomly on low-pay symbols. Changing bet levels updates the coins collected relative to the bet. When the Super Spinner is activated, it awards cash prizes of 80-5,000x, 10-25 free spins, cash prizes of 10-25x, or 10-25 Nitro Spins. The Super Spinner can be bought where the base cost is 60x the bet.Nitro SpinsActivating Nitro Spins in the base game makes wild axes hit more frequently with higher chances of hitting the bullseye, increases free spins scatters, collects coins more frequently, and the Super Spinner triggers more often. A Nitro Spin increases the stake by 50% or costs 4 coins per spin.Bloodaxe slot - free spinsBloodaxe: Slot VerdictWhen it comes to designing slots, so far, Four Leaf Gaming has played it pretty safe. At least in terms of picking themes, the studio has chosen topics like jokers, pirates, clovers, and now Vikings. Not criticising the studio's choices, a lot of developers stick with tried and true subject matter after all. Also, Four Leaf Gaming has reproduced a fairly immersive Viking world to get lost in for a bit while trying to get axes bandying about the place. So the tee-up wasn't bad, how did the rest follow through?Bloodaxe had its ups and downs. Maybe players looking for a Viking slot with a stack of extra gambling opportunities might be chuffed if picking Bloodaxe. A lot of the extras are standard Four Leaf Gaming features you can find on any number of the studio's slots, but the newer additions are intriguing in themselves. One of the pinnacle moments has to be Bloodaxe Spins, when the wilds achieved by the collections are plastered onto the reels. Some wilds, if the collection went well, come with a handy x2 multiplier attached, too. It's a method reminiscent of something Relax Gaming might do as thoughts drifted to Wild Chapo, where certain positions turn into wilds or multiplier wilds for the last spin of the bonus round. Here, you get 4 final spins, yet Bloodaxe didn't have the same high-tension feel to it that Wild Chapo had.Perhaps we just weren't lucky enough with the wild symbol collecting to reach the same adrenalised levels. On paper, with its 10,000x the bet max win, Bloodaxe can turn up the heat, but the game felt a little flat. Maybe it's got something to do with the drama-less way the reels spin, or something? It's hard to put a finger on what exactly caused the reaction to be lukewarmer than first suspected. The artwork is tops, and the features are interesting, maybe it's the feeling Bloodaxe relies so much on the additional betting opportunities to be thrilling that just vanilla gambling on it was a titch hollow.But chucking coins at every conceivable opportunity to bet is a Four Leaf Gaming slot's MO. This means players who have appreciated getting the chance to do so in other slots from this provider might appreciate those chances here. If so, best be sharpening those blades. Otherwise, if extra gambles aren't so much of an interest, and you're desiring a less option-filled Viking betting experience, there are question marks over how well those desires will be satiated.

title: Reactor
structured_summary: Reactor is a futuristic-themed slot set in a sci-fi fusion reactor environment. review:
Reactor (Red Tiger Gaming) - IntroductionHaving been exclusively available at a few selected casinos, it's now time for the network-wide launch of Reactor by Red Tiger Gaming. This futuristic looking creation is played on a 5-reel, 20-payline reel set that allows players to win both ways. The sound effects team have done a solid job too adding excitement to the gameplay although the main theme, that has this game show kind of vibe going on, seems a bit out of place.In any case, the result is an impressive one and it's quite apparent that a lot of time and labour has been invested into the production, not to mention the RNG working in the background to balance the slot.Reactor (Red Tiger Gaming) - Symbols & PaytableOn the reels you'll find 4 neon coloured radioactive stones and 4 high-value reactor parts out of which the cross-shaped one is the most lucrative of the standard symbols, giving you 20 times your stake for 5 across a full payline. The ball-shaped electric cloud is the wild and substitutes for all symbols bar the Battery symbol and is worth 25x per payline.Being a win-both-ways slot, winning combinations can start from either reel 1 or reel 5 and, as the symbols appear fully stacked on the reels, there is an ok 600x win potential on offer in the main game without the involvement of any features.Reactor (Red Tiger Gaming) - Battery Re-spin FeatureCentral to the game is the Battery re-spin feature. The reel enhancing extras on offer, however, can combine to dramatic effect with a max win potential of 5000 times your stake, so if you're a fan of high variance, you'll most likely enjoy this electrifying beast.
In writing, Reactor can come across as slightly complicated although it is not. In fact, it is a rather simple slot, and once you've triggered a couple of re-respins, you'll soon get the hang of what's going on.

title: Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash
structured_summary: Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash is a fishing-themed slot that recycles ideas from previous games in the genre. It features a 5x3 reel setup with 25 paylines, multiple RTP options, and bonus mechanics like Express Collect, a Bonus Wheel, Link&Win respins, and free spins with multipliers. The reviewer finds the game uninspired and dull, lacking originality compared to other fishing slots. Visually plain with a simple water background, it offers cheerful, bouncy music but little else to engage players.
review: Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash: Slot OverviewJust when we'd got the smell of fish off our hands from the last fish slot review, we get Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash from Games Global partner Gold Coin Studios. Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash is a follow-up to Fishing Floats of Cash (2022), which in turn appears to have been a reskin of Fiona's Fortune (2022). The recycling of bits and bobs and ideas and gaming components is evidently strong with this one. Never mind, time to grab a virtual rod and see what we can dredge up with Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash.To begin with, Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash is cheerful if plain looking. Fishing slots tend to be upbeat affairs, and Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash certainly is that - largely thanks to its bouncy music. Sorry to use the same word twice so close together, but the visuals are plain, boring even, the base game background depicting some water and a hint of a cloudless sky. The rotating prize wheel is one incentive, perhaps, as are the three prize values displayed along the top of the game grid, though apart from the cheerful tunes, there isn't much about Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash that screamed to us, 'play me, you wanna be fisherperson.'Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash slot - base gameTurning our attention to Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash's inner workings, we find a highly volatile math model and four RTP configurations, 96.04% being the preferred one. The higher RTP model comes with a theoretical hit rate of 30.05% and bet limits of 20 p/c to $/€25 per spin. Sitting centre stage is a 5-reel, 3-row gaming panel with 25 paylines where regular line wins may land.While the main focus may be on winning elsewhere, regular wins begin from the leftmost side of the board, left to right across a payline on adjacent reels. For low pays, Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash has 10 to A card royals, paying 2.4 to 3 times the bet for 5 OAK, then an anchor, a seagull, and a marlin are the high pays worth 6 to 8 times the bet for 5-of-a-kind. Appearing on reels 2 to 5, helping link wins together is the fisherman wild, which can substitute for any pay symbol.Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash: Slot FeaturesFishing Deeper Floats of Cash slot - WheelFishing Deeper Floats of Cash Not makes up for not having a heck of a lot of pay symbols by possessing a fair few features. These are the Express Collect, a Bonus Wheel, a Link&Win Respins feature, and free spins.Express ConnectExpress Connect prize symbols may land on reels 1 to 4, with values of 1 to 200 times the bet or displaying the Mini 20x the bet or Major 600x the bet prizes. When a Trigger symbol lands on reel 5, any Express Connect prize symbols also in view award their values.Wheel BonusLanding a Trigger symbol on reel 5 and a Wheel Bonus symbol on reel 1 triggers the Wheel Bonus. The Wheel spins to award 2x, 5x, or 10x the bet, the Link&Win feature, or the Mini, Major, or Mega Prize worth 20x, 600x, or 7,500x the bet, respectively.Link&WinThe Link&Win feature starts with 3 spins where only special symbols or blank spaces may land. Any new Link&Win symbols that hit reset the spin count. At the end, the values of all prizes are awarded. If all 15 positions are filled, the Mega Prize 7,500x the bet is also awarded.Free SpinsLanding 3 scatter symbols on reels 2-4 triggers 10 free spins. Whenever a Trigger symbol lands on the fifth reel, the Feature Trail is progressed by +1 position. Up to 3 Trigger symbols can land on a spin. Upon reaching each third position on the Trail, a multiplier applies to any future Express Collect wins and +5 additional free spins are awarded. The multiplier progresses like so - x2, x3, x5, then x10. The Trail has 12 positions to progress along.Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash slot - free spinsFishing Deeper Floats of Cash: Slot VerdictWell, it's a fishing game, alright, but it could be anything, really. When digging into Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash's past, it quickly became apparent how much recycling of gaming components and general reskinning went on to spawn the current game. Couple that with the plain visuals, and it was hard to fight off an overwhelming feeling of tedious boredom while playing Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash.For starters, there is a significant number of fishing slots already on the market, which is no bad thing in and of itself. And yet, if someone is planning to make yet another one, why not do something interesting with it? What's the point of churning out another reskin, or a Fishin' Frenzy/Big Bass Bonanza wanna-be? It doesn't mean the game has to light up the sky with incandescent innovation. Just something, anything to give the game an original spark. Not singling any one studio out here, by the way; just ranting into the wind. Fishing Floats of Cash kinda got away with it, maybe, since it was the first in this series, yet Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash is just a more volatile version with a higher max win. Perhaps the previous game was a hit? Fair dues to Gold Coin Studios if it was. But for non-fans, or if coming in for the first time, Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash may well just fall flat, delivering a bunch of same old same old gaming, which was tiring to struggle though.Apologies for the bad vibes, but Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash just didn't float the boat. It's technically got the required parts to thrill players who strike it lucky, though with other more exciting fishing games on the market – the Big Bass range, Golden Catch, 4 Fantastic Fish in Egypt, and even iterations of Fishin' Frenzy, for example, Fishing Deeper Floats of Cash was like ordering frozen fish from a restaurant rather than something freshly caught.

title: Undead Fortune
structured_summary: Undead Fortune is a zombie-themed slot by Hacksaw Gaming blending undead horror with a lively, retro vibe. review: Undead Fortune: Slot OverviewJust speculating here, but the act of grave robbing has probably been around for as long as people have buried with their riches. Perhaps it was people planning to be entombed with their wealth who came up with the idea of zombies in an attempt to scare off would-be tomb raiders? Whatever the origin might be, players get a taste of the undead in an online slot from Hacksaw Gaming titled Undead Fortune which is another slot that reveals the darker side of Hacksaw Gaming's personality. It follows a path laid down by prior slots such as Hand of Anubis and Gladiator legends, expanding on Hacksaw Gaming's DuelReels mechanic whilst combining it with a treasure trove of features such as Walking duels, Expanding DuelReels, The Curse bonus round, and The Tomb bonus round.Initially, Undead Fortune didn't make the same impact Hand of Anubis did which had a heavy atmosphere that felt like you'd been judged for your earthly deeds and been found wanting. Undead Fortune is chock full of horrifying images, including a huge, hooded cobra, but it didn't evoke the same level of despair. It's very lively, though, ironically, and soon enough, animated undead denizens will be lighting up the reels via the game's features and, hopefully, letting slip some of their fortunes.Undead Fortune slot - base gameHacksaw Gaming slots do tend to lean on the volatile side, and if our test sessions are anything to go by, Undead Fortune certainly warrants its 4 out of 5 volatility rating. As per usual, it comes in a variety of RTP settings with a maximum value of 96.29%, which at that level has a hit frequency of 26.77%. When playing regularly, stakes of 10 p/c to $/€100 may be selected, available on mobile, desktop, or tablet devices.Surrounded by hieroglyphically carved stone structure sits Undead Fortune's 5-reel, 4-row game panel. Running across it are 10 fixed paylines for landing winning combinations of three to five or a kind. For pay symbols, 10-A card royals are used as the low pays, while five monster/character symbols make up the premium tiles. Hitting a five-of-a-kind winning line awards 1-1.5x the bet for five royals or 4-10x the bet for five premiums. Wrapping this section up is the wild symbol, appearing on all reels to substitute any regular pay symbol. If five wilds hit along a payline, they award 10 times the stake.Undead Fortune: Slot FeaturesUndead Fortune slot - The Tomb free spinsUndead Fortune builds off slots that preceded it while doing its own thing at the same time. Features to be found in the game are Walking duels, Expanded DuelReels, The Curse, The Tomb, and several bonus buys for eligible players.Walking DuelsLanding Walk VS symbols activities Walking duels. Walking duels are wild symbols that expand to cover the whole reel. They reveal a monster and a multiplier value. If the monster is defeated, the multiplier is applied to the whole reel, boosting any wins that pass through it. Should more than one Walking duel be part of the same win, the multiplier values are added together before being used. Multipliers can have values of x2 to x200. Defeating the monster also awards a respin, and the expanded Walking duel symbol moves one reel to the left unless it is blocked by another Walking duel symbol or the edge of the grid. At the new position, another duel takes place, repeating the procedure mentioned above. New Walk VS symbols can land on respins.Expanding DuelReelsExpand VS symbols appear on reels 2, 3, 4, or 5, triggering Expanding duels when they hit. Expanding duel symbols are wild and expand to cover the whole reel, displaying a monster and a multiplier. If the monster is defeated, the multiplier is saved, and the Expanding duel expands one reel to the left unless blocked by the edge of the board. Once expanded, another monster and multiplier appear, repeating the process. If the monster is defeated after the expansion, the new multiplier is added to the current value. Multiplier values are x2 to x200. If the monster is not defeated or the Expanding duel cannot expand any further, any winning lines connected to it are multiplied by the multiplier. Walk VS and Expand VS symbols are not able to appear at the same time.The CurseGetting 3 Curse symbols on reels 1, 3, and 5 on a single base game round triggers The Curse bonus game. For The Curse, 10 free spins are awarded with a greater chance of landing Walk VS and Expand VS symbols.The TombLanding 3 Tomb scatters in a game on reels 1, 3, and 5 in a single game round triggers The Tomb bonus round. This round begins with multiplier values above each reel. Some reels are locked, some are active. Landing Tomb VS symbols on an active reel reveals a monster and a multiplier value of 2x to 200x. Defeating the monster adds the multiplier to the value above it. Losing the duel locks the reel. When all five reels are locked, the feature ends, and the values above the reels are awarded. However, it is possible to unlock reels. When 4 unlock symbols land on a locked reel, it is unlocked, or when the Golden Unlock symbol lands, all locked reels are unlocked.One more symbol which may land during the feature is the Epic Vs scatter. When hit, the whole grid becomes a duel, displaying monsters and a multiplier value. Win this duel, and all active reel values are either multiplied by x2 to x20 or have a value of 25x to 200x added to them. Losing this duel locks the reel the Epic VS symbol landed on.Buy BonusUndead Fortune's feature buy menu provides these five ways of playing the game:Bonus Featurespins – 3x the bet where each spin is 5 times more likely to award a bonus game. Very highly volatile.Walking Duel Featurespins – 10x the bet to guarantee at least one Walk VS symbol lands. Very highly volatile.Expanding Duel Featurespins – 50x the bet to guarantee that one Expand VS symbol hits. Extremely volatile.The Curse – 100x the bet. Very high volatility.The Tomb – 200x the bet. Very high volatility.Undead Fortune slot - feature buy menuUndead Fortune: Slot VerdictHand of Anubis came blowing onto our screen like a dread chill wind from the underworld and immediately grabbed attention with its bleak visuals. Undead Fortune has some of that effect, but it's not so pronounced. In part because Hand of Anubis was first, therefore stole its thunder, and partly from the sprinklings of neon giving the game an undead at a 90s retro party vibe. It certainly contains a lot of horrific imagery, though (for an online slot); the chaps with the big, stretched mouths are practicality vile. Maybe play the game during the day or with all the house lights on when the sun goes down if you happen to get night terrors. There are a few things here that may well feed them.On the gaming side, Undead Fortune is classic Hacksaw. It stands on the shoulders of slots the studio has released in the past while taking players' hands and leading them somewhere new. Walking Wilds might not be super new, but here, they get the chance to award multipliers when walking or, in the Expanding duel form, grow to cover parts of the grid while accumulating multipliers. Both are available in the base game or during The Curse, where they are technically more likely to trigger. Or, you can buy them from the feature buy, though getting repeatedly slapped down in consecutive losing duels can be irritating.The Tomb is something else altogether and could be outrageously unpredictable. Bonus buy results ranged from something like 4x the bet up to 4,651x. Others weren't quite so extreme, yet Hacksaw Gaming slots have a reputation for volatility which The Tomb certainly displayed during the review. At full strength, Undead Fortune can reach payouts up to 10,000x the bet. With the studio's track record and stacks of potential multipliers in Undead Fortune, it certainly seems doable.From an initial focus on online scratch cards, Hacksaw Gaming has become something of a darling amongst certain streamers, and it's not hard to envisage them (amongst others) destroying Undead Fortune's feature buy button, too. Fortunately, recreational gamblers should be able to extract entertainment from Undead Fortune as well, provided they're braced for a potentially rocky, volatile ride, and don't mind a horde of undead beings regularly trying to administer a beating.

title: Rising Royals
structured_summary: Rising Royals is a royal-themed slot set in 18th Century France, capturing the era’s aristocratic luxury and revolutionary spirit. The game features a respin mechanic with symbol locks and upgrades but lacks additional bonus features like wilds or free spins. The reviewer finds it visually stunning but offers low payouts and limited excitement, making it less appealing compared to similar slots. Its bright, rich graphics and lavish palace backdrop are complemented by elegant design, though the audio is not specifically mentioned.
review: Rising Royals : OverviewJust for the Win’s new slot continues their tradition of making gorgeous looking games that belie a medium volatility with low returns. Royal themed slots pop up from time to time but aren’t all that common. There is an opportunity there for developers to make a big impact and stake a claim in a fairly sparse category. Competition includes slots such as the LeoVegas original Royal Family from Yggdrasil and Play n’ GO’s Royal Masquerade. So, how does Rising Royals measure up?First is the royal theme which has a lot of promise due to the rich, overblown imagery that could be used. Where Royal Masquerade was based around the Italian upper classes, Rising Royals focuses on 18th Century France. As we know, the French Aristocracy famously came to a sticky end during the Revolution. The lower classes, tired of being oppressed by their self-proclaimed betters, rose up and took back control in a sea of blood and executions. In a way, Rising Royals has managed to capture the spirit of the age quite accurately in this new slot. After a few spins, players will get a glimpse of how an exploited French worker back then might have felt.The 18th-century upper class lived unbelievable lives of luxury. We are talking bling that continues to amaze even today. The huge palace on load screen is an example of such ostentatiousness. When the 5x3, 20-payline reel set, flanked by shimmering chandeliers grace the screen, it's hard not to produce an involuntary gasp. The graphics, typical of Just for the Win, are pretty indeed - bright and rich in colour. But don’t let them dazzle you. There is less to this game than initially meets the eye.The first let down occurs when you visit the paytable. For starters, there aren’t many symbols, and their values are pitiful. The low pay J - A symbols start things off with 0.8x to 3x the stake. There are four high pay symbols comprised of a curly-haired lesser noble, a duchess, a duke and the game’s logo. Payouts for these symbols start at 1x and go as high as 15 times your stake for five of the logo. Not exactly the princely sum you would expect from the cashed-up aristocratic set.Bets start at 10 c/p and can be set as high as $/€250 per spin. For that, players get a decent RTP of 96.01% and medium volatility. The game does tend to payout frequently, but wins are frustratingly low - even when locking in a good number of the high pay symbols. Usually, in this situation, you could count on a bundle of extra features to come swooping in to save the day, alas…Rising Royals : FeaturesRespins feature in actionRising Royals is surprisingly light on features. There are two that work in tandem - a Respin feature which can also trigger a symbol upgrade. How it works is that when a combination of high pay symbols land, they are locked in place and trigger a respin. If another high pay combination or more symbols from the first combo land, they are locked into place as well. This process repeats until no more appropriate symbols land, or the reels are covered in locked symbols, then the player is paid out.In addition, each time there is a symbol lock the chandelier meter on the side of the reels lights up. There are three sections, and when they are all lit, the locked symbols get Upgraded to the next highest on the paytable. The process can be repeated. So if the meter is filled again then the symbols are upgraded once more to the next highest level.As far as features go it works quite well. In combination with a multiplier, or higher value symbols, it could have been pretty potent. As it is, it does get a tad repetitive, and the returns just aren’t enough to keep you hitting the spin button. It’s not mandatory that a game offers a wild or scatter of course, and slots can achieve greatness without them. But, in the case of Royals Rising they would not have gone amiss.Rising Royals: VerdictOnce again Just for the Win has produced another pretty yet unexciting low-value slot. It begs the question, who is playing these games? Because there must be a lot of satisfied punters lapping these games up to justify the steady stream that are churned out. The answer must be recreational gamers happy with regular low value wins to keep the spins ticking over.Low symbol values aren’t necessarily a cause for concern - as long as a slot’s features are able to work with them to create decent wins. Sadly, that is missing, and Rising Royal’s features don’t come anywhere close to providing much intensity. With a top prize of around 300 times your stake why bother? The respins/upgrade feature is okay, but the game is screaming out for more. Multipliers, free spins, or a wild at the least could have provided more thrills. But, the French Aristocracy was never known for its generosity, so let them eat cake we guess. In that way you could say Just for the Win have captured the essence of 18th Century French Aristocracy nicely.In the royal/aristocrat slot category, Rising Royals has come up short against the competition. Royal Masquerade, for example, keeps things to the point with a solid top prize and extreme volatility, not to mention a lot more extra features. The bottom line is if you are in the mood for gambling with royalty, there are better options out there.

title: Cat Wilde and the Doom of Dead

review: Cat Wilde and the Doom of Dead: OverviewRich Wilde, the debonair scholar gentleman, is back in this… Hold up, wait a minute. Scratch that. The series has sent him to all manner of far-flung destinations and now sees his daughter take over the family business.So how did she do? Not too bad at all, though copying a guaranteed winning formula has certainly helped her chances. For a first solo outing, a 'Book of' copy is a fairly safe bet, so it would be nice to see Cat branch out if Play n’ GO choose to use her again in the future.Fans of this style will be pleased to know that despite a switch-up in characters, the gameplay and potential remain bang on point. title: Shifting Seas

review: Shifting Seas: Slot OverviewAccording to science, the face of the planet has changed a lot over the millennia as land masses have formed, shifted, and moved across it. Since humans popped onto the scene, one constant has been our desire to travel between these land masses, across seas, and sometimes plunder on them. Shifting Seas from Swedish software provider Thunderkick is an online slot that explores some of these concepts of change. It's a pirate-themed game played on a dynamic, shifting reel set, offering Avalanches, Shift Wins, three Special Wild features, and a Wild Reel bonus round.Part of the reason for pirating's enduring romanticism has got to be the gorgeous weather and exotic locations that often accompany it. Characteristic of a Thunderkick slot, a cartoon element enters the game in the form of its pirate crew symbols, creating an inviting scene for a bit of keyboard swashbuckling.Shifting Seas slot - base gameNot just keyboards; any device may be used to play Shifting Seas on where stakes of 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin may be selected. In all four return settings, players get a highly volatile math model.On the front end, one of the first things you notice about Shifting Seas is its unusual, though not unique, grid matrix made up of 6 reels, laid out in a 4-4-3-3-2-2 pattern. The rightmost reel is removed, and a new reel is added to the left-most side of the grid. On each Shift Win, each new reel increases in height by +1 symbol, up to a maximum of 7 symbols high.Avalanche FeatureIn addition to the Shift Win, the symbols that were used to make the winning combination are removed from the reels by the Avalanche feature. New or existing symbols drop down from above into the empty positions. Avalanches continue as long as new pay way wins hit.Shifting Seas slot - Wild Surge feature in actionSpecial WildsWhen a Special Wild feature symbol is used in a win or pushed off the game area, its respective Special Wild feature is activated. If more than one Special Wild feature is triggered, they play out in this order – Boost Shift, Symbol Rush, and Wild Surge:Boost Shift – triggers an extra reel shift, enabling a new reel to be added to the left-most side. All symbols on the previous left-most reel are copied to the new reel.Symbol Rush – randomly transforms 4-8 symbols into new identical symbols.Wild Surge – randomly transforms 1-3 symbols into wild symbols.Free Spins Bonus GameWhen players manage to Shift Win the bonus symbol off the grid, 8 free spins are awarded. If during the bonus round the bonus symbol is shifted off the board, an additional +4 free spins are awarded. In free spins, a Wild Reel may appear with a starting multiplier of x1. After a Shift Win, the Wild Reel moves one position to the right. If the Wild Reel is moved off the board by a Shift Win, it reappears on the left-most reel, increasing its multiplier by +1 and awarding an additional free spin.Shifting Seas slot - free spinsShifting Seas: Slot VerdictSwashbuckling is one of those slot themes that comes around again and again, yet the good thing about it is, for whatever reason, developers often do something unusual with it. From Relax Gaming's Dead Man's Trail to Yggdrasil's Pirates 2 Mutiny to Foxium's Boom Pirates. Shoot, look at the Branded Megaways franchise that followed on from Iron Dog's Pirate Kingdom Megaways. Not always, but there is something about the salty tang, warm wind on skin, or the sniff of treasure in the air that inspires certain studios to get creative.Some blue sky thinking certainly went into Shifting Seas' list of features, growing reels, rows, and ways. There's a hint of Infinity Reels/InfiniReels going in, what with the way new reels are added. However, instead of growing reels, the shifting symbols off the right side of the grid play nicely into several feature triggers. Doing things this way creates a snowballing effect which works hand in glove with the Avalanche mechanic as well. Special Wild symbols and their trio of effects add variety, and the increasing Wild Reel multiplier is the icing on the cake. Shifting Seas brings everything together to create a next-level interplay of several different parts. The loot part is taken care of, too, theoretically speaking, where wins of up to 15,000x the bet are technically possible, making Shifting Seas one of Thunderkick's higher potential slots. Having said that, epic Thunderkick wins are quite rare to see on social media so a more realistic aim should be around 500-3,000x.At times, Shifting Sands multiple parts might seem like piecing together scattered shreds of a map for a chance to find treasure. That may be the case, but like Ralph Waldo Emerson said, 'It's not the destination, It's the journey.' And there is plenty in Shifting Seas to enjoy along the way. Still, despite what the aphorism might say, making it all the way to Shifting Seas' ultimate destination wouldn't be too shabby at all.

title: Hyper Gold All In

review: Hyper Gold All In: Slot OverviewHear the words 'all in' in connection with gambling, and you know something big is about to go down, right? So yeah, not exactly getting off to an 'all in' start.Hyper Gold All In does get off to a certain level of sensory overload, though, full of so many flashing lights it almost needs to come with a warning. To the left side, for some reason, is a bundle of skyrockets to celebrate a solid result, perhaps, alongside commentary such as 'Go for the gold' or 'Nice move'. Eh, the fireworks effects are low-key amusing, as is the audio. Movin' right along.Hyper Gold All In slot - base gameBet selection in Hyper Gold All In goes from a low of 20 cents to a high of $/€60 per spin. The number of tokens collected by each bonus enhancer helps determine what is awarded for the bonus feature.Green token - collected by the bonus prize indicator, awards a bonus prize. Up to 9 bonus prizes can be collected in the base game.Blue token - contributes 0.5x increase to the multiplier up to x10, as recorded by the bonusmultiplier indicator.Purple token - contributes a bonus spin to the bonus feature. Up to 12 bonus spins can be collected in the base game.Bonus enhancers reset when the bonus feature is complete. They reset with up to 3 bonus prizes, x2 bonus multiplier, and 5 bonus spins when returning to the base game.Bonus FeatureScatters are collected when they land for a chance of randomly triggering the bonus feature. When activated, whatever bonus enhancers have been collected are awarded for the round. At best, it is possible to win up to 20 bonus prizes, an x10 bonus multiplier, and 12 bonus spins. The combination of prizes is determined when the feature triggers.The bonus round displays bonus prizes and bonus tiles. Bonus tiles can also randomly change to bonus prizes, and additional bonus prizes can be awarded during bonus spins. The multiplier can be randomly applied to a bonus prize on every bonus spin - up to a maximum of 12 bonus prizes. At the end, prize values on the screen are paid out, plus, getting 5, 10, 15, 18, or 20 bonus prizes awards an extra 5x, 15x, 30x, 50x, or 1,000x the bet.Hyper Gold All In slot - bonusHyper Gold All In: Slot VerdictHmm, don't want to sound all bratty elitist or anything, but it didn't really feel like Gameburger Studios went all in when making Hyper Gold All In. Partially in? Maybe. Basically, Hyper Gold All In was a rerun of Mining Pots of Gold with a jazzy, Vegasy makeover. It looks generic, flashy yes, but generic, and has nothing new or interesting mechanical to check out, so few thrills were experienced during the review. Perhaps the Games Global fan base will be satiated for the five minutes it takes for the next mutation to come along, but to put it nicely, Hyper Gold All In didn't seem destined to make a big splash on the gambling scene.But, there must be a sizable crowd ready and willing to lap up what the Games Global studios sling at them, and Hyper Gold All In likely has an appreciable audience out there, too. It's 4,000x the bet max win shoots for the mid-ground, in a game that, on the whole, shoots for the mid-ground as well. Recycled gaming in a jazzy skin is tough to big up, and it's hard to think of much more to add other than Hyper Gold All In's pop was closer to a Christmas cracker than an extravagant skyrocket. By the end, there wasn't much about Hyper Gold All In that was either 'hyper' or 'all in'. Rather, Hyper Gold All In was another one of these Games Global studios' slots that patches together parts of previous games and is marched out the door to keep the freight train of mediocrity rumbling along.

title: Mayan Eagle Nobleways
structured_summary: Mayan Eagle Nobleways is a Central American-themed slot set in the Yucatan Peninsula, featuring classic Mesoamerican symbols and temples. Its key features include the Nobleways mechanic with 15,625 fixed win ways, Rolling Reels, Mystery Symbols, and free spins with a progressive multiplier. The reviewer finds the game very high volatility with infrequent free spins, making it challenging but rewarding for patient players. Visually, it offers a nice thematic backdrop with step pyramids and rhythmic drumming, though the symbols appear somewhat dull and overly bright simultaneously.
review: Mayan Eagle: OverviewMicrogaming partner All41Studios is the mastermind behind the Central American driven slot Mayan Eagle. The theme might not be new, but the game is the first to use the in-house designed Nobleways mechanic. Sounds pretty, well, noble, but in effect, it's not the most innovative device you'll come across - nor the most sophisticated.It plays well with the other features though, Rolling Reels in particular, but don't expect to be dazzled on the whole. On that note, buckle up for a trek through the steamy Yucatan Peninsula for some Mayan infused gaming.Step Pyramids, temples, and carvings great players once the game loads. It's a classic Mesoamerican view, and quite a nice looking one indeed. Not so pleasing to the eyes is the 6 reel, 5 row game area, unfortunately. There is something a little off about the symbols. Somehow they manage to be just a little too bright, yet dull at the same time. Anyway, no biggie once they get going. Rhythmical drumming completes the picture, which welds to the gameplay after a while, in a throbbingly repetitive way.Players set stakes by hitting the coin icon where options from 20 p/c per to $/€20 are located. Hold on to your hats because volatility has been rated as not just high, but 'Very High'. Testing could find nothing to refute this claim. RTP is decent at 96.43%, but what helps keep things ticking along is a rather high hit frequency of 37.6%. On the other end of the spectrum is the free spins frequency of 1 in 434 spins which roughly puts it in the same league as Bonanza. Encountering a dry spell can be a killer.Mayan Eagle's centrepiece is the trademarked Nobleways mechanic. In essence, Nobleways is 15,625 fixed win ways over the game's 6 reels. It is a lot of win ways to have in play at once, though maybe not quite a slot revolution. Still, the high number of win ways combined with Microgaming's Rolling Reels can be a potent mix.There is nothing complicated about winning on the Nobleways system. Three or more symbols, left to right, create a winning combination – just two or more in the case of the golden mask. Matching symbols may sit in any row, hence the high number of win ways. Landing a win triggers the Rolling Reels feature which clears those symbols off the grid. New ones fall into the spaces causing a chain of hits one after the other. When no new wins appear the sequence is over and the total prize paid.The symbols involved are split into low pay 9-A royals, and four high pays. Classic Mayan masks make up the premiums, coloured green, blue, red, and gold, returning 2x to 50 times the stake for six of a kind. The wild symbols slots in here nicely, appearing on reels 2 to 5 only, to substitute for any of the regular pay symbols.Mayan Eagle: FeaturesMayan Eagle - free spinsAs well as Nobleways and Rolling Reels, players get Mystery Symbols plus Free Spins to make use of. Mystery Symbols can turn up on any spin, either base or free. They only land on the initial spin, never through a subsequent Rolling Reel. All Mystery Symbols in view change to reveal the same matching symbol. They arrive in groups of eight or more, morphing into anything except the wild or the scatter.The most profitable part of the game is the free spins - 12 are awarded when four M-A-Y-A scatters land in view simultaneously. Should any more scatters be present, then they add +2 free spins each. During free spins, players benefit from a progressive win multiplier, starting at x2 and increasing by +1 on every Rolling Reel. The multiplier does not reset between spins but continues ever upwards with no set limit. Should another 4 scatters land in view during the round, then 12 more free spins are added to the total.Mayan Eagle: VerdictWell, no one said slashing through deep bush would be a walk in the park. The earlier explorers or conquerors, if you prefer to call them, didn't have it easy, and neither do players. Catching Mayan Eagle on a down patch is like having the jungle hack you with the machete. What kills it is the free spins frequency - 1 in 434 is no joke and is demoralising enough on paper. In practice, it felt like a full revolution of the Mayan Calendar had passed before free spins finally eventuated. An approach like that might work with a complex slot like Bonanza, not as well here.Strangely, the bankroll remained more or less neutral throughout, helped by the high hit rate and the features. Not just Rolling Reels, but Mystery Symbols popped up often enough to keep the interest level somewhat high. If we weren't conducting a review though, it would have been easy to give up after the first 500 spins lead to a whole bunch of tail chasing. The game makes no bones about being very highly volatile, so if patience is one of your virtues, then rewards are there. Specifically, potential of up to 13,000 times the stake, if you do crack it.However, after playing through free spins once or twice and receiving modest rewards, it is unbelievably tough to stay motivated for the base game again. It's hard not to doubt your tenacity when faced with jogging on the spot for another aeon of regular spins.The new-fangled Nobleways mechanic doesn't really offer anything new. The 15,625 fixed win ways is a lot, but it has popped up in the past. With mystery symbols and all, it's obvious they went for a sort of Blueprint Megaways approach here, and so it comes off as a bit of a knock-off. It's not nearly as sophisticated, refined, or compelling to play though.Mayan Eagle has its moments, there is no denying that, but they can be achingly few and far between. Potential is there, as is some intriguing gameplay via the blend of Nobleways and Rolling Reels. All up, it’s perhaps better suited to wannabe Hernández de Córdobas who enjoy exploring this part of the world.For even more win ways we also suggest you have a look at All41 Studios' first ever Megaways release Shamrock Holmes Megaways.
