title: Big Money Wheel
structured_summary: Big Money Wheel is a retro cartoon-themed slot with a groovy, jazzy game show vibe. It features a unique 2-2-4-4-4-4 reel layout, respins, free spins with sticky Mystery symbols, and a prize wheel bonus offering multipliers up to 1,000x. The reviewer finds it a decent, fun game with solid winning potential but less sophisticated than competitors’ titles. The game sports a finger-clicking, Hanna-Barbera-style aesthetic paired with engaging, upbeat audio.
review: Big Money Wheel: Slot OverviewHuge, mega, bonanza, gold, thrilling, when you pick descriptive, hype words in the online slot biz, they've got to be BIG. The bigger the better, even if reality doesn't reflect the boast. You never see titles like Averagely Flaming Fruit or Low to Medium Jackpot Bronze, even if the game in question and its rewards are on the meagre side. Can't be labelling the possible payouts in casino game maker NetEnt's slot Big Money Wheel as being meagre, though. As well as sizable winning potential, it does have a fair-sized wheel, from which prizes may be gleaned, to go with its respins, free spins, and bonus buys.As well as all that, Big Money Wheel wraps everything in a snazzy outer coating. The look is a teensy generic, yet the game's maker has managed to imbue Big Money Wheel with a finger-clicking, retro cartoon style, Hanna Barbera, or Top Cat, or something along those lines type mood. Several prior slots came to mind as well, but more on them later. A 'groovy, jazzy game show' is how the info sheet described Big Money Wheel, and while game docs are often packed with hyperbole, a glimmer of truth rings through in this instance.Big Money Wheel slot - base gameOne noticeable thing about Big Money Wheel when the game opens up is its 2-2-4-4-4-4 aligned, 6-reel gaming grid. Lopsided matrices aren't exactly as rare as Black Lotus Magic the Gathering cards, yet they're not superabundant either. Pragmatic Play used one in Wild Wild Riches Megaways and NetEnt, too, in the slot Rage. Yes, there is an element of unnecessary gimmick to them, but okay, they're a bit unusual, which is welcome. Welcome also is the default RTP of 96.07% and the volatility for players who like it on the high side. Bets of 20 c to $/€40 per spin are selectable, and this particular matrix provides 1,024 ways to win.Regular ways wins begin from the leftmost side of the grid and hit over consecutive reels. Jack to Ace royals make up the lower-paying symbols, while records, shoes, double basses, and horns are the highs. Wilds hit on reels 3, 4, 5, and 6, as well, substituting for any regular paying symbol type.Big Money Wheel: Slot FeaturesBig Money Wheel slot - respins with coin symbolsOne main objective in Big Money Wheel is collecting the values from Coin symbols, which is possible in the main game during respins or in the free spins bonus round.Coins, Colossal Coins, and RespinsDuring the base game, respins or free spins, coins with random multiplier values of x1 to x25 may land anywhere on the grid, while those bearing values of x50 or x100 may appear only on the two leftmost reels. Moreover, colossal-sized 2x2 coins only appear on the two leftmost reels. In the main game, any Colossal Coin landing with at least one other coin triggers a respin. If at least one coin appears on the reels during the respin, another respin is awarded. When respins end, thecoin values are awarded.Free SpinsA Colossal Big Money Wheel scatter may appear on the two leftmost reels in the base game. When it does, it activates free spins on a 4x6 gaming area. The feature starts with 3 free spins. Landing a new Coin or Mystery symbol on the grid resets the number of free spins. All symbols are sticky until the end of the feature.When the free spin counter reaches 0, and there is at least 1 Mystery symbol on the grid, then the Big Money feature triggers. The wheel spins once, stopping on multipliers of x5 to x1,000, Double, or Triple rewards. The landed wheel result adds the bet multiplier value to all Mystery symbols on the reels. If it lands on Double or Triple, the wheel spins again but can only land on multipliers. This multiplier gets boosted by Double or Triple, whichever is relevant, and the resulting value is placed on the Mystery symbols.Feature BuyAt the feature buy, players can activate free spins with 1 guaranteed Mystery symbol at the start for 90x the bet or free spins with 3 guaranteed Mystery symbols at the start for 150x the bet.Big Money Wheel slot - free spinsBig Money Wheel: Slot VerdictBig Money Wheel was a game that got subtly better than when it first appeared. Initially, the graphics and features didn't make a huge impression, causing harsh words of criticism to boil up in the mind. After holding back the critique to take in what Big Money Wheel presents, the picture got rosier. Okay, the final reaction wasn't exactly 'Ooh, how did NetEnt do that?', but there are positives, and if a game brings to mind a host of, albeit better, prior reviews, it can't be all bad, can it?Those prior games included Slotmill's Money Jar and Money Jar 2, Push Gaming's Dinopolis, as well as Relax Gaming's Bill & Coin, and Chip Spin. No doubt the coin element, a popular slot addition, helped unite them. Whilst Big Money Wheel has a 2+4 unusual grid layout, it is arguably less sophisticated than these other slots. The base game has a fairly basic hold and respin coin feature, and the free spins round is hardly the gambling version of a flight simulator. However, NetEnt has cleverly incorporated a prize wheel mechanic which might create a measure of suspense - if Mystery symbols have landed on the grid, though. Finishing free spins without a Mystery symbol in view might be disappointing. But, get some in there, and the wheel is capable of awarding chonky results, keeping in mind the Double and Triple effects are able to help ramp up the suspense even further if you can get them.The top prize in Big Money Wheel is a cool 12,026 times the bet, which, fair enough, is pretty big money compared to much of what NetEnt had been putting out around the same time - Golden Realms, Gladiator Clash, Mermaids, etc. Still, you know, this is NetEnt, so it's kinda sad to see competitors completely outclass the veteran studio in terms of sophistication. But Big Money Wheel has a fun vibe, and its relatively uncomplex coin reward system has merit.

title: Hot Shots 2
structured_summary: Hot Shots 2 is a football-themed slot set on a sandy pitch in a lively forest environment. Key features include expanding wilds, a progressive multiplier in free spins, and the innovative Ultra Bet mode offering boosted RTP and jackpot chances. The reviewer finds the game a solid follow-up with enjoyable gameplay, highlighting Ultra Bet as a standout addition that enhances value. Visually, it features bold animal symbols and a cheerful, upbeat soundtrack with crowd reactions adding to the fun atmosphere.
review: Hot Shots 2: OverviewNo, not the epic Charlie Sheen parody film of the same name, Hot Shots 2 is the follow up to iSoftBet’s football in a forest slot. Most of the gang have returned and the game is set on the same sandy football pitch as before. Other core elements of the original have returned, but interesting adjustments to the math model and features have also been made. The most notable being the addition of iSoftBet’s new Ultra Bet feature. If you have ever wondered what it's like to play footy in a leafy forest while its inhabitants cheer you on, let’s kick-off.Located in a sunny glade, Hot Shots 2 uses a straightforward and popular grid set up of 5 reels, 3 rows with 243 win ways. A patch of land has been cleared for the football pitch with the grid located smack bang in the middle. This time around, the reels are not transparent but are still surrounded by a crowd that celebrates the wins and lets out a disappointing ‘ooh’ sound when the scatters don’t quite hit. A jolly tune plays throughout, and the overall vibe is a fun and cheerful one.Setting bets will get you in the game, which is available from 25 p/c up to $/€25 per spin. While we are looking at the numbers, RTP varies from 96% in standard play, up to 96.5% when the Ultra Bet is active. The first Hot Shot came with a medium variance math model whereas the follow up has been pushed up into the medium/high range.The paytable sees most of the same animal characters again – with a bit of a shuffle. The top dog, so to speak, is now the German Shephard drinking beer - 5 of him pay out 10 times the stake. He is followed by the chicken, the bull, the bulldog, and the fox for the high pay symbols. The premiums are backed up by 9-A royal symbols that have been designed in a big, bold Hollywood style like the font used for the movie The Mask. Obviously, not many sports-oriented tiles on the paytable, though this is partly offset by the football wild symbol. This wild can land on reels 3, 4 and 5 and not only substitutes for any of the regular pay symbols, but it also expands vertically and horizontally to increase wins.Hot Shots 2: FeaturesUltra Bet in playAs well as the expanding wild there are a couple more features which get the crowd cheering. The first is a Free Spins Bonus game with a win multiplier that starts at x1. It is triggered when 3, 4, or 5 Hot Shots logo scatter symbols land anywhere in view to award 10, 15 or 20 free spins respectively.During free spins, the regular wild is replaced by the Golden Wild symbol. This new symbol acts in the same way as the standard wild by substituting symbols and expanding horizontally and vertically. However, every Golden Wild in view also increases the win multiplier by +1. The logo scatter remains in the bonus game meaning it can be retriggered.The second addition, the Ultra Bet, is the more intriguing feature from an evolution of slots standpoint. To activate it, players hit the Ultra Bet button which costs 50 times the stake to receive a batch of 50 spins. During the feature, which is sped up, the rules are the same as normal play, except that stars can appear on symbols and be collected.At the end of the 50 spins, the number of stars collected can translate into a reward. The reward starts at 5 times the stake for 5 stars and goes up to a 1,000 times the stake jackpot if 15 stars are collected. Final point, if the free spins bonus game is hit in that time, it is played after the Ultra Bet spins finish.Hot Shots 2: VerdictAt first glance, not a lot has changed since Hot Shots 1 - either graphically or feature wise. The setting is more or less the same, as are the majority of the characters. On a positive note, the best parts of the first one remain, which is good, such as the expanding football wilds and the decent number of free spins up for grabs. The main changes are the progressive multiplier during free spins, and of course, the new Ultra Bet feature. The original multiplier was stuck on x3 throughout the bonus game whereas the progressive one here can lead to better wins and ups the volatility.The highlight here, however, is the newly introduced Ultra Bet feature which has been quite unusually designed. The interesting thing is that it significantly improves the RTP and adds a chance to land a jackpot reward, yet the 50x cost is the same as you’d pay for 50 regular spins anyway. It’s unusual to see such a sweet deal in a feature buy. In fact, it’s so sweet that it makes regular spins redundant.On a side note, even with the Ultra Bet activated, RTP is a bit lower than the original was, so that is something to keep in mind if you are thinking about some pet filled football fun. When it comes to potential, Hot Shots 2 has its moments. As well as the 1,000x available during Ultra Bets, a full screen of wilds and German Shepherds is technically worth 2,430 times the stake. Add in multipliers from free spins and the game is capable of cracking up some really big wins.All up, Hot Shots 2 can get quite good. Those expanding wilds can be effective at pulling together a bunch of symbols in a solid win, for example. The Ultra Bet is what makes the game, however, as it seems to enhance the slot at absolutely no extra cost, which feels peculiar in a good way. It might not be a big hitter, but for some football-lite play, you could do worse than Hot Shots 2.

title: Wild Donuts
structured_summary: Wild Donuts is a candy-themed slot centered around donuts in a pastel-hued, molten sugar world. It features cluster wins, cascades, wild multipliers, a Random Wild feature, free spins, and a buy bonus option. The reviewer finds it a solid but somewhat formulaic slot with enjoyable gameplay and potential big wins. Visually, the game is bright and sweet-looking with catchy audio but follows typical candy slot aesthetics.
review: Wild Donuts: Slot OverviewEver wondered why donuts have holes in the middle of them? After diving into the subject, most of the answers we uncovered included practical explanations. These ranged from helping ensure donuts cook evenly to the Ancient Egyptians making circular bread so they could hang them on poles above ground where critters and the like couldn't reach them. These days, donuts are both a popular food item and a popular prop in candy, sweet-themed slots. Here is another one by the name of Wild Donuts which comes from Max Win Gaming via Relax Gaming's Silver Bullet platform.Players who like their sweet slots as eye-achingly bright as they are tooth-achingly styled should be pleased with the way Max Win Gaming has presented Wild Donuts. The base game takes place in a pastel-hued molten sugar dream world, oozing sweet stuff wherever you lay your eyes. On the right of the reels is what appears to be the Wild Donuts dinner, while the other side of the screen has what looks like Rio De Janeiro's Sugarloaf Mountain if it was covered in icing sugar. The scene is certainly set for a candy-filled, donut-dripping, glazed sweet slot; let's see what happens next.Wild Donuts slot - base gameThe first thing to do is pick a stake where the options begin at 20 p/c before maxing out at $/€100 per spin. Any device may be used to play this highly volatile slot, which generates a theoretical return to player value of 96.3% when playing normally, or 96.5% when buying free spins. The gaming part of Wild Donuts occurs on a 6x6 sized grid, awarding wins when at least five matching symbols are adjacent to each other, vertically or horizontally.Being a grid slot, hitting a five-of-a-kind cluster win pays 0.1x to 1x the stake, rising to 15x to 100x the bet if a winning cluster includes 14 or more matching symbols. From low to high, the items on the paytable are made up of orange, blue, green, pink, purple, and red treats, with a rainbow-striped donut as the most valuable of the bunch.Wild Donuts: Slot FeaturesWild Donuts slot - free spinsWhen mixing up this batch of donuts, Max Win Gaming has stirred in features such as a cascade mechanic, wild multipliers, a Random Wild feature, free spins, and a bonus buy.Cascades Win MechanicWhen a winning cluster hits, the symbols involved in the cluster (except wilds) are removed from the grid. Symbols then drop down into the empty cells, and if a new cluster is created after the drop, it also gets removed from the board. Cascades continue until no new wins are formed.Wild MultipliersGolden crowned donuts are wild, which substitute for any regular pay symbol. Wild Donuts land with a random multiplier of x2 to x10, applied to any win they are part of. When more than one wild multiplier is part of a cluster, the wilds take turns applying their values to the win. Wilds also increase their multiplier for each winning cluster they have participated in. When a cluster has been removed from the board by the cascade feature, wilds may move to a new position before the empty spaces are filled.Random Wild FeatureWhen the Random Wild feature triggers, 1 to 6 wilds are added to the grid, one per reel before the regular symbols appear.Free SpinsLanding 3 chef-covered bonus symbols awards 10 free spins. Any more bonus symbols than 3 in view award an extra +2 free spins each. During free spins, the Random Wild feature is active before each free spin. Hitting 3 or more bonus symbols while the feature is active retriggers it.Buy FeatureIf available, clicking the Buy Free Spins button lets players buy the free spins bonus round at a cost of 100 times the total bet, instantly triggering free spins rather than having to chase it.Wild Donuts slot - free spinsWild Donuts: Slot VerdictThere you have it, fairly short and sweet, which is apt really for a game about donuts. Two of the main elements in this slot are audio-visuals and gameplay. The former element Max Win has pretty much nailed, creating a game that drips with unhealthy yet delicious-looking snacks. At the same time, Wild Donuts' look is a little formulaic, though, sweety slots often tend to look the same, with the exception of trailblazers like Big Time Gaming which located its iconic Donuts game in the middle of a desert of all places. Wild Donuts is more traditional, following slots like Sweet Bonanza and the like when it comes to the game's environment.The gameplay is a tad formulaic as well in some ways but fits in with the spirit of this slot genre. Essentially, Wild Donuts boils down to a mix of clusters, cascades, and wild multipliers, which, fair dues, is a solid selection of features when things are rolling your way. The only slight irritant some may have is a possible laggy quality to the Random Wild feature. It's really not that bad, but the way it cycles through all six reels might be a bit slow-paced for some tastes. Others may appreciate the possible build-up of tension this method provides, and the added wilds can go on to cause a bit of mayhem, as well. Like, say, Jammin' Jars, it's when more than one bouncing progressive wild multiplier is being applied to wins that the pace can ramp up. On the subject of mayhem, Wild Donuts is capable of spinning together some pretty impressive numbers, climaxing in a top win figure of 10,000 times the stake.Speaking of Jammin' Jars, many of the features in Wild Donuts have a strong familiarity to them, as does the presentation. As such, Wild Donuts doesn't light the imagination like a Willy Wonka's Whipple Scrumptious Fudgemallow Delight bar might, but it's a competent candy-themed slot with a comfortable look and features that can get the job done when the game's chef mixes them just so.

title: Halloween Horrors Megaways
structured_summary: Halloween Horrors Megaways is a Halloween-themed slot set in a generic graveyard scene with standard spooky motifs. It features a 6-reel Megaways setup with tumbling wins, free spins with locking reels, win multipliers, and a buy spins option. The reviewer finds the game unoriginal and dull, reusing old mechanics and lacking engaging thematic elements. Visually, it is bland but functional, with decent music that offers some atmospheric support.
review: Halloween Horrors Megaways: Slot OverviewProving that you can, to a degree, predict the time of the year by the sort of slots being released comes Halloween Horrors Megaways from developer Iron Dog Studio. Okay, that was a bit of an exaggeration, but you can certainly tell when Halloween and Christmas are getting closer as casino game makers release their seasonally themed games. Sometimes, you get lucky, and the studio in question designs something completely original, like Lucksome's irreverently humoured Christmas slot Saint Nicked. Other times, you get stocking fillers like Halloween Horrors Megaways, which felt like they were knocked out in an afternoon using spare parts.Okay, maybe not an afternoon, but Halloween Horrors Megaways is a close (though not entirely the same) reskin of Pirate Kingdom Megaways, one of Iron Dog Studio's early Megaways slots released in 2019, which also went on to serve as a foundation for the studio's Branded Megaways concept. This means there really isn't anything in the way of novel features to look forward to. On the front end, Halloween Horrors Megaways presents a pretty bland Halloween scene, as well. The location is a graveyard at night, full of twisty branched trees, gravestones, a green-eyed pumpkin, candles, a house on the hill, that sort of thing. It's all unimaginatively generic, not an eyesore as such, yet visually, Halloween Horrors Megaways lacks anything interesting or engaging to remark on. The music's pretty decent, though.Halloween Horrors Megaways slot - base gameHalloween Horrors Megaways plays out on a 6-reel gaming grid, landing 2 to 7 symbols on each reel on each spin. This mixes up the ways to win, where the maximum number possible is 117,649. Motoring along with a highly volatile math model, the RTP comes in at 96.13%, which for the record is slightly lower than Pirate Kingdom's 96.2%. Wins pay left to right from the leftmost side of the reels, and players may pick a stake of 20 p/c to $/€20 to go trick or treating.Whenever a winning way occurs, the winning symbols are removed, and the symbols remaining on the reel strips tumble down. If after the symbols drop, another win is created, the tumble feature will repeat the process. Ten regular pay symbols line the pay table, with 10 to A spookily decorated card ranks as the lows and 5 progressively scary-looking high pay character symbols. The high pays are a Frankenstein's monster character, a wolf, a witch, a mummy, and a pumpkin head fellow. Hitting a 6 OAK low pay win awards 0.6 to 1 times the bet or a 6 premium symbols win pays 2 to 25 times the bet. Wilds are present on all but the leftmost reel and substitute for all non-special symbols. X2 Wilds also land on reels 2-6 and may substitute for any non-special symbol. Up to 3 X2 Wilds can appear on the same spin, multiplying their values up to x8.Halloween Horrors Megaways: Slot FeaturesHalloween Horrors Megaways slot - free spinsFollowers of Iron Dog Studio's work will feel at home amongst Halloween Horrors Megaways' features, which include stalwarts such as free spins with locking reels and a win multiplier, plus a suite of free spins buy options.Free SpinsTumbles not only lead to repeat wins, but enough consecutive tumbles trigger the free spins round. More specifically, getting 4 consecutive tumbles in a row awards 8 free spins, plus you get +2 free spins for tumble 5, 6, and 7+. 14 free spins are the most you can get. Free spins have a win multiplier, which starts on x1 and increases by +1 following each win. Also, if a reel shows 7 symbols on it, it becomes locked so that it will always land 7 symbols until the end of the round. Each time a reel locks, a +1 free spin is awarded, even if it happens on the final spin. Another way to get more free spins is to achieve 4+ consecutive tumbles. Each consecutive tumble from 4 and onwards awards +2 free spins up to 14.Buy Free SpinsFrom the feature buy menu, players can buy 6, 8, or 10 free spins with either 0 or 1 starting locked reels. Prices range from 30x to 130x the bet and return values are 96.15% to 96.45%, depending on the option chosen.Halloween Horrors Megaways slot - free spinsHalloween Horrors Megaways: Slot VerdictIt feels like Iron Dog Studio was treading water with this one since Halloween Horrors Megaways is a rehash of a slot released about 4 years ago with nothing new mechanically to speak of. That situation wouldn't be such an issue if the theme use wasn't so bland, but Halloween Horrors Megaways' appearance has nothing noteworthy, nothing of major interest, nothing that hasn't been used to prop up any number of Halloween slots in the past. You could say the same goes for Halloween slots in general since designers are limited in some ways as to what they can put into them. Even so, Halloween Horrors Megaways feels drier than they usually do, and aside from a few charismatic character symbols, there's little to nothing here to stop your eyeballs from falling asleep.Moving past the sensorial impressions, Halloween Horrors Megaways' gameplay didn't fare much better. Again, if Iron Dog Studio hadn't used pretty much this exact same combination of features numerous times already, the feeling of redundancy might have lessened. Add the two sides of the coin together: low-energy theme use and the umpteenth time this gaming combination has appeared, and you've got a slot it was extraordinarily difficult to feel remotely engaged with or excited about. The stats are sturdy, though, where the max win has been registered as 25,000x the bet on the game info page.To end up, if Halloween Horrors Megaways knocked on our door demanding candy while implying tricks we're in store, if we didn't cough up a Skittle or two, it would be hard to take it seriously. Iron Dog Studio has come up with some good ideas over the years, but it clings to them like a psycho ex who refuses to accept a break-up months after the event occurred and won't stop spam texting or banging on your door at 2 a.m.

title: In the Zone
structured_summary: In the Zone is a modern classic fruit-themed slot blending vintage vibes with contemporary gameplay twists. It features 3 reels with Bigways paylines, multipliers, nudging wilds, linked spins, respins, and five X-iter bonus buy modes. The reviewer finds it a tasteful mix of old and new, offering decent depth but limited appeal beyond niche players due to modest max wins and below-average RTP. Visually, it’s plain and minimalistic, with simple graphics set in a bare, brassy room, lacking ELK Studios' usual visual flair.
review: In the Zone: Slot OverviewA while back, software provider ELK Studios went on a classic slot binge, releasing games such as Win Win, Hit it Hard, and Knockout Diamonds. Proving that the pull of the past is too hard to resist, the team has once again found inspiration from yesteryear and mingled the spirit of an earlier time with modern twists and turns. The outcome is In the Zone, a modern fruit slot that squeezes quite a lot of gameplay onto its limited grid space, mixing old and new into something ELK Studios calls a 'Modern Classic.'If you're used to ELK slots exploding off the screen with gorgeous graphics, deep gaming worlds, and popping artwork, you better take a deep breath before having a peek at In the Zone. That's because while In the Zone has been tastefully painted, it does look plain when judged by the developer's own standards. A lot of developers' standards, really, where the grid sits in a bare, brassy contraption in a bare, stripy room. The graphics probably aren't going to blow hair back, but fortunately, the gameplay is more intricate than a first impression might suggest.In the Zone slot - base gameFor starters, even though In the Zone might only utilise 3 reels, thanks to what ELK Studios calls Bigways, on every spin, including respins, the grid lands 2, 3, or 6 symbols per reel, producing 8 to 44 connecting paylines. Wins are generated when matching symbols are connected horizontally or diagonally on all reels. The studio has worked out a way to bolt on five feature buys, which are optional, though base bet choice is mandatory, and the options range from 20 c to $/€100.Going through the pay symbols from the lowest value to the highest, we find cherries, lemons, oranges, watermelons, bells, bars, sevens, crowns, and diamonds. Payout values vary from 1x the bet when landing 3 winning cherries up to 25x if 3 diamond symbols create a win. When wild symbols hit, they may be used to substitute any regular paying symbol.In the Zone: Slot FeaturesIn the Zone slot - bonus gameFor a small-looking slot, In the Zone comes with a lot of bells and whistles. The extras are multipliers, respins, Nudging Wilds, Linked Spins, a bonus game, and X-iter feature buys. Nudging reels keep the same number of symbols on them and Linked Spins always land with the same number of symbols on them.Gameplay FeaturesMultiplier - Multipliers can randomly appear above any symbol except scatters. Each payline going through a multiplier position is multiplied.Respin - If 2 reels display the same symbols but there is no win, the 2 reels lock in place, and a respin occurs on the third reel. Multipliers on a locked reel are persistent and stay in their positions. Multipliers on a locked reel stay in their positions and are persistent.Nudging Wilds - Landing a wild on a reel forces the reel to nudge down 1 step at a time, triggering respins on the other reels until the wild is no longer in view. Multipliers on nudging reels follow their respective positions, nudging down with the reel and are persistent.Linked Spin - The Linked Spin feature links 2 or 3 reels together by landing identical symbols on them.Bonus GameHitting 3 scatters triggers the bonus game with free spins and a global multiplier. Landing scatters on a free spin triggers additional free spins. The global multiplier starts at x1 and increases for each new free spin and multiplies each win with its current value.X-iterIn the Zone also manages to wedge in five X-iter bonus modes. First is the Bonus Hunt, giving players more than triple the chance of triggering the bonus game at a cost of 3x the bet. Multiplier Mania costs 10x the bet and buys 1 spin with at least 1 guaranteed multiplier on each reel. The Locked Spin buys a spin, guaranteeing the Linked Spin feature for 25x the bet, while the bonus game can be bought for 100x. At a cost of 250x, players can guarantee a Super Spin where the leftmost and rightmost reels only show diamonds.In the Zone slot - bonus gameIn the Zone: Slot VerdictIn the Zone has been billed as a 'Modern Classic', but it's hard to see the same gamblers who got their rocks off playing contemporary slots like those in the Nitropolis range, for example, having the same reaction to this. Some may find it a little too classic than modern for their tastes. However, In the Zone is not as old-fashioned as it might first seem. ELK Studios has built up considerable experience in making classic-looking slots stacked with a wealth of features, and In the Zone certainly counts as one of those.It starts by doing so via the reels themselves, so even though there are just 3 reels, they can land up to 6 symbols and create up to 44 connected ways to win, providing more space to manoeuvre. Within these parameters, the game gets to work nudging reels, nudging wilds, respinning, linking, all sorts, giving curious players a fair amount of details to explore. A lot of these things, maybe all of them on a feature-by-feature basis, don't glow with originality, but mixing them together in a game like this manages to give In the Zone a spark of individuality.After weighing the angles, In the Zone seems to have enough spark to attract players who enjoy blending classic and modern elements in their gameplay. It stands apart from the usual 3x3, 5-payline fruit or joker slots, offering a bit more flair. That said, it's a tricky one to pin down. While it has appeal for a niche audience, the relatively modest 2,500x potential, basic gameplay, and lower-than-ideal RTP might not be enough to entice more hardcore players to give it a spin.

title: Beetlejuice Megaways
