review: Savanna Roar: Slot OverviewIn October 2020, it was announced that Yggdrasil had signed up emerging mobile-first game developer Jelly through its insatiable YGS Masters Programme. Nearly a year later, their first slot rolled off their production line. To say the YGS Masters Programme has been a mixed bag is putting it lightly, firing off slots in a vast range of styles, themes, and quality. You get the impression Jelly has aimed for the middle ground with Savanna Roar, a safe game that is in no way ground-breaking, but which also does its best not to put a step wrong.With YGS, there is simply no telling what to expect next from the patchwork quilt of studios, though in this case, there are a few clues about Savanna Roar from its title. We are indeed back in the heated lands of Africa, the sun rising over a fecund savanna full of wild animals, mountains, acacia trees, and flocks of birds. It's a view experienced players will be well acquainted with, and Jelly has ticked boxes to pull it off to an adequate degree. However, the palate is a little flat, meaning Savanna Roar doesn't have the dazzling colour some African themed slots do, though it does blaze brighter during free spins. The soundtrack is a good one, being an uplifting choral number that is pleasant on your ears.To satisfy Savanna Roar's target demographic, the math model has been set to medium/high while producing a theoretical return to player value of 96.5%. Potential is quite high, aided by a round of free spins and half a dozen animal-based modifiers. It all takes place on a 5x4, 1024 ways action area, allowing stakes from 25 p/c to $/€100 per spin.Winning combinations occur at a rate of roughly 1 in 3 spins when 3 or more matching symbols land in adjacent reels from reel number 1. Jelly keeps it simple by filling the grid with 8 regular pay symbols split between Q-A card ranks and four premium beast symbols. These are buffalo, rhinos, leopards, and elephants worth 0.8 to 8x the bet for a five of a kind winning combination. The king of the jungle doesn't miss out in Savanna Roar either, appearing on the wild to substitute for any paying symbol to help complete ways wins.Savanna Roar: Slot FeaturesSavanna Roar - free spinsThe studio's stated goal was to supply straightforward mechanics, which they've done, though players get quite a few features to liven the game. Here you'll come across four base game modifiers, a respin feature, and a free spins bonus game. The base game modifiers can be triggered randomly on any paid spin:Rhino Stampede! – turns random positions into mystery symbols which transform to reveal the same matching type.Wild Leopard Spotted! – all leopard symbols in view turn wild.Buffalo Charge! – any buffalo symbol in view may spread to adjacent reel positions.Untamed Elephant Spotted! – any elephant symbol in view may expand into a 3x3 sized symbol.When triggered, the respins feature locks reels with bonus symbols in place and awards a respin. If additional bonus symbols land on the spun reels, they are locked as well, and another respin is awarded. Respins continue until no further bonus symbols land, potentially activating free spins.Landing 6 or more bonus symbols triggers the free spins game. Specifically, landing 6, 7-8, 9-11, or 12-20 bonus symbols award 10, 12, 15, or 25 free spins from the base game or retriggers them if the bonus is currently active. During free spins, a couple more modifiers may appear. One is the Wild Leopard Multiplier that turns leopard symbols wild and gives them multipliers of x1, x2, or x3. Also, landing 5 or fewer bonus symbols triggers the Savage Lion modifier, where the bonus symbols in view turn wild.Savanna Roar: Slot VerdictSavanna Roar isn't exactly daring, livin' on the edge game design, but it is a reliable debut from the new studio. Nothing from the theme to the features is particularly imaginative, so don't pick Savanna Roar if you want to see wild creativity while you’re playing a slot. It's understandable in a way since this is Jelly's first release, and they want to make a good impression. Like a first date, you don't want to let all the skeletons out of the closet. Then again, you want some of your personality to shine lest you come across too starchy. Savanna Roar tends towards mediocrity since it was so cautiously designed.On a positive note, there are quite a lot of features in Savanna Roar, so players in its scope have plenty to enjoy. Again, all are carefully curated effects which have popped up in slots since forever, so there is little in the way of innovation. It is the sheer number of them that do their best to keep up player interest. Triggering free spins with a minimum of 6 scatters might seem a lot, but they appear in stacks of threes on the reels, so not as tall an order as you might think. During testing, they landed in threes, so two reels were usually enough to launch the bonus game. Plus, you get the locking respins feature, lending a helping hand.That just leaves winning potential, and this is one thing about Savanna Roar which doesn't disappoint. During a billion simulated spins, Jelly managed to get the game stampeding and recorded a win of 10,459 times the stake.Jelly's aim with Savanna Roar was to produce a slot for players who prefer simplicity over complex games, using a familiar theme and proven mechanics. Job done in this case, as Jelly has nailed its objectives; however, Savanna Roar is so familiar as to be forgettable. Now the cherry's popped, hopefully Jelly can let more of their individual creativity shine next time.

Naturally, it won't happen too often, but the thought of getting the maximum number of 50 free spins with all 15 wilds on each of them is quite a stirring one. Having so many spins and wilds would come in handy for having a crack at Gods of Troy's potential of 6157.7x the bet, a higher figure than many Red Tiger slots released around the same time have had. As well as the possibility of getting a bunch of wilds in free spins, whether players will want to stick around will likely come down to how they feel about the 10-spin system and the theme. Both are kind of traditional, and when mixed together, Gods of Troy is a rather old-fashioned game in a way. Perhaps the conventionality factor will be a major draw for some players.Gods of Troy's ten spins wild addition feature, which, while not unique, isn't a system that crops up every other day. If you've felt the desire to try this sort of thing out, Gods of Troy is as good a place as any to do so. The reels are crossed by 10 paylines on which to form combinations of three matching symbols or more for a payout.Symbol values are rather high right across the board. First up are the low paying J – A royals, all well-styled according to the theme. Next up are the high pays where we get a lotus flower, Ankh, scorpion, snake, and the gods Bastet and Horus. The falcon god Horus brings in a solid 100 times the stake when five appear on a payline. The standard wild, which is a shiny scarab ornament, will give you 100 times the stake for five of a kind while also performing its usual duty of substituting for any other standard pay symbol.Hardcore players will be pleased to see a high volatility rating here (7/10), albeit not as high as Book of Dead for example which comes in at 1o out of 10 in terms of volatility score. Keep an eye on the RTP, which is comes in at 96.23% by default but which can vary by market.Dawn of Egypt (Play'n GO): Features﻿Alongside decent returns during the base game, the developer wizards at Play’n GO have put together a real mash-up of features. It is nice to see that more though went into developing them then it did with choosing the genre. Like exploring ancient ruins, the key feature is a two-tiered level of Free Spins. Initially, free spins are triggered by three or more scatter symbols which can land on any reel. The mysteriously blue pyramid scatter also brings top returns with it. Get four of five on a payline for 5x or 20x the stake. However, get lucky, and score 5 scatters then you are looking at a 1,000x payout.The free spin round begins by spinning the Wheel of the Gods to determine how many spins there will be. The wheel can produce 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 15, or 20 free spins in total. On every single free spin, one high paying symbol is randomly selected. Any lesser value high pay symbols that land on that spin are automatically upgraded to the chosen high pay symbol.Not only that, but during free spins, the pyramid scatter changes into a wild scatter. On the one hand, the wild scatter acts like a normal wild and can substitute for any of the pay symbols. Also, if 2 or more wild scatters land on a free spin they pause the round and trigger Pyramid Spins. Each wild scatter is worth up to 4 Pyramid Spins. This means up to 20 Pyramid Spins are possible and they can also be retriggered indefinitely. What makes Pyramid spins special is that they retain the chosen high pay symbol from the free spin the feature was launched from. This can mean a run of just the chosen symbol, wilds, and royals in play. Once Pyramid Spins have run out the game returns to the free spins round.Dawn of Egypt (Play'n GO): VerdictAs mentioned in the intro, Play’n GO has a soft spot for Ancient Egypt flavoured slot. The benefit for players is that they pull them off well, which you’d expect after all that practice. The interesting thing is that they are starting to kind of look alike. Symbols and backgrounds vary from slot to slot, sure, but they have a familiar ‘quality’ to them. You just know when you are playing a Play’n GO Egyptian themed slot.That’s not a bad thing though as their quality is typically good. On a positive note, Dawn of Egypt’s parts all add up to a dependably enjoyable slot. Potential is equally juicy and is the familiar 5,000 times the stake that Play’n GO like to go with. Dawn of Egypt’s high volatility rating means that when it goes off, lucrative rolls are possible. This is more likely to happen during free spins naturally. The way free spins can lead to Pyramid Spins is not only a great idea but adds an extra dimension to the nerves as well as well as to winnings. The game is not just all about its free spins though. Decent symbol values during the base game prevent it from being a snore-fest. Of course, lines of the highest paying symbols are rare, but they are there lurking should Horus feel the urge to bestow some coins on his acolytes.If you don’t mind a little unoriginality, players will find an entertaining slot with Dawn of Egypt. It ticks all the right boxes, and there is nothing glaring with it in the slightest. Of course, five minutes after playing it can blur into obscurity along with a score of other Ancient Egypt slots. But while its reels are spinning, Dawn of Egypt is more than capable of doling out gratifying gaming.

title: Marlin Catch
structured_summary: Marlin Catch is a fishing-themed slot offering an aquatic adventure with a birds-eye view of clear waters and lively marine life. Key features include sticky multiplier wilds in free spins, a collection bar system, gamble option, and four bonus buy choices. The reviewer sees it as a fresh take on a familiar concept, delivering higher win potential and a more original experience than expected. Visually, the game is bright and friendly with transparent reels showing detailed underwater scenes, enhancing immersion.
review: Marlin Catch: Slot OverviewFishing is a highly popular pastime, spilling over from lakes, rivers, and seas to the reels in abundance. Pragmatic Play's hit Big Bass Bonanza is one of many to strike the right note with armchair anglers, and its success must have caught the eye of rival studio Stakelogic. Stakelogic is no stranger to riding the coattails of others, and this time they've come up with a fishing-themed slot that feels very similar to BBB. However, the resulting slot Marlin Catch isn't what you would call a direct port, since there are no money symbols, ergo, no money symbol collection which was a hallmark of Big Bass Bonanza and others like it. Instead, Stakelogic has tinkered with several elements to produce a much gruntier slot all around. Time to cast off?Marlin Catch either takes players beneath the waves or gives them a birds-eye view of some very clear water, where fish meander and coral sits there doing its thing. Like other similar fishing slots, Marline Catch is big, bright, and friendly-looking, with chunkified symbols all over its reels. Reels happen to be transparent, so players keen on the great outdoors get a better view of the aquatic life bubbling away down there.As fishing is for anyone with a rod, Marlin Catch is suitable for playing on any device, where stakes of 10 p/c to $/€20 are available. A medium/high volatile game, rated 4 out of 5, the RTP comes in different configurations, as high as 96.5%, though there is no mention of whether the return value changes whether you play in the default mode or when activating one of the four possible bonus buy options.Played on a 5x3 sized game panel, with 10 fixed paylines, the job is to hit winning combinations of three or more from the lefthand side across them. The first five symbols on the paytable are puffy BBB-style 10-A card royals which pay 1-5x the bet for a line of five. Then there are hooks, rods, coral, and life rings as premiums, paying out 10-200x the bet for five of a kind. Wilds have the same value as the top premium and substitute for any normal paying symbols.Marlin Catch: Slot FeaturesInterestingly, Marlin Catch does not feature a money symbol collection, which came as a surprise. What it does have is free spins with sticky multiplier wilds, a collection bar system, a gamble feature, and feature buys.Gamble OptionEach winning combination may be gambled or the prize money collected. To gamble, picking the correct suit or colour of a face-down card quadruples or doubles the amount, while picking incorrectly forfeits the winnings.Free SpinsLanding 3, 4, or 5 marlin scatter symbols awards 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. A few new rules come into play here. One is that when wilds land, they stick in position for the next spin. If new wilds land on the new spin, all previous wilds get a +1 multiplier increase – up to a maximum of x7. If no wilds land on the next spin, the previous wild multipliers are reduced by 1, or if they have no multiplier, they are removed from the reels.A collection symbol and collection bar also appear during free spins. Whenever the fisherman symbol lands, it is collected on the bar, even if it lands behind a sticky wild. Each 3 fishermen symbols collected awards more spins and increases the win multiplier:3 collectors award +10 free spins and an x2 win multiplier6 collectors award +8 free spins and an x3 win multiplier9 collectors award +6 free spins and an x5 win multiplier12 collectors award +4 free spins and an x10 win multiplierBuy FeatureIf you are able to, Marlin Catch offers four ways to buy the bonus round. Shelling out 100x, 500x, or 1,000x the bet gets you 10, 15, or 20 free spins. Or you can try your luck by paying 375x the bet for a lucky dip option.Marlin Catch: Slot VerdictAfter the positive reception Big Bass Bonanza and its follow-ups received, there are no surprises to see copycats creeping out of the woodwork. The fact that it comes from Stakelogic, who has no qualms borrowing other people's ideas, just adds an extra layer of inevitability. Well, no ethical qualms perhaps, but Avatar UX's legal challenge over their PopWins mechanic saw Stakelogic paint themselves into a corner where the only way out was to licence it.It feels unlikely the same thing will happen over Marlin Catch between Stakelogic and Pragmatic Play. Partly because Big Bass Bonanza itself was strongly influenced by outside sources. Perhaps Stakelogic has learnt their lesson because the similarities between this and BBB are more tenuous. For one, the money symbol collection has been axed and replaced by a sticky wild multiplier feature which can actually, really go off. Clever the way existing wild multiplier values increase when new wilds hit or are reduced when none do.Having the chance to buy free spins right away is sure to appeal to certain impatient anglers out there, too. It's as if Stakelogic took the bits they liked, gutted the bits they didn't, and went wild with what was leftover. One of the biggest differentiators is the vast difference in the two game's potential. Where BBB topped out at 2,100x, Marlin Catch heads for much deeper waters where players can technically haul in catches worth up to 25,000x the bet.Marlin Catch does things differently enough to sit side by side the slot it resembles rather than just push it completely out of the limelight. There is a place for both slots, in other words. The things that Stakelogic have added, moulded, or changed have made Marlin Catch a more original experience than first suspected. There's the same getting out on the water spirit as before. Just this time, players can buy their way to the bonus, gamble wins if they want, and snag sticky wild multipliers in free spins, meaning much bigger fish on the menu.

title: Dragon Chase
structured_summary: Dragon Chase by Quickspin features an Asian dragon theme set in heavenly realms with warm red and gold tones. The game offers Wildfire cascading symbols, a Free Spins bonus with extra Wildfires, and a Dragon Pearl Respin jackpot feature with four progressive jackpots. The reviewer finds it a solid but uninspiring first jackpot slot for Quickspin, relying heavily on the progressive for appeal. Visually, it boasts polished artwork with swirling fireflies and thematic symbols, complemented by atmospheric audio enhancing the immersive experience.
review: Dragon Chase (Quickspin): ReviewNo other provider has made such a radical change to its core DNA as Quickspin, and though few have ever questioned the company's creative talent, the paytables, on the other hand, have historically been rather disappointing. This changed quite drastically after the release of Dwarfs Gone Wild, a slot that was to be Quickspin's "flagship" title but instead quickly fell into oblivion. With a multitude of features and lots of eye-candy, it made big promises but ultimately failed to deliver. In a time where extreme volatility and massive payouts is the trend, Dwarfs made little (no pun intended) sense.In the wake of Dwarfs, Quickspin decided it was time to grow up, and a few hard-hitting, highly volatile beasts down the road, the company had managed to work its way up to become relevant again by today's standards. While monsterous 5000x+ Quickspin wins still appear to be relatively rare (possibly because they're not played as much as other providers or because the win frequency is lower), the change has been a welcomed one, offering players a broader variety in terms of volatility. With its new Asian-themed Dragon Chase slot, Quckspin takes another important step forward as it marks the release of the studios first jackpot game. Playable from 20 cents to 100€ per spin across all devices, this 5-reel, 3-row, 20-payline slot comes with a Wildfire feature where symbols move downwards with each spin. There's also a Free Spins Bonus where you'll benefit from extra Wildfire symbols as well as a Dragon Pearl Respin feature that can lead to potentially life-changing wins should you trigger the progressive jackpot.Set in the heavenly realms of the dragons, Dragon Chase is designed with a warm colour palette almost entirely made out of red and gold. With fireflies swirling in the background and a fierce dragon resting on the reels, symbols include A to 10 lower value royals as well as more lucrative gold rings, Chinese ingots, frog and dragon statues - the latter being the most rewarding giving you 50 times your stake for a full payline. Of the same value as the dragon statue is the flaming ball which serves as a wild, substituting for all symbols except the scatter.Dragon Chase (Quickspin): FeatureTriggering randomly in the base game, when a Wildfire symbol lands on the reels, it remains in place and move down 1 position each spin until falling out of view. Up to 5 of these can land in one spin and up to 10 Wildfire symbols can appear on the reels together.Dragon Chase also comes with a Free Spins feature which activates when 3 scatter symbols appear on the 3 middle reels. Starting with 10 spins, you can re-trigger the feature with 3 extra spins if you land 2 scatter symbols on reels 2 and 4. The bonus is not too different from the base game, but you'll benefit from extra Wildfire symbols to increase the winning potential. At the end of the bonus, any Wildfire symbols present on the reels will be carried through to the base game. There is a chance to land wins of up to 1170 times your stake here.The Dragon Pearl Respin feature is where the big bucks can be won. Activated when 3 jackpot symbols appear in view, you get 3 spins played on a grid with 15 sparately spinning positions. Whenever a Dragon Pearl symbol hit the reels, it sticks in place while the number of spins resets to 3. The respin feature comes to an end when you either run out of spins or if all 15 positions have been taken up by a Dragon Pearl symbol. Now, each of these symbols will give you a random cash prize worth up to 7 times your stake. More importantly, 4 or more of them will trigger one of the four jackpots accordingly:Mini Jackpot - 4 to 7 Dragon Pearl symbols give you 8 times your stake.Minor Jackpot - 8 to 11 Dragon Pearl symbols give you 28 times your stake.Major Jackpot - 12 to 14 Dragon Pearl symbols give you 138 times your stake.Grand Jackpot - 15 Dragon Pearl symbols triggers the progressive jackpot.Dragon Chase (Quickspin): VerdictAs a first jackpot slot, Dragon Chase is not bad, but at the same time it also brings back memories of the meagre old Quickspin days with its low payouts. When push comes to shove, it's all about the progressive jackpot here and nothing else hardly seems to matter much. Moreover, as a near-clone of NetEnt's jackpot slot Divine Fortune, it doesn't really bring anything new to the table.There is absolutely nothing to complain about in terms of mechanics, gameplay, or artwork, but as a slot it's just not very exciting. Unless you believe you have a realistic chance of triggering the progressive, there's little incentive to play Dragon Chase unfortunately.

title: Jelly Slice
structured_summary: Jelly Slice is a cute, anime-inspired slot themed around jiggly jelly creatures with a playful, sweet aesthetic. The game features a unique Slicer mechanic that slices symbols to increase ways to win, along with tumbling reels, a Razor-Sharp bonus round, and multiple feature buys. The reviewer finds the slot light and less impactful compared to other Hacksaw Gaming titles but acknowledges its innovative mechanics and solid winning potential. Visually, the game is colorful and charming with a pink and cyan palette, complemented by a flowing pink-haired character and a catchy, upbeat style.
review: Jelly Slice: Slot OverviewDepending on which side of the Atlantic you reside on, the word 'jelly' can have different meanings. Broadly speaking, on the American side, jelly is close to the British equivalent of jam, while on the other side of the pond, jelly is usually the jiggly gelatinous substance otherwise referred to as Jello. It's this jiggly stuff which wiggles about in software provider Hacksaw Gaming's slot Jelly Slice, a relatively simple slot that dials up the cuteness factor while easing back the complexity.In fact, the cuteness quotient has been cranked so high for this one it veers dangerously close to almost too sweet for certain tastes. However, some people can't get enough sweetness in their lives, and those appetites might be a better fit for Jelly Slice. To the right-hand side of the screen, we've got a flowing pink-haired, almost anime-style female character, clipboard in hand, while adorable little jelly people land on the reels in a pink and cyan-heavy game world. If your teeth or eyes aren't throbbing in pain yet, that's a positive signal to keep the investigation going.Jelly Slice slot - base gameNext on the list, or clipboard as the case may be, is picking a stake, and the options go as low as 10 cents or as high as $/€100 per paid spin. When pressing the spin button, symbols drop out of shoots onto a 5-reel, 4-row active gaming area where there can be anywhere from 1,024 to 1,048,576 ways to win. When symbols start getting sliced, that's when the ways to win increase. When regular betting, Jelly Slice's volatility is medium, and the default RTP is 96.24%.The tumble mechanic removes winning symbols from the reels after they have paid, then drops symbols to fill the vacated spaces. Tumbles keep triggering as long as new wins keep appearing after the drop. Winning combinations start from the leftmost reel, and matching symbols must land on adjacent reels. The low pays are jelly-ish 10 to A symbols, while the highs are 5 jelly creatures in various colours. Hitting a 5 OAK royal win pays 1 times the bet for all of them, rising to 2-10 times the bet for a 5 OAK high pay win. Rainbow star wilds substitute for any regular pay symbols from any reel. A 5 wild symbol hit pays 20 times the stake.Jelly Slice: Slot FeaturesJelly Slice slot - free spinsSlice by name slice by nature, as Jelly Slice has a Slice Mechanic that chops symbols into bits, as well as tumbles, a Razor-Sharp bonus round, and feature buys.Slicer MechanicDuring the game, it is possible to activate 1 Slicer per reel before the drop starts. The Slicer slices all symbols passing through it into 2, 3, or 4 pieces, depending on the value displayed on the Slicer. Each sliced part counts as one symbol for any potential wins. Slicers persist through tumbles, and any symbol dropping through a Slicer due to a tumble also gets sliced.Razor-Sharp BonusLanding 5 to 20 FS scatter symbols in the base game activates the Razor-Sharp bonus round. Each FS symbol that lands awards 1 free spin for the bonus. During the bound round, there is an increased chance of activating Slicers. The number of FS symbols in view translates to the number of free spins awarded after the scatters have or have not been sliced. For example, 1, 2, 3, or 4 FS symbols in view awards +1, +2, +3, or +4 extra free spins, respectively.Bonus BuyJelly Slice's feature buy section comes with these choices:BonusHunt FeatureSpins - 3x the bet for a spin that is 5 times more likely to trigger a bonus game. Highly volatile, RTP 96.39%.Slicer FeatureSpins - 20x the bet for a spin, which guarantees at least 1 Slicer. Very highly volatile, RTP 96.33%.Razor-Sharp Bonus - 100x the bet. Highly volatile, RTP 96.37%.Jelly Slice slot - free spinsJelly Slice: Slot VerdictJelly Slice has an interesting feature, but it is packaged within a slot that doesn't punch as forcefully as it might have. Some people may argue otherwise, fair enough, and if sweet, adorable, faux anime environments are the absolute bee's knees, then Jelly Slice could be just the thing. Jelly Slice felt light for a Hacksaw Gaming slot and not in the same charming way as, say, a Canny the Can game. It seemed closer in spirit to anomalies like Bouncy Bombs or Vending Machine. As when reviewing those two, Jelly Slice didn't create the impression it was going to be one of Hacksaw Gaming's top performers, but there are points of interest.One is the Slicer feature. It combines perfectly with cascading wins since if a winning symbol or symbols are removed from beneath a Slicer, any symbol tumbling through the Slicer will be sliced in turn. This system has the makings of sweet cascade runs, potentially, not to mention a monstrous number of possible ways to win, provided a bunch of symbols on the grid cut through the Slicer. As a flow-on effect, winning potential of 10,000x the bet is a sizable shake of icing on top and is achievable in all game modes.To wrap up, Hacksaw Gaming has bravely taken a break from the multiplier reel effect to experiment with alternative ways of entertaining gamblers, which is appreciated. The resulting feature has promise, and as is often the studio's way, if the team tinkers with it in future releases, this wouldn't be a bad thing.

title: The Bowery Boys
structured_summary: The Bowery Boys is a gritty 19th-century New York gang-themed slot with a graphic novel style. It features cascades, multipliers, three distinct bonus games, and an all-scatter win system with a wild symbol. The reviewer praises its high volatility, engaging gameplay, and up to 10,000x win potential despite some familiar mechanics. The game boasts moody, cinematic visuals with dark skies and cobblestone streets, complemented by intense, atmospheric audio.
review: The Bowery Boys: Slot OverviewDeveloper Hacksaw Gaming rewinds the clock to the 19th century and heads to one of the most infamous parts of New York City, Hell's Kitchen, in an online slot titled The Bowery Boys. The Bowery Boys were one of New York's earliest gangs, noted for their anti-immigrant, anti-Catholic leanings, and based in the Bowery neighbourhood. They probably weren't the sort of chaps a respectable person would want to associate with, but which make interesting characters in popular culture from movies, books, to online slots.In The Bowery Boys, Hacksaw Gaming has taken a graphic novel approach, dropping the usual cutesy angle for something more cinematographic. It's nothing like the paper mache, fruit 'n veg, cute form their games often take, making The Bowery Boys closer in look to Wanted Dead or a Wild. It's also close in spirit too, as both games delve into a grittier side of life. Played on a 6x5 sized game panel, players find themselves in a dimly lit part of town, possessing a strong Watchmen type vibe. It's all moody skies, yellow moon, cobblestones, with a hint of violence about to explode at any moment. This being Hacksaw Gaming, the action on the reels can pop and bubble just as violently.From a mathematical perspective, The Bowery Boys is a highly volatile game, available in a number of RTP models. The most generous has a value of 96.41% and can be quickly checked by opening up the paytable information. Available on tablet, mobile, or desktop devices, armchair gangsters can load up stakes from 10 p/c to as high as $/€100 per spin.One of The Bowery Boys surprise moments was finding out it does not use cluster pays, which is a Hacksaw Gaming speciality. Instead, makes use of a so-called All-scatter wins system similar to the one used in Joker Bombs and Pragmatic's Sweet Bonanza. Here, all symbols in the game pay like scatters, so as long as at least 8 matching symbols are in view, they create a win. The paytable starts off with 10-A card royals, worth 0.1 to 20 times your bet for landing 8-15+ identical symbols. This increases to 1-100x for landing 8-15+ of the premium boys, fighting men, guns, couples, or lady tiles. Interestingly, there is a wild symbol, landing in the form of a powder keg to substitute any regular pay symbol.The Bowery Boys: Slot FeaturesOne thing The Bowery Boys is not short of is features. Extras to cover here include cascades, Strongboxes, Blasting Bomb Multipliers, and three bonus games.CascadesWhen winning symbols hit, they are removed from the grid, and the gaps are filled by new symbols dropping down from above. This may lead to another win, and cascades continue until no new win appears. Prize money is collected and displayed above the reels as the pending amount. When cascades end, the total pending win amount is awarded and reset to 0.StrongboxesIf a Strongbox symbol lands at the same time as a key symbol, it is opened, and its contents awarded. The three Strongbox types available are small, medium, and large, each awarding a prize worth 2x-5x, 10x-25x, or 50x-250x the bet, respectively. These prizes are added to the total pending win amount above the reels.Blasting Bomb MultipliersThese are bombs that carry values of x2 to x100 and are applied to the current pending win amount. If more than one bomb lands, the values are added together before being applied. Multipliers will only activate if there is a pending win amount currently displayed.Bonus GamesLanding 1, 2, or 3 bonus symbols in the base game awards the Strongbox Storage, Daisy's Dynamite, or Bowery Savings Bank bonus games, respectively:Strongbox Storage comes with 10 free spins. Here, you can store up to 5 Strongboxes in a storage space if they land without a key. When a key does land, it opens any Strongbox on the reels and any in the storage. Each bonus symbol landing in view awards an additional free spin.Daisy's Dynamite awards 10 free spins where Dynamite Multipliers and Detonator symbols come into play. Dynamite Multipliers have values of x2 to x100 and are stored in a Dynamite Box until a Detonator lands. The Detonator triggers all stored Dynamite Multipliers, which are applied to the pending win for the current round.In Bowery Savings Bank, which also comes with 10 free spins, for every win, the same amount is stored in a separate Vault. Keep in mind the original win is always paid. Landing Dice symbols multiplies the value in the Vault by x2-x12. If a Police Officer Badge hits, the police will have to be paid off with 10-50% removed from the current Vault value. When a dollar sign symbol hits, the money in the Vault is won.Bonus BuyIf available, players can buy their way to the Strongbox Storage, Daisy's Dynamite, or Bowery Savings Bank features for 80x, 200x, or 300x their total stake.The Bowery Boys: Slot VerdictIt sometimes feels like Hacksaw Gaming has a real Jekyll & Hyde thing going on. One minute they're producing games full of things like personified food; the other minute, the team's getting about as bleak as it gets in an online slot. Obviously, The Bowery Boys leans towards the latter side of the spectrum. The good news is Hacksaw is as adept at creating gritty games as it is at exploring the adorable side of life. One of their major talents is crafting insanely playable slots, of which The Bowery Boys is another excellent example.This time around, they might not have been as completely original as they usually are, as The Bowery Boys' gameplay has a strong Sweet Bonanza hangover. Scatter win systems aren't super common, though, so it makes a nice change from clusters and can definitely go mental with a solid multiplier onboard. One thing different is the inclusion of a wild symbol which most developers have shied away from when using the scatter pays system, so it's worth a look if you're curious to see how it pans out.Where The Bowery Boys also breaks away from a game like Sweet Bonanza isn't just the inclusion of a wild but is in its set of three bonus games. Each one of them is typical Hacksaw Gaming too. Meaning they're capable of epic teasing when the game is running against you. For example, not getting the Detonator when you've got a few Dynamite Multipliers stored, not getting the key to unlock Strongboxes, or watching your profits evaporate to paying off the cops, oof. Hacksaw games are well equipped to reward, too, though, and if you find yourself on the positive side of The Bowery Boys' volatility, you can win up to 10,000x the bet.Often, Hacksaw builds a game around one or two clever features that get expanded upon in free spins. In The Bowery Boys, players benefit from several compelling features, a trio of tantalisingly good bonus rounds, and a rich world to enjoy them in, or not; these games can be hugely volatile after all.

title: Africa X UP
structured_summary:
Africa X UP is an African-themed slot featuring wildlife and cultural motifs with a 5-reel, 243-ways layout.  
Its key features include a scatter collection system that builds multipliers, free spins with increasing multipliers, and a bonus buy option.  
The reviewer praises its imaginative take on a common theme, high volatility, and strong winning potential up to 30,000x the stake.  
The game boasts rich visuals of African plains and animals, complemented by a Lion King-style soundtrack for immersive play.
review: Africa X UP: Slot OverviewMicrogaming partner Alchemy Gaming transports players to the warm African continent, once again, for an exotically themed slot titled Africa X UP. If you're a relatively young studio, taking on a generic topic runs the risk of being overlooked unless you can do something special with it. To that end, Africa X UP uses a scatter collection system to build win multipliers which then get unleashed when free spins are triggered. Taking a page out of White Rabbit's playbook, players can buy free spins at a reduced cost if they have already collected a few scatters.At first glance, you'd be forgiven for thinking Alchemy Gaming has gone down the 9 Masks of Fire imitation route, with the collection meter and all the cultural touches. But, at closer inspection, the meter actually awards multipliers rather than cash prizes. Alchemy has also delved into the African imagery in more depth, so players get a rich view of a dusty plain, all tussock grass, acacia trees, and distant mountains. A Lion King-like soundtrack completes the scene as players spin a 5-reel, 3-row game grid using 243 ways to win.Highly volatile and playable on any device, Africa X UP offers a range of stakes starting at 30 p/c on the lower end, going up to $/€37.50 per spin. Wins hit when at least three matching symbols land left to right from reel number one. There are 10 pay symbols to work with - five are 10-A card icons; the rest are buffalo, rhinos, elephants, a warrioress and a warrior. Landing a winning combination of five symbols in length is worth a payout of 3.33 to 4.67 times the stake. Moreover, wild symbols appear anywhere and expand to cover all positions on their reel whenever the land. They substitute any pay symbols to complete wins and are worth payouts up to 50 times the bet for five of a kind.Africa X UP: Slot FeaturesAfrica X UP - free spinsThe goal of Africa X UP is to collect X UP scatter symbols to increase a win multiplier which is available when free spins are triggered. X UP symbols land on any reel, and when 2 are in view, they are collected on a multiplier trail located to the left of the reels. The more you collect, the bigger the multiplier becomes, starting at x2, going through x3, x4, x5, x7, x10, x15, and finally x25. Multipliers are stored at each bet level, so changing the stake starts the trail again. If you move back to previous stake levels, you continue from where the trail left off.If three X UP symbols land, then 8 free spins are awarded, and whatever multiplier is active on the trail is applied to all wins during the round. In free spins, landing 2 scatters awards +2 additional free spins and helps increase the free spins multiplier.Africa X UP is a game that may reward patience, yet players not in the mood for some base game collecting can buy the bonus game instead. There are several options here though all award 8 free spins. What changes is you can start them with an x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x7, x10, x15, or x25 multiplier for 18.67, 26.67, 38.67, 50.33, 61.67, 86.33, 120, 181, 300 times the base stake. Or, you can pay 80 times the stake for a random starting multiplier of x2 to x25. If you've already collected a few X UP symbols, then the cost of buying the feature decreases.Africa X UP: Slot VerdictUp until now, we've been used to seeing mainly jackpot style slots like Goldaur Guardians or Wheel of Wishes from Alchemy Gaming. For a young studio forging an identity, the encouraging thing about Africa X UP is that while the team has selected a common theme, the game is relatively imaginative. There's an interesting Wakanda thing going on, coupled with a quasi-spiritual representation of Africa's big animals. No doubt it will help if you've got the biggest multiplier on board, though lesser multipliers can be pretty effective as well. title: Lucky Nuggets Megaways

review: Lucky Nuggets Megaways: Slot OverviewHead beneath the soil for a chance to collect precious items in Lucky Nuggets Megaways, an online slot from software provider Blueprint Gaming. Lucky Nuggets has a wild symbol in the form of a cheerful Prospector, but he doesn't appear until the bonus round, where he also plays another important role; let's take a look.Lucky Nuggets Megaways: Slot FeaturesLanding 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatter symbols awards 10, 15, 20, or 25 free spins, respectively. This is when the Prospector Scatter symbol comes into play, which can substitute for any regular pay symbol. Just as importantly, if not more so, when the Prospector lands in view at the same time as gold or diamond money symbols, he collects them for the player. Money symbol values range from 2x to 2,000x the bet.In addition, whenever the Prospector hits, he is collected on a meter located above the reels. For every 4 Prospectors collected, the game is upgraded, like so:Collecting 4 Prospectors awards +10 free spins and applies an x2 multiplier to any money symbols he collects.Collecting 8 Prospectors awards +10 free spins and applies an x4 multiplier to any money symbols he collects.Collecting 12 Prospectors awards +15 free spins and applies an x10 multiplier to any money symbols he collects.Wait, there's more. If at least 1 new money symbol lands, another respin takes place. It's a textbook example of the way Blueprint Gaming mixes and matches themes, features, and previous games together like an all you can eat salad bar. Taking a bit from there, slicing off a modifier from here to feed the ravenous production line. The result is playable enough for players into mining or money symbol collects, yet Lucky Nuggets felt more like an obligation than an obsession. title: Bust the Bank

review: Bust the Bank (Microgaming): OverviewThere’s a lot that goes into the robbing of a bank. There’s meticulous planning in most cases. A specific date and time need to be chosen. A particular method of getting into the bank and a getaway car for speeding away with the loot should be involved. However, for the robbers in Microgaming's classic 2013 release Bust the Bank, it seems as though none of these things have been considered. Then comes the policewoman driving the cop car, followed by a symbol of her male colleague. The two bank robbers make up the highest-paying symbols of the slot though, with the guy wearing the green cap offering up pay-outs of up to 50 times your stake for 5 on a full payline.Last but not least, it’s important to note that Bust the Bank has its own Wild Symbol, too. Instead, it incorporates some truly thrilling inbuilt features as well.To ensure that this bank job goes down successfully, Bust the Bank has had a few special features imbued into it. The first of these is the game’s Safe Bonus feature. From this, you’re able to win up to six prizes on a single spin. You’ll need to watch out for the bonus safe symbol coming into position on reels one or five. Whenever this lands, it will open and award you with a coin win. If the symbol lands on any other reels, then coins from the safe will pour down and duplicate the coin award over every symbol below it.The slot also includes something known as the Piggy Bank Bonus. Keep an eye out for the piggy bank symbol coming into view in any position on the third reel of the game. This will trigger the special feature, and you’re simply required to click on the piggy bank to smash it. This will then reward you with the Smashing Wild Coin Prize.One other thing to make you aware of, is that the two robbers (known as Larry and Bob) may randomly show up. Once underway, the first and last reels are completely wild throughout the free spins round, offering up greater opportunities to land big wins. Moreover, if a scatter comes into view, you’ll receive an additional free spin on top of the amount you currently have.Bust the Bank (Microgaming): VerdictThere’s very rarely anything negative that can be said about the older generation of Microgaming slots, and this remains true for Bust the Bank as well. It’s a very entertaining slot, featuring a great theme and well-executed graphics to tell the story behind it. When you also factor in the great special features that it provides, Bust the Bank is one of those that shouldn’t be missed out on by anyone.Medium variance, the mathematical design is quite forgiving and will offer plenty of value for your cash more often than not, something that also make it a suitable wagering slot. The entertainment value behind it is second to none, while the great soundtrack, the impressive graphics and overall betting options add to its appeal. These slots typically don’t cause much more than a ripple, but there are a lot of them and they are increasing at an exponential rate.Crystal Mirror finds itself squarely in this camp. title: Apollo Pays Megaways

title: Temple Frenzy Lightning Chase

review: Temple Frenzy Lightning Chase: Slot OverviewFor Boomerang's second instalment of the Lightning Chase range, the studio has moved away from the swords and sorcery of Lady Merlin to a steaming, rather dangerous jungle. Players can still trigger The Lightning Chase Hold & Respin feature from free spins.As well as triggering free spins with scatter symbols, there is a chance they are awarded at random following any paid spin.Temple Frenzy Lightning Chase: Slot VerdictIn several ways, Temple Frenzy Lightning Chase is a step up from Lady Merlin, and strangely, it's not because of what Boomerang has added but what they've taken away. What's left is a colourful jungle romp, which could appeal to players into the hold & respin phenomenon that shows absolutely no signs of subsiding.If anything, there was a major glut of this sort of feature at the time of review, and naturally, some developers do it better than others. At one end of the spectrum, you've got the likes of Nolimit City and Relax Gaming rocking the slots world, while waves of hold & win bandwagoners make up the numbers at the bottom. No need to point any fingers. Temple Frenzy sits in the middle of the scale, not really offering anything particularly novel to the genre. Where Temple Frenzy scores quite well in this regard is its money symbols may possess much larger than normal values of up to 888x each. Prizes this high aren't something you should expect to see often, yet the possibility is there to be surprised.As mentioned, the axing of the Boom+ feature is no great loss. It's great to have betting options but withholding free spins and max potential unless you pay extra feels a tad disingenuous. Well, there's none of that in Temple Frenzy, where all players are spinning for a max win valued at 17,760 times their stake. What's not so raging is the removal of the wild multiplier, though it feels worth it in exchange for a level playing field for all players, not just ballers prepared to ante up.The potential might not be as astonishing as Lady Merlin, yet Temple Frenzy is a better game in just about every other respect. It's probably loud and colourful enough to entertain casual players into hold & wins, though those who prefer extra kick might not find it quite frenzied enough.

Its extra bonus game adds something new, though it's the graphical upgrade that really separates the two games, making Fishin' Reels feel like a proper reboot. Though not a bad game as such, weak potential lets the game down and could prove to be a deal-breaker for those choosing between fishing themed slots.

RTP 96.32%.Oozing RotoGrid FeatureSpins - 75x the bet, each spin guarantees at least 2 Blue Oozing Beakers and 1 RotoGrid symbol land. Purple Oozing Beakers do not appear in this mode. RTP 96.27%.Unleash the Ooze! - 100x the bet. RTP 96.29%.The Twist of the Twisted - 200x the bet. RTP 96.33%.Twisted Lab RotoGrid slot - The Twist of the Twisted! featureTwisted Lab RotoGrid: Slot VerdictAnyone following Hacksaw Gaming's work should be well aware of the studio's fondness for creating spreading wild multipliers, as has been seen on numerous occasions in the past. Having several Beakers oozing into each other as the grid rotates, generating consecutive wins can be really swell. It is clever stuff, bringing together many elements Hacksaw Gaming excels at.Technically potent stuff as well, as attested to by a 15,000x the bet max win that is achievable in all game modes. Once again Play’n GO has pulled in imagery and niche symbols to build a singular game world in which to try your luck. It won't necessarily win the slot of the year award, but nevertheless, it's a solid, well crafted slot that is both engaging and beautiful to look at.You get the feeling Play’n GO could make solid slots with both hands tied behind their back. Perhaps because they produce so many games of decent quality, it makes it harder for anything they create to really stand out. Ring of Odin is guilty of the same. There is nothing negative to report, stats are respectable, and the game is easy on the eyes. It’s just that Ring of Odin feels like another above-average Play’n GO slot that possibly could have been even greater if the developers weren’t so busy already working on the next title on the production schedule.

Subtle in some ways, and to be honest, a bigger, hair-blowing climax was expected, but Win-O-Mart held back from being a total mind melt.To its detriment? Not necessarily, but it would have been interesting to see Print push Win-O-Mart into total head fudge territory. Its hints of madness are fun, though. It also wouldn't have hurt if the base game was a little more interesting, as not much happens on that aisle. The Bonus Bundle is where the trip really begins, and travelling a level or two isn't too hard a task to accomplish. Each level has its plus point; Level 5 is obviously the most desirable of the lot. The Prize Wheel was a stand out due to the way it can be upgraded before finally awarding a prize on the last spin. Like a lot of boundary pushers, some players will get it and be down with Win-O-Mart's singular way of operating. title: Cops'n'Robbers
structured_summary: Cops'n'Robbers is a classic cops-and-robbers themed 5-reel slot with up to 9 adjustable paylines. review: Cops'n'Robbers IntroductionCops'n'Robbers is a 5-reel, 3-row online slot with up to 9 adjustable paylines. It's playable on all devices from €0.01 to €90. This is a remake of a very old Play'n GO slot although it is pretty much a completely different game due to having a new math model.The theme is a classic one that has been done many times before by many of the top providers - Cops'n Robbers by Novomatic, Reel Heist by Red Tiger and Cops and Robbers by Microgaming to name a few.This version by Play'n GO is a bit lower in variance compared to the games recently released by them, which is probably a good move. The wild symbol is the most valuable one by far and gives a return of 3000x for a wild line.Cops'n'Robbers Free SpinsThe Car Chase bonus in actionThree or more police car symbols anywhere on the reels trigger the Car Chase bonus. A sequence of free spins commences in which prizes are awarded more frequently than in the main game. Choosing direction in the bonus didn't really seem to make much difference. We expected to crash and burn if choosing wrong direction, but that never happened (maybe we just excel at picking). Our guess is that the choice makes no difference and that the outcome is already decided. Either you get away, or you don't. Simple as that.With that said, we did enjoy the game and if you enjoy playing less volatile slots, it's very likely you will enjoy it too because of it's intensity, good max win potential and for the relatively frequent bonus triggers.Normally we're not that hyped about medium variance games, but seeing this one has a 14,480x max win potential makes it interesting to say the least. Obviously, something like that will be close to impossible to achieve and it possibly requires multiple wild lines, but seeing the bonus round can go on for quite a lot of spins it's not unlikely that it can reward some good wins.

title: Dynamite Diggin Doug
structured_summary: Dynamite Diggin Doug is a mining-themed slot featuring a cheerful prospector named Doug exploring underground riches. The game offers instant prizes via dynamite symbols and a streak respin Dynamite Bonus with multipliers and lives. review: Dynamite Diggin Doug: Slot OverviewShock news flash folks, the Pragmatic Play and Reel Kingdom duo have put down their fishing rods to create an online slot which does not involve fish, money symbols, or being anywhere near the sea. On the contrary, Dynamite Diggin Doug moves far beneath the Earth's surface in order to play the part of a mining slot, complete with a bearded prospector named Doug. Doug's a cheerful sort, and he fronts a cheerful game that might not be a heavyweight but may attract gamblers in the mood for instant prizes triggered by scatter symbols and a streak respin style round with explosive elements.One of the first things about Dynamite Diggin Doug that grabbed attention was the strangely compelling music. It felt completely out of place, situated down a mine shaft, yet very listenable at the same time. It's a shame the artwork wasn't as striking. There's nothing eye-maiming going on, but nothing wondrous whatsoever either, and some of the animations could be painfully slow. Doug is there, however. He seems like a nice person, but Reel Kingdom's knack for creating slots that look as if they came out years ago is all too apparent in Dynamite Diggin Doug.Dynamite Diggin Doug slot - base gamePropped up in the middle of the scene is Dynamite Diggin Doug's 5x3 gaming grid, which has 10 paylines built in for evaluating winning combinations. The official game information puts the volatility at a potentially scary 'very high' while of the three RTPs, 96.52% is the max figure. With a minimum total bet of 10 c per spin and a maximum of $/€250, players also have access to a bonus buy and an ante bet. The ante bet ups the stake by 50% when activated, granting a higher chance of getting the feature.Symbols now, and down here, Doug is in command of 9-A card rank low pays, as well as items of mining such as spades, lanterns, pickaxes, and carts. Hitting 5 OAK low pay combinations pays you up to 5 times the bet, while a 5-of-a-kind premium win is worth 10 to 100 times the bet. Maybe it got lost in the tunnels, but no wild symbol landed in Dynamite Diggin Doug at any stage.Dynamite Diggin Doug: Slot FeaturesDynamite Diggin Doug slot - free spinsWhile you're bashing on rocks playing Dynamite Diggin Doug, be sure to be on the prospect for instant prizes awarded by the dynamite symbols (or are they candles?) and a streak respin type round going by the name of the Dynamite Bonus. Doug sure likes his dynamite.Instant Dynamite PrizesTo the left of the gaming grid is a list of prize values, running from 0.5x to 100x the bet. The top three prizes also include the Bronze, Silver, and Gold bonuses, which would appear to be upgraded versions of the bonus round. Next to each prize is a number. When a number of dynamite symbols land on the grid, the corresponding prize is awarded. Occasionally, Doug appears on the reels to pop a detonator and award a prize.Dynamite BonusWhen triggered by landing at least 3 scatter symbols, the Dynamite Bonus is held on a gaming grid landing only dynamite symbols and blank spaces. The round starts with 3 lives, which reset when a new symbol lands on the grid. Next to the reels is a lit fuse that is able to grant multipliers when the fuse is completely burned out.Now, when a new dynamite symbol lands, all of the dynamite symbols move down one position, and the fuse burns one step. Dynamite prizes that fall off the bottom of the grid are collected by Doug, awarding their values to the player, who then throws the dynamite back onto the reels, increasing already existing prize symbols or adding new ones. It is possible to buy entrance to the bonus round for a cost of 100 times the bet.Dynamite Diggin Doug slot - free spinsDynamite Diggin Doug: Slot VerdictReel Kingdom might have struck massive success with its Big Bass range of slots, but when you play a game like Dynamite Diggin Doug, you kinda wonder how they did it. It's just not great. From the budget visuals to the so-so-at-best features to the meh-win stats, the studio really stumbled onto paydirt when reeling in its fish range. This is possibly why the studio continues to cling so tightly to it, releasing endless reams of clones, reskins, and follow-ups. As such, encountering a Reel Kingdom production that doesn't leave your fingers smelling like fish should be a joyous occasion. Dynamite Diggin Doug steps up by presenting an amiable environment, and the music is oddly compelling, yet the game doesn't follow through well, and as far as mining slots go, there are far stronger examples.Other contenders for the highly volatile, high-stakes mining slots would be those like Dead Canary or the Fire in the Hole games. Dynamite Diggin Doug taps away at the dirt on the other end of the scale than those two, as evidenced in part by its 3,000x win cap. The entertainment wasn't massive either. The base game inched along, producing few wins, and those that did hit tended to be of the 3, maybe 4, dynamite prize variety, which really wasn't enough to keep the balance very buoyant. Line wins were oddly rare. The Dynamite Bonus round is an odd one as well, refusing to pay out unless cash symbols are forced off the bottom of the reels for Doug to collect. He does throw sticks back onto the grid to potentially stack rewards, and the multiplier helps make a noticeable difference to end results if you're able to get it.Dynamite Diggin Doug was a game which struggled to ever take off, to the point there was a wonder it actually could. Ah, well, it's not a fishing game, but weirdly, after Dynamite Diggin Doug had been put through its paces, there was a thought that maybe Reel Kingdom is better off sticking to their winning BB formula if this is the alternative.

title: Towering Pays Valhalla
structured_summary:
1. Towering Pays Valhalla is a Norse mythology-themed slot by GamesLab featuring expanding towers on reels.  
2. Key features include Mega Tower Magic, expanding grids up to 5x8, multipliers, and a four-stage free spins trail with increasing complexity.  
3. The reviewer finds the game somewhat outdated and convoluted, with limited paylines and modest wins despite the expanding grid and features.  
4. The game offers high-quality graphics with eerie blue-lit Viking imagery and an immersive, haunting soundtrack.
review: Towering Pays Valhalla: Slot OverviewScrolling through software provider GamesLab's catalogue of releases, it quickly becomes apparent the studio has a soft spot for mythology. They've got Egypt in there naturally, as well as Asian fantasy, Aztec, and now another Norse themed game. This one is titled Towering Pays Valhalla and is a repeat performance of the studio's Towering Pays mechanism. If you haven't come across this before, it's where towers of symbols appear on certain reels, expanding the number of rows and paylines when they hit. Is it all gimmick or ingenious innovation? Let's join several Norse Gods to see.Towering Pays Valhalla starts on a 5-reel, 3-row grid providing 15 fixed paylines to landing winning combinations across. Graphically, the standard is quite high, the background imagery bathed in an eerie blue light, featuring Viking longships, an unusual red leafed tree, and one of those fabulous Norwegian stave churches in the background. Equally eerie is the soundtrack, and when added together, the game does a good job of drawing you in to explore whatever else it might have to offer.Setting bets is the first step, where choices range from 25 p/c to $/€31.25 per spin, available on any device. Math models in all Towering Pays games so far have been pretty similar, here meaning medium volatility and an RTP value of 95.75%, dropping to 95.65% when buying the bonus feature. This one does offer the greatest potential, however, so players who liked past use of the mechanic but were turned off by a low top prize will be happy to see GamesLab loosen the purse strings for Towering Pays Valhalla.Winning combinations are formed when three to five matching symbols line up across one of the bet ways. Horns of Odin wilds help in this task by replacing any of the pay symbols. Wilds are also worth up to 10x the stake for a line of five. In total, 10 symbols make up the regular pay symbols, divided into card suits - clubs, diamonds, spades, and hearts as the low pays worth up to 0.8x for five of a kind. Next are some nicely designed icons such as dragons, two-headed eagles, horses, rams, wolves, and a Viking warrior. Landing a five symbol combination of these is worth a payout of 1 to 6 times the stake. Not a whole lot, considering the number of paylines, but a growing grid and multipliers are used to boost what Towering Pays Valhalla has to offer.Towering Pays Valhalla: Slot FeaturesFeatures in Towering Pays Valhalla include Mega Tower Magic, Stage Play, Prize Multipliers, and a Feature Trail where four rounds of free spins are unlocked – a little like Thunderstruck II.Mega Tower Magic revolves around Towers (stacks) of special golden symbols, grouped on reels 1, 2, and 3 in the base game. When Towers hit, they transform into regular paying symbols and also lead into other features.Whenever a Tower appears on every reel that holds them, play progresses to the next Stage. Each Stage adds 1 extra row of symbols and 10 extra paylines. This continues until reaching 5x8 in size, where 65 paylines are active. At the end of free spins, or if free spins are rejected, the grid resets back to its starting size.At random, a multiplier may be applied to the prize amount on any winning spin. The possible value is dependent on the Stage, so the more rows in play, the higher the multiplier can be from x2 to x10.When at least 1 Tower appears on reels 1-3 on the 5x8 sized grid, a feature is offered. It may be accepted or rejected to play on for a better feature. There are 4 features offered in sequential order – Valkyrie, Loki, Thor, and Odin. Each awards 7 free spins and starts on the regular 5x3 reel size. When at least 1 Tower appears during the feature on all applicable reels, an extra free spin is awarded.Valkyrie and Loki Free Spins are similar to the base game where Towers appear on reels 1-3, except in Loki, the win multipliers are guaranteed. In Thor or Odin rounds, Towers appear on reels 1 to 4. When the grid has fully expanded in the Odin feature, Towers appear on all 5 reels where the game's biggest potential has a chance to be won.Players not in the mood to build rows or wait around for Towers may be able to buy the feature instead. Doing so costs 50 times the stake. Once purchased, players spin a wheel divided into segments: 10 segments award Valkyrie, 3 for Loki, 2  for Thor, and 1 segment awards Odin.Towering Pays Valhalla: Slot VerdictTowering Pays Valhalla has its ups, but it also feels like a game that would have been high tech several years ago. It suffers from the same criticism afflicting Reflex Gaming's game Sea God we reviewed not long before this one. The issue is the relatively restrictive number of paylines that have a knack for confining you to a tiny corner of a fully expanded grid, even when masses of the same symbol type seem to appear. Not always, of course, yet it's just the near misses are more apparent when the screen overflows with eight rows and some pitiful three symbol combo hits in the bottom left corner.On the flip side, occasionally the larger grid does connect larger value combinations, helped by Towers which act like mystery symbols. The four bonus feature trail is kind of interesting, though there's not a lot separating one from the other, except more towers on Thor and Odin, climaxing at all five reels when the grid expands during the later one. It gives players something to shoot for, but you really have to be into the game to stick around for so long. Does Towering Pays Valhalla do enough to hold interest? For some maybe, for others, building rows and pay ways will get stale pretty fast.There are rewards, where up to 6,500x the bet can be won during Odin free spins. Odin's selling point is its Towers on all five reels, yet even if they cover the screen in the top symbol, you're looking at a win of 390x the bet, which seems meagre for an eight-row grid. Win multipliers can drastically improve that amount, but still. Also, there's no mention of what the other bonus games can produce, which could well be a deal-breaker since it's no easy task triggering the Odin bonus, either organically or from the bonus buy.In the end, a clear plan has been laid out for progressing through Towering Pays Valhalla some may enjoy, and it's executed in attractive surroundings. It ends up being a little convoluted, though and might have worked better if GamesLab had condensed everything into one bonus round or updated the pay system to something more contemporary.

title: Floating Dragon Boat Festival

Features include the Hold & Spinner, and free spins.Hold & SpinnerMoney symbols possess random values of 1x to 2,000x the total bet. When at least 3 Money symbols hit, they trigger the Hold & Spinner Bonus. The triggering symbols are held in place while all others fade away. The triggering symbols add their values to a win total. The round starts with 3 respins, and all Money symbols which hit reset the spin count. In addition, when new Money symbols hit, all of the Money symbols in view add their values to the total win amount – including the locked triggering Money symbols. When spins run out, the feature ends and the total win amount accrued is paid.Free SpinsHitting 3, 4 or 5 scatter symbols awards 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. During free spins, when wild symbols hit, they award the values of all Fish Money symbols in view. Wild symbols are also collected when they land. Every 4th collected wild symbol retriggers the feature, awarding 10 free spins each time. A multiplier of x2 is added to the first retrigger, an x3 for the second retrigger, and x10 for the third retrigger. The multiplier applies to Money symbol collections, and retriggered spins begin when the current batch ends. After the third retrigger, no more retriggers are possible. At random, if there is at least 1 wild symbol on the board at the end of a spin, Fish Money symbols may randomly be added to the reels.Floating Dragon Boat Festival slot - hold and spin featureFloating Dragon Boat Festival: Slot VerdictIf the original Floating Dragon slot didn't, err, float your boat for whatever reason, then the sequel is likely to be more of a Bore Festival than anything else. There might have been criticism that Pragmatic Play simply transformed Big Bass Bonanza into an Asian slot and rammed on a hold & win feature, then called it a day. It is hard to argue with such an assessment; however, that didn't stop the game from finding an appreciative audience, eventually going on to encourage a Megaways makeover and now a Dragon Boat version.On the flip side, if Floating Dragon pushed all the right buttons, then there's an excellent chance Floating Dragon Boat Festival will too. The gaming environment is exceedingly pleasant, nothing over the top, no overwhelming masses of cliched iconography. Just a laid-back spot by that water for willing players to enjoy the tunes and try their luck on the reels. Pragmatic Play has laid out buy buttons for both bonus rounds as well as providing the Ante Bet, giving users a lot of control over how they'd like to play the game. A nice touch, matching the nice audio-visuals. Some of the biggest changes are the vastly expanded prize values on the Fish Money symbols as well as the overall winning potential. Where Floating Dragon hit its ceiling at 5,000x the bet, Floating Dragon Boat Festival does so at 10,000x.So no, Floating Dragon Boat Festival doesn't set out to transform the wheel by reinventing itself. Rather, it delivers fans of the first the same thing essentially, just more of it, or at least vastly greater Fish Money symbol values and max win. If you were on board with the last two, then Floating Dragon Boat Festival has got all the necessary bits for some entertaining paddling about.

title: Charlie Chance XreelZ
structured_summary: Charlie Chance XreelZ revisits the 1930s underworld theme with a darker, more serious twist on the original character's misfortune. review:
Charlie Chance XreelZ: Slot OverviewPlayers, let's spare a minute for poor Charlie Chance. Here's a man whose fortune bobs back and forward like a demented see-saw. One minute he's being offered a fortune from strange women; the next, he's in the underworld wondering where it all went wrong. Apparently, in his haste for quick riches, Charlie neglected to read the fine print and now finds himself battling for his very survival. On the plus side, it is still possible for players to collect riches, even more so now in this remake of Play'n GO's original slot Charlie Chance in Hell To Pay.On the visual front, we get the same charming early black and white animated looks carrying the action. However, several major changes have been made to Charlie Chance XreelZ slot, mechanically speaking. This one also has a touch more colour, as the game grid has grown from 3x3 to 5 reels in size, making the leap from fruit slot gaming to something more modern, whilst also expanding win ways to 243 in the process. Complementing the old school looks is a soundtrack from a swinging era, which creates the sort of carefree irreverence found in early Disney/ Betty Boop style cartoon strips.Charlie's main adversary certainly has a Betty Boop vibe, but she is a whole lot more serious this time around. The game engine reflects this shift too, where volatility has increased from 7 to 9 out of 10, and the default RTP has risen a titch to 96.25%. RTP can be found lower, depending on the market, to 94.79% or less, so be on the lookout for that. The biggest shift, numbers-wise, is winning potential, where a significantly larger pile of cash is up for grabs. Descending to the underworld is possible on any device, where bets of 10 p/c to $/€100 are available.Despite the fancy XreelZ name, wins hit in the normal manner - at least three matching pay symbols are needed left to right from reel one to connect for a win. Here, 8 pays make up the table, split between 4 low values, 3 mids and 1 high pay. From the mids on up, where we find things like imps and bells, a winning combination of 5 symbols in length is worth a payout of 20 times your stake. An intricately designed wild symbol has the same value as the top premium, as well as substituting other pay tiles to complete a line. It is also linked to the XreelZ feature; let's take a look.Charlie Chance XreelZ: Slot FeaturesHow the XreelZ mechanic works is that a wild win in the base game creates a highlighted reel. At the same time, there is a multiplier reel located above the game grid, spinning horizontally. The multiplier which lands on the horizontal strip above the highlighted reel is awarded to all wins created from the respective reel.As well as this feature is Second Chance respins and free spins. When 2 or more scatters land, Second Chance Respins are triggered. The scatter's reels are held in place as the rest respin. If another scatter lands, the process is repeated until no more scatters land.As for the free spins, these come in three different versions. The one you get to play corresponds to the number of triggering scatters. The differences between them are covered below, but what they all have in common is that the XreelZ mechanic is active on every spin without needing wild symbols to trigger it;3 scatters in view award Flaming Free Spins with multipliers of x2, x3, and x5.
4 scatters award Inferno Free Spins with multipliers of x5, x6, and x8.5 scatters award Hellfire Free Spins with multipliers of x8, x9, and x25.In all free spin games, any wilds that land remain on the reels for the duration of the feature, moving to a new position on each spin.Charlie Chance XreelZ: Slot VerdictIt might look similar, but this is a very different Charlie Chance than we encountered the last time. Gone is the goofy, slapstick nature, replaced by one much heavier, darker, and more serious. Whatever Charlie did has really ticked the underworld lady off, and she means business, resulting in a less happy-go-lucky experience than the one found previously. The payoff for players from the attitude adjustment is a more volatile game, loaded with vastly greater rewards. Charlie Chance XreelZ has the same 1930s feel as before, though from there, the similarities end, and it's a whole new ball game.The XreelZ mechanic is pretty effective, though essentially it's a random win multiplier, a concept Play'n GO has used in many of their games. It does boost free spins appeal; it has to be said since you know every hit will be exponentially larger than most from the base game. With a x25 multiplier lurking, you might be wondering what Charlie Chance XreelZ is packing in the max win department. The original came with a figure of 6,666x, while the extra reels, ways, and new features push that to 20,000 times the stake. Play'n GO's tendency to produce ever higher-paying games continues.Charlie Chance XreelZ is a relatively simple game that shares little but the aesthetics of the first. Charlie's playful antics might saunter away as ever on the surface, yet beneath the sheen lies a totally new engine, designed to thrill a different gambling clique altogether.

The prize values they displayed weren't exactly eye-popping, in the review at least, but things can apparently add up. title: 1 Million Megaways BC

review: 1 Million Megaways BC: OverviewGet ready for a blast from the past in Iron Dog Studio's slot 1 Million Megaways BC. The title isn't just a nifty eye-catcher. The game also has an ice enclosed wild which appears on reels 2 - 7 to substitute for any regular pay symbol to help make a combo.1 Million Megaways BC: Features1 Million Megaways BC - free spinsAlongside the tumble/win multiplier features, 1 Million Megaways BC comes within an expansive round of free spins. Each successive tumble beyond 4, adds 2 extra free spins up to a maximum of 14.When free spins begin, a new reel is wedged into the middle of the grid. This is the Mammoth reel which can hold up to 9 symbols. With the extra reel added, the maximum number of ways to win increases to 1,058,841 when maxed out.During the feature, whenever a regular reel maxes out at 7 symbols, it locks at that number for the duration of the feature whilst also adding x1 to the multiplier. Moreover, if the Mammoth reel maxes out at 9 symbols, then it also locks whilst awarding 5 more free spins.The Mammoth reel can also land Sticky Wilds which remain in place for the feature. It is technically possible to cover this reel with 9 sticky wilds. The tumble mechanic continues to be used in free spins, increasing the win multiplier on consecutive tumbles. The difference now is that it does not reset on a winless spin.Free spins are where it's at, so Iron Dog Studio provides a feature buy option. Players can buy from 6 to 14 free spins with a price tag of 50x to 270x the stake. Unlike their other slots, it is not possible to pre-buy locked reels.1 Million Megaways BC: VerdictIron Dog Studio continues their unique method of dealing with Megaways that began in the high seas success of Pirate Kingdom. That one introduced their reel lock concept which continues in 1 Million Megaways BC. Here they have taken it to another level though, introducing the Mammoth Reel and sending the number of potential Megaways right off the Richter.Does it work? In many ways, yes. Pirate Kingdom's locking reels meant there could be a ton of symbols on screen, so you can imagine what an extra seventh reel with nine locked symbols is like. The number of symbols on screen can be surreal at times during free spins, and when married to a decent multiplier, even the most humble royal can be worth a fat stack.Free spins are by far the main draw because up until they triggered, the base game wasn't lighting too many fires. The x2-x8 base game multiplier sounds better on paper than it usually turns out to be, and the jerky, fragile nature of the reels might make your eyes water.Once free spins were allowed to breathe then the game's potential finally had a chance to shine. Speaking of potential, Iron Dog's official figure states possible wins of up to 45,000 times the stake, so there is plenty to play for. The bonus buy option is achingly tempting after you've seen what 1 Million Megaways BC is capable of, though it does get a little pricey at the upper tier.Okay, it's not perfect, there are a few areas of concern, a few wrinkles for Iron Dog Studio to iron out. But along with clones such as Branded Megaways, the studio is clearly also aiming high. Not content to just crank out generic Megaways driven slots, which is probably tempting to do, Iron Dog has pushed what the famed engine is capable of in 1 Million Megaways BC.

title: Bookie of Odds

Before the bonus is played, one of the standard symbols is randomly chosen as the special expanding symbol. When it lands on the reels (3 required for low-value symbols and 2 for premiums), the symbol expands to become fully stacked.Bookie of Odds (Triple Edge Studios): VerdictBook of Oz is undoubtedly a great slot and naturally, being a clone, so is Bookie of Odds. The lack of originality, however, makes it a rather pointless release, unless you're a great horse racing enthusiast that also happens to be into online slots.For players who were around when Book of Oz came out, there's really nothing new to explore or discover here. Bookie of Odds only really feels like a hasty re-skin, released with the sole purpose of cashing in on the horse racing hype NetEnt promoted over the past few weeks. How do you rate a clone? Not A for effort, that's for sure.

title: Big Top Bonanza Megaways

Then, it collects the values of all relic symbols that are adjacent to it, horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. title: Elemental Gems Megaways
structured_summary: Elemental Gems Megaways features an Asian-inspired theme with traditional symbols and purple dragons framing the reels.
