The game offers muted EDM audio and simple visuals consistent with classic slot symbols and a subdued backdrop.
review: Mystery Drop: Slot OverviewLiving up to the 'If you can't be bothered to beat 'em, copy 'em' attitude prevalent in the industry is Mystery Drop from developer Stakelogic. Mystery Drop is a game that replaces winning symbols with two new ones, thereby increasing reels and ways, climaxing in free spins where a growing win multiplier is used. It sounds very much like a new Avatar UX game, yet Stakelogic has added a couple of unique flourishes, so Mystery Drop isn't completely the same. However, most of the time, it's hard to tell the difference.Any fan of the PopWins series will soon realise that there is a strong resemblance here to CherryPop, arguably the most successful in Avatar UX's range to date. Both games are covered in classic slot symbols, use a blurred nondescript background, and treat your ears to low key EDM. Even the layout is uncannily similar where a ways-to-win counter sits to the right of a 5x3 game grid, with a starting value of 486, reaching as high as 15,552 when maxed out during the base game. Mystery Drop is such an obvious knock off you kind of just go with it, such as the state of disbelief it induces.Not everything is the same, Stakelogic has added a few of their own touches, and one of them is the Super Stake feature. This is an optional bet enhancer that doubles the stake to randomly trigger the bonus game on non-winning base game spins. It may also award extra free spins during the bonus game. To minimise exposure from such a high potential game, base stakes max out at $/€5 per spin, dropping to 20 p/c at the lower end of the spectrum. Matching the big win figure is a highly volatile math model, generating a default theoretical return value of 95.59%.Thirteen pay symbols appear on the table, divided into 9-A card ranks, then superseded by cherries, lemons, plums, grapes, bells, stars, and sevens as the premiums. Values for the higher value symbols are 2.5 to 8 times the stake when a five of a kind combination lands. Wilds are not used in the game, but it's possible mystery symbols appear in free spins. When they do, they all reveal the same pay symbol type.Mystery Drop: Slot FeaturesMystery Drop - free spins gamble featureMystery Drop comes equipped with several features, such as a PopWins style win mechanism, a Gamble Drop, free spins + growing multiplier, and a standard gamble feature.Winning combinations in Mystery Drop form when at least three matching symbols land on adjacent reels from the leftmost or rightmost side. When wins hit, the symbols pop from the board and are replaced by two new ones, increasing the reel height and ways to win. Like cascading features, this can lead to repeat wins from single spins. In the base game, the reels max out at 6 positions high, providing 15,552 ways. When no new wins appear in the base game, the grid resets to its normal 3-row height.When all reels reach 6 rows high in the base game, 5 free spins are awarded. Before the bonus game starts, players can gamble their free spins to win more. The gamble takes place on a Pachinko style board where a ball drops from top to bottom. If it lands on a number, that amount of free spins is added to the total. If it lands on an 'X', you lose the free spins and go back to the base game.In free spins, the grid doubles to a starting height of 6 rows, which can expand up to 9 via the win mechanism. At full capacity, 118,098 ways to win are active. As well as the grid change and mystery symbols mentioned earlier, free spins also use a win multiplier. It starts on x2, increases by +1 for every win and +4 if all reels reach a size of 9. From then on, it increments by +3. If the Super Stake is switched on, then scatters can appear in free spins too - landing 3 scatters in view during the feature awards +5 free spins.Following each win, a gamble feature triggers. Players can collect or gamble their winnings by picking the correct colour or suit of a face-down card. Getting it right doubles or quads the win; getting it wrong loses it all. The gamble feature can be disabled completely if unneeded.Last on the feature list is the Buy Bonus button. If available, players can click this and shell out 150x the base bet to enter the bonus game with 5 free spins. From here, you can take advantage of the Gamble Drop first if you so choose.Mystery Drop: Slot VerdictStakelogic's has popped off all manner of innovations as they've grown over the years, but they've also had no problem copying other studios' work either. We got a taste of the shamelessness in Mayan Rush – a Valley of the Gods doppelganger, now we've got Mystery Drop, which is the spitting image of CherryPop. It almost seems as if some dev jumped ship from Avatar UX and brought their technical knowledge to Stakelogic. It's weird how close the two games are.Yet, there are a few differences lurking in the wings. One is the Super Stake which did trigger bonus games occasionally from dead base game spins. Free spins triggered this way did tend to produce minimal results for some reason, though no doubt an unfortunate coincidence. The Gamble Drop is a new feature to approach with a dose of caution. It essentially functions the same as a prize wheel in that you either win or you lose. However, there is something about the way the ball teeters on an edge before falling onto an 'X' which can be extra infuriating. On the other hand, winning additional spins can significantly change the outcome of a bonus round, so it's a tough call.Interestingly, Mystery Drop's stake range is more limited than CherryPop's, and the bonus buy costs twice as much, but the max win is similar in both cases – at 50,000x the bet. Does this mean Mystery Drop is more likely to produce epic wins, or it's just pricier? Impossible to say since the applicable frequency stats aren't provided. RTP is, however, and Mystery Drop's figure is lower than CherryPop's, so something to keep in mind when trying to choose either game.Despite the nuances, it remains a mystery why someone would pick Mystery Drop over CherryPop, or any number of PopWins powered games. Avatar UX' game has the higher RTP, slightly larger max win, its bonus buy costs 50% less, and there's the fact they came up with the idea first. That leaves Super Stake, which provides extra options, and players can always test their nerve on the Pachinko style Gamble Drop. Still, a few peripheral changes don't stop Mystery Drop coming across as a piece of PopWins flattery.

In all four Shining Hots, landing 3, 4, or 5 scatters anywhere in view triggers a payout worth 5, 15, or 500 times the stake, respectively.Shining Hot: Slot VerdictClearly, players who like some innovation, a bit of something new, or just a bit of anything really, would do well to pass on the Shining Hot range. While humanity teeters on the cusp of migrating to the metaverse, Shining Hot feels like a real anachronism. Maybe that's the point. A rejection of modernity because the old ways were seen as better? Nostalgia is popular in slots, after all, but Shining Hot doesn't offer the uber-cool form of it you can find in games like Hellcatraz or Banana Town. This is more of an option for those who may be into retro-style, land-based gaming.As a middle ground, players who like the old ways with a modern streak might do well to check out a game like Pragmatic Play's own Fire Strike 2. A fruity slot with a stack of features and massive potential. Shining Hot, by comparison, musters up wins as high as 2,500x the bet. Not a massive total, yet an amount that fits quite well with everything else the range has to offer, which isn't a whole lot. title: Wildest Gambit

review: Wildest Gambit: Slot OverviewOne of the most adventurous families you're ever likely to come across while utilising the services of an online slot are those intrepid Wildes. Depending on which destination the feature is triggered from, the relevant lead and support wild features are always active.Wildest Gambit slot - free spinsWildest Gambit: Slot VerdictFamily reunions have the potential to trigger all sorts of emotions and reactions. Buried grievances come to the fore, friendships are reignited, bonds strengthened. Gerard's Gambit, like Wildest Gambit, was a travel slot boasting a ton of different levels to visit. Ten, to be precise, though levels did crossover, using the same locations at times. While the travel list was large, the modest winning potential took some of the wind out of the game, which by the end had started to fizzle.No such case with Wildest Gambit's 20,000x the bet winning potential, though, providing a sizable pot of gold at the end of the journey for the luckiest of participants. Not bad features to sample along the way, though nothing amazing either when viewed individually. Wilds, wild multipliers, expanding wilds, 'book of' chosen symbols, that sort of thing. Basically, random wilds hit, and wild upgrades may or may not trigger, that's it. Takes some of the magic out, perhaps, but this system can work pretty dramatically.So, those Wildes ay, they end up in all sorts of planetary places. A cash symbol can become a Grabber or Booster. A Booster, Zapper, or Booster are upgraded to the Brutal version.Expander - unlocks 3 random positions from the locked area.Feature BuyBuying the bonus game triggered by at least 3 scatters costs 40x the bet, or buying the bonus game triggered by at least 5 scatters costs 185x the bet.Cash Truck Begins slot - free spinsCash Truck Begins: Slot VerdictSince the Money Train juggernaut came to a grinding halt with the release of Money Train 4 in 2023, few studios have chosen to release their own contenders in an attempt to dethrone the king. If there were hopes Cash Truck Begins could be one, it might be good to temper those expectations. Probably the biggest caveat is that the game is basically a remake of Cash Truck 3 Turbo, returning virtually the same set of features.Don't want to be negative, and this might sound horrendously materialistic, but Cash Truck Begins also loses a few cool points on account of its winning potential. For sure, few gamblers would be shedding tears over a 20,000x the bet hit, but weirdly, it is the smallest figure in the series and looks more than a little sad compared to Money Train 4's 150,000x. As already stated, few would rue pocketing a 20,000x hit, but the diminished win cap makes Cash Truck Begins a lighter-weight slot and lessens its impact.The lessening continues when considering how close Cash Truck Begins is to Cash Track 3 Turbo mechanically. While the fantasy-esque theme change is interesting, taking CT3, halving the potential and axing the gamble for more Expanders features doesn't feel like a boss move. On the flip side, bargain-hunting gamblers may appreciate cheaper price tags for triggering the bonus games, and there is about double the probability of hitting the win cap. Ah well, consumer choice is an important component of economics, and in Cash Truck Begins, gamblers get a freshly presented Cash Truck slot with alterations around winning potential, though very little to nothing new mechanically beneath the facelift.

review: Sweet PowerNudge: Slot OverviewCasino game maker Pragmatic Play adds to its PowerNudge range of slots with a third release bearing the title Sweet PowerNudge. Whilst there is likely well thought-through strategy behind it, going for the uncomplicated feelgood Candy Crush style presentation and all, Sweet Powernudge displays little on the screen that players with candy slot experience won't be familiar with.Sweet PowerNudge slot - base gameBacktracking a bit now, the first two PowerNudge games, Goblin Heist PowerNudge and Rise of Giza PowerNudge, had similar grid setups which Sweet PowerNudge deviates from. When a win appears on the board, the reels holding the winning symbols nudge down one position, and new symbols appear at the top. Non-winning reels remain stationary. The game pays again for any winning symbols in view after the nudge down. New wins can appear after a nudge, and the nudge feature ends when no more winning combinations are present. Then, the next paid spin or free spin can begin.Multiplier ReelThis reel has multiplier values of x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, or x10. By default, it's disabled in the base game but can randomly activate. When it does, it also nudges on that spin for any winning reel nudges. After each nudge, the multiplier value in the middle position is added to a total multiplier which is applied to the win of the current nudge. At the end of the spin, the multiplier resets to x1, and the reel is disabled.Free SpinsScatter symbols are collected when they land, and in the base game, collecting 4 or more of them triggers the free spins round. If more than 4 scatters trigger the feature, the extra scatters carry over to free spins, possibly contributing to retriggers. Now, the bonus round begins with 7 free spins and each time 4 scatters are collected, +3 additional free spins are awarded. One of the benefits of free spins is the multiplier reel is switched on for the full duration. The last thing to mention is the feature buy option which players can use to buy free spins for the cost of 100 times the stake.Sweet PowerNudge slot - free spinsSweet PowerNudge: Slot VerdictIt's hard to know what to say about Sweet PowerNudge. It's not a game that commanded attention from the outset with its low-key title, and where the low-keyness was followed through when the game's regular batch of candy graphics filled the screen. Guess we were expecting something more after the devious-looking goblins of Goblin Heist PowerNudge and the cyborg pharaohs in Rise of Giza PowerNudge. This one's a lot more conventional, presenting mainly, well, sweets, which has been done enough times in the past to make Sweet PowerNudge feel a little passe.Still, looks and sounds are only one part of the equation; how about the gameplay? Again, it's alright, but nothing hugely exciting. Pragmatic Play is no stranger to the multiplier reel idea, having popped up before in games like Hot Safari and Aztec Gems. It has the ability to work quite well when it's firing off multiplier values, ramping up the collective multiplier during a nudge sequence, which it has the ability to randomly do in the base game or on each free spin. It might take patience to sit through batches of dead spins, yet Sweet PowerNudge has the type of features and pay mechanic that are capable of snowballing off of each other. With a max win of 5,000 times the bet, there are no doubt opportunities here for some pretty exciting snowballing, too.After the two previous PowerNudge games' bursts of creativity, it was a tad disappointing to see Pragmatic Play fall back on such a generic theme presentation. Then again, candy slots are immensely popular, in particular those coming from the Pragmatic Play production line, so perhaps picking such a cosy game world will wind up making this a PowerNudge break-out slot, or perhaps it'll end up being one of those games that's okay for a spin or two but hard to justify returning back to. title: Deal or No Deal Megaways
structured_summary: Deal or No Deal Megaways brings the popular TV show theme to life, letting players relive the suspense of beating the banker. It features the Megaways engine with cascading reels, mystery symbols, multiple Deal or No Deal bonus tiers, free spins with increasing multipliers, and a Jackpot King Deluxe progressive jackpot. review: Deal or No Deal Megaways (Blueprint Gaming): OverviewHow many people sitting at home watching Deal or No Deal think they can beat the banker? Well, here's your chance. Thanks to Blueprint Gaming, we now have yet another version to play out of the countless others available on the digital slot shelves. The Deal or No Deal television show is quite big in several countries, including the UK, and fans of the show will feel right at home here. Blueprint Gaming has managed to pack in most of the show’s best bits such as selecting boxes, phone calls from the banker, and the tough take it or leave it choice. The only thing missing is Noel Edmonds, which could be a good thing for a lot of people.Noel might be gone, but in his place, we get the ever-popular Megaways game engine from Big Time Gaming. This provides 6 reels that spin vertically with up to 7 symbols on each, and one more along the top with 4 more symbols. There are no paylines as such, but win ways up to 117,649 when the reels are maxed out. It matches the theme nicely, fitting in with the box selection part of the game. Moreover, with the cascading reels mechanic in play, winning combinations disappear from the grid letting other symbols fall into place, which can create cascading winners.Medium to high variance, stakes start at 20 c/p and go up to $/€10 per spin. That might not sound too tempting for high rollers, but bear with us, the high winning potential might just be worth it. Hold any reservations while we deal with the symbol values too. Due to Megaways cascading wins and multiple win ways on one spin, individual winning combos seem a little low. First up are the card royals 9 to A which are then followed by symbols of the show – a question mug, ‘B’ seal, sealed envelope, and game logo for 0.3x – 50x the stake for a 6 of a kind combination. The Wild appears above the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th reel and substitutes for any symbol except the scatter.Deal or No Deal Megaways (Blueprint Gaming): FeaturesDeal or No Deal Mega BonusDeal or No Deal has quite a selection of extras so it’s best if we break them down one by one. First up is the question mark icon which is the Mystery Symbol. Appearing on all reels, more than one can land at once. When they do, they all flip to reveal the same matching symbols, which could be anything except the scatter.When you land more than 3 consecutive win cascades, the Deal or No Deal Bonus Game is activated. There are three offer increasing rewards:4 consecutive cascades – Standard Deal or No Deal.5 consecutive cascades – Super Deal or No Deal.6 consecutive cascades – Mega Deal or No Deal.The action shifts to an arena with 22 boxes in the middle, and prizes of cash and free spins flanking the screen. Players take turns choosing boxes which remove prizes from the two columns while the banker calls on the phone with offers to buy your allocated box. Players can either take the offer and leave the game or hold out until the end and open their box – just like on the show.Free Spins come with a number of mystery symbols and an unlimited multiplier which increases by 1 with each cascade. Free spins can also be re-triggered by +5 if 3 free spin scatters land, or +10 if 4 scatters land.Finally, why not throw one more extra feature in for good measure? The Jackpot King Deluxe pot system feature can launch randomly on any spin. When triggered, players spin the reels to collect crowns – the more they get the further up the win ladder they move. Get 15 or more crowns to unlock the Wheel King Bonus to win either big bet multipliers or a progressive jackpot. After any spin, players choose a regal looking icon which lets them either spin again, collect the prize they are on, or spin the Wheel King.Deal or No Deal Megaways (Blueprint Gaming): VerdictDeal or No Deal is no stranger to the slot world. There are several options out there both physical and online. Blueprint Gaming’s latest addition, with the inclusion of the Megaways system, puts it firmly in the top spot. How it gets there is due to several factors, one of them being emotional. If you have seen the show, you know how tough it can be for contestants to risk the bankers offer for the chance to win even more, or less. You know you are going to win something in that situation which makes it a nice spot to be in, but still, it can be intense all the same.During the audition process, the show’s producers would conduct psychological tests to assess the character of each contestant. Those that showed a natural propensity for gambling were often the ones that had the nerve to hold out under the toughest choices. Hopefully, that is good news for the hardcore players out there because a lot is at stake. Deal or No Deal Megaways delivers the goods in the rewards department with 10,000 times your stake up for grabs, (capped at $250,000) which is plenty to play for. More than enough to overcome anyone’s aversion to Noel Edmond if he had fronted the game.If you are looking for a hard-hitting, fast-paced, shot of adrenaline then it might be best to look elsewhere. The way the bonus rounds shift away from the base game might break up the flow too much. But followers of the TV show might very well enjoy this Megaways slot version, as will those looking for real bang for their buck, and a slot full of extras.

title: The Expendables New Mission Megaways
structured_summary:
The Expendables New Mission Megaways slots into the action movie theme with a gritty mercenary vibe inspired by the third film and Grand Theft Auto V.

review: The Expendables New Mission Megaways: OverviewDeveloper Stakelogic revives everyone’s favourite mercenaries in their mouthful of a slot, The Expendables New Mission Megaways. Most of the team are back, in a game that takes cues from the third instalment in the popular action movie series, and which takes heavy visual inspiration from Grand Theft Auto V.The first Expendables slot was well received by the gaming public, but it felt a little starchy, as though it was capable of more. Expendables New Mission isn’t a complete break from the first, but it does feel looser, less restrained, and kitted out with more features than a merc has safe houses.One sign the game has loosened up is that the gang has swapped their all-black uniforms for civvies. What’s not low is the high volatility, working hand in hand with equally high potential.Winning symbols are made up of 3 or more matching symbols left to right from the first reel. The exception to the rule is Sly, who only needs 2 of a kind. When wins hit, a cascade feature kicks in, removing winning symbols to let new ones drop into place. In this way, consecutive runs of wins are possible on single spins, and continue to cascade until no new combinations appear.When it comes to the symbol department, we get Terry Crews in a Panama hat, alongside Dolph Lundgren, Jason Statham, and Sylvester Stallone starring as the four premiums. Sly is worth by far the most at 62.5x for six of a kind - compare that to the next premium down, Jason Statham, at 12.5x for a line of six.The remaining regular symbols are a bunch of metallic-looking, bullet-ridden low paying 9-A royals. Helping score wins are two wild symbols. The dynamite one conducts standard substitute for pay symbol duties; while the second has a multiplier we’ll at look shortly.The Expendables New Mission Megaways: FeaturesFree spins feature with Stallone modifier in actionThere are a few similarities to the original, but on the whole, features are another area of Expendables New Mission that has been revamped. Players can look forward to Free Spins, Super Stakes, Golden Skulls, Mystery Symbols and Multiplier Wilds.These last three are easy, when Golden Skulls appear on the reels they transform into the same matching symbol. Multiplier Wilds perform the same task as the regular wild while also adding a multiplier of x2, x3, x5, or x10 on for good measure. Combinations of Multiplier Wilds are multiplied together. Last in this set are Mystery Symbols which can transform into scatter symbols, extra wilds, matching regular symbols, or multiplier wilds.Fans will be stoked so know their man Sly Stallone makes more of an appearance in Expendables New Mission Megaways. Every so often he randomly pops on screen to toss grenades onto the reels. Grenades function like mystery symbols, modifying a spin as described above.From skulls to dog tags as the games scatters this time around. Having 4 dog tags in view at the end of a cascade sequence awards 12 free spins, while any extra scatters in view awards an additional 5 free spins each. Free spins begin with a win multiplier starting at x1 which may increase at random on any spin by x1 to x5 - without a set limit. You'll also benefit from an increase in rate of which Stallone appears to reward modifiers. Moreover, landing 3 or 4 scatters during the feature wins an extra 5 or 10 free spins respectively.Stakelogic’s trademarked Super Stake feature also makes a return. The first time we ran into it was via the Ancient Egyptian slot Gods of Death. There it had two benefits, one of which was helping trigger the bonus game. In The Expendables New Mission Megaways, it’s not quite so useful, though the cost is the same – double the bet.The benefit is randomly adding extra Golden Skulls to the reels while they spin, providing higher chances of bigger wins. Up to 222 Golden Skulls may be added, which has an average hit frequency of one in every 38 spins.Lastly, the Stakelogic special - a gamble feature. Real simple, this can be activated after a win, provided auto-spins are disengaged, for an extra chance at winning (or losing). Players guess the correct colour or suit of a blind card for double/quadruple or nothing.The Expendables New Mission Megaways: VerdictExpendables fans will be happy to know the lads are back, and bigger than ever. Like most branded slots, Expendable New Mission Megaways will appeal more to enthusiasts, but the new features and better graphics will help broaden its appeal. The changes aren’t revolutionary, but there is a lot more action going on this time around making New Mission a better use of the brand.For one it just looks nicer, for another, Sly makes more of an appearance in the game, adding more personality. The first time he popped up, we hadn’t fully absorbed the paytable, and he lobbed a grenade onto the reels which turned into what looked like a handbag. There were chuckles all round before the bag became an x5 multiplier ending up in a tidy return. From there it was kind of game on, racking up more entertainment miles than the first Expendables slot.What hopefully hasn’t changed is the impressive potential of over 20,000x which the first one was capable of. No doubt New Mission packs a solid potential, though there is no official word at the time of writing. Alongside big potential, the math model feels like it’s had an overhaul too. Trying to trigger free spins when playing The Expendables part one could be quite a painful experience. While it’s not a walk in the park, features were more frequent here, better pace, more fun, and the result felt more like how a branded slot should.Stakelogic’s first Expendables slot proved to be somewhat popular with punters, and with the new enhancements, there is no reason to suspect New Mission won’t be even bigger. Stakelogic has stepped up the explosions; it’s livelier, there’s more character involvement, so an overall enjoyable game.

title: Path of Destiny
structured_summary: Path of Destiny explores a Hindu culture theme set in a Maharaja's palace with restrained but authentic Indian influences. The game features 5 reels, 20 paylines, free spins, Ganesha Coins, and Mega Ganesha Coins for bonus wins. The reviewer praises its originality and soundtrack but notes modest max winnings and medium+ volatility. review: Path of Destiny: Slot OverviewConsidering the size of the country, not to mention its long and varied history, it's surprising there aren't more slots to use Indian themes. Asian, that is to say, Chinese imagery abounds, but its cross Himalayan neighbours aren't quite so populous. Red Tiger and partner studio R7 take on the challenge of doing Hindu culture some justice in their slot Path of Destiny. To quicken the process, they appear to have taken the bare bones of an older, ahem, Chinese themed slot, Dragon's Luck and played around with a few things. One main change is the inclusion of free spins which adds a new dimension, as well as increasing the potential.The game is set in some sort of Maharaja's palace, or Indian themed casino, it's a little hard to tell. It's not super gaudy, so respect goes to the team for showing restraint with a theme that could have seen them go nuts. Then again, if you've watched a full-blown Bollywood operatic, an explosion of life and colour might have been more appropriate. As it is, we get a 5-reel, 20-payline slot, with a lot of gold and burgundy trim. The music is nicely in theme too, adding to the overall atmosphere.Path of Destiny can be played on any device, offering bets from 10 p/c to $/€40 per spin. Fans of high rolling Dragon's Luck will notice the max bet has dropped by twenty quid, and that's not the only thing to have taken a hit. RTP is down from its Dragony cousin, from 96.24% to a default setting of 95.71%. Volatility tends to the medium+ side, so it's not exactly a fight through New Delhi traffic on your device.Getting a win requires landing three or more matching symbols anywhere on a payline. As long as they are adjacent, they can land in the middle, or from either side of the reels, it doesn't matter. As for the paytable, we find nine regular pays split into five low 10-A royals and four high pays. These are lotus flowers, pots, some kind of ornament, plus an elaborate looking mask worth from 9.4 to 69 times the stake. Symbol values are denoted in coins where a lot of '8s' appear. A hangover from their use in the Asian game, though the number doesn't have the same auspiciousness in Indian culture. Quite the opposite actually, with many considering it an unlucky number, particularly in the south.There is one minor matter to clear up. The hooked digit which looks like a '7' is actually a '1'. At first, the stated potential on the home screen looks pretty impressive, until the 10 symbol clears away the initial thrill by several orders of magnitude. Finally, there are no wild symbols to be found in Path of Destiny.Path of Destiny: Slot FeaturesDistancing itself from its predecessor, Path of Destiny has dropped the Dragon's Help feature, replacing it with a batch of free spins. The bonus game is joined by Ganesha Coins, and Ganesha Mega Coins.The elephant-headed Ganesha Coins may land on any reel in random numbers at any time. They then spin to reveal a matching symbol. Ganesha may randomly trigger one more coin spin, guaranteeing a win when he does so.The Free spins round, or Lucky Spins as they are called, are triggered when 3 Lucky Spin symbols land on reels 1, 3, and 5. This awards 10 free spins, which is extended by 5 if two Lucky Spin symbols land on the first and last reel. Here you'll benefit from Mega Ganesha Coins, a 3x3 sized Super Symbol which divides into multiple Ganesha Coins for a guaranteed win.Path of Destiny: Slot VerdictIt might be similar to older Red Tiger creations, but the choice of theme is more original. Asian slots primarily mean China, or Japan at a stretch, while the vast Indian land is less well frequented. It feels like a missed opportunity when you consider the size of the population and the popularity of gambling in India. With a population of over one billion, you'd expect developers to target them more than they do. Maybe Red Tiger/R7 has formed the vanguard, the first pioneering incursion into the sub-continent. As well as the sheer size of the market, the culture is an ancient one, full of legends, gods, heroes, and imagery, just ripe to be used by studios for slot development.Red Tiger/R7 has done a pretty good job too, bringing some of it into Path of Destiny, and overall, the theme is quite well handled. The stand out is the banging soundtrack that works itself into a right frenzy during the larger count ups. You can see why the Beatles wanted to jam with these guys back in their experimental phase.Except don't expect too big a count up. Swapping the Dragon's Help feature for free spins seems like a decent trade, as it has led to higher potential, though not a heck of a lot more. The most you can possibly win here is a modest 2,253.7 times your stake. Symbols land stacked, so full screens of the mask symbol are worth 1,380x which isn't bad - helped in free spins by the Mega Ganesha Coins symbol, or the base game by standard Ganesha Coin. Still, it's not exactly a max wins, max thrills type of game.If you played Dragon's Luck, then whatever your judgements of it are likely to cross over to Path of Destiny. In some ways, this is a superior slot. For one, the theme offers a greater level of originality, the potential is up, and there are free spins. If Path of Destiny blows up in any way, should we expect to see a Megaways version like its Dragon’s Luck cousin?

title: Club Tropicana

review: Club Tropicana: Slot OverviewIf there's a two-word combo that evokes images of somewhere the party never stops, where every partygoer is happy, carefree, and up for whatever, 'Club Tropicana' has got to be a strong contender. As well as being used to name things like at least one hotel, clubs, and of course the 1983 Wham! hit song, it's now been used as an online slot from Pragmatic Play and partner Reel Kingdom. Club Tropicana might be an upbeat title, but it's not the most original, and neither is its gameplay. The reason is Club Tropicana is a straight clone of Bigger Bass Blizzard, which means Money symbol collects, and free spins where collected wilds lead to money multipliers.First up, a question. That bearded sunglasses chap who has started in numerous Bass-related slots, has he got a name? If not, then he has surely earned one by now. The guy has cropped up reeling in fish all over the place, and here he appears to be this Club Tropicana's bartender. He bobs about on the side of the screen, occasionally shaking cocktails, as foliage waves on the other side of the grid, while the top portion displays a line of black silhouetted palm trees. Factor in a swinging soundtrack and this Club Tropicana is a pretty sweet place to kick back for a bit - cheesy perhaps, but in a good way, and despite the flipped theme, it does feel like a Big Bass relative. Though the connection could've been psychological.Club Tropicana slot - base gameWe mentioned straight clone in the intro, and that was no exaggeration. Whereas Bigger Bass Blizzard differed slightly from its predecessor Bigger Bass Bonanza, this one shares all of the same stats as before. For one, the math model is equally volatile (rated 5 out of 5), and the maximum RTP when playing the game normally or when using the Ante Bet is 96.08%, dropping a titch to 96.07% when buying free spins. Bet levels are a little unusual, starting at 12 p/c per spin, rising to $/€240, though activating the Ante Bet, which adds more scatter, increases the cost by 50%.Club Tropicana is available on any device and is played on a 5x4 game grid with 12 fixed paylines. Regular symbols pay from left to right, starting on the first reel along a payline. The game's lows are cherries, lemons, oranges, plums, and watermelons, while highs are a pool ring, a cocktail, cocktail umbrellas, and a pouring drink. Hit a five-of-a-kind low pay combo awards 10x the bet, or 50 to 200 for the high pays. Money symbols land with random values of 2x to 4,000x the bet. They pay the total of their values if a five-of-a-kind line of Money symbols hits.Club Tropicana: Slot FeaturesClub Tropicana slot - free spins splash screenThe trio of drinks symbol is the scatter, which is present on all five reels. Hitting 3, 4, or 5 scatters anywhere on the board awards 10, 15, or 20 free spins, respectively. In the base game, if 2 scatters land, there's a chance a hook randomly appears to pull the third scatter into view.In free spins, wild symbols are added to the reels. Wilds can substitute for any pay symbol to complete winning lines. In addition, when Money symbols land, their values are collected by each wild symbol also in view at the same time. Wild symbols are collected when they land as well. Every fourth wild collected awards +10 extra free spins with a multiplier for any Money symbol collections. The multiplier is x2, x3 or x10 for the first, second, and third retrigger, respectively. Retriggered free spins are played when the current batch ends with the applicable multiplier activated. After the third retrigger, no more retriggers are possible. Moreover, at random, when 1 or 2 wild symbols are on the board, at the end of a free spin, Money symbols can be placed in random cells. Alternately, reels can be randomly pushed up at the end of a spin to reveal wild and Money symbols.Lastly, free spins can be bought for 100x the bet, where applicable. On a bought triggering spin, 3, 4, or 5 scatters may land.Club Tropicana slot - free spinsClub Tropicana: Slot VerdictTalk about making hay while the sun shines. With Club Tropicana, Reel Kingdom, and Pragmatic Play, squeeze a bit of extra milk from the cash cow. Needless to say, players who can't get enough of the Big/Bigger Bass franchise should get a kick or two out of Club Tropicana as well. Kind of hard not to since it's a direct port-over of Bigger Bass Blizzard, so catching fish, or in this case, literal money-adorned Money symbols, is back on the menu. The opposite is true too. If you are fed up to the gills with the whole Bass phenomenon, run for the hills now because Club Tropicana plays out in exactly the same way.The Big/Bigger Bass shtick is massively popular and has been enjoyed by a huge number of online slot enthusiasts since Big Bass Bonanza exploded on the scene back in the latter part of 2020. In some ways a surprise hit since it felt like a basic Fishin' Frenzy wannabe, which in some ways, it was. However, it struck the right chord, and after several follow-ups, here we are in Club Tropicana, getting a repeat performance. Nothing has been updated mechanically or numerically, including the 4,000x win cap, so Bass zealots will have an excellent idea of what to expect should they choose to load up Club Tropicana.Due to the ubiquity of the Big/Bigger Bass selection of slots, there probably isn't much need for delving deeply into the gameplay. For those who are new, though, rest assured that as far as Fishin' Frenzy type slots go, Pragmatic Play/Reel Kingdom's many contributions are about as good as Money symbol collection gaming gets. Since Club Tropicana has no surprises lying in wait, keen Money symbol collectors have the opportunity to gear up for another Bass-style party, while those fed up can call it a night and get the heck out of there.

title: Vampy Party
structured_summary: Vampy Party is a vampire-themed slot set in a gothic castle hosting a seemingly quiet party. The reviewer finds it entertaining but somewhat limited compared to similar high-multiplier slots. The game boasts a moody atmosphere with flashing lights and a sexy saxophone funk soundtrack.
review: Vampy Party: Slot OverviewIf you were an immortal, as in you couldn't get sick or die, surely, eventually, you'd slide into complete boredom after having done and seen absolutely everything there is to offer? Presumably, this is one of the downsides to being a vampire, well, that and the need to murder the living in order to drink their lifeblood. One way a vampire might be able to stave off boredom is to throw a big party for all their friends. Even if the vampire in question doesn't end up having a good time, they can at least drag others down to their level of catatonic despair. Oh, the joy.To be honest, Pragmatic Play's nosferatu slot Vampy Party looks like it might be a bit of fun. Vampy and his bat pal are having a party in a castle, decked out in flashing lights and bopping tunes. The game world timing appears to be either before the celebrations kick off or afterwards because the gothic stone room hosting the action is completely devoid of people, bats, and whoever else Vampy has invited. This hasn't completely obliterated the party atmosphere, though, in large part because of the sexy saxophone funk track, and the foam.Vampy Party slot - base gameGetting jiggy in the middle of the room is a 3-4-5-5-4-3 game grid in possession of 3,600 ways to win. Above it is a multiplier trail, displaying its minimum and maximum values from the outset. A wide range of stakes are on offer, starting from 20 c and going up to a maximum of $/€240. Activating the ante bet increases the stake by a further 40% in order to have double the chance of triggering free spins. Maxing the RTP out at 96%, Vampy Party is a highly volatile slot.Eight pay symbols, divided into 4 J-A card royals and premiums, appear on the reels. Combinations of 6 matching royals are worth 0.25 to 0.6 times the bet, while a combination of 6 glasses of suspicious red liquid, records, bats, or vampires pay 1 to 2.5 times the bet. Wilds replace any pay symbol. The tumble feature is responsible for removing winning symbols from the screen and dropping others down to plug the gaps. Tumbling continues in this vein until no new win appears.Vampy Party: Slot FeaturesVampy Party slot - free spins gambleThe lineup at Vampy Party includes a tumble feature, marked symbols, tumble multipliers, free spins, and feature buys.Highlighted SymbolsAt random on any spin, regular highlighted paying symbols may appear on random positions on reels 3 and 4. When winning combinations include highlighted symbols, they turn into wilds for the next tumble.Tumble MultipliersIn the main game, a win multiplier starting at x1 is used. After each winning tumble, the win multiplier doubles up to a maxim of x1,024. The multiplier resets at the end of tumbles.Free SpinsHitting 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatters triggers 12 free spins with a starting multiplier of x8, x16, x32, or x64, respectively. Before the feature starts, it is possible to gamble to double the starting multiplier or collect the value. Gambles occur on a segmented wheel. If the gamble is successful, the multiplier can be doubled up to x256. Losing gambles ends the bonus round altogether.During free spins, all wins are multiplied by the starting multiplier, which doubles on subsequent tumbles up to x1,024. The multiplier resets to its starting value between free spins. Hitting 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatter symbols resets the spin count back to 12 and upgrades the starting multiplier by multiplying it with x2, x4, x8, or x16, respectively, up to x1,024.Feature BuyFree spins can be bought for 78x the bet for a 3 scatter trigger, 150x for a 4 scatter trigger, 288x for a 5 scatter trigger, or 128x for 3, 4, 5, or 6 scatters.Vampy Party slot - free spinsVampy Party: Slot VerdictIf you've ever had a massive all-nighter that's carried on into the next day, you may be aware of the dread brought about by creeping sunlight and chirping birds. Spare a thought then for vampires who are weakened, some say killed, in the same scenario. Vampy Party didn't put on the sort of shindig that prompted all night excess, but it was fun while it lasted. Part of its success has to be attributed to the double-up multiplier which functions a lot like Yggdrasil Gaming's DoubleMax mechanic, as debuted to spectacular effect in Raptor DoubleMax. The two systems are not completely the same, but you know, they're pretty close.What sets them apart is that in Vampy Party, a wild symbol is not guaranteed to be placed in one of the removed winning symbols' empty spots. Also, the multiplier in Vampy Party is capped quite low. Well, x1,024 is far from low, but compared to DoubleMax, it is a rigid block. DoubleMax people may be turning their noses up in disdain at Vampy Party. Not only because, you know, this is a kind of a copy, but also because the multiplier resets during free spins rather than persisting into the stratosphere. For example, in Barbarossa Revenge, the multiplier can hit into the many thousands. Holding Vampy Party back is that when the multiplier grows in free spins, it does not stay at the higher level but drops back to its starting value, which cannot be increased once the bonus round has started. When comparing both systems and considering the 5,000x the bet win cap, Vampy Party does seem to come out as the limper of the two.Admittedly, Vampy Party proved to be quite entertaining despite the comparative straitjacketing. And yet, it feels like we're being a bit polite too, like showing up to say hi at an acquaintance's little get-together out of a sense of social obligation, all the while knowing there's an immense gathering of bacchanalian proportions happening at your best mate's house across town.

title: Jungle Spirit: Call of the Wild
structured_summary:
Jungle Spirit: Call of the Wild immerses players in a vibrant jungle teeming with wildlife and lush plant life.  
Key features include Symbol Expansion, Butterfly Boost, and a high-volatility Free Spins round with selectable risk levels.  
The reviewer praises its engaging gameplay, strong potential payouts, and overall appeal as one of NetEnt's top releases.  
Stunning graphics and animations are complemented by rhythmic drums and rich animal sounds for a fully immersive experience.
review: Jungle Spirit: Call of the Wild: OverviewJungle Spirit: Call of the Wild is a realm where wildlife populates the reels, and 'danger lurks behind every tree' - NetEnt's words, not ours. Along with the peril, Jungle Spirit is also an immersive game with some great features and a twist or two lurking in the dark. It starts with the visuals. Jungle Spirit is a gorgeous game. Part of NetEnt's fame has come from its lush visuals and Jungle Spirit is another strong example of their graphical talent. The name is a bit of a giveaway as the game is set in deepest, darkest, jungle bursting at the seams with wildlife. Along with the beasts is a wide range of plant life, with the grid draped in multi-hued flowers and hanging foliage.Player's ears don't miss out either with a drum track and cacophony of animal noises thickening up the experience. Wild by name, wild by nature means a high volatility level which will suit brave explorers, though the above-average RTP of 96.47% is a stat any player can get behind.The game grid itself is kind of interesting though it might not appear that way, to begin with. During the base game, players spin 5 reels, with 3 rows and 243 ways to win – a set up that expands during the bonus game as you will see. For now, the goal is landing three or matching symbols consecutively in any row from the first reel onwards.Playable from 20 p/c up to $/€100 per spin, symbols making up the paytable are no less impressive than the rest of the game is. Even the 10-A low pay royals have been designed in a stone covered in creeping ivy look like a forgotten corner of Angkor Wat. The game literally comes to life via the premium symbols which include cobras, crocs, bears, elephants, and tigers.Premiums appear in 1x1 tile size but can be expanded, and as to premium values, five of a kinds range from 3 times to 7.5 times the stake. Interestingly, there is no wild symbol, although with the way the features work, you won't even miss them.Jungle Spirit: Call of the Wild: FeaturesSo no wild symbols. But there is plenty stashed away in the features department to make up for any shortcomings. One that can appear during the base and bonus game is the Symbol Expansion feature. Any symbol in the game, except the scatter, may be marked by butterflies which land at random. If a marked symbol is part of a winning combination, it expands to cover a full reel and increase the win value.Butterflies also appear with the Butterfly Boost feature which is activated randomly in the main game when a winner appears. Here butterflies waft around and expand 1 to 3 of the winning symbols to cover their respective reels and power up the payout.The highlight is the Free Spins game which is triggered when 3 or more flower scatter symbols land. If 4 or 5 scatters trigger the feature, then players benefit from an additional win of 15x or 50x the stake respectively. During free spins, the grid expands to 5x4 size, which not only adds another row, but increases the bet ways up to 1,024. Before the bonus game kicks off, however, players choose 1 of 5 options that range from low to high risk:Cobra: 20 free spins with all high paying symbols transformed into cobra symbols for the duration of the feature.Crocodile: 16 free spins with all high paying symbols transformed into crocodile symbols.Bear: 12 free spins with all high paying symbols transformed into bear symbols.Elephant: 8 free spins with all high paying symbols transformed into elephant symbols.Tiger: 4 free spins with all high paying symbols transformed into tiger symbols.The animal chosen then becomes the only premium symbol that will appear during the round. The options with less free spins are higher risk/higher reward, while those with more spins have lower risk and lower potential rewards. Keep in mind too that free spins cannot be retriggered.Jungle Spirit: Call of the Wild: VerdictEvery top team goes through a dry spell now and then and Jungle Spirit certainly cleared the slate after a spate of so-so releases. In fact, Jungle Spirit more than just clears the way, it comes darting out of nowhere like, well, one of the rabid animals in the game.The animals themselves provide a lot of the game's appeal and are not only well-drawn, but come roaring to life via some slick animations. The whole jungle theme has been expertly dealt with and is another example of NetEnt's top graphic and sound talent.Jungle Spirit showcases another aspect of NetEnt's development chops via its features. Symbol Expansions and Butterfly Boosts keep the base game interesting. When those glowing little butterflies appear anticipation builds nicely over where they are going to land.The free spins have also been excellently designed and provide hardcore gamblers with a kick via the high volatility option. Those looking to stretch their gambling dollar with the low volatility choice. So does fortune favour the brave in this jungle? Can do, with solid potential during the base game of up to 1,822 time the stake, ramped up to 7,768 times the stake during free spins.All up, Jungle Spirit: Call of the Wild is a solid slot from the creative chaps at NetEnt that has become one of the most popular titles ever released by the studio. Its base game cruises nicely while the base game comes with options that will satisfy most gambling approaches – you can even change the soundtrack if you like. Dress it all up in the stunning visuals and you have a highly entertaining slot on your hands.

title: Vikings
structured_summary: Vikings is a Norse-themed slot inspired by the popular historical TV series featuring characters from the show. It offers a 243-ways-to-win base game, expanding to 78,125 ways during free spins, with unique features like the Hotspot and Shield Wall. The reviewer praises Vikings as a well-balanced, captivating slot with impressive win potential, comparable to NetEnt’s best releases. The game boasts high-quality visuals and an atmospheric Norse setting with a wintry landscape and thematic audio enhancing immersion.
review: Vikings (NetEnt): IntroductionIt was during the iGaming conference earlier this year that NetEnt presented not only one but two massive blockbuster titles - Narcos and Vikings. At the time when the information was first made public, the launch of Yggdrasil's third Vikings slot was fast approaching, and so we couldn't help but wonder if NetEnt would fall into the trap of ripping off Yggdrasil. Turns out these are entirely different games as you will see. For those not familiar with the Vikings tv-series, it's a historical tv-series drama created for the History channel and HBO. It follows Ragnar Lothbrok, a legendary Viking ruler, and his crew on their exploits as laid down in old sagas such as Ragnars saga Loðbrókar from the 13th century. Those of you who are fans of the series will be happy to see the actors known from the series represented on the reels.Raid spinsThe grand visual production came not as a surprise although we must say that we still managed to get caught off guard by the awesome intro that definitely helped set the mood right from the start and boost our expectations. Clicking our way into the game itself, we were pleasantly surprised to see the win-all-ways setup, which must be considered exotic when it comes to NetEnt and something that worked very well for them in Jungle Spirit which was released in 2017.If you're familiar with the series, you will feel right at home upon entering the game. If not, you're still likely to appreciate the work that NetEnt has put into the visual production with the reels set against a wintry, gloomy, Norse landscape made out of imposing hills that slope towards an icy lake. Don't be bothered by the lone raven watching your every move!As already mentioned, Vikings is a slot without pay lines. The 243 ways setup ensure that you win if 3 or more identical symbols land anywhere on subsequent reels. In the main game, Vikings is played on a 5x3 reel set but is switched to a 7x5 setup during the free spins feature, expanding the win ways to an astonishing 78,125 ways.Furthermore, the game comes with several different features which we will look into further below. Playable on all devices, players can bet between €0.20 to €200 per spin. The relatively high max bet is actually a tell-tale sign that it's not a super high potential slot. The 96.05% return to player is nothing out of the ordinary and more or less within the expected range.Vikings (NetEnt): Symbols & FeaturesVikings comes with a set of 10 symbols, 5 of which are of low-value symbols represented by 10, J, Q, K, and A made out of steel and covered in blood. In contrast, being a licensed and branded slot, the premiums are represented by characters known from the series although the Vikings logo has been chosen as the top paying symbol worth 0.5x for 5 of a kind. The premium symbols appear stacked on the reels in both the main game and the free spins feature. Interestingly, there is no Wild symbol to be seen, which likely had to stand back for the extra premium symbol.Included in the game is something known as the Hotspot feature. In the main game, reel 3 is illuminated by an electric flow to highlight its presence. When a stacked Viking symbol lands to fully cover the third reel, all the other Viking symbols will transform into that particular symbol. The beauty here is that the Viking symbols don't have to connect. All Viking symbols will be taken into consideration when wins are evaluated.A random feature known as the Shield Wall Feature has also been thrown in. It can activate at any time in both the main game and in the free spins feature and appears as a cluster of 3x2 or 5x2 shield mystery symbols on random areas of the reel set. The shields will then go on to reveal a premium symbol and wins are evaluated. This feature won't activate when the Hotspot feature is in play.7 free spins are awarded upon landing 3 scatter symbols on reels 3, 4 and 5. The bonus cannot re-activate as scatter symbols have been removed during the free spins game, but there is still a decent amount of potential packed in the Raid Spins as it's referred to. You basically get more of the same here, with a reel set that has been stretched out to substantially improve the potential. The 5x3, 243 win ways reel set has been transformed to a setup of 7x5, 78,125 win ways and the sole Hotspot reel now covers the three middle reels.Just like in the main game, if a Viking symbol lands in any of the Hotspot reels, all other Viking symbols will be transformed into that symbol. If 2 different Viking symbols cover the Hotspot reels, the one furthest to the left will be chosen as the transforming symbol. With the help of the Hotspot feature it's possible to land wins of up to 10,000 times the stake per single spin which is quite impressive!Vikings (NetEnt): ConclusionVikings could very well turn out to be NetEnt's best game since the release of Jungle Spirit. Sure, it can be a bit frustrating to end up with dead spins and plenty of low paying bonus rounds despite a trillion win ways, although to be fair, there are providers that are far worse when it comes to this aspect.Vikings is without a doubt a mega potential slot that is not nearly as brutal as Novomatic or Merkur slots tend to be just to make a comparison. Furthermore, Vikings appears to be well balanced with capacity to entertain and captivate players.

title: Colt Lightning Firestorm
structured_summary:

review: Colt Lightning Firestorm: Slot OverviewCast your minds back to February 2023, when Play'n GO released its horsey meets lightning slot Colt Lightning. Don't remember? Maybe the opening sequence, where a horse dashes across the landscape before getting obliterated by a bolt of lightning, might jog your memory. Yes, no? No matter, either way, Play'n GO and its ponies have cantered back for a follow-up going by the name of Colt Lightning Firestorm. The vibe is close, but the game's makers have seen fit to come up with different features while dramatically boosting one of the key numbers.A dry grassy zone is where we find ourselves for Colt Lightning Firestorm's base game. A desolate Wild West-style twangy guitar chunks up the atmosphere as if a titanic showdown is about to take place. Fortunately for horse lovers, no colts were obliterated at the start of the game, so the lol moment was absent. Otherwise, the look and feel of Colt Lightning Firestorm is about on par with the slot that preceded it.Colt Lightning Firestorm slot - base gameColt Lightning Firestorm's gaming panel has a more regular setup than before. This time, hitting spin sets in motion a 5-reel, 4-row game board, which has 1,024 ways to win on it. Before doing so, players are able to pick a stake of 10 c to $/€100. The volatility sits around medium-high, going by the 7 out of 10 ratings, while the default RTP, from the five different return configurations, is 96.2%.Blocky stone 10-A royals are Colt Lightning Firestorm's low-pay symbols, worth 1.2x to 1.6x when a 5 OAK winning combination lands on the grid. Next are snakes, wolves, cougars, eagles, and Colts, paying 2 to 8 times the bet for a 5-of-a-kind hit. Colts appear only in the base game and are replaced by Fire Colts in the free spins round. A combination of 5 Fire Colts pays 8 times the bet. Wilds are able to help complete winning ways by substituting any regular pay symbol. They are present on the three middle reels.Colt Lightning Firestorm: Slot FeaturesColt Lightning Firestorm slot - free spins splash screenOn the whole, Colt Lightning Firestorm's gameplay can be said to be fairly divergent from the previous slot, where its features are Lightning Blaze, Firestorm Feature, Firestorm Strike, and Fire Free Spins.Lightning BlazeLightning Blaze is triggered on any spin when a horseshoe symbol lands on the middle reel. During Lightning Blaze, 3 to 20 Fire Frames randomly appear on the reels, transforming symbols into one type of animal symbol.Firestorm FeatureLanding 4 Firestorm scatters on reels 2, 3, and 4 triggers the Firestorm feature. The Firestorm Feature consists of Fortune Strike and Fire Free Spins, both of which will be triggered during the Firestorm feature. At least, this is how the feature is worded in the game sheet. In the demo, when 3 scatters landed, they triggered just one of the features, not both. The Firestorm Strike offers an instant prize of 5x to 200x the total bet.Fire Free Spins awards 8 free spins, played on a gaming grid expanded by one extra row, upping the number of ways to win to 3,125. During Fire Free Spins, no Colt symbols appear on the reels, as they are transformed into Fire Colt symbols that pay double. Hitting the Horseshoe symbol triggers the Lightning Blaze feature. During this Lightning Blaze, 1 to 4 Fire Frames appear at random on the reels, and stick for the remainder of the round. At the end of Fire Free Spins, all Fire Frames in view transform into one type of animal symbol. Lastly, each Fire Ball scatter landing during Fire Free Spins awards +1 additional free spin, up to a maximum of 46 free spins.Colt Lightning Firestorm slot - free spinsColt Lightning Firestorm: Slot VerdictColt Lightning Firestorm is one of those slots where colossal winning potential threatens to eclipse the rest of the game's other goodies, or, smudge out the deficits. Have to say, the first downer occurred when 3 scatters landed to trigger the Firestorm feature. The way the feature is explained in the game docs makes it seem as though you're about to be granted both a Firestorm Strike instant prize and Fire Free Spins. But no, only one or the other ever triggered. For the first encounter, only Firestorm Strike was activated, spinning through its reel of prizes before ending up on the awarded cash total, 10x the bet, or something like that for anyone interested. What's funny is the reel teased by half-stopping on 200x, the largest possible prize value, before skipping away to something less thrilling. Tilting stuff in other words.Those two aspects left a bad taste in the mouth that Colt Lightning Firestorm struggled to prance its way out of at times. For the most part, it didn't really. You can see the possibilities, however, and that 50,000x the bet advertised max win might be like blinkers for any gamblers who are predominantly fixated on big numbers to the exclusion of all else. Yeah, it is a big number and double what the original Colt Lightning slot commanded, though there might be a greater chance of seeing a horse get pulverised by lightning in real life than witnessing either slot hit their full potential (it happens LESS than once in a billion spins, whatever that means - 0.10 in 1 billion?).Apologies if that sounded overly snarky, as Colt Lightning Firestorm didn't go too badly, all things considered. Free spins could produce a good number of frames, and filling them with the same high-pay symbol at the end of a bonus round could be exciting. Fair dues. However, cover over the massive maximum winning number for a moment, and Colt Lightning Firestorm loses a chunk of its allure.

title: Hammer of Gods

Megapays randomly triggers on any paid spin, shifting away from the game show to a sunny Las Vegas type scene. One pay symbol flashes up on screen (from 9-A) to be the Megapays symbol. Then, a 6x7 sized reel set spins and whenever the chosen symbol hits, it is collected. When no new Megapays symbols land, the bonus game ends, and the number of collected symbols equates to a jackpot as long as at least 4 have been gathered.Collecting 4-7 Megapays symbols awards the Mini jackpot (€100 seed value)Collecting 8-11 Megapays symbols awards the Midi jackpot (€1,500 seed value)Collecting 12-14 Megapays symbols awards the Major jackpot (€20,000 seed value)Collecting 15+ Megapays symbols awards the Mega jackpot (€300,000 seed value)Keep in mind during the Megapays feature, matching symbols on the grid do not pay, nor is the reaction mechanic active.
