title: Safari of Wealth
structured_summary: Safari of Wealth is an African safari-themed slot featuring iconic savannah animals. Its main features include a Gold Reel pick 'n click bonus and a free spins round with multiple grid size options. The reviewer finds the game dependable but unremarkable, offering straightforward gameplay without surprises. Visually, it presents classic savannah scenery with vibrant graphics and a bubbly soundtrack.
review: Safari of Wealth: Slot OverviewSafari of Wealth's title got us thinking about what an actual safari through other people's wealth would be like. Imagine a journey through jewels, high-end goods, labelled clothing, bling, etc., like window shopping in the expensive part of town while waiting patiently for payday. Fortunately, Safari of Wealth from Play'n GO isn't like that. It's a regular safari type game set in Africa, rather than a tantalising stroll through a gold souk. As well as admiring the dangerous animals, players benefit from a Gold Reel pick 'n click feature and a five option free spins bonus round.Safari of Wealth ticks the right boxes graphically speaking for this sort of game. Wavy grass, a snaking river, trees, mountains, blue skies with a chance of rain, and plenty of bucket list beasts. Most of the screen is taken up by a 5x3, 243 ways grid, but you get a nice taste of the African Savannah, and the soundtrack is equally bubbly. However, there is little here players won't have seen before, and Safari of Wealth isn't exactly a slot Play'n GO probably had to push themselves to produce.Safari of Wealth - Wild Prize feature triggeredIt is easy on the eyes and ears, though, and is equipped with an equally dependable math model. RTP comes in a number of configurations, depending on the market, so if you want the best value, be on the lookout for the 96.2% version. In all RTP cases, it's highly volatile, while stakes range from 10 p/c to $/€100 per spin.For the most part, Safari of Wealth is pretty straightforward. Actually, there's nothing here remotely complicated which may not excite players looking for something new to go with the common theme. Winning combinations pay left to right and need at least three matching symbols to do so. On the low side are 10-A card ranks paying 0.4 to 0.8x the bet for five of a kind, moving up to premium leopards, rhinos, lions, elephants, and wildebeests. Five premium symbol combos award 3 to 10 times your stake. The wild symbol appears in any reel to substitute all symbols except the scatter. If wild symbols create winning ways, they are worth the same as the highest value wildebeest.Safari of Wealth: Slot FeaturesTo potentially help get your hands on some wealth, the base game is padded out with a Gold Reel feature, while free spins have several choices for players to try their luck with.Gold Reel FeatureOn any base game spin, 1-5 reels may randomly turn gold. If a wild symbol lands on one of the gold symbols, the game shifts to a Wild Prize pick 'n click game. Here, 15 logo symbols appear on the screen, and players click one at a time to reveal an animal. When 3 matching animals have been revealed, the corresponding prize is awarded. Rhinos, lions, elephants, or wildebeests pay 10x, 25x, 500x, or 5,000x the bet, respectively.Free SpinsSafari of Wealth Free Spins are awarded when 3 or more scatters land in view. As well as activating the bonus game, players collect a payout of 5x, 10x, or 50x the bet for 3, 4, or 5 scatters on the reels. Before the bonus begins, players choose the layout and number of free spins they would like to collect:20 free spins on the regular 5x3, 243 ways to win game board.15 free spins on a 5x4, 1,024 ways to win game board.10 free spins on a 5x5, 3,125 ways to win game board.5 free spins on a 5x6, 7,776 ways to win game board.Mystery pick which randomly mixes free spins with grid size from the previous four options.Just to reiterate, the Gold Reel feature cannot be activated during the bonus game, but free spins can be retriggered when 3 or more scatters symbols hit.Safari of Wealth: Slot VerdictSafari of Wealth is one of those games that does what it says on the tin while trying hard not to rock any boats. Players can pretty much count on getting what they are signing up for, and there are unlikely to be any surprises. As such, if you're tooling around for dependably straightforward Africa gaming, then Safari of Wealth could be the right choice. This dependability is as much a liability as a benefit, though. From theme to features, there is little to get overly excited about, and you kind of expect more from a studio as established as Play'n GO. Still, with such a busy schedule, they're sure to fire off the odd shelf filler, and Safari of Wealth does feel a lot like that.There's nothing overly critical to say from a technical standpoint, and Safari of Wealth has a couple of okay features. The base game isn't the most engaging, relying on an old-fashioned pick 'n click with an admittedly valuable wildebeest top prize to mix up the flow. Free spins are just as simplistic, too, really. Having options is always nice, but nothing overly special happens in free spins aside from some grid height alterations. Hey ho, good things can certainly occur here, and potential is positive as Safari of Wealth maxes out at 10,000x the bet.Apologies if this review is coming across a bit bland. The reaction to Safari of Wealth was just so lukewarm. If only it did something glaringly wrong to pick apart or something amazing to laud, we'd have stronger talking points. However, Safari of Wealth has neither of these things and ended up as a totally middle of the road game in most regards. It's like a movie that had all the foul language and offensive scenes cut out to garner a more marketable PG rating rather than R18, but in doing so, lost its most memorable parts.

title: Legends Battle Of Earth
structured_summary: Legends Battle Of Earth is a superhero-themed slot where heroes and villains clash in a comic book-style battle. Key features include a 6x4 grid, Wild Toolbox modifiers, and an engaging Showdown Spins bonus with allies and enemies battling for cash prizes. The reviewer finds it an exciting yet familiar combat slot, praising the dynamic free spins but noting the base game can feel slow. The game boasts high-quality comic book visuals and animations that enhance the immersive superhero atmosphere.
review:
Legends Battle For Earth: Slot OverviewHere's a little thought experiment: if you were a superhero, what superpowers would you want to have? Flight would be cool. Mega strength and invulnerability are desirable traits, but how about something more originally exotic? Whatever your preference, gamblers have the chance to pretend they're superheroes for the day, defending the world from diabolical villains in the online slot Legends Battle For Earth. Designed by Octoplay and pals Combat Royale, here's a slot where goodies and baddies face off to fight each other, awarding cash prizes as battle unfolds.Are the makers of Legends Battle For Earth big comic book fans? Going by the looks of this game, you'd suspect they are, as Legends Battle For Earth has an excellent comic-book appearance to it, as if the characters and setting have leapt right off the page into the realms of online gambling. Then again, the team has a knack for bringing subject matter to life, no matter the topic, as seen in the apocalyptic playground of Dystopia Rebel Road and the anime/manga delight Eternal Clash - both Showdown Spins slots like Legends Battle For Earth if you haven't caught them yet.Legends Battle Of Earth slot - base gameIn the base game, Legends Battle For Earth rages out on a 6x4-reel gaming grid with 20 paylines for hitting combos across. As for the math model, Showdown Spins slots come in all shapes and sizes, of which Legends Battle For Earth is of the medium volatility variety. Its RTP is 95.7% when wagering 10 c to $/€150 per spin or 95.79% when using the Double Chance. Activating Double Chance increases the stake by 40%, doubling the chance of triggering the free spins round.Ten to Ace playing card ranks are Legends Battle For Earth's least exciting symbols. They pay 3 to 10 times the bet for a 6 OAK winning combination. Next up are 5 hero character symbols, paying 12 to 50 times the bet for a 6-matching symbol winning line. Wilds pay 100x for a 5 wild win line and also substitute any pay symbols to help create wins.Legends Battle For Earth: Slot FeaturesLegends Battle Of Earth slot - free spinsThese combat slots often drop a teaser feature in the base game before climaxing during the battling it out Showdown Spins bonus. In Legends Battle For Earth, the base game feature is its modifier bestowing Wild Toolbox.Wild ToolboxThe Wild Toolbox symbol substitutes for all other symbols except the scatter. Up to 2 Wild Toolboxes may land on the grid at the same time - one on the first three reels, one on the other three reels. Each Wild Toolbox triggers 3 to 8 modifiers on the reels, up to 5 modifiers of the same type. The modifiers are:Wild Symbol - turns a random symbol into wild, substituting for any pay symbol.Multiple Modifier - awards a random symbol a multiplier of x2, x3, or x5. If more than one multiplier lands on the same position, the values are added.Showdown SpinsLanding at least 3 scatter symbols in the base game triggers Showdown Spins. Depending on the number of trigger scatters, the round starts with different settings:3 Scatters - 1000 Player and Enemy Health Points.4 Scatters - 1250 Player and Enemy Health Points, one Ally 1 to 3, plus one Enemy 1 to 3 guaranteed on the first spin.5 Scatters - 1500 Player and Enemy Health Points, two Allies 1 to 3, plus two Enemies 1 to 3 guaranteed on the first spin.6 Scatters - 2000 Player and Enemy Health Points, the Ally Mini-Boss, plus the Enemy Mini-Boss guaranteed on the first spin.The bonus plays out on a 6-reel, 1-row grid, where the only symbols landing are allies, enemies, Boost Toolboxes, and empty spaces. When allies and enemies are in view, they battle each other. Characters lose Attack Power equal to the Attack Power of their opponent. When the Attack Power reaches 0, they are destroyed and are removed from the reels. Allies and Enemies possess Cash Prizes. When enemies are destroyed, their Cash Prize is collected, up to a maximum of 3,000x. When allies are destroyed, their Cash Prize is added to the Prize Pool, up to a maximum of 3,000x. The Prize Pool is awarded if the round ends in a win.If all enemy characters are destroyed and there are allies in view, they attack the Enemy Health Points, deducting their Attack Power from it. Allied characters that survive a spin get +10 Attack Power at the end of each spin. The opposite occurs, too, meaning enemy characters attack Players Health Points if there are no allies in view to battle. The feature ends when Enemy Health Points reach 0, meaning the players win. Or, they are defeated if Players Health Points reach 0.CharactersIn Showdown Spins, characters land on the reels with these attributes:Allied Characters
Ally 1: 20 Attack Power, 3x the stake Cash Prize. Ally 2: 50 Attack Power, 10x the stake Cash Prize. Ally 3: 150 Attack Power, 30x the stake Cash Prize. Ally 4: 300 Attack Power, 150x the stake Cash Prize. Ally 5: 600 Attack Power, 500x, 1,000x, 1,500x, or 2,000x the stake Cash Prize.Enemy Characters
Enemy 1: 50 Attack Power, 2x - 200x the stake Cash Prize. Enemy 2: 100 Attack Power, 5x - 200x the stake Cash Prize. Enemy 3: 200 Attack Power, 20x - 300x the stake Cash Prize. Enemy 4: 400 Attack Power, 100x - 300x the stake Cash Prize. Enemy 5: 800 Attack Power, 500x, 1,000x, 1,500x, or 2,000x the stake Cash Prize.Booster ToolboxBooster Toolbox symbols may land on the reels during Showdown Spins. When they land on the allied part, they award +25 Attack Power for each level of the Booster Toolbox to all allies. When they land on the enemy part, they award +10 to the Cash Prize of each level of the Booster Toolbox to all enemies. If the Booster Toolbox is present when there is a character in their part of the grid, they are activated and their level increases by +1 on each activation up to 10.Feature BuyPlayers may use the bonus buy to jump straight into the Showdown Spins feature for 100x the bet. The RTP for doing so is 95.85%.Legends Battle Of Earth slot - free spinsLegends Battle For Earth: Slot VerdictIn some ways, Octoplay tiptoed on the wild side with this one and mostly pulled it off. The challenge was making a game with generic, nobody superheroes that players can connect with and putting them in a slot delivering gaming mechanics the studio has used before more than once. The good news is the developer has stepped up, ensuring Legends Battle For Earth is another exciting Showdown Spins slot, where allies and enemies meet, punch each other, as players settle in to enjoy the conflict.On the theme front, Octoplay has done a great job of crossing superheroes and villains over from the comic book page to the online gambling screen. Some characters have a vague familiarity to them. Perhaps that helped. For example, the purple hero has a Deadpool touch, while the blue villain rang a faint Captain America bell; maybe he was in his Hydra phase. They helped form an emotional connection, as did the high standard of the artwork in general, plus all the animations. Despite this, the base game might be a bit of a plodder. Twenty paylines are a little overwhelmed by a 6x4 gaming grid, though the Wild Toolbox can spray it with wilds. Naturally, in these combat slots, the focus is on getting to the Showdown Spins phase, so the base game is a bit of a formality.Changes to the free spins round have altered the dynamic. One way is that enemies collect prize values when they defeat allies, and this collected pool of dough is only awarded if players win the round by reducing Enemy Health Points to zero. So you've got potential situations of wanting to pummel the enemy, but not too much too soon, in order to draw the whole session out so the enemy prize pool grows as well. For example, it's possible to get one of the big ally hitters, with no one to hit, smashing the Enemy Health Bar to pieces with an unappealing value in the Prize Pool. On the other hand, you might be lucky enough to bear witness to an epic back-and-forth battle. The slot's top prize tops out at 6,000x, sitting Legends Battle For Earth between Eternal Clash and Dystopia Rebel Road in terms of winning potential. When the dust cleared, Legends Battle For Earth's exciting presentation and intriguing rule changes should encourage fans of Showdown Spins rounds to break out the spandex.

title: Alice in Adventureland
structured_summary: Alice in Adventureland is a fantasy-themed slot inspired by Lewis Carroll’s Alice, set in a unique alternate world called Adventureland. The game features wild multipliers, Rocketkats that upgrade symbols, Ultrabombs, free spins with scatter collection, and a rare Adventure Spin bonus. The reviewer finds it a charming, moderately imaginative slot with exciting feature interactions, though the top bonus is elusive. Visually, it offers a misty emerald valley backdrop with a quirky soundtrack, creating a pleasant but less psychedelic atmosphere than typical Alice-themed slots.
review: Alice in Adventureland: Slot OverviewStockholm based provider Fantasma Games keeps their love affair for all things fantasy slash fictional going with an online slot called Alice in Adventureland. As you might have guessed from the title, the studio has picked a recognisable theme to colour the action, that of Lewis Carrol's Alice and her mind-bending escapades. This time, she's not in Wonderland as such, but an alternate reality called Adventureland. There are similarities and crossovers between the two worlds. However, this one possesses more bombs than before, which appear in certain features alongside wild transformations, wild multipliers, and free spins.Basing our assessment from Alice in Adventureland's imagery, Adventureland isn't as wacky a looking place as Wonderland. The background is made up of an emerald green valley, all misty and inviting beneath a pink and purple sky. Weapons lie littered about the place, though, hidden most of the time behind a 5x4, 20-payline game panel. The soundtrack is pretty wacky, in a good way, and though not as richly designed as Fantasma games can be, the whole scene is agreeable enough to prompt further investigation as to how deep the rabbit hole goes.It actually goes fairly deep, progressing from the base game to free spins, then to an extra Adventure Spin if you can make it so far. At all times, winning combinations are formed when matching symbols land left to right across one of the 20 fixed paylines. This feeds into a theoretical return to player value of 96.26%, rising to 96.3% when buying free spins. Medium/high volatile, Alice in Adventureland is available on any device and provides stakes of 20 p/c to $/€80 per spin.As for the paytable, there are nine regular pay symbols, wilds, and several special ones. For the low pays, we get the four card suits – diamonds, clubs, spades, and hearts, paying 2-2.5x the bet for five of a kind. Next are knights, teapots, pocket watches, Rabbits with what look like boxing gloves, and Alice as the premium symbols. Land five of these to collect a payout worth 3 to 10 times your stake. The wilds are worth more at 15x the bet for a line of five and also replace any other pay symbol on the reels.Alice in Adventureland: Slot FeaturesOn your journey through Adventureland, the features to look out for include Rocketkats, Ultrabombs, wild multipliers, and Adventure Free Spins, where a scatter collection system is used.RocketkatsThe Rocketkat is a wild symbol that can land on reels 2-5 in the base or bonus game. If Rocketkat symbols appear on more than one reel, they activate the Rocketkat feature. When this happens, each Rocketkat symbol moves as far to the left as possible, randomly upgrading symbols they pass over. Rocketkats always leave a wild symbol in their original position. If upgraded, regular and scatter symbols become wilds, while wild symbols become x2 wilds. Any wilds already carrying a multiplier have their value increased by +1, up to a maximum of x9. If more than one multiplier wild is used in a win, their values are added together before being applied.UltrabombsThe Ultrabomb is wild and appears with a number on it on the leftmost reel in Adventure Free Spins or on reels 1-3 on the Adventure Spin. Ultrabombs are activated when a Rocketkat symbol passes over them. When this happens, a number of symbols equal to the number the Ultrabomb displays is upgraded. Ultrabomb upgrades work the same way as Rocketkat upgrades, so regulars become wild, wilds become wild multipliers.Adventure Free SpinsA total of 12 free spins are awarded when three scatter symbols land in the base game. During free spins, when scatter symbols land, they are collected in a meter and change the rules when a certain amount is collected:Level 1 – achieved when 4 scatters are collected. This activates the Ultrabomb feature described above and awards +4 free spins.Level 2 – achieved when 9 scatters are collected. Now, Rocketkat symbols always upgrade the positions they travel over.Level 3 – when 15 scatters are collected, the game awards an Adventure Spin, played when the Adventure Free Spins are complete.Adventure SpinMake it this far, and you get 1 free spin with 3-12 Ultrabombs, plus 3-7 Rocketkat symbols added to the reels. For this spin, Rocketkats can move in five directions instead of just to the left and always upgrade the symbols they touch.Buy Free SpinsIf this is a possibility in your jurisdiction, then Adventure free spins can be brought for the cost of 100x the total bet.Alice in Adventureland: Slot VerdictAlice in Adventureland was a charming game with a few interesting things going for it. Fantasma hasn't drenched the game in an Alice theme, which can be a good or bad thing, depending on your preference. It's closer to something like Plunderland in vibe than others that like to go full psychedelic dreamland. Then again, we are dealing with Adventureland rather than Wonderland; a Fantasma made construct where they are free to create the world however they like. What they've gone for isn't as fantastical as some of their slots can be; Serpent Shrine and Twisted Turbine are two which sprang to mind as contrasting slots that really build an in-depth game world to explore.But hey, Alice in Adventureland is a decent option for players after an Alice-themed slot hit. The action taking place on the reels got good at times, though it was dependent on a few elements firing at the same time. The best results during the review occurred when the Ultrabomb feature had been activated, at the same time as waves of Rocketkats upgrading wilds to multiplier wilds. Those spins could be pretty exciting, even though moving wild multiplier values past x2 or x3 was tough. The Adventure Spin is intriguing as well, but don't count on that one hitting often. It was a real unicorn event during testing. The elusive Adventure Spin would no doubt be helpful for cracking Alice in Adventureland's max win potential.To wrap up, Alice in Adventureland isn't the most out-there Alice based slot on the market, nor as imaginative as others Fantasma has done, if you're looking for a major break from reality. But it had its fun moments during testing, and there is an interesting interplay of features going on, the enjoyment of which came down to how closely they worked together.

title: Last Chance Saloon
structured_summary: Last Chance Saloon is a Wild West-themed slot set in a 19th-century saloon, evoking the final stop for a drink before entering a harsh frontier. The game features Coin multipliers, Bullet Spins with growing multipliers, a Double or Nothing gamble, and a Second Chance flip for added excitement. The reviewer finds it charming and atmospheric, though not groundbreaking, with enjoyable gameplay and decent winning potential. The visuals are simple with a dusty frontier vibe, complemented by a stripped-down but effective soundtrack enhancing the bleak mood.
review: Last Chance Saloon: Slot OverviewSaddle up with Red Tiger partner R7 as they travail the Wild West in a smoky slot called Last Chance Saloon. Common back in the day, bars in 19th century USA would often use a variation of the name, 'The Last Chance Saloon', to indicate people were nearing an area where booze was not easy to obtain. Or even outright prohibited. These saloons were quite literally the last chance for a good while of partaking in alcoholic beverages. The phrase Last Chance Saloon has since gone on to be used in a wider range of contexts, though always indicating that someone is reaching a point where fortune or hope starts to fade away.Going back to its original meaning, R7 has given Last Chance Saloon a nice Wild West atmosphere which can grow on you if you go with the glow. Initially, the graphics aren't amazing compared to what some of the competition is putting out, yet the unassuming nature does have appeal. Saloon doors wave in the wind; cowboy accessories hang on the walls while triggering free spins gains you access to the building where on the table lies whiskey, a hat, a pistol, bullets, cards, and cash - everything an outlaw might ever need. It's worth taking a few moments to soak in the vibe to get in the mood before diving in – the excellent stripped-down music helps here.Last Chance Saloon is a 5-reel, 4-row video slot, providing 30 fixed paylines. Hit spin and some of the game's Western dignity is buried beneath a stock set of slot bleeping noises, diminishing the effect to a degree, though not completely so. Bet selection is up first, where players choose from 10 p/c to $/€20 per spin, possible on any device. A highly volatile game, The Last Saloon produces a default theoretical return figure of 95.79%, though this number can be lower depending on where you play.Hitting at least three identical symbols across a payline starting on the leftmost side results in a coin win, and eight paying tiles make up the table. These are J-A royals as the low pays, then dice, cards, Bars, and Sevens as the highs. Most are classic slot symbols we've seen a million times before, but they are quite individually done, five of them covered in what looks like wheat. Values for premium symbols landing in a five of a kind combination is 2 to 5 times the stake.Last Chance Saloon: Slot FeaturesLast Chance Saloon - free spinsLast Chance Saloon's features are all about Coin multipliers, Bullet Spins, Double or Nothing, and ironically a Second Chance feature.Coin FeatureCoins are wild and substitute for all paying symbols. They appear only on the middle reel and have a win multiplier on their back side. If a coin participates in a line win, it flips, so there is a chance it may land on its multiplier or non-multiplier side. Values can be as high as x50.Bullet SpinsLanding 3 Bullet Symbols on reels 1, 3, and 5 triggers 6 to 8 free Bullet Spins. In Bullet Spins, at least one Coin symbol is guaranteed to land on the central reel. Whenever a Coin awards a multiplier, it is added to a growing global win multiplier that applies to all winning lines – resetting when free spins end. Scatters do not land during the round, so retriggers are not possible.Double or NothingWhen Bullet Spins end, players have the choice of collecting the winnings or gambling them. If gamble is picked, a coin with a blank side and a 'double' side is flipped. Landing on blank means you lose the lot; landing on 'double' literally doubles the prize money.Second ChanceAt random in the base game, if one or more coins is flipped and did not award a multiplier, a Second Chance may activate to flip them to their multiplier side. This feature also applies to the Double or Nothing flip after free spins. So, landing a blank can be flipped to its 'double' side.Last Chance Saloon: Slot VerdictLast Chance Saloon turned out to be quite fun, and much of the entertainment was tied to the theme treatment. R7 hasn't displayed the chops of a Nolimit City or a NetEnt, yet its simple design is not without its charm. Perhaps the name was an influence, but you do kind of get the feeling that the bar in this game teeters on the edge between relative civilisation and desolation. As if just outside lies a dusty wasteland where destiny awaits. As such, slingers might as well slam away a few beverages, and have one last throw of the dice, or coin flip as is the case in Last Chance Saloon. Beneath the beeping noises, the soundtrack helps to create an excellently bleak atmosphere, one which conjures up images of a windswept frontier.The gameplay side isn't life-altering, but it can be enjoyable. Wild coins provide a little thrill whenever they flip, as they tease between will it be a multiplier or won't it? Thrills and stakes significantly up the ante when presented with the Double or Nothing option after Bullet Spins. Due to the Double Chance feature, the paytable mentions this increases the odds of hitting 'double'. You know what they say about a bird in the hand and all that, but the game docs do also mention the best strategy is to gamble, so is something for players to take into account. The final piece of the puzzle is potential, which like the rest of Last Chance Saloon isn't stand out yet decent enough at 4,982x the bet.Last Chance Saloon has nowhere near the pizazz of something like say, Deadwood or Dead or Alive 2, but it evokes a certain frontier allure, inviting players to lay their hat at the table to try their luck.

title: Rich Wilde and the Shield of Athena

review: Rich Wilde and the Shield of Athena: OverviewRich Wilde has proven to be a hugely successful franchise for Swedish developer Play’n GO. His victory is perhaps why the snake haired Gorgon is depicted on the shield. What the shield’s other powers might be is shrouded in mystery. Perhaps following Rich on his journey, we can uncover them.In Shield of Athena, players don’t just team up with the steely-eyed explorer. This time we are also joined by his daughter Cat Wilde who is a sort of mix between Jennifer Anniston and Lara Croft. To be honest, she seems a little too old to be Rich’s (who appears to have aged gracefully) daughter, but that’s poetic license after all.After the cascading grid format of Tome of Madness, Rich has returned to a more conventional set up using 5 reels, 3 rows, and 10 fixed paylines. In that sense, this is probably the closest we've been to an actual Book of Dead sequel. Surrounding the grid are Greek styled columns, while a whole lot of water cascades down into the background. It’s a brooding scene, matched only by Rich’s deeply brooding gaze. Pick a bet from 10 p/c to $/€100 for the deep-diving to begin.The rules are easy, land three matching symbols left to right on a payline to score a prize. The symbols used are as well-drawn as the rest of the scenery, split into 5 low and 4 high pays. Low pays might be common 10-A royals, but they are beautifully crafted out of stone dipped in a colourful effect. The high pays are even more enticing and include a Golden Owl, a Pendant of Courage, the Ring of Wisdom, the Helm of Athena, and the Shield of Athena.Values are massive with 5 standard Shields on a payline worth a considerable 500 times the stake - double when it turns into a Wild Shield. Rich is the regular wild, and he is worth 1,000 times the stake when five of him turn up on a line. Wilds can substitute for any pay symbol to help pull together more winners.Players who like basic gaming with lashings of volatility will find it in Shield of Athena. Play’n GO has rated the volatility at 10/10 so, pretty much as high as it can get, creating a potent combination with the rest of the game’s elements. No qualms over the RTP rated 96.25% on the default setting. The RTP can be lowered though, so a quick browse through the paytable to clarify things is a must.Rich Wilde and the Shield of Athena: FeaturesPaytable - free spins explainedThis section is all about respins and free spins which work effectively on their own or in tandem. First is the Medusa Respin feature which may activate on any spin if the Shield of Athena wild lands on the reels. When triggered, one respins is awarded with the standard Shield of Athena symbol now transforming into a wild.During the respin, all Shield of Athena symbols, plus any winning symbols, are held in position. If any more Shields or winning symbols appear, they are locked as well and the reels respin again. Respins continue until no more Shield of Athena symbols or winning symbols land, at which point wins are paid out. One last point, all instances of Rich Wilde wilds or Cat Wilde scatters are turned into Wild Shields.Now, the Medusa Respin also makes an appearance in the second feature - the Medusa’s Gaze Free Spins. Unlike the storybook Medusa who turned heroes into stone, this one is much more desirable. It is triggered when 3, 4, or 5 Cat Wilde scatters are in view to award 10, 12, or 15 Medusa’s Gaze Free Spins. Here you'll benefit from the Medusa Respin always remaining active throughout the feature. The feature can also be retriggered indefinitely, so 3, 4, 5, scatters award another 10, 12, or 15 free spins.Rich Wilde and the Shield of Athena: VerdictRiche Wilde and the Shield of Athena is a really well-made slot. It doesn’t do anything particularly ground-breaking, but everything it does do has been splendidly crafted, meshing each element perfectly together - from the high-quality graphics to the paytable and the superb features. There might only be two features mixing the gameplay up, but they can go berserk, especially the Medusa Respins when they rack up stacks of Wild Shields.After the grid slot antics of the previous instalment, Shield of Athena is more of a return to its Book of Dead-style roots. The gameplay is straight forward, uses a traditional setup, and provides plenty of winning opportunities with maximum wins of up to 10,000 times the stake possible.It’s not too much of a stretch to call Shield of Athena one of Rich Wilde’s best outings to date. It’s simple, possesses well-tuned features, and is devoid of any major flaws. The math model has the ability to crush unsuspecting gamblers who aren’t prepared perhaps, but others will love it. Overall, the gameplay perfectly matches the math model and the high pay symbols to combine for some excellent gaming. As it stands, Shield of Athena is a worthy sequel to Book of Dead. If it is to become another classic, however, is yet to be seen.

title: Fat Drac
structured_summary: Fat Drac is a vampire-themed slot set in a spooky Transylvania backdrop, continuing Push Gaming's 'Fat' series with a darker twist. It features a revealing Fat Drac symbol, instant bubble prizes, a Fat Bat feature, pick 'n click coffins, and escalating free spins with an expanding symbol. The reviewer views it as a challenging, high-volatility game with huge win potential but warns it may alienate fans of earlier, lighter titles. The game boasts detailed, cartoonish graphics and playful piano music that add charm to its eerie atmosphere.
review: Fat Drac: Slot OverviewPlayers, prepare to get your gorge on in Fat Drac, the third slot in Push Gaming's seasonal and somewhat insensitively named 'Fat' series. The first was the classic Fat Rabbit, of course, a cute game that captured all sorts of hearts, then Fat Santa, which didn't create such a lasting impression despite being one of the first Push Gaming slots to offer a bonus buy. So, we've gone from feasting on carrots, then cherry pies, to… blood, in the third 'Fat' slot, Fat Drac. In this one, nosferatu chases goblets of blood around the screen triggering free spins where he increases in size. Drac is joined by instant bubble rewards, pick 'n clicks, and a fat bat feature, yet one significant change might upset the broth for certain fans.Around three and a half years have passed since Fat Rabbit was released, and things have noticeably moved on. A lot more pixels have been used to create a more intricately looking, high-definition scene. The game is set in a mountainous location, presumably Transylvania, where the Drac's towered home perches precariously on a rocky outcrop, threatening to tip-off at any moment, while withered trees and skulls make up the foreground. An element of good-natured humour has been used throughout Fat Drac, from the cartoon-like symbols, adorable bats to the excellent music which sounds like a plinking piano piece you could imagine the vampire from Sesame Street singing a song about numbers to.Fat Drac is a big Push game, though, so the good nature is only skin deep. Sink your fangs in a bit deeper to find a highly volatile math model that's less friendly than Fat Rabbit or Fat Santa was. Potential has been jacked far beyond what either previous slot could even dream of but beware, the rest of the game has followed suit, so this is no quick nip in the neck, welcome to immortality. No complaints about the RTP, though, which comes in at 96.57%.As before, the game is played on a 5-reel, 5-row game grid, this time providing 40 fixed ways to hit winning combinations on. Regular paying symbols start with the four card suits – spades, diamonds, hearts, and clubs, while premiums consist of false teeth, parchment, skeletons, and an Elizabethan era looking guy. Land a combination of five premiums, and the payout is worth 5 to 25 times your stake. Interestingly, the Fat Drac symbol is not wild, but there is a golden wild symbol, landing anywhere to substitute regular pay symbols. The wild also pays out in combinations of itself, up to 250x the bet for five on a payline.Fat Drac: Slot FeaturesSo we dropped the bombshell that the expanding Drac symbol isn't wild; instead, it acts as a revealing symbol. As well as this is Bat Symbols, Instant Bubble Prizes, a Fat Bat feature, Coffin Symbol pick 'n clicks, and free games.Fat Drac SymbolThe Fat Drac is a revealing symbol, landing anywhere on the board. When a Fat Drac hits, he transforms to reveal any paying symbol or a Bat symbol.Bat Symbol and BubblesNext to the reels is a line of 7 bubbles, displaying Instant Prizes. When the Fat Drac reveals bats, they fly to the line of bubbles and pop them. The Instant Prize they contain are released and awarded as a multiple of the bet. Instant Prize values could be 1x, 2x, 5x, 10x, 25x, 50x, 100x, 250x, 500x, 1,000x, 5,000x, 10,000x, or 50,000x the bet.Fat BatThe Fat Bat feature triggers at random on any base game spin. When activated, a Fat Bat hits the reels and collects all of the bubble prizes, awarding them to the player.Coffin SymbolWhen a coffin symbol lands anywhere on the reels, the Pick feature is triggered - 4 tiles appear on screen for the player to choose one of. In the base game, tiles may reveal 1-5 bats or a goblet symbol - only if a Fat Drac symbol is present on reel 1.Free Games FeatureWhen at least 1 Goblet symbol lands at the same time as a Fat Drac symbol, then 5 free spins are awarded. The Fat Drac symbol remains on the reels for the full duration of free spins, and whenever a new Goblet Symbol lands, the Drac moves to collect it. Also, during the feature, tiles may reveal 1-5 additional free spins, Goblet symbols, or up to 5 bats. Starting as a 1x1 symbol, as the Drac Symbol collects Goblets, it increases in size at set intervals, like so:5 collected goblets increase him to 2x2 and award +4 free spins.5 additional goblets increase him to 3x3 and award +3 free spins.3 additional goblets increase him to 4x4 and award +2 free spins.2 additional goblets increase him to 5x5 and award +2 free spins.Fat Drac: Slot VerdictYou can imagine the dilemma Push Gaming may or may not have gone through when designing Fat Drac. Do they stick close to the previous games, get accused of being soft, or worse, of being unoriginal? Or do they do as they have done and drastically up the ante by creating a more challenging yet potentially rewarding slot? Pick the second route and you build a hardcore game that may alienate some fans of the first who were keen for some cutey pie gaming. It's a tightrope, yet Push has committed to their choice and powered on with it.Players after another cuddly bunny experience from Fat Drac may end up unexpectedly burned. Like contestants on talent shows who unfortunately don't have much talent but who's friends and family members never told them. So, when they inevitably butcher the song they've chosen, the judges, in turn, hack them back to reality. If that's the first time someone has faced real criticism, on television with millions of people watching, it must be a soul-destroying experience.Okay, Fat Drac isn't so drastic, but as well as its mathematical alterations, the fact the Fat Drac tile is a revealing symbol rather than a wild (basically a mystery symbol) might disappoint a few fans. This change, combined with fewer paylines than before, has tightened the experience in some ways, possibly making it tougher to get ahead. The expanding symbol aspect is still highly entertaining when a good roll is on it must be said. Plus, the extra Pick feature, bats and Bubbles give the game more depth, as well as new ways to potentially win. Speaking of potential, Fat Drac's max win has been capped at 50,000x the bet, which is way higher than the previous two games could go. For the record, any given bet has a 1 in 76,613,180 chance of serving up the maximum prize.Push Gaming has navigated the 'Fat' series into new and potentially more turbulent waters. The core expanding symbol in free spins feature remains, but this is a different category of beast than what came before in every respect. Being so boldly different, some players are sure to embrace the radical changes; others may well recoil to a safe place like a vampire when the sun comes up.

title: A Tale of Elves
structured_summary: A Tale of Elves is a Christmas-themed slot set in a snowy forest and an elves' workshop, evoking traditional holiday cheer. It features a 5-reel, 243-ways layout with free spins offering four volatility options, random cash prizes, and retriggerable bonuses. The reviewer praises its classic Microgaming gameplay and high volatility, making it appealing to veteran players despite a modest RTP. The game boasts charming festive visuals with snow-covered trees, colorful elves, and a cozy, heartwarming audio atmosphere.
review: A Tale of Elves: Slot OverviewOne of the good things about Christmas from a developer's point of view, is how versatile it is. Some go for a light sprinkling of the season like NetEnt did in Aloha! Christmas Edition, others go for the mid-ground. Microgaming, on the other hand, has created a slot so infused with Christmas cheer, if it popped you'd be showered in mince pies and mistletoe. To give it an even more traditional feel, Microgaming has packed it's 2020 Christmas contribution with some heartwarmingly classic gaming.The base game of A Tale of Elves plays out in a snow-covered forest, in the depths of winter, before the big day. Here the 5-reel, 243 ways game area is framed by trees and Christmas lights. Triggering free spins shifts the action to the elves' workshop, where the wee guys are busy making toys for all the good boys and girls. Old fashioned toys like wooden trains that elves hammer away on in movies which kids these days don't really go for anymore.Playable on any device, A Tale of Elves offers a modest range of bets starting at 30 p/c per spin, rising to $/€12 at the top end. From the outside, the game comes across as quite amiable; beneath the surface, you'll find a cold-hearted math model Microgaming rates as very highly volatile. It might look causal friendly, but this thing can fire off runs of dead spins or pop its clogs at any moment. Potential is huge too, a veritable Santa's Sack of goodies lies in wait good boys and girls, lucky ones at least. RTP is probably the biggest let down. It's not a reindeer hoof to the face, but 95.07% seems unnecessarily low without a jackpot in sight, yet sort of expected given the current development in the industry with increased regulation. On the bright side, Microgaming remains a transparent provider and has not introduced flexible RTP as many of its competitors have.The low end of the paytable consists of J-A royals, all puffy white like snowmen, followed by the four elves of the tale. They come in blue, green, orange, and yellow suits where 5 of a kind is worth 5x to 8.33x the stake. A line of 5 wreath wilds is worth double the top premium, only trumped by the scatter as the most valuable symbol. Wilds land anywhere to replace regular pays to make a winning combination.A Tale of Elves: Slot FeaturesA Tale of Elves - bonus options screenA Tale of Elves might not seem the most generous at first, stashing just two features into your stocking. They are quite useful though, well free spins can be; scatter awards aren't quite so rewarding. They do help break up the base game monotony though.Jolly old Santa is the scatter, landing anywhere on the reels - 2 of the stout chap in view triggers the Random Cash Prize feature. When activated, the game picks a random cash prize of up to 50x the bet for the trouble. This one's pretty frequent, landing once every 19 spins on average.The plum in the pudding is free spins. To trigger them, at least 3 Santas need to be in view. When they are, 3, 4, or 5 Santas equates to a top-up payout of 1x, 20x, or 200x the stake, plus access to the free spins feature. Here players get to choose from four options, offering a variety of spins, win multipliers, stacked symbols, and ultimately, volatility to suit:Blue Elf Spins offers 18 free spins with an x2 win multiplier where the Blue Elf appears stacked 6 symbols high.Green Elf Spins offers 14 free spins with an x3 win multiplier where the Green Elf appears stacked 5 symbols high.Orange Elf Spins offers 10 free spins with an x4 win multiplier where the Orange Elf appears stacked 4 symbols high.Yellow Elf Spins offers 8 free spins with an x5 win multiplier where the Yellow Elf appears stacked 3 symbols high.The Random Cash Prize remains in play during free spins, so it's possible to keep picking up those one-off wins here and there. It's also possible to retrigger free spins when 3 or more scatters land, re-adding the same option that was originally selected. As you'd imagine, free spins will take a bit more time to hit, theoretically triggering every 209 spins.A Tale of Elves: Slot VerdictAt first, it might be easy to write A Tale of Elves off without giving it a second glance. It's so in theme it kind of feels like a blatant Christmas cash-in, yet there is more going on here than you might think. It's not a slot that leans on the envelope, about to burst forth with mind-altering innovations, at all.This is the sort of classic Microgaming action that made the studio so incredibly popular back in the days and that is sure to bring joy to many veteran gamers. In a way, A Tale of Elves is a bit of a Christmas gift to the generation of players who were around to experience the release of iconic slots such as Jurassic Park, Immortal Romance, Bust The Bank, Fish Party, Game of Thrones, and all those other fantastic 243 ways games that still hold up today.When it comes to volatility, A Tale of Two Elves certainly lives up to its rating, being unpredictably all over the place. One minute it's draining balances like a thirsty reindeer, the next it's linking up high-value symbols with wild stacks and multipliers for eyebrow-raising results. Having four free spins options broadens the appeal by allowing volatility to be influenced to an extent. It's also the same one seen in Game of Thrones, which proved popular. Being retriggerable is another sweetener, leading to potential of up to 20,166 times the stake. To hit that cap you would need to land a full screen of wilds/yellow helpers twice during the bonus (8.33x243x5=10,120x) - not impossible, but don't expect it to happen anytime soon either.If you want an uncomplicated Christmas game that’s unashamedly seasonal A Tale of Elves is definitely worth a look. For something to settle into on a cold winter's night, while the snow is drifting in, the winds are howling, and you're toasty warm by a roaring fire, it could be worse.

title: Fruit Shop Megaways
structured_summary: Fruit Shop Megaways revamps the classic fruit-themed slot with a lively market stall setting. It features a 6-reel Megaways system, free spins triggered by fruit wins, and a win multiplier up to x10. The reviewer finds it a playable, entertaining upgrade with higher volatility but notes it can feel repetitive without cascades. Aesthetics remain bright and simple, retaining original sounds for a clean, faithful vibe.
review: Fruit Shop Megaways: Slot OverviewApologies for the awful pun, but NetEnt’s acquisition of Red Tiger and the associated Megaways license continues to bear fruit. Case in point, and proving no classic slot in the NetEnt back catalogue is safe from an upgrade; the fruity-tastic game Fruit Shop has received a Megaways upgrade. The original was renowned for basic, straight-forward gaming, nevertheless, its clever free spin feature made it hard to put down. NetEnt has captured all of that while expanding just about every other aspect of the game – not just the reel setup.The view certainly is a familiar one when Fruit Shop Megaways loads up. The 6 reel Megaways powered grid is located in a market stall, backgrounded by plenty of lush plant life and clear blue skies. It’s the very picture of simplicity, matching the gameplay to a tee. As well as the look, many of the sound effects have been retained, including the music. It all produces a nice, clean vibe, evidence of NetEnt staying faithful to the charm of the first one which saw the light of day back in 2013.After admiring the view, bets can be set from 20 p/c up to $/€100 per spin. As to math model, Megaways has brought with it its tendency to ramp just about everything up, including volatility which moves to a slightly higher setting than before. RTP is one area that has not increased, unfortunately, dropping a few points to the still respectable value of 96.06%, so more or less average. Max win has increased as you’d expect, while the already highly playable nature gets a healthy boost of Megaways magic.Landing a win requires three or more matching symbols, sitting adjacently, from the leftmost reel. This does not apply to the highest paying symbol, the cherries, as these snacks need only two or more to pay. NetEnt has split the 10 pay symbols into two groups. One is the low pay 10-A royals which have kept their puffy blue design; the other is the medium pay fruits. In this latter group are watermelons, oranges, lemons, plums, and the aforementioned cherries. Rewards in the mid pay fruit group are worth 1.5 to 12.5 times the stake for a six of a kind win.Fans of cascade features will be disappointed to see they are not part of Fruit Shop Megaways this time around. With the way free spins are triggered, it would have been mayhem so they have been dropped. There is a wild though, landing on reels 2, 3, 4, or 5 in the main game or in free spins. The wild substitutes for all symbols.Fruit Shop Megaways: Slot FeaturesThe original Fruit Shop was a lesson in compelling simplicity and captivating flow and rhythm - the Megaways redo is no different. If anything, it’s even harder to put down. What makes it so are free spins which often trigger, albeit in reduced numbers.Every fruit symbol win triggers free spins. The amount awarded depends on the symbol and the length of the combination. Any medium win combo of 3, 4, 5, or 6 symbol length awards 2, 3, 4, or 5 free spins respectively. One exception to the rule is the cherries which dole out 1 free spin for a two of a kind win.This mechanic is available during free spins as well, the difference being that low pay symbol wins now award free spins too. So, 3, 4, 5, or 6 length low pay wins add 1, 2, 3, or 4 more spins to the amount. The second addition to free spins is a win multiplier. As usual, it starts at x1, and increases by 1 following every winning spin. The maximum value the multiplier can reach is x10.Fruit Shop Megaways: Slot VerdictFruit Shop slips effortlessly into Megaways mode as if it was born to do so. The free spins feature suits the format and produces some pretty keen gaming. If you haven’t spun the first one, just how playable the game is might not be overly apparent. However, score a few free spins retriggers and you can see the potential. It gets some nice lengthy rolls on but would have been deadly with a cascades feature on board as well. You can see why it was omitted, but the exclusion does hold back the base game somewhat.A potential issue when re-releasing older slots with modern makeovers is that the point can be lost on those who weren’t there the first time around. In some ways, if you haven’t played and enjoyed the original Fruit Shop, it might not be so easy to catch the Megaways version’s charm. It does get quite repetitive if you’re stuck in a patch of base game spins, or muddling free spins that fail to spark. There is nothing else to look forward to if the basic rules don’t grab your interest. Like most Megaways game’s Fruit Shop Megaways can fire when it wants to, but when it doesn’t, some may quickly lose motivation. Rewards are there for the perseverant, or lucky, where max wins can reach as high as 10,000 times the stake. Just hope the stall is serving up plenty of free spins/multiplier dual action to get close to hitting it though.For players who remember the original fondly, there is no reason the Megaways upgrade won’t blow their hair back. Volatility is up, potential is up, and Megaways lends its exciting predictableness to the whole show. Fruit Shop Megaways does teeter on being a little overly repetitious at times, and for many, it won’t be a game to return to soon after an experimental crack. Yet, if that’s not an issue, or for a trip back to an earlier era, then the cheerful, fruity gaming is bound to entertain.

title: Crystal Robot
structured_summary: Crystal Robot combines a futuristic robot theme with a mysterious crystal mining backdrop. The game features a 5x5 grid, wild reels with multipliers, two distinct free spin modes, and bonus buy options offering varied gameplay intensity. The reviewer finds it reliable and solid, praising its effective mechanics though noting a lack of groundbreaking innovation. Visually, the slot presents a charming robot world with a cool, mechanical atmosphere complemented by fitting audio elements.
review: Crystal Robot: Slot OverviewBack in the day, robots were looked on favourably for their ability to manufacture cars, do repetitive stuff people don't want to do, and maybe one day even enforce the law, aka Robocop (1987). Now, with the rise and rise of AI, a question mark has arisen. Will robots one day achieve sentience, realise they're better off without us organics and transform the Terminator films from an exhilarating popcorn movie franchise into a full-blown prophecy? They land with a multiplier of x2 to x100, which is taken from the symbol and added to the Global Multiplier. A 5 wild winning line pays 25x the bet.Crystal Robot: Slot FeaturesCrystal Robot slot - free spinsRolling off the production line are Crystal Robot's features, including wild reels, a global multiplier, Rampage free spins, Overclocked free spins, and bonus buys.Wild Reels & Global MultiplierWhen the Mystery symbol lands on the reels, it expands into a wild reel and adds an x2 to x100 multiplier to the global multiplier. The global multiplier is present in all game modes and multiplies all wins on the reels. In the two bonus games, the global multiplier is persistent for the full duration.Free SpinsRampage - Hitting 3 robot head scatters in the base game triggers 10 free spins in the Rampage bonus. In this feature, Mystery symbols do not land, but all wilds become sticky for the remainder of the round.Overclocked - Overclocked is triggered by landing 3 robot hand scatters in the base game. Players get 10 free spins and an increased chance of landing Mystery symbols. The global multiplier is persistent for the whole round.Bonus BuyAt the bonus buy, players may activate BonusHunt FeatureSpins for 2x the bet, where each spin is 3 times more likely to trigger free spins. Teardown FeatureSpins may be had for 75x the bet to guarantee that 2+ Mystery symbols land on each spin. From there, the Rampage bonus may be bought for 100x or Overclocked for 200x.Crystal Robot slot - free spinsCrystal Robot: Slot VerdictThe characters in Crystal Robot might have achieved some level of sentience, maybe not, but they don't seem like the type that want to overthrow their organic overlords and create a mechanical utopia on earth for their transistor brethren. They're more like Bumblebee from the Transformers, a cheerful buddy to the humans. However, the slot these two chaps inhabit is all business. Backseat Gaming has filled it with features that don't push a lot of innovative boundaries, yet each constituent part is a rock-steady component that can lock bits in place to ratchet up the potency and slam out a solid result.When the going's good, of course, keeping in mind Crystal Robot is no broken ATM machine, after all. It has no problems churning out bundles of x2s or maybe x3s on its wilds, which aren't as helpful as they could be. But, wild symbols also theoretically bandy about values of up to x100, and the global multiplier can grow quite nicely in its persistent state during free spins. The mechanics are very Hacksaw Gaming-ish, which has a fame for injecting similar sorts of features into its slots. Backseat Gaming has clearly been paying attention because it has made a game that stands up quite well when compared to its more established daddy studio's impressive portfolio.Top Crystal Robot off with a maximum win of 12,500x that can hit in any game mode, and there's a lot to like. As mentioned, not a whole lot here is super innovative feature-wise. But, it's hard to begrudge the mechanics the game does possess due to their simple, straightforward potential effectiveness. A charming robot theme sweetens the experience and helps punters take their minds off possible distant futures where we've all been reduced to batteries to power a planet-wide reactor.

title: Hand of Anubis
structured_summary: Hand of Anubis is a dark, brooding Ancient Egyptian-themed slot featuring the god Anubis with a heavy, foreboding atmosphere. The game offers cluster pays, two unique bonus rounds—Underworld and Judgement—with extensive multiplier mechanics and feature buy options. The reviewer praises its creative, intense gameplay and rich atmosphere, highlighting its potential for huge wins despite high volatility. Visually, it uses a dark palette with steely-eyed jackal deities and a sinister setting, complemented by an eerie audio backdrop enhancing the immersive experience.
review: Hand of Anubis: Slot OverviewIt's interesting, a lot of the time, the Ancient Egyptian god Anubis is presented in a benevolent fashion. In slots, for example, Anubis is often found in his jackal statue form. That can't have been edgy enough for developer Hacksaw Gaming which has chosen a completely different way of using the god in their online slot, Hand of Anubis. That is some awesome power and responsibility right there since eternity is a really long time.Players picking Hand of Anubis might wonder if the weight of their deeds have come up short because the jackal-headed god does not look overly pleased in this game. On one side of the grid stands a steely blue-eyed jackal-headed deity, while an equally steely red-eyed one stands on the other side. Hacksaw has used a very dark palette throughout the whole game, and whilst there's a pyramid in the background, Hand of Anubis is the very antithesis of what Egypt themed games usually look like. There's a Stakelogic's Gods of Death meets ELK's Cygnus, meets ripped jackal sort of thing going on. It's heavy, foreboding, and perhaps not for the faint-hearted Egypt fan.The game's layout is also vaguely reminiscent of ELK too, as each spin sees 30 symbols tumble into a 5-column, 6-row panel, with the goal of landing clusters of at least 5 adjoining matching symbols. Volatility has been rated 5 out of 5, and in a Hacksaw slot, that's no joking matter. Check for RTP, as it comes in four settings, topping out at 96.24%, alongside a hit frequency of 36.92%. Bet levels can be found as low as 10 p/c before going as high as $/€100 per paid drop, while any device may be used to host the action.To build clusters, players are equipped with ten normal tiles to do so. 10-A card ranks are provided on the lower side of the paytable, with five golden jewelled Egyptian style tokens as the highs. Entry-level wins made up of 5 low symbols are worth 0.1x the bet, up to 15x the bet for 11+ symbols. Landing 5 high pays will get you 0.3-1x the stake, up to 11+ sized premium clusters worth 20-60 times your stake.Hand of Anubis: Slot FeaturesFeatures in Hand of Anubis include Soul Orbs, an Underworld bonus game, a Judgement bonus game, and feature buy options.Soul OrbsIn the base game, there is a chance a red Soul Orb, a blue Soul Orb, or both may randomly hit. Orbs are wild symbols with progressive multipliers. The red Soul Orb's multiplier increases by +1 for every symbol in each winning cluster, while the blue Soul Orb's multiplier increases by +1 per winning cluster. Multipliers are applied to any win the Orbs are part of, and they multiply each other if more than one is involved in a win.UnderworldLanding exactly 3 bonus symbols activates the Underworld bonus round which takes place in an even more wicked-looking place than the base game. The first thing to note is five numbers located below the grid; each is a multiplier starting on zero. Whenever a winning cluster hits, the number of winning symbols on each reel is added to the corresponding multiplier below it. Also, Anubis Skull symbols can land; when they do, they multiply the number below them by x2, x3, x4, x5, or x10. However, these lower multiplier values are inactive at first and need a green Soul Orb to land above them on a corresponding reel to activate. Each time a number is activated, +3 spins are awarded. Just as importantly, if not more so, the sum of all active multipliers is applied to winning clusters. The max value of each multiplier is x9,999.Hand of Anubis - Underworld bonusJudgementLanding 4 bonus symbols triggers Judgement. In this game, regular symbols are removed, and only blank blocks or special blocks land. This hold & win round starts with 3 spins with multipliers above each reel (similar in fashion to Chaos Crew). Now, when Multiplier Modifier Blocks land, they increase the multiplier above them. There are four types:Skulls increase the value directly above them by +1-100.Epic Skulls add +1-100 to all multipliers.Anubis Skulls multiply the value above them by x2-x10.Epic Anubis Skulls multiply all values by x2 to x10.When an Ice Block drops, it disappears, and a Multiplier Block fills the empty space, taking the value of the multiplier above it. At the end of a spin, Multiplier Blocks stack at the bottom of the grid while blank blocks are removed. Then the next drop occurs. Moreover, Crusher blocks may land, smashing Multiplier Blocks beneath them and collating their values into one block. Crushers also reset the spin count to 3. Three consecutive spins without landing a Multiplier Block, Multiplier Modifier Block, or Crusher ends the bonus.Bonus BuyWhere possible, players can use the feature buy button to buy their way strong into the Underworld bonus for 129x the bet (RTP 96.29%) or Judgement for 200x the bet (RTP 96.18%).Hand of Anubis - Judgment bonusHand of Anubis: Slot VerdictYou have to admire Hacksaw Gaming's creative spirit. There might be as many Egyptian themed slots as there are grains in a handful of desert sand, but none are like Hand of Anubis. The studio has done away with all the flash, golden, physical slot trim that often accompanies these sorts of games, and there's not a single expanding symbol in sight. Well, it's a cluster pays game, but you get the point. Hacksaw once again proves they are masters of designing dark, brooding slots, which are a joy to lose yourself in.They are also masters of the sort of frighteningly good features you find in Hand of Anubis, and it's hard to think of another game we used the word 'multiplier' so extensively in a review for. Multipliers are extensively used in Hand of Anubis during all phases of play. Obviously, much more in bonus rounds, and our very first Underworld trigger was an excellent example of the sort of magic they can perform when an x500+ multiplier was produced. Fortunately, several green Soul Orbs had activated their values meaning they could be used to boost wins. One can only imagine the torment of building huge multipliers only to have them locked until the feature ended.Perhaps that positive first result clouded our judgement, but Underworld did tend to be more nail-biting than Judgement. As it is, there's little doubt this is a game capable of pummelling its 10,000x win cap.And so, Hand of Anubis is another monster of a game from Hacksaw. Make no mistake, Hand of Anubis can punish unsuspecting players with remorseless brutality, but it's also got the goods to produce some truly heroic moments as well.

title: Raging Riches
structured_summary: Raging Riches is a prairie-themed slot blending classic Americana with modern slot mechanics.
