Land 3, 4, or 5 scatters to be rewarded with 7, 9 or 12 free spins respectively. During Reanimated Free Spins, whenever a Vampire Wild lands, it acts as it was described in the previous paragraph. Vampire Wilds also have the added benefit of sticking in position for the full duration of the feature. On each new spin, Vampire Wilds leap to a new position to conduct its transformation abilities.Also, on any free spin, it is possible for 3-9 Talisman Wild symbols to appear on reels 1 to 4. Talisman Wilds substitute for regular pay symbols, but it is also sticky, so they remain in the feature until free spins are gone. The last piece of good news, every Vampire Wild or Talisman wild that lands awards one extra free spin.Vampire Senpai: VerdictQuickspin has done a decent job here in a slot that ticks most of the right boxes. Yes, Vampire Senpai is Asian themed, but far from being a cliché. The game reveals a different facet of Asian culture than we usually see, which makes a refreshing change.Players get a darker side of the culture, but the way it’s been presented completely tempers what could have a little creepy, and the cartoon visuals mesh perfectly with all the popping transformative fun going on. In that regard, Vampire Senpai also reminiscent of Quickspin grid slots like Wild Cauldron thanks to all of those cutie pie characters populating the game.The icing on the cake from a gamblers standpoint is potential weighing in at 8,800 times the bet. An impressive total to be sure, though when browsing the big win forums, there aren't exactly volumes of hits to admire that are close to the advertised max wins.Now to the downsides. The 5x5, 40-payline setup is not the most exciting and makes little sense. It's not a grid slot, so it doesn't really benefit from such a large game area - on the contrary. There's also something about Vampire Senpai that makes it come across as somewhat generic. It could be the Asian theme, after all, but a large game area populated mostly by low pays just looks incredibly dull.Some might find Vampire Senpai too simplistic, perhaps, and the base game is not exactly intoxicating. Thankfully, it comes with a free spins feature that sort of makes up for its weaknesses. Chains of transforming wilds can get their fangs in and be pretty infectious. Add in Vampire Senpai’s good-time vibe, unusual subject matter, plus decent potential, and you’ve got a nicely playable slot to crack."

title: Fishin' For Gold
structured_summary: Fishin' For Gold is an ice fishing-themed slot set on frozen waters with a cozy yet chilly vibe. It features a 5x3 reel layout, a Bonus Chance Meter triggering free spins with wilds and multipliers, plus collectible symbols for extra spins. The reviewer finds gameplay slow with many inactive spins, requiring patience before the bonus round livens things up. The game sports bright, cartoonish visuals and upbeat music that add warmth to its icy setting.
review: 5.5,"Fishin’ For Gold (iSoftBet): OverviewIt there is one universal pastime it just might be fishing. Anglers across the globe feel the primal urge to bait up and cast off in hopes of landing the big one. In a way, it’s similar to playing slots, and there are quite a few fishing themed games floating around. Not many take place on the ice though which is where iSoftBet's latest is set. If you are one of those people that don't get the lure of fishing, then ice fishing must seem the strangest variant of all. It involves sitting for hours in the freezing cold, hoping that a fish will come along and bite. Fishin' For Gold gives players the chance for some icy angling action from the warm and cosy comfort of their device.The recent batch of slots from iSoftBet have used a mix of conventional and unorthodox setups. Fishin' For Gold is a more traditional take, however, that uses 5 reels, 3 rows, and 25 fixed paylines. Visually, it has a cartoon feel with bright colours and great design. The backdrop of this icy world is populated by a mash up of creatures from both hemispheres whilst the music is unbelievably jolly - this combines with the cute characters to add a bit of warmth to the icy theme. Players bait up each spin with bets ranging from 25 p/c to $/€25 each by selecting appropriate coin values. The base game is super straight forward - match three or more symbols on a payline for a win, with no wilds on hand to help out.The 8 symbols that fill out the paytable are like night and day. On one hand are uninspiring J – A royals that are completely devoid of personality. The high pays are more interesting and include a classic old boot that every cartoon character reels in when they are fishing. Next is a bucket of fish, a southern penguin, and a northern polar bear. The polar bear is worth the most at 40 times the stake for five on a payline. As mentioned before, there are no wilds during the base game, but they do appear later in the bonus round to spice things up.At the time of writing, many of the key stats were not officially available. The boffins with their slide rulers are still calculating the RTP which currently sits in TBC status. Going by iSoftBet's recent releases, it is likely to turn out to be something in the 95% - 97% range. Volatility is also not officially confirmed yet either, but test runs were brutal, so a high(ish) rating is certainly on the cards. Often the cutest looking slots ends up being a rough ride and Fishin For Gold reaffirmed that concept. Like real fishing, there is a lot of hanging around not doing much. In this case, it means a fair number of dead spins where a wild might have helped tie players over till the bonus game is unlocked.Fishin’ For Gold (iSoftBet): FeaturesBonus game in actionDuring the base game, an extra bump of excitement comes from the Bonus Symbol. When exactly 2 of these fishy icons land, they are added to the Bonus Chance Meter that sits above the reels. The meter is divided into 100 red parts to start with, and each pair of Bonus Symbol turns one of those parts green. Players can activate the meter at any time, which costs 1x the current bet. It spins a needle, and if it lands on the green area, then the Bonus Game is triggered. If the needle lands in the red there is no Bonus Game and the meter is reset back to its starting level.Alternatively, if three Bonus Symbols land, they automatically trigger the Fishin' For Gold Bonus. This game starts by allowing you to choose one of four keen animal anglers – a polar bear, penguin, walrus, and a grumpy looking lion. Each one sits over a hole in the ice with a pole and pulls in their catch. Each fish they pull in is worth a free spin, and each symbol pulled up adds a wild. Some wilds can even come with multipliers of x2, x3, or x5 attached to them. What helps is that when more than one multiplier is part of a combination their values are added for better results.During free spins, one more symbol appears on the reels. This is the Gone Fishing symbol which players collect when they appear. Every time three of these symbols are collected they add 2 more free spins to the pile.Fishin’ For Gold (iSoftBet): VerdictLike its physical counterpart there can be a lot of downtime doing nothing with Fishin’ For Gold. And just like real fishing, there will be some people who are quite content with waiting around for the big one to bite. It’s unlikely too many players have the desire to sit through so many dead spins, and low action spins before something exciting happens though. Not to mention the amount of time it takes to rack up a decent number on the Bonus Chance Meter. After a quiet patch, it is hard not to hit the bonus button, even if only a few symbols have been collected. Needless to say, shed loads of luck is required for the needle to trigger the bonus round in that scenario.When the Bonus Round does come to life the game can improve. To stay with the metaphor, this is the moment a fisherman has finally hooked something and is battling to reel it in. With the introduction of wilds and multipliers, the game finally kicks it up a gear with a chance for quite decent rewards. Collect a few Gone Fishin’ symbols for extra spins, and things start looking up. Yet, it's all over soon enough, and it's back to sitting on a bucket by the ices’ edge, staring at a line in the water.In short, patience is not just a virtue but a requirement when it comes to playing Fishin' For Gold. Guards that stand outside royal palaces and aren't allowed to budge a muscle might be good candidates. They'd have the mental prep for setting up a bunch of auto spins and watching them tick by while they stand stock still. Most players want a bit more excitement than that though."

title: WaterBlox Gigablox
structured_summary: WaterBlox Gigablox immerses players in a mystical aquatic theme where forests meet fjords, featuring aquatic creatures and magical elements. The game highlights Gigablox oversized symbols, roaming wild respins, multipliers in free spins, and a buy bonus for enhanced gameplay. The reviewer praises its unique Peter & Sons artistry and engaging mechanics, deeming it a highly playable and visually captivating slot. Aesthetic design is intricate and whimsical, with detailed aquatic visuals and enchanting audio that complement the mystical atmosphere.
review: 2022",7.5,"Water Blox Gigablox: Slot OverviewCrafted in association with partner studio Yggdrasil, Water Blox is the second slot from designer Peter & Sons to use the flourishing Gigablox feature. The first one, Monster Blox, was an exquisite looking game that was so Peter & Sons it was easy to forget you were playing a Gigablox powered game. The follow-up, Water Blox, is no different, and along with Gigablox, delivers roaming wild respins, an increasing multiplier in free spins, all located in a land where the forests of Walarya meet blue water in fjord country.When dealing with a Peter & Sons release, 'crafted' is a more appropriate word than usual as their games have a distinct look which is utterly unique to the studio. Water Blox is a prime example and provides players with a bizarre (in a good way) almost mystical world, celebrating a piscine side of life. At the bottom of the screen is a lily pad laden pond, replete with a jumping fish, while more creatures living in or around water litter the 6x6, 50-payline game grid. Mystics and magic are popular Peter & Sons tropes, and we get one in Water Blox standing next to the game panel. Occasionally, he dons a fish suit, as if embodying the spirit of our aquatic brothers and sisters, to blast modifiers onto the reels. We've come to expect a bit of magic when we review a Peter & Sons game, and Water Blox did not disappoint.Stats don't disappoint either, and Water Blox's highly volatile math model produces a neatly average theoretical return value of 96%. Players can expect a win to hit 21.01% of the time, or roughly 1 in every five spins, occurring when at least three matching symbols land from the lefthand side on a payline. When it comes to bet selection, choices range from 20 p/c to $/€50 per spin.Players get 8 regular paying symbols in Water Blox. The 4 lower values are neatly designed spades, clubs, hearts, and diamonds, paying 0.8x the bet for a line of six. Then comes 4 premium animal symbols – frogs, pufferfish, purple fish, and a truly excellent octopus, paying 2 to 10 times the stake for six of a kind. The wild is represented by an angry gold coloured fish, which lands on any reel to replace all paying symbols. If a winning line made up of six wild symbols hits, it has the same value as the octopus, 10x the bet.Water Blox Gigablox: Slot FeaturesIn Water Blox, Yggdrasil's Gigablox feature shares the reels with roaming wilds, respins, Monster Free Spins, and a buy bonus.GigabloxGigablox are oversized symbols that can be anything from 2x2 to 6x6 in size. They can appear on any reel, and for win evaluations are split into their 1x1 sized tiles.Wild RespinsAt random in the base game, 1-3 symbols are changed into wild symbols. After any wins are awarded, a respin is triggered, where the wilds move to a random position. The number of roaming wilds depends on the size of the symbols transformed – 1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 4x4, 5x5, or 6x6 sized blocks create 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 wilds, respectively. During the respin, if a roaming wild lands on a big block, it converts the whole thing into a wild.Monster Free SpinsLanding at least 5 scatter symbols in the base game triggers free spins. The number awarded is equal to the number of scatters in view, and any scatter landing in the bonus round awards an additional free spin. The Wild Respin feature is active on every free spin, so 1-3 random symbols on the panel are changed into wilds, as described above. In addition, each wild symbol is collected, adding a point to a meter. When collecting 20, 45, 75, or 125 wilds, the win multiplier increases to x2, x3, x5, then x10. Also, at each collection level, +2 free spins are awarded. Keep in mind wilds from respins are not collected.Buy BonusIf available, players have access to three bonus buy options. Paying 58x the bet gets you 5 free spins, 580x for 20 free spins, or 140x the bet for a random number of free spins.Water Blox Gigablox: Slot VerdictWe were impressed by the look of Monster Blox, and Water Blox is not bad either. The game is chock full of the sort of intricate touches Peter & Sons are masters of and appear to be getting better at. The studio is adept at ramming a load of superb details into their slots to create something special, and Water Blox is an excellent example. Just feast your eyes on that octopus or the way the fish belted shaman pulls on his fish skin disguise. Water Blox's world is weird, in all the right ways, and is another P&S game which is easy to surrender yourself to. Ever read the children's book Where the Wild Things Are? Water Blox has a similar feel.So the visuals are nailed, how about the gameplay? For the most part, it's pretty decent too. Using Gigablox means the studio is straitjacketed, in a way, by the core rules governing the mechanic. Still, Gigablox can be thrilling in its own right, and roaming wilds is a clever feature to combine with it. They led to some nice moments in the base game when they transformed larger Gigablox tiles into wilds and even nicer moments in the bonus round.The chances of collecting big wins seriously improved when a greater number of initial free spins were awarded. You can say that about any game, but it was noticeable in Water Blox since it could take time to collect enough wilds to activate better multipliers. Starting with a low number of free spins generally made the task a lot more difficult. On the topic of potential, the game advertises wins of over 10,000x the bet, meaning solid wins are possible when your luck is in.Ultimately, how you view the Gigablox feature will be a strong determinant of your overall enjoyment of Water Blox. In the end, it's an attractive P&S stamped entry, and the use of roaming wild respins makes it a highly playable addition to the Gigablox family of slots."

title: Parthenon Quest For Immortality
structured_summary: Parthenon Quest for Immortality is an Ancient Greek-themed slot inspired by classical culture and mythology. It features a 6-reel layout with wild generations, avalanches, multipliers, and a free spins round with increasing multipliers. The reviewer finds it a distinctive, enjoyable game for Grecophiles, though free spins can be slow to trigger and payouts moderate. The game boasts airy, classical visuals with statues and temples, complemented by a fitting light, thematic audio atmosphere.
review: Out Now,7,"Parthenon Quest for Immortality: Slot OverviewParthenon Quest for Immortality builds on a previous NetEnt Egyptian-themed slot titled Pyramid Quest for Immortality, with both games following similar lines. As well as focusing on a long-lost culture in the midst of their golden age, the two games use features such as wild generations, avalanches, and multipliers. Parthenon Quest for Immortality ups the stakes by piling on more of everything while tacking on a round of free spins for good measure.NetEnt raises an interesting question in connection with Parthenon Quest for Immortality – would we have had a god of slots if they had been around in Ancient Greek times? There is a good chance. Dionysus was famously the god of wine, and most of the rest were passionately portrayed in the classics, after all. Then again, can you imagine the torrent of lightning bolts being tossed around if someone in Olympus was on a losing streak?Returning to the task at hand in the mortal realms, we find a 6-reel grid laid out in 4-5-5-5-5-4 formation. The upper 4-position row is called the Wild Generation Zone, which functions in the same way as Pyramid Quest for Immortality’s did. This might sound odd, but there is no other way of saying the game has a very Greek feel about it. Statues, temples, angular fonts, all contribute, as well as a light, airy presentation evoking the Classical Age. NetEnt used a similar approach in Rome The Golden Age, making the two slots relatives of sorts.With 10,000 ways to win, winning combinations are made up of three or more matching symbols landing adjacently from the leftmost reel in any row. Each win triggers an avalanche which removes the winning symbols allowing new or existing symbols to drop into the gaps. The avalanche feature keeps the process going until no new wins appear.Symbols are in keeping with the Hellenic spirit, which start with 10-A card symbols, then there are tridents, snakes, Pegasus, triremes, and snake-haired Medusa. Medusa offers good value at up 40x the bet for 6 of a kind, dropping to 2.5x at the most for the other premiums. Wilds play a central role in the action, substituting for any symbol except free spin scatters. Wilds have no value of their own and may land in any position or be created in the Wild Generation Zone.Parthenon Quest for Immortality: Slot FeaturesParthenon Quest For Immortality - free spinsUnlike Pyramid Quest for Immortality, this version comes with a round of free spins, offering the best chance of making some serious cash. As well as this new feature, Parthenon Quest for Immortality uses the same wild creation device players benefited from in the Pyramid game.How it works is if symbols on the top row are used in a win, instead of dropping random symbols into the newly formed spaces, they are turned into wild symbols. If these wild symbols are used in a subsequent win, they are removed as normal - they are not sticky or persistent or anything like that.The next feature is free spins, triggered when 3 or more scatter symbols are in view after an avalanche sequence - 3 scatters gets you 8 free spins, while each extra scatter adds +4 free spins. When the bonus round is active, collecting 3 collection symbols awards +2 more free spins. The main benefit here is the Free Spins Multiplier feature. It starts at x1 and increases by 1 whenever a symbol is transformed into a wild, as described above. The Free Spins Multiplier has an upper limit of x20.Parthenon Quest for Immortality: Slot VerdictThere’s a good chance Grecophiles will be effortlessly drawn to Parthenon Quest for Immortality’s dreamy, classical vibe. There is no end of Greek-themed slots, but NetEnt has given their game a look that stands out, to a degree, from the bunch. Mechanically it’s a bit different as well, so players who dig the style won’t be disappointed by what Parthenon Quest for Immortality delivers.The gameplay isn’t bad either, though it should be mentioned that free spins can often take ages to trigger while the balance just seems to go up and down, leaving you with a feeling of not getting anywhere. The official hit rate figures were not available, yet it seemed wins occurred more often than they did in Pyramid Quest for Immortality. Perhaps because the avalanche multiplier feature was dropped, the game is able to loosen up when it comes to generating regular wins.It is still possible to line up a stack of consecutive hits with the help of the Wild Generation Zone. Amusing situations during testing occurred when wilds on reels 2 and 3 kept connecting with reel 1 over and over again. In spite of the long win sequences, payouts tended to max out at around a rather disappointing 50x the bet in these cases, yet there is no technical reason why they couldn’t be much higher. Especially so in free spins since firing up the Wild Generation Zone also brings multipliers into play.To conclude, Parthenon Quest for Immortality does enough to give it a measure of individuality. Maybe if NetEnt had included one extra minor modifier in the base game it would help offset the feeling of repetition, which occasionally sets in - though a good run of avalanches can do a decent enough job on its own. Add it all up, and Parthenon Quest for Immortality is a fairly decent addition to the persistently popular Ancient Greek lineup. Now that we’ve had Egypt and Greece, anyone taking bets the next Quest for Immortality is Viking or Irish based?"

title: Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws
structured_summary: Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws is a Wild West-themed slot featuring outlaw characters and a dusty frontier town setting. The game offers 'book of' style expanding symbols, scatter-triggered free spins, and a unique Super Spins bonus on multiple grids. The reviewer finds it entertaining with decent rewards and engaging variations on familiar mechanics. The slot boasts classic Western visuals and atmospheric audio that enhance its rugged, lawless vibe.
review: 2021",7,"Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws: Slot OverviewWelcome pardner to the good ole Wild West, again, for a video slot from iSoftBet called Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws, a real saddlebag of familiar visuals and features culled from all over the place, mixed together and given an individual touch to produce something new - relatively speaking. It's also an addition to iSoftBet's Xtreme Pays Series, a line of games the developer has designed to be 'higher than normal in volatility with the chance to win bigger.' Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws doesn't exactly offer enormous rewards, but respectable all the same. To win them, you'll have to harness its 'book of' style mechanic, available in the base game and its various free spin bonus rounds.As well as familiar features, Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws has a look that brings to mind NetEnt's classic Wild West games Dead or Alive, or its sequel, pick a favourite. A 5-reel, 10-payline game grid has been built into a creaky, bullet hole-ridden wooden structure in the middle of a dusty, lawless looking settlement that could be anywhere from Oklahoma to California. Wherever we are, it looks like the sort of place where smoke rises from the countertop when the bar person accidentally spills liquor when pouring it.Playable on any device, users may set stakes starting at 10 p/c per spin, rising to $/€10 per spin for the higher rolling gunslingers. Since this is an Xtreme Pays slot, the volatility is high, while the default theoretical return value is 96%. Roughly one in four spins produces a win (20.4%) on average, occurring when at least three matching symbols land adjacently across one of the game's 10 fixed paylines.Landing on the reels is nine paying symbols; five of them are 10-A card rank icons, and four of them outlaws. Van Der Wilde is the most valuable at a hefty 250x the stake for five of a kind, while below him are Bonney Cassidy, Buffalo Butch, and Mad Dog – worth 10 to 50 times the stake. If there's one thing we know about the West, it's to steer clear of people called Mad Dog. The only other symbol appearing on the reels is a wild/scatter.Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws: Slot FeaturesVan Der Wilde & The Outlaws - free spinsThe features in Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws have a definite 'book of' feel, but iSoftBet has made numerous rule adjustments to novelise them. The 'Outlaws' symbol is both scatter and wild. As the wild, it replaces any other symbol to form winning combinations. Any win with the scatter wild symbol causes the expanding wins feature. When triggered, the initial win is paid, then any of the symbols forming the win, except wilds, expand to cover all positions on the reel and a new win evaluation is made. This includes the initial win line again. If more than one symbol type formed an initial winning combination, then the symbols expand one after the other. Expanding wins pay left to right, only on connecting paylines, from the leftmost reel.Landing 3 or more scatter symbols anywhere on the reels triggers free games. Next, a reel spins to award Van der Wilde, Bonney Cassidy, Buffalo Butch or Mad Dog Free Spins. Winning one of these bonuses awards 8 free spins and turns the respective character symbol into a Super Symbol. Super Symbols always expand if they form a winning line; they do not need to involve wilds. Moreover, 3+ scatters in view retriggers +8 free spins, keeping the current Super Symbol as was initially awarded.Alternatively, when spinning the reel after winning free games, instead of getting one of the characters, you may win Super Free Spins instead. This bonus awards 5 Super Spins played on 4 simultaneously spinning game grids. Each grid has one of the character symbols transformed into a Super Symbol. This bonus game can be retriggered as well when at least 3 scatters symbols hit.Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws: Slot VerdictAdd up Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws' various parts, and you've got a pretty entertaining slot on your hands. The features have been altered enough to make them interesting, and they can produce decent results when combined with a helping of luck. The Wild West theme brings such great visuals and music that half the job of design is practically done for you, yet iSoftBet has made an attractive game regardless, even if it similar to several others out there.Moving on to gameplay, where there are subtle differences between this and standard 'book of' expanding symbols. In Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws, two big ones are that expanding symbols must be adjacent to each other on a payline, and must start from the leftmost reel to win. There's no landing expanding symbols on reels 2, 4 and 5 to receive a payout like you would in a conventional book game. Also, let's say you've got expanding symbols on reels 1 and 3 and a wild on the bottom row of reel 2. You're only rewarded for wins running through paylines connected by the wild since it does not expand.Landing three scatters wasn't a particularly rare occurrence, yet they almost always ended up triggering one of the outlaw free spins. Super Spins, by comparison, were not easy to win. Being the game's main attraction, this is presumably where the best chance of cracking the game's potential is, which happens to be 8,000x the bet. You might have been expecting more since Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws is an Xtreme Pays slot, but 8k is more than your typical book game coughs up.If you break Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws into its constituent components, each one does feel quite familiar. Put them all together, though, and well, they still have that familiar feel to them. Even so, the game's got a fun Western attitude, and the features are good enough to entice fans of expanding symbols, making Van Der Wilde & The Outlaws worth a look to see what it's made of."

title: Candy Island Princess
structured_summary: Candy Island Princess is an anime-themed slot set on a tropical island, featuring a candy contest with three cartoon female contestants. Key features include Candy Splash expanding wins, Behind the Scenes instant cash prizes, Lucky Respins, free spins with retriggers, and a post-spin multiplier choice. The reviewer sees it as a light, low-volatility game aimed at anime fans, offering modest wins and a relaxed vibe rather than big payouts. The game sports bright, playful cartoon visuals and upbeat audio that complement its sunny, carefree atmosphere.
review: 0.05/100,"June 3, 2021",5.5,"Candy Island Princess: Slot OverviewConsidering how huge anime is, it's a wonder there aren't more slots based around the cultural phenomenon. Possibly the fact online casinos are illegal in Japan, the homeland of anime, has dented game developers' enthusiasm for exploring the theme. One studio that hasn't shied away is Play'n GO, known for having released quite possibly the biggest anime-themed slot to date, Moon Princess. The team is back with more charismatic cartoon females in Candy Island Princess, a slot sure to excite its target audience while leaving others a little bemused.The game's story will reinforce the division. Three contestants have been flown to an exotic island to show off their 'talents'. Bon Bon, the host, leads the event to find a new candy girl queen in a showdown that's either a ball of laughs or bizarre cartoon lady exploitation. The gameplay is pretty light all around, with a low to medium volatile math model matching the rest of the game's attitude. As always, RTP is variable, so be on the lookout for different values. The highest possible theoretical return in this case is 96.2%, dropping to 94.2% or less depending on the market.Three-of-a-kind wins are the only ones possible in Candy Island Princess, where 7 symbols make up the paytable. The first 4 are lower-paying candy symbols shaped like hearts, diamonds, flowers, or circles, while the 3 high pays are the three female contestants. The ladies are worth payouts of 2 to 6 times the stake when pure combinations land, or 1 times the stake for three mixed high pay symbols. The game does not use wild symbols, relying on two scatter types to provide more impressive winning possibilities.Candy Island Princess: Slot FeaturesThe features in Candy Island Princess revolve around a ticket scatter, a camera scatter and builds on its three contestant symbols. The Candy Splash feature triggers every time a three-of-a-kind win occurs using contestant symbols - the specific contestant symbols expand to pay out on all 5 paylines. These winning combinations must be of one contestant type since a mixed contestant symbol win will not trigger the Candy Splash feature.Camera scatters land anywhere, and 3 in view triggers the Behind the Scenes feature. Here you can score 1 of 6 instant wins paying out a cash prize of 5x, 10x, 20x, 80x, 500, or 2,000x your bet.Also, keep an eye out for the ticket scatters; landing 2 of them triggers a Lucky Respin, where the reel not showing a ticket scatter is respun for another chance to land all 3 scatters. When 3 scatters are in view on the reels, free spins are awarded. What changes for free spins is the Candy Splash feature is activated when winning combinations made up of mixed contestant symbols hit. On the final free spin, ticket scatters are added to the reels, and the feature can be retriggered up to 5 times.When free spins conclude, the Jelly Jiggle Delight takes place. Here, players choose 1 of 3 options for the chance to be awarded an x2 multiplier that applies to the total amount won during free spins.Candy Island Princess: Slot VerdictReplace the grid slot complexity of Moon Princess with basic 3x3 fruit slot type gaming, drop the volatility/max win, then add some skimpy bikinis, and you've got a pretty good idea of what Candy Island Princess is all about. It's a game aimed squarely at players into anime (or the Asian market) who might also be interested in taking a punt on the reels. If a sunny environment, a positive attitude, and compliant anime girls take precedence, then Candy Island Princess might be worth a look.Candy Island Princess is not a game with huge rewards, however. Players might be able to collect a decent win during the Behind the Scenes feature, but outside that, Candy Island Princess isn't a game you play to clear your debts if you hit the max win. The top prize from the Behind the Scenes feature is your best chance at a solid return, while the most you can win overall is 2,200x the bet. In the base or bonus game, The Candy Splash feature is useful in topping you up every now and then. However, at best, 30x the bet wins aren't exactly game-changers. Still, they add to the flow and carefree vibe the game is aiming for.Candy Island Princess might not be a high octane slot, yet it was never designed to be one. Instead, it's almost entirely made for players with a soft spot for smiling cartoon femme's with big eyes, flowing bangs, and chesty assets. If that sounds pretty neat, then Candy Island Princess is sure to whisk you away to a sunny island paradise where everyone is friendly and you might walk away with an okay prize win. If not, then Candy Island Princess comes across as giggly, low thrill cheese."

title: 5 Lions Dance
structured_summary: 5 Lions Dance is an Asian-themed slot set during a Chinese festival with traditional motifs and a guzheng soundtrack. The reviewer finds it a modest, balanced game suited for players seeking a gentler, steady experience rather than big thrills. review: Medium (3/5),0.20/100,"October 15, 2020",5.5,"5 Lions Dance: OverviewWith 5 Lions Dance, Pragmatic Play returns to one of their favoured themes, Asian, in a slot brimming with lions and other motifs from the genre, but also a more subdued affair on all fronts. structured_summary: Buster's Bones is a Wild West-themed slot featuring mischievous, playful dogs set against a canyon backdrop. review: 6.5,"﻿Buster's Bones: Slot OverviewVeteran game designer NetEnt invites players to 'Ride down the dusty back roads of a never-ending canyon and immerse yourself in the mischievous world of Buster's Bones.' When he rests, Buster uses the multiplier to boost payouts when he is part of a win. title: Slurpy
structured_summary: Slurpy is a unique slot themed around symbol-collecting in a Japanese-inspired kitchen setting. It features grid expansion, multiple collectors called Slurpies, various bonus rounds, and a global win multiplier. The reviewer finds it oddly entertaining with a soothing yet upbeat vibe, despite a lower max win of 5,000x bet. The game offers harmonious visuals with a calm atmosphere and joyous 8-bit style audio.
review: 0.20/100,"September 3, 2024",8,"Slurpy: Slot OverviewIf you should never judge a book by its cover, perhaps the same advice applies to slots and their titles. It's hard not to at times though, as some titles give a clear indication of what to expect from the game that follows. In the case of Slurpy from ELK Studios, the title doesn't initially give away a lot of information. What exactly is being slurped, and who is doing the slurping? After giving the game a few spins, okay, the title will make a lot of sense. Without trying to reveal too much at the start, let's say Slurpy involves a lot of symbol-collecting action, grid expansion, feature symbols, and two bonus rounds - regular as well as super.Slurpy looks as though it is held in a kitchen, a Japanese-inspired one as evidenced by a bonsai tree, maybe a sushi kitchen that turns out delicate little morsels of food? The setting is open to interpretation to an extent. Slurpy lacks the visual pop often accompanying an ELK Studios slot, but everything is harmoniously laid out, and the tunes are nothing but joyous.Slurpy slot - base gameTime to see how Slurpy plays, and for starters, its active area begins each base game spin by dropping symbols into a 5x5 space, with a collector, otherwise known as a Slurpie, standing at the top. Each paid spin will cost you 20 c to $/€100, and there are five choices from the X-iter to potentially hurry things along. A highly volatile math model runs the show, spitting out an RTP of 94% whether betting on individual spins as normal or when using the X-iter feature buy options.Slurpy does not have paylines or ways; it is not a regular cluster pays slot or a scatter pays machine. Instead, pay symbols possess values that are awarded when the Slurpie character at the top collects them. The smallest collection grouping is 1 to 3 matching symbols, which pays 0.05 times the bet, while the largest is a 40+ sized group of collected symbols paying 200 times the bet.Slurpy: Slot FeaturesSlurpy slot - free spinsSlurpy has 6 collectors (known as Slurpies), each one colour linked to corresponding pay symbols. Pay symbols that are connected to their collector with a cleared path to the top row create a win. All connected symbols of the same type pay out then are removed from the reels. Clearing all pay symbols expands the grid in 3 levels. The first level is 5x5, the next level is 6x6, and the last is 7x7. Removing all symbols at the top level increases the global multiplier by +5. The global multiplier multiplies every win.The game starts with 1 Slurpie in view, collecting all matching pay symbols with a cleared path to the top. If a win occurs and no more winning symbols have a cleared path to the top, then a new collector is added. The grid refills and the new collector collects any matching pay symbols with a cleared path to the top row. When no more winning symbols can be collected, and a win has happened since the newest collector appeared, the leftmost collector is removed, and a new collector is added. This continues till the collectors cannot collect any more symbols.Second ChanceIf the collectors in view do not match the pay symbols, and one of the other collectors could collect all remaining pay symbols on the reels, the second chance feature triggers. The leftmost collector is removed, adding a new collector.Feature SymbolsAll feature symbols, Coins, and bonus symbols trigger when there is a clear path to the top row.Coin - pays the value displayed times the bet.Multiplier - adds its value to the global multiplier.Level Up - expands the grid up to 7x7.Extra Slurpie - adds an additional Slurpie. Three collectors at the same time is the limit.Super Straw - collects all pay symbols matching the Slurpie who uses the super straw, when the matching symbols do not have a clear path to the top row.Long Straw - collects one cluster of matching pay symbols not connected to the top row.Wild Symbol - links any symbols it is connected to.Double Symbol - can connect two different pay symbols.Bonus GameCollecting 3 scatter symbols triggers 5 free drops. The number of Slurpies, the grid size, and the global multiplier remain when entering the bonus round and between free drops. The bonus starts with a new set of symbols on the grid. If one of the triggering scatters is a super scatter, the super bonus is awarded. In the super bonus, players get 3 Slurpies and a 7x7 grid. One new collected scatter symbol adds +2 free drops.X-iterSlurpy's X-iter menu has these bonus buy choices:Bonus Hunt - 3x the bet, each game round has more than triple the chance of triggering the bonus game.Extra Collector - 10x the bet buys a game round with 3 collectors.Coin Drop - 25x the bet buys a game round, guaranteeing Coins on the reels.Bonus Game - 100x the bet.Super Bonus Game - 500x the bet.Slurpy slot - free spinsSlurpy: Slot VerdictPerhaps when drawing the Battle of Nitropolis series to a close, culminating in the release of Nitropolis 5, ELK Studios was done making wild, gritty, high-octane slots and needed a breather. Since then, we've had Squeeze and now Slurpy, two cheerfully bubbly, about as anti-Nitropolis slots get in just about all regards. It was odd loading up the last two ELK Studios games and not getting that same adrenal tickle as if you've just reached the top of a roller coaster ride and it's about to drop at high speed down the steep side. Slurpy exuded a calm, almost zen atmosphere at first, but hit spin, and it's able to be oddly entertaining.The game is definitely unique, no arguments there, and like a cascading slot, lengthy rolls can ensue when the right-coloured Slurpies keep sliding in from the side at the top of the reels to clear symbols out of the way. You've also got a list of feature symbols augmenting play, from Coin wins to reel expansions, the win multiplier and more. Slurpy's flow is similar to a cluster-paying cascade game, but here, only clusters that can reach the top of the grid to be slurped are awarded. It's odd, but Slurpy sort of works in a never been seen before quite like this type of way, sharing shelf space alongside other ELK Studios experiments such as Jeff & Scully, Sumo Sumo, and Night Trax.In other words, Slurpy is worth having a try, if for nothing else than to experience reel-bound activity you're unlikely to have seen anywhere else. At 5,000x max win, Slurpy steps down a notch or two from the massive winning potential machines we've become accustomed to receiving from ELK Studios, but this doesn't prevent the game from being one to demo if you're feeling adventurous. There was something strangely soothing about the slurping, bleeping, upbeat 8-bit tuned personality Slurpy presents to the world, like a Eurovision act that knows it's not going to win but is having fun in the spotlight anyway."

title: Midas Golden Touch Christmas Edition

review: 2023",7.5,"Midas Golden Touch Christmas Edition: Slot OverviewThe man with the golden touch is back in an updated Xmas version of Thunderkick's mythologically themed 2019 release Midas Golden Touch. Anyway, Midas Golden Touch, the original, was already a pretty fine-looking game, heavy on the golden tones, held in a building that looked like King Midas had been on a touching binge. Then there's a chest, a chalice, a crown, and King Midas as the premiums, paying 15 to 75 times the bet for a 5 OAK hit. King Midas' golden hands are the game's wild symbol, present on all reels. Wilds have the same payout value as the normal Midas pay symbol, and wilds may also be used to substitute for any regular pay symbol. Furthermore, any payline including a wild gets a multiplier depending on the number of wilds in the line. When 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 wilds are used, the multiplier value is x2, x4, x8, x16, or x32, respectively.Midas Golden Touch Christmas Edition: Slot FeaturesMidas Golden Touch Christmas Edition slot - free spinsAdditional features in Midas Golden Touch Christmas Edition are a free spins bonus round where a special respin mechanic comes into play. Hitting 3, 4, or 5 scatter symbols awards 10, 15, or 20 free spins. While free spins are active, collecting 3 scatter symbols during the respin feature grants an extra +10 free spins.Any win in the free spins round triggers the respin feature. During the respin feature, any winning symbols are locked in place while the remaining symbols respin. The respin feature continues until no additional winning symbols are locked. In addition, a single random wild is placed on the reels at the start of each free spin.Midas Golden Touch Christmas Edition slot - free spinsMidas Golden Touch Christmas Edition: Slot VerdictKinda weird celebrating the Christmas season with a character who was said to have been around before the special day had even been invented, but oh well, no biggie, this is gambling, not a history lesson. Then again, Midas Golden Touch was released about 4 years before this Christmas version was, and with the speed slots are dropped (not to mention the sheer number of them), does that length of time constitute iGaming Ancient History? Whatever the answer, Midas Golden Touch was a solid, fairly straightforward slot that plays out just as well in the Christmas Edition. Better, really, due to the virtually unnoticeable in practice yet psychologically uplifting increase in RTP (though flexible RTP wasn't really a thing back then, so you knew what you were getting) and, for bonus buyers, the opportunity to dive right into the main feature.Back when Midas Golden Touch came out, Thunderkick weren't exactly renowned for being feature-buy peeps. This situation has since gone on to totally change, where now, a buy feature in a Thunderkick slot is nothing new. Following on from that, since Midas Golden Touch hit the scene, a bunch of extra winning symbol respin style games have accumulated on the gambling landscape, from the scare fest of Serial to lighter renditions like Hula Balua, for example. What separates Midas Golden Touch Christmas Edition from a lot of them, however, is the way more wilds in a winning line lead to a larger multiplier. A feature so good, Thunderkick has used it not only in the Midas games but also in Phoenix Paradise and Lava Lava.In other words, reviewing Midas Golden Touch Christmas Edition was a bit of a who's who of the gambling world, potentially influencing and/or being influenced by a number of different sources. Putting aside the name-dropping, Midas Golden Touch Christmas Edition is a solid Christmas slot, in some ways arguably better than the original, with the same 10,100 x the bet max win to play for, set within an Xmas meets Ancient History environment."

Or, you can spin the gamble wheel to start with up to 9 free spins and a starting multiplier of up to x10.HippoPop - free spinsHippoPop PopWins: Slot VerdictHippoPop PopWins doesn't do much that its predecessors don't, though the theme is a bit different. It might come across as a slight mismatch of cultures, but it makes a nice break from Egyptian or Irish. AvatarUX has largely avoided using the most obvious themes so far, though, at the rate they are churning these PopWins games out, how long will it be before they run out of original ideas and fall back on the clichés?Moving on to the topic of gameplay, AvatarUX hasn't really pushed to evolve their PopWins mechanic. Not so HippoPop PopWins, which is one of the more straightforward entries in the range. title: Ocean Hunter

review: 2022",5,"Ocean Hunter: Slot OverviewSeriously, what's up with all the fish-based games of late? Here, players need to keep an eye out for Wild Frenzies, free spins, and a couple of optional betting choices.Wild FrenzyAt random on any spin, sharks attack the reels as part of the Wild Frenzy extra. If sharks attack the same symbol more than once, its win multiplier increases by +1 each time, up to a maximum value of x5.Extra Bait BetActivating the Extra Bait Bet puts half an extra virtual worm on the hook. In other words, the stake is increased by 50%, which, in turn, also increases the chance of triggering the Wild Frenzy.Free SpinsLanding 3 radar bonus symbols on reels 1, 3, and 5 awards 15 free spins. On any free spin, oxygen tank symbols may land, and are collected when they hit. When 10, 20, or 30 oxygen tanks have been collected, then reel-set 2, 3, and 4 are unlocked. If it's there, clicking it allows you to pay 100x the bet to instantly trigger free spins.Ocean Hunter: Slot VerdictWhilst Ocean Hunter was an okay game to playthrough, it does feel like the standard dipped between this one and Tyrant Gold Megaways. If not, there isn't much else about Ocean Hunter to really go wild and crazy about. It looks average, comes across as an imitator rather than an innovator despite the new bits, and, doesn't feel like iSoftBet put their 10x coders on it.Some of the more positive things about Ocean Hunter. Okay, well, the Wild Frenzy can indeed get pretty frantic, and the chance of adding wild multipliers to the reels is generally a good thing. The relatively innovative addition of wild reels in free spins has merit too. If wild reels on one grid gets you going, then slapping them on up to four grids at once might be just the ticket. Admittedly, having reels 3, 4, and 5 display a big, teeth bearing wild shark on four grid matrices at once is quite a sight. Having all three reels wild will also go a long way in helping players crack the game's potential.All in all, Ocean Hunter was a pretty average game, though an interest in sharks might aid its allure. Perhaps with all the sharp pointy teeth and talk of apex predators, we were expecting something with a bit more bite than what Ocean Hunter delivered."

title: Book of Cleopatra
structured_summary:
Book of Cleopatra is an Ancient Egypt-themed slot centered around Cleopatra and temple motifs.  
Key features include a free spins bonus triggered by the Book symbol, gamble options to increase free spins, and a bonus buy feature.

review: 6,"Book of Cleopatra: OverviewDeveloper Stakelogic roll out a perennial crowd favourite, the ever rehashed ‘Book of ‘ style in their slot Book of Cleopatra. If you’ve played one, you’ve sort of played them all, to a degree. It might be a little hard to get super excited over test driving yet another ‘Book of’ slot since there are so many clambering over each other in a bid to get players’ attention. You never know, though. Modern developers are a creative bunch, so let’s clear the slate and enter the fray with as open a mind as possible.As everyone knows, Cleopatra was the queen of Egypt, so it is to that otherworldly part of the planet we venture. The 5-reel, 10-payline grid is located in a temple structure, all pillars, statues, and moody crimson skies - the whole shebang. Stakelogic proved their Ancient Egypt chops with Gods of Death, but Book of Cleopatra isn’t quite as atmospheric. It does look like a classic entry into the genre though, plus the soundtrack wafts around in an Arabic manner, so it is a pretty good setting for some book action.Playable from 10 p/c to $/€50 per spin and with a solid RTP of 96.21%, Book of Cleopatra is a highly volatile slot that stays true to its roots by keeping the rules nice and simple. There are just 10 paylines in operation, for players to hit winners of three or more matching symbols on.The symbols include 10 to Ace royals as the low pays, followed by Cat Gods, Bird Gods, a Book of Dead-style Pharaoh, and Cleopatra. Symbols are as high is it gets in this genre which is nice to see. No surprises over Cleopatra being the most valuable at 500 times the stake for five of a kind. Helping matters, in more ways than one, is the Book symbol. One of its jobs is wild, where it can substitute for any other pay symbol.Book of Cleopatra: FeaturesBook of Cleopatra - free spinsIf you’ve played any ‘Book of’ style game or a Stakelogic slot, then there won’t be much here to surprise. The show stopper is, of course, the free spins bonus game, as well as a handy buy feature, and a gamble option.The book symbol is the most desirable one during the base game. Not only does it act as a wild, but it is also the scatter - 3 or more trigger the free spins bonus game, paying 2x, 20x, or 200 times the stake for 3, 4, or 5 in view respectively.Before free spins begin, two events take place. Firstly, you can gamble for more free spins. The initial amount is 10, but players may increase or decrease this number by +5 or -5 per gamble. If you reach 25, the feature automatically moves to the next step. Reach 0, and the bonus game comes crashing to an end.On the next step, the book flips open to choose one of the regular pay symbols. During free spins, this chosen symbol expands to cover the full reel, if winning combinations can be created. Full reel expanded symbols award all 10 paylines and do not need to be adjacent to do so. As a one-off example, expanded symbols on reels 1, 4, 5 payout.Can’t get enough of the bonus game but don’t want to wait? Stakelogic has added a bonus buy feature to short cut the process. For the cost of 80 times the stake, the free spins bonus game is triggered on the next spin. For the record, scatter wins are still valid even if you have paid for them to land.The final segment in this section is the obligatory Stakelogic gamble feature. Each time players get a win; they have the chance to collect the reward or gamble it. This is pretty standard fare. One card is located in the middle of the screen face down. Players guess the correct card colour for double or nothing, or, guess the right suit for quadruple or nothing. If it’s a fail, the win is forfeit; if it’s a win, players may collect or gamble again. The gamble feature is limited to up to 5x or 2,500 coins. The gamble feature may also be available after free spins have concluded.Book of Cleopatra: VerdictOther than the lack of originality, there is little else to complain about in general with Book of Cleopatra. One thing we found annoying is the inability to skip count ups when you land a winner or during the bonus when symbols expand. Still, Stakelogic has captured the look and spirit nicely, symbol values are high, and the gameplay is as good as any other ‘Book of’ slot. Fans should thoroughly enjoy the result. As will any player looking for a straight forward, uncomplicated time. Individual spin potential is in the region of 5,000 times your stake, so there are plenty of rewards to be had.Developers can’t really redo these slots without offering something new, no matter how insignificant the twist might be. Book of Cleopatra has a couple of decent elements that provide individuality. Having the chance to gamble for more free spins should charm some players, and is super satisfying when it works out. The bonus buy functionality will probably have an even wider appeal. ‘Book of’ slots are infamous for their expanding symbols during free spins. So, having the option of sidestepping the base game to head straight to them is a juicy temptation.All up, Book of Cleopatra is a competent slot in a crowded category. It is hard to find faults since Stakelogic has stayed so close to the formula, but its new bits do help it stand out."

title: Aztec Bonanza
structured_summary: Aztec Bonanza explores the ancient Aztec culture with a neon twist, featuring a unique diamond-shaped 5-reel grid and an evolving play area. Key features include the Tumble mechanic, Symbol Unlocking with corner blockers, and a Free Spins round with random modifiers. The reviewer finds the gameplay quickly becomes dull due to uninspired symbols and some frustrating features, despite a high win potential. Visually, the game contrasts detailed Aztec backgrounds with bright, glowing neon symbols, creating a clash that some may find off-putting.
review: 000+",Medium (3.5/5),0.30/150,Out Now,6.5,"Aztec Bonanza (Pragmatic Play): OverviewYou can see why developers are tempted to keep revisiting the Aztec theme. The art, architecture, and ruins provide designers with a ton of great inspiration to incorporate into their game. Not to mention the mystery that surrounds it. It’s a shame Pragmatic couldn’t have used more of it with Aztec Bonanza. While the background art recreates the ancient civilisation quite well, the game area, the part that players spend the most time looking at, is wildly out of place. Join us as we don shades and spin Pragmatic’s latest exotically themed slot.As the title signifies, Aztec Bonanza takes players on a trip through the ancient and mysterious culture of the Aztecs. That is, if they’d survived to the present day and developed a fixation with neon. The setup is quite an unusual one, although not unseen before, and begins with symbols arranged in a diamond-like shape - there are 5 reels, with rows in a 2-4-6-4-2 pattern. On each corner of the grid are blockers which are removed at certain points and can open up the grid. Obviously, this seriously affects win ways which can go as high as 7,776 when the full 5x6 grid is in play. To get started, players are able to manipulate the bet level from 1-10, and the coin value from 0.01 – 0.50. These options provide total stakes from 30 p/c up to $/€150 per spin.When it comes to the rest of the numbers, Aztec Bonanza proudly displays a substantial top prize on the intro screen. Pragmatic’s volatility meter is also on display and at 3.5/5 bolts suggests a medium setting which is a bit lower than they have tended to go recently. The default RTP, meanwhile, is comfortably on the respectable side with a solid rating of 96.53% although this can be  lower depending on where you play the game.The neon nightmare is most pronouncedly expressed with the paytable which is rife with random glowing symbols. On the low side are bright clubs, hearts, and spades – yet no diamonds for some reason. Triangles and squares make up the mid-table, followed by a moon, a blue gem, and a green orb thing as the three premiums. The green orb is worth the most at 2.5 times the stake. There are low values across the board due to the inclusion of a cascade win system known as the Tumble mechanic. Wins are formed by 3 or more adjacent matching symbols on any row. When a winning combination appears on the reels, the symbols part of the winning combination are removed to allow new symbols to fall into the gaps. This can result in chain reactions of wins which not only crank up the payouts but also ties into the features below.Aztec Bonanza (Pragmatic Play): FeaturesAs alluded to, the Tumble feature works hand in hand with the Symbol Unlocking feature. Every 2 tumbles remove one of the blocked corners of the reels. This brings more symbols and win ways into the game, increasing the chances of landing more combinations. Also, whenever one of the corner blockers is removed, it triggers one of the bonus features.When the top left corner is unlocked, Mystery Symbols are added to the reels. The gold, the green-eyed statue is the mystery symbol and all change into matching random pay symbols. Uncovering the top right corner transforms up to three low-value symbols on the board with high-value ones. If the blockers are removed from the bottom left corner, reels 1 and 2 kind of combine, and big 2x2 expanded symbols can land. Lastly, when the bottom right corner is uncovered, the same thing happens to reels 4 and 5. That is, they sort of combine to allow Big 2x2 Symbols as well.When the blockers on all four corners are removed, and no more tumble are possible, then the game triggers the Free Spins feature. The Free Spins round uses the full 5x6 grid for its whole duration - 5 free spins are awarded, and every single spin has one of the modifiers randomly applied to it – Mystery Symbols, Symbol Transform, or Giant Symbols. The rules for these modifiers are the same as explained in the previous paragraph. The Free Spins round cannot be retriggered.Aztec Bonanza (Pragmatic Play): VerdictWhen booting up the game for the first time, we were intrigued by the setup and full of hope due to the juicy winning potential advertised on the splash screen. It didn't take too long, however, for the magic to disappear out the window as the gameplay quickly started to wear thin. First of all, Pragmatic Play has decided to go for the same generic look and feel as Yggdrasil did with their Aztec themed slot Temple Stacks. Literally no effort has gone into making the symbols stand out and even after an hour of playing we couldn't really tell them apart by value. In other words, it gets boring after a while.This issue isn't helped by the fact that some of the features are flat out ridiculous. Take the symbol transformation feature for example. Most of the time its useless and all it does is to annoy the player as it skips the second reel (which prevents symbols from forming winning combinations) whilst insisting on going through with the full animation while you sit there waiting like a fool. Moreover, the free spins feature, if you leave out the fact that it's the part of the game that holds all the potential, is actually less interesting than the base game.Its saving grace, of course, is that huge potential dangled before players on the intro screen. Up to 19,000 times the stake is a mighty tempting lure to be sure. How many spins it took to hit that amount during simulations would be an interesting stat, especially since Pragmatic are known to over-exaggerate the winning potential. For now, even that significant potential isn’t enough to induce a return to this luminous patch of South America.To surmise, Aztec Bonanza has set the standard for this type of slot relatively low. The good thing for fans of the genre is that there are bound to be new alternatives popping up soon enough."

title: Bombuster
structured_summary: Bombuster is a Minesweeper-inspired grid slot with a futuristic, space-themed setting. Its main features include three types of bombs—Destroy, Wild, and Swap—that trigger chain reactions on a 7x7 grid to create cluster wins. The reviewer finds it a middling, casual game with modest volatility and a max win potential of 2,020x stake, lacking big thrills or advanced bonuses. Visually, it offers a minimalist, sleek space vibe with low-key EDM soundtrack, making for a pleasant but understated experience.
review: 6,"Bombuster: OverviewWay back in the day, in between Excel work or dragging files from one folder to another, PC users had the option of killing time with Microsoft's Entertainment Pack. One of the pre-installed games was Minesweeper, an infuriating title where players had to reveal squares that did not contain bombs. Trigger a bomb, one of those round ones with a fuse, and it was game over. Minesweeper was phased out from Windows 8 onwards, but for those who would like a taste of the old days, there is now Bombuster from Red Tiger.Like Minesweeper, Bombuster uses a grid to host the action, this one 7x7 in size. The difference between the two is that now you want the bombs to go off, as this is the gateway to Bombuster's extras. It's not exactly a feature bonanza, but players have Destroy Bombs, Wild Bombs, and Swap Bombs to look out for.At first glance, Bombuster brings to mind Fruit Snap, a previous Red Tiger grid slot, due to the minimal background and the fruity/classic slot symbols. Bombuster has a more futuristic appearance than its predecessor though. Red Tiger has gone for the slot in space vibe, setting the game on the event horizon of a black hole, or something like that. Both games' soundtracks are quite similar too, pumping out some low key EDM while the clusters tumble in. The package is minimalist, yet still easy on the eyes and ears.Playable from 10 p/c to $/€40 per spin and with a 95.74% RTP, Bombuster isn't exactly aiming to be a high-performance grid slot as both potential and volatility sit on the more modest side of the scale. In other words, expect more laid back gaming rather than explosive action.Players hit a win when a cluster of 5 or more similar symbols connect vertically or horizontally. When this happens, winning symbols are removed to let new ones tumble in to the gaps giving more chances to win. The official hit rate hasn’t been released as of yet, though testing produced quite a steady frequency of wins, albeit on the smaller side for the majority of the time.Decent one-off wins are technically possible when symbols land in larger groupings though. For instance, a cluster of 40+ 7's (the highest paying symbol) will net you 1,000 times the stake. From there in descending order, the rest of the symbols are bells, stars, watermelons, plums, oranges, lemons, and cherries. All generic iconography worth from 200 to 900 times the stake for a cluster of 40 or more. The remaining symbol is the big golden 'W' which is wild. It can substitute for any other pay symbol on the board to help make clusters.Bombuster: FeaturesBombuster - bomb feature in actionSo, decent wins are possible from larger clusters, but one thing that might actually prevent them forming are the three bombs which make up the features. These explosive devices appear randomly on the grid where they sit for a certain length of time before exploding to release their modifying powers.When the bombs appear, they have one or more pointers attached. These are called blast patterns indicating the way their effects will go. For example, you might get a Wild Bomb on the first column pointing to the right. You know when this bomb goes off, the row of symbols to the right of it will turn wild. Also, when a bomb goes off, its blast travels all the way to the edge of the grid, triggering any other bombs in its path.The red Destroy Bomb sits on the grid for up to three spins before detonating. When the Destroy Bomb blows, it removes everything in its path, allowing new symbols to fall into place. This bomb cannot destroy symbols created by the Wild or Swap Bombs.The green Swap Bomb remains on the grid for up to 50 spins before it explodes. When it goes off, it leaves one type of symbol along its explosive path. It is possible to have more than one Swap Bomb go off in a sequence, and when this happens all bombs create the same symbol.Yellow Wild Bombs are the most elusive of the trio, remaining on the grid for up to 200 spins before activating. When this one explodes, it places a wild symbol on all positions in its path. Wild symbols will always be revealed, even if other explosions overlap them.Bombuster: VerdictRed Tiger has built up quite a portfolio of grid slots now, of a wide and varied collection. This variety also applies to the xylophone of quality, and you never know quite what you are going to get. Bombuster is one which hovers around the middle of the scale. It's not bad, yet it's not great. The game ticks along in neutral most of the time, nuking the odd symbol, while larger wins threaten to hit. Occasionally, you'll get on a roll of cluster wins, amplified by chain reactions of bombs blowing each other up, adding more mayhem to the procedure.Yet, Bombuster is far from being a grid slot that goes berserk. Without free spins, sticky wilds, or multipliers, it is limited in what it can do. Utilising the tools Bombuster does have, potential of up to just 2,020 times the stake is possible. Massive wins or thrills this is not.All up, casual punters, those who Red Tiger is adept at capturing, may enjoy a lighter grid slot, presented in a pleasant futuristic style. For anything more, players are better off looking elsewhere. These are wilds, Power Glyphs, the Power-Up & Power-Up Stack, plus Magical Maze Free Spins.Wilds & Power GlyphWinning combinations of 3 or more medium symbols or wilds spawn a Power Glyph symbol. During free spins, the Power-Up linked to the Free Spins World is more powerful as well as more frequent.Queen of Hearts Free Spins – the Queen of Hearts removes 2 columns of symbols and creates a Power Glyph in the middle of them.Cheshire Cat Free Spins – the Cheshire Cat picks 2 random low-pay symbol types on the reels and transforms them to a more valuable type.Mad Hatter free Spins – the Mad Hatter gives the grid a better result when shuffled. The White Rabbit is not shuffled.Getting the White Rabbit to the hole at the bottom of the screen awards an additional 1 to 5 free spins and moves into 1 of the 3 different Free Spins Worlds.Buy FeatureInstead of waiting for the White Rabbit to traipse on in to the rabbit hole, players may buy access to the bonus round instead for the cost of 60x the bet. review: Out Now,8.5,"Dragon Maiden (Play'n GO): OverviewPlay'n GO are back with a new title that actually looks quite interesting and one we believe has potential to top the charts of trending slots. title: Goblin Heist Powernudge
structured_summary: Goblin Heist Powernudge is a fantasy-themed slot featuring a mischievous goblin heist storyline set against a fairy tale castle backdrop. The game highlights the innovative Powernudge mechanic combined with a Money Respin feature that awards multipliers and respins triggered by Mystery Money symbols. review: 2022",7,"Goblin Heist Powernudge: Slot OverviewGoblin Heist Powernudge is a fantasy-based slot from developer Pragmatic Play and the second game to use their Powernudge feature. The first was Rise of Giza, an Egyptian odyssey which was a relatively safe way of showcasing the new feature. Goblin Heist pushes the boat out into deeper waters by utilising a more imaginative theme while pairing the Powernudge mechanic with a new and potentially intriguing nudging style Money Respin feature.The intrigue begins the minute Goblin Heist Powernudge appears. Pragmatic Play has turned out an attractive, fairy tale looking slot, and its music adds a thick layer of mystery to the proceedings. Even more so in the bonus game when the soundtrack takes on a funky ska/metal mode. There is little in the way of a back story, but a devious looking goblin stands in the bottom left-hand corner clutching a bag of loot, so let's assume he's just burgled the picture book castle in the background and carry on with the adventure.Hopefully, the goblin has left some treasure over for players to nab, which they can potentially do on a 5x3, 10-payline grid. Winning combinations require at least three matching symbols on a payline, though what's different is that wins can start from any reel. So, a three-symbol hit can land on reels 3, 4, and 5, for example. Also, when a win lands, the Powernudge mechanic activates. After the payout has taken place, all reels that contain at least one winning symbol nudge down one position, while the non-winning reels respin. Nudges continue like this until there are no more winning combinations on the screen.To get the heist rolling, players pick a base stake of 20 p/c to $/€100 and decide whether to activate the Ante Bet option or not. Doing so increases the stake by 25% and adds more Mystery Money symbols to the reels, thus increasing the chance of triggering the bonus game. Playing in normal mode comes with a maximum RTP of 96.47%, dropping slightly to 96.44% when the Ante Bet is switched on.The fantasy theme continues on the paytable, where we find seven regular pay symbols. From lowest value to highest, there are skull keys, scrolls, horns, goblin head-shaped bombs, chests, elven warriors, and goblins. When landing a complete five symbol winning combination, payouts range from 1 to 20 times the stake. Possibly to counteract the Powernudge respin mechanic, or maybe because it messed up the maths, but Goblin Heist does not feature wilds at any time.Goblin Heist Powernudge: Slot FeaturesThe only other symbol to keep a lookout for in Goblin Heist Powernudge is the golden lion Mystery Money symbol, which appears on all five reels. When 6 or more Mystery Money symbols are in view, they trigger the Money Respin feature. When triggered, regular symbols vanish from the reels leaving just Money Symbols or blank spaces behind. Above the main reels, a line of multiplier values starting at x1 appears - one above each of the reels. During the feature, when the reels stop spinning, if Mystery Money Symbols land, they reveal:A cash value of 0.1 to 50 times the total bet.A local multiplier of x1, x2, or x3 which is added to the multiplier above it on the respective reel.A global multiplier of x1, x2, or x3 which is added to all multipliers above each reel.After Money Symbols reveal cash values, they are multiplied by the multiplier above them before being awarded. They then transform back to their lion state and drop down one position while all other reels respin. The bonus round continues in this way until all existing Money Symbols fall off the bottom of the reels and no new ones land.As well as waiting for six Money Symbols to land organically, if the option is available, players can buy the Respin feature for 100 times the stake. RTP when buying fee spins is 96.47%.Goblin Heist Powernudge: Slot VerdictDespite the overhauled theme and completely new bonus round, Goblin Heist felt very similar to Rise of Giza, sharing many of the same pros and cons. On the positive side, Powernudge might not be a paradigm shift, but it's quite original and gives players looking for a cascades alternative something to consider. Try not to expect major windfalls from Powernudge, though, as the limited number of paylines, lack of wilds, and symbol values help keep it in check a lot of the time.The same set of pros and cons go for the Money Respin feature as well really. It has a fairly novel way of going about the business of serving up, then reusing Money symbols, plus the addition of multipliers is pretty much always a good thing. Some players may be enticed by the simplicity of the whole thing, just as much as other players are bored by the lack of sophistication. We wouldn't exactly call Goblin Heist's main feature a massive roiling machine frothing with latent energy. At full power, Goblin Heist Powernudge can produce wins of up to 4,000x the bet; well, this is the win cap at least, and the feature will shut down if it reaches this point. While not the most exciting amount and quickly eclipsed by other bigger respin games, 4K feels like a decent-sized reward for those whom Goblin Heist is presumably aimed at.Let's wrap up by saying the high production values make the game easier to enjoy than it might have been, and Goblin Heist is a decent Rise of Giza follow-on, keeping some things while branching off into new territory. Powernudge wasn't particularly astonishing the first time around, but those who enjoyed Rise of Giza's charms should have no trouble enjoying Goblin Heist's."

title: Heart of Rio

review: 0.25/125,"June 10, 2021",6,"Heart of Rio: Slot OverviewIt's no secret Brazilians like to have a good time, and the crowning jewel in their calendar is the Rio Carnival, a party of truly epic proportions. Wilds land on reels 2, 3, 4, or 5 only.Heart of Rio: Slot FeaturesHeart of Rio - free spinsIf you're a fan of money collect style features or free spins, you're in luck because Heart of Rio has both of them. Disco balls are the money symbols which land on reels 1 to 4. On each spin, the money symbol takes on a random value from a predefined set. If 1 or more money symbols hit at the same time as one of the 5 collect symbol variations on the last reel, then one of the following occurs:Collect – the values of all money symbols in view are added together and paid.Extra credit collect – the value from the extra credit collect symbol is added to all money symbols in view, then the total is paid.Multiplier collect – the value of all money symbols on the reels is multiplied by the value of the multiplier collect symbol, then the product is awarded.Expanding collect – all reels holding a money symbol become covered in money symbols of random values. All are then tallied up and paid.Respin collect – all money symbols in view lock in place and the remaining cells respin. The value of locked money symbols is added to any new ones from the respin and paid.A pair of bongo drums are the scatter symbols, and 3 in view on reels 2-4 award 8 free spins plus a token payout worth 1 times the bet. During free spins, the rules are the same as normal spins regarding the money collect feature, with one key difference. When money symbols hit, their values are also collected in a prize pot. After free spins end, the value of the bonus pot is returned to the reels in the form of a giant money symbol on reels 1-4. A respin occurs, and if a collect symbol hits on reel number 5 the bonus pot is paid. One last point, +8 additional free spins are awarded should 3 scatters land during the feature, with no limit.Heart of Rio: Slot VerdictThe reskin might make Heart of Rio more appealing than its predecessor was for players keen on partying but have a full schedule of commitments. Really though, Heart of Rio is essentially the same as El Dorado City of Gold was, provoking similar reactions. Its mid volatility might be a little too much for some totally laid back casual entertainment, yet not enough for a really wild time either. The middle of the road gaming certainly produced mixed results during test runs.The money collect system offers a quicker, relatively intense experience compared to standard hold & wins. However, unlike regular hold & wins, you don't get the chance to build something massive – in the base game at least. The extra bonus pot is a nice addition during free spins and can get quite exciting for the final respin. It's tough to get that all-important collect symbol on the last spin needed to claim the prize but it is sure to get the blood running when it does drop. Big pots are possible too, and Pragmatic Play claims players can collect wins as high as 10,500 times the stake while spinning Heart of Rio (which should probably be taken with a grain of salt).Despite the claimed sizeable potential, Heart of Rio feels like it's trying to give off the impression it's bigger than it actually is. There are okay moments - decent prize pots are technically possible, plus the money collect turns out alright occasionally, but most of the time, Heart of Rio is closer to a street barbecue than a global celebration of life."

This will become clear shortly. Volatility, with all this going on, is in the medium-high category. At first, the base game is a little so-so. It’s not until wins start to fall, or scatters land that the game starts to get more intense.Prison Escape Slot (Inspired): FeaturesBonus Trail feature in playPrison Escape is a surprisingly complex slot. It doesn’t seem like it at first, but wait till you get the first win. Then, you can Gamble the winnings or collect. If you gamble, the two crooks slide down a zip line. If they make it to the far side, the Blueprint Bonus round is triggered. If they fall, the win is forfeit, and it’s back to the base game. There are three different rooms with three different mini-games to unlock:Wardens Office Bonus: Players open lockers to reveal more keys or stake multipliers. It gives advice based on what will return the highest average pay. The paytable is clear on this, and the low RTP reflects it. The second approach is to play it safe and never gamble, and listen to the walkie-talkie’s advice every time. This results in better odds, but is that playing it too safe?It’s a dilemma and it is very hard not to gamble each win - the small ones at least. It’s a real gamblers game. Wins of 1,000 times the stake are up for grabs if you make it to the end of the Trail with both lives, which is tough to pull off though. Alternatively, a full grid of logos is worth a modest 200 times the stake.Prison Escape’s cheerful look has the potential to seriously sting players who aren’t ready for a volatile ride. If you are up for a solid punt, a bit of risk, where your decisions can lead to intense gaming, then it could be worth a spin. It is a brutal game and quite unconventional game though, so be prepared for that. After the initial excitement of gambling for bonuses the novelty wears off. What really hurts Prison Escape are the very low odds if you gamble wins regularly and the low value rewards for doing so."

review: 0.20/280,"November 21, 2023",8.5,"﻿Nine To Five: Slot Overview""Working nine to five, what a way to make a livin', barely gettin' by, it's all takin' and no givin'', as sang Dolly Parton might be true, but for vast swathes of the population, putting your nose to the grindstone for 8 hours per day is just what you gotta do to get by.
